# Brainrot Visual System — "Every Name Gets a Body"

**Game:** Skip a Brainrot (Roblox)
**Date:** 2026-07-25
**Status:** Approved design, pending implementation plan
**Depends on / feeds:** `2026-07-25-bounded-supply-design.md` (guest debuts use its SEASONS machinery)

## Goal

Brainrots are currently 2.5-stud Neon cubes. Give every roster name a fixed,
recognizable, owned-forever body built from primitives, without touching the
server systems that make brainrots earn, trade, and persist.

## Decisions (settled with the user)

- **Roster**: the 213 originals stay the backbone (verified collision-free by
  the 2026-07-25 provenance research — zero overlaps with real memes or other
  games). **~12 verified-safe guest memes** join over time, drip-fed as
  seasonal `Debut`s per the bounded-supply spec.
- **Guest curation rule**: only names classified MEME with a documented
  outside creator AND no enforcement signals. Excluded explicitly:
  Tung Tung Tung Sahur, Ballerina Cappuccina, Brr Brr Patapim (rights-holder
  activity: Fortnite licenses / Mementum filings / C&D), and Cappuccino
  Assassino (near-duplicate of our Ammazzacaffe Nerissimo). Candidate pool
  (final 12 picked at implementation): Lirilì Larilà, Tim Cheese, Trippi
  Troppi, Boneca Ambalabu, Bandito Bobritto, Glorbo Fruttodrillo, Chimpanzini
  Bananini, Bombombini Gusini, Frigo Camelo, La Vacca Saturno Saturnita,
  Trulimero Trulicina, Bombardiro Crocodilo. Verdict data:
  https://claude.ai/code/artifact/76704d76-76a8-435d-9764-405c850c6e89
  Standing caveat: "no enforcement found" ≠ "no risk" — guests must always be
  individually removable (vaultable) without touching anything else.
- **Look language** (settled last session): goofy creature WITH a face —
  body shape + two eyes + sometimes mouth + stubby limbs + one accessory,
  ~10–16 primitives (Block/Ball/Cylinder/Wedge/CornerWedge only; no uploads,
  no MeshParts, no CSG). One fixed look per name, forever, derived from the
  name — never randomized, identical for every player on every server.
- **Architecture** (revised at implementation, 2026-07-25): bodies are
  generated as **server-side Models in `ServerStorage.BrainrotModels`**,
  consumed by the spawner's EXISTING authored-model path. Idle motion runs
  client-side on tagged models.

## Why the existing model path (architecture revision)

The spec originally proposed client-built bodies over invisible anchors, to
protect three integration points that assumed a brainrot is a single Part.
Reading the live code killed that premise: `BrainrotSpawner` already has a
complete authored-model path — "if ServerStorage.BrainrotModels holds a model
whose name matches the config entry, it is cloned" (its own header calls a
new model "a content drop, not a code change"), with height normalization,
base seating, Model-aware billboard/prompt/mutation-VFX — and `IncomeLoop` /
`BrainrotMover` find brainrots by the `PadIndex` ATTRIBUTE, not by class.
Secret Pete (47 parts, hand-authored, presumably the collaborator's) is live
proof. So we generate 213 Models into that folder at server start and change
ZERO battle-tested server code. Trade-off accepted vs. the client-side idea:
placed bodies replicate (~1,400 parts at full plots) — normal for the genre
and far cheaper than maintaining a parallel rendering path.

## Components

### 1. `ReplicatedStorage.Modules.BrainrotLooks` (new, data)
One explicit recipe per name (all 214 authored entries + guests as they
debut):
```lua
["Scarpa Volante"] = {
  Body = "shoe", BodyColor = <Color3>, Accent = <Color3>,
  Size = 1.0,                 -- scale factor; tier nudges presence
  Face = "happy",             -- eye/mouth preset key
  Accessory = "wings",        -- one accessory key, may be nil
  Motion = "hover",           -- idle animation preset
},
```
Recipes are explicit data — reviewable, hand-tweakable, diffable. They are
GENERATED at authoring time via the lexicon (below), then frozen.

### 2. The Italian lexicon (authoring tool + doc, not runtime code)
~70 word→visual rules mapping the roster's Italian vocabulary to body
shapes, accessories, palettes, and motions (scarpa→shoe body, caffè→cup +
espresso brown, torpedo→long tapered body, volante→wings + hover,
mandolino→instrument accessory…). Applied by the authoring fleet to draft
all 213 recipes; ships as `docs/brainrot-lexicon.md` so future waves inherit
the rules. The name/look joke is the product: "Scarpa Volante" must BE a
flying shoe.

### 3. `ReplicatedStorage.Modules.BrainrotBodyBuilder` (new, pure)
`Build(recipe) → Model` of welded, anchored primitives. Deterministic, no
random calls. Body presets (~12 shapes), face presets (~6), accessory presets
(~15), each a small part-list function. Also used by the Index for
ViewportFrame thumbnails, so the roster UI finally shows creatures.
Budget: ≤16 parts standard, ≤24 for Secrets.

### 4. `ServerScriptService.BrainrotModelFactory` (new)
At server start: builds every BrainrotLooks recipe into a Model inside
`ServerStorage.BrainrotModels` (pcall per name — a bad recipe skips, never
blocks), SKIPPING names that already have hand-authored models (Secret Pete
must never be overwritten). Templates carry the CollectionService tag
"BrainrotBody" and a `Motion` attribute; clones inherit both. The existing
spawner then finds the templates naturally — no spawner changes.

### 5. `StarterPlayer.StarterPlayerScripts.BrainrotIdleClient` (new)
Client-side idle motion for models tagged "BrainrotBody": one Heartbeat loop
for all bodies, motion preset per the model's `Motion` attribute (bob / sway /
hover / spin / shiver / none), phases staggered by name-hash (never
math.random — looks must be stable), distance-gated beyond ~120 studs, and
capped at the nearest 80 bodies. Server parts are anchored, so client-local
CFrame writes never replicate back.

### 6. Bespoke tiers
The 11 Secrets + Secret Pete get hand-authored bespoke recipes (still
primitives, up to 24 parts) — they are the trophies and get the extra care.
Guest memes get bespoke primitive INTERPRETATIONS of their canonical look —
always our own build from scratch, never imported assets.

## Quality gates

1. **Uniqueness check (automated)**: no two recipes may share
   (Body, Accessory, quantized BodyColor) — a script over BrainrotLooks
   fails loudly on collision.
2. **Coverage check (automated)**: every name in BrainrotConfig has a recipe;
   every recipe key exists in BrainrotConfig (no orphans).
3. **Part-budget check (automated)**: Build() each recipe once in Studio,
   count parts, assert ≤16 (≤24 bespoke).
4. **Visual sampling (manual + screenshots)**: Play-mode screenshots of a
   spread of tiers from the player's actual viewpoint (standing rule:
   verify from the user's angle, measure real footprints — see
   verify-spatial-fix memory).
5. **Regression**: income still ticks, store/trade prompts still work, and
   billboards still track with bodies rendered (the 3 integration points).

## Edge cases

- **Body removed mid-animation** → animator cleanup is driven by the
  "BrainrotBody" tag-removed signal / AncestryChanged, never polled.
- **Player joins with plots already full** → animator starts from
  `CollectionService:GetTagged`, then listens for additions.
- **Unknown name (future wave before recipes ship)** → fallback recipe (the
  classic cube, as a wink) + warn once; never error.
- **Index thumbnails for locked names** → silhouette-only render (black
  body, eyes visible) to preserve the reveal.
- **Low-end devices** → bodies are static beyond distance gate; motion loop
  budget capped (single loop, staggered phases, no per-body connections).

## Testing

- Studio Play mode: spawn a spread of tiers on a plot, screenshot from
  player viewpoint, verify silhouettes read at gameplay distance.
- Automated gates 1–3 run as a Studio command script before ship.
- Trade/store/income smoke test with bodies live.


===== FILE: docs/specs/2026-07-25-cafe-restyle-design.md =====
# Cafe Restyle — Design

**Date:** 2026-07-25
**Status:** Approved (user said "go" 2026-07-25)
**Scope:** Art direction only. Zero gameplay change.

## Goal

Make "Skip a Brainrot" read as **bubbly / cozy-cartoon**, matching the look and feel of
the Roblox game **[☕] Own a Cafe** (universeId `8935993972`, placeId `131906518201863`).

The user's words: *"I like where the cabin is, the plots, the dock. But if you could just
change the materials and make it all bubbly vibes."*

## Non-goals

- **Nothing moves.** Cabin, plots, dock, shops, throw zone, trading island all keep their
  exact positions. This is explicitly not a layout change.
- **No gameplay, economy, data-schema or remote changes.** Every button keeps its current
  behaviour. If a change alters what a control *does*, it is out of scope.
- Not a world rebuild. Terrain geometry (the heightmap valley, lake, mountains) is kept;
  only its *colours and materials* are in play.

## Reference

Own a Cafe: launched 2025-10-13, ~1,891 concurrent players, 937k visits, 10.6k favourites,
updated 2026-07-26. Actively maintained, so it is a safe style to chase.

### Extracted style recipe

Read from two in-game screenshots supplied by the user (the "Hire Friends" panel and an
NPC dialogue prompt):

| Element | Treatment |
|---|---|
| Panel body | Cream, **light** — approx `rgb(247,235,216)` |
| Header | Solid warm-brown bar, approx `rgb(192,117,46)`, faint coffee-bean pattern |
| Outline | Thick **dark brown** approx `rgb(62,34,19)` on every shape *and* every glyph. Never black. |
| Corner radius | Generous, applied everywhere |
| Card | Cream `rgb(245,220,192)`, dark-brown outline, rounded |
| Buttons | Colour carries meaning: green confirm `rgb(79,194,79)`, gold primary CTA `rgb(245,193,58)` with diagonal stripes, pink close `rgb(240,71,155)` |
| Text | Rounded bubbly font, always stroked; italic for flavour lines |
| Header icon | Chunky icon left of the title |
| World | Flat saturated green, no texture detail, chunky low-poly conifers, soft shadows |

Colour values are eyeballed from screenshots and will be tuned against the real thing
during Stage 5.

## Current state

### The lucky part

`ReplicatedStorage.Modules.UITheme` already implements most of this recipe under
`UITheme.Camp`: heavy outlines on shapes and glyphs, one accent colour per card carried
through border + title + sunburst, chunky overhanging header, two-tone gradients, fat
pills. Twelve ScreenGuis were already converted onto it on 2026-07-24 (`ClientMain`,
`SideRail`, `SeasonClient`, `DailyRewardClient`, `QuestClient`, `IndexClient`,
`RebirthClient`, `FusionClient`, `OfflineEarningsClient`, `ToastClient`,
`RareCatchClient`, `LuckHUDClient`).

So the cafe conversion is a **token and helper swap inside one module**, not a rewrite.
Four deltas:

1. Panels are dark → make them cream
2. Ink is black → make it dark brown
3. Ribbon headers → solid header bar
4. Sunbursts behind icons → removed

### Known current values

- Terrain `SetMaterialColor`: Grass `(94,110,56)`, LeafyGrass `(74,101,54)`,
  Rock `(138,136,132)`, Ground `(120,100,74)`, Snow `(236,240,245)`, Sand `(198,186,158)`
- Water: `WaterColor(10,92,118)`, Transparency `0.13`, Reflectance `0.22`
- Lighting: ClockTime ~14, Brightness `2.1`, ExposureCompensation `0`,
  ColorShift_Top `(255,244,224)`, OutdoorAmbient `(150,156,148)`, Ambient `(80,100,120)`,
  Atmosphere Density `0.05`, Haze `0.5`, GlobalShadows on, ShadowSoftness `0.2`,
  GeographicLatitude `41`; Bloom + SunRays + DepthOfField + ColorCorrection present
- Trees: `TreeCandidateA` clones — ~618 in `GameWorld.Forest`, more in
  `GameWorld.MountainForest` and `GameWorld.Scenery`, plus 5 per plot camp
- Dock: `GameWorld.SkipDock`, WoodPlanks warm oak `(150,110,68)`, deck top y3.4

### Known blockers

- **Two competing style systems.** `ReplicatedStorage.Modules.UIStyle` (the collaborator's,
  newer) and `UITheme.Camp` (ours) both exist. `SideRail` has already been moved onto
  `UIStyle`. One must be chosen as canonical before Stage 5, or the restyle will be undone
  by whoever edits next. **This is a conversation with the collaborator, not a code fix.**
- **Studio MCP is not connected in this session.** Nothing can be changed until the user
  toggles Assistant settings → MCP Servers → "Enable Studio as MCP server" off then on.
- **Stages 3 and 4 touch shared ground** — the throw area and terrain are the
  collaborator's section. They need a heads-up before either runs.

## The five stages

Each stage is independently shippable, verified in play, and revertible. The user reviews
after each and decides whether to continue.

### Stage 1 — Low-poly trees

Replace ~618 realistic pines with chunky low-poly cartoon trees. This carries more of the
"bubbly" read than anything else on the list.

- **Source:** free Creator Store low-poly nature pack (user's choice). Vet each candidate
  for part count before committing — 618 trees times a heavy model will destroy framerate.
  Target is a handful of parts per tree, `CanCollide = false`, no scripts, no meshes with
  huge texture memory.
- **Method:** swap the source model, re-run the existing raycast scatter (it already
  handles surface-seating, slope rejection, and water avoidance).
- **Touches:** `GameWorld.Forest`, `GameWorld.MountainForest`, `GameWorld.Scenery`, and the
  5 pines per plot camp.
- **Verify:** tree count matches before/after; no tree floating or buried; framerate in
  play is not worse; no tree intersects the dock, shops or plots.
- **Rollback:** keep the old `TreeCandidateA` model in ServerStorage; re-run scatter with it.

### Stage 2 — Flat cartoon lighting

Cartoon lighting is **low contrast**: bright ambient fill, soft shadows, minimal haze.

- Raise `Ambient` and `OutdoorAmbient` so shadows lift toward mid-grey rather than black
- Reduce contrast; keep `Brightness` near current so the scene does not blow out
- Increase `ShadowSoftness`; keep `Atmosphere.Density` low (the far-peak visibility fix
  from 2026-07-23 must not regress)
- Retune `ColorCorrection` toward higher saturation, lower contrast
- **Verify:** far peaks still visible; dock and camp read clearly; no blown highlights
- **Rollback:** ~10 properties, captured before the change and restored verbatim

### Stage 3 — Parts to SmoothPlastic

Sweep world Parts to `SmoothPlastic` with a soft saturated colour map. This is what kills
the "realistic" read on the dock, plots, shops and props.

- Explicitly **excluded**: anything whose material is load-bearing for gameplay or reading
  (Neon accents, water, invisible barriers/hitboxes, ProximityPrompt parts)
- **Requires collaborator heads-up** — touches the shared throw area
- **Verify:** no collision or `CanQuery` change; throw still works from every dock spot;
  prompts still fire
- **Rollback:** snapshot `{instance, Material, Color}` for every part touched before writing

### Stage 4 — Flatten terrain tints

- Brighten and saturate the `SetMaterialColor` palette toward the flat cartoon greens seen
  in the reference
- Set `LeafyGrass`'s material colour **equal to** `Grass` so the two read as one flat green.
  Explicitly *not* `ReplaceMaterial` — no voxel is rewritten, so this stays a pure colour
  change and reverts by restoring one value.
- Evaluate turning terrain decoration off
- **Requires collaborator heads-up**
- **Verify:** lake shore still reads; the dock water-pier carve is untouched; no terrain
  geometry regenerated (colour-only operations — no `WriteVoxels`, `FillBlock`, or
  `ReplaceMaterial`)
- **Rollback:** restore the six recorded material colours

### Stage 5 — Cafe UI and font

- **Font:** build a proof board in Studio rendering real menu strings in candidate Roblox
  fonts (FredokaOne, Grandstander, LuckiestGuy, Nunito, Bangers) side by side; screenshot;
  user picks. Do not guess the font from marketing art.
- **Tokens:** swap `UITheme.Camp` values — dark panel to cream, black ink to dark brown
- **Helpers:** `M.ribbon` gains (or is joined by) a solid header-bar variant; `M.sunburst`
  calls are retired from card icons
- **Propagation:** the 12 already-converted ScreenGuis inherit the change
- **Verify:** every ScreenGui still initialises with no load errors; all rail tiles present;
  each panel opens and its buttons still fire their existing handlers
- **Rollback:** the token table is one commit; revert it

## Risks

- **`UIGradient` tints the parent's own text.** Already burned us once. Keep gradients on
  the button and put text in a child `TextLabel`. `UITheme.campButton` is *not yet audited*
  for this on its dark/locked states — Stage 5 must sweep it.
- **`ClipsDescendants` does not clip rotated descendants.** Relevant if any rotated
  decoration survives into the cafe style.
- **Collaborator collision.** `yeep1234` is often live in the same Studio session. Stages
  touching shared areas must be announced, and no stage should run while they are editing
  the same objects.
- **Nothing is committed to git.** All UI code lives only in Studio; `game-src/` mirrors
  just 11 gameplay files. A bad stage cannot be recovered with `git checkout` — hence the
  explicit per-stage snapshot requirement.

## Out of scope

- Publishing. The game is still private and the `Brainrot pack1` IP problem is unresolved.
- The idle/offline-earnings layer discussed earlier as an Own a Cafe mechanic. That is a
  gameplay feature, tracked separately.


===== FILE: docs/specs/2026-07-27-catch-reveal-design.md =====
# Catch Reveal — Design

**Date:** 2026-07-27
**Status:** Approved (user approved the ladder and the plumbing 2026-07-27)
**Scope:** Client presentation only. Zero server, economy, data-schema or remote changes.

## Goal

When you catch a brainrot, **the brainrot itself appears on your screen and spins slowly**,
escalating with rarity. The user's words: *"I dont want a card I want a 3d brainrot
spinning"* and *"escalate by rarity is also perfect."*

Today a catch produces a small text card — `LEGENDARY` / the name / `Distance: 340m | +$1.2k/s` —
so you never see the thing you caught. The 150 models already sit in
`ReplicatedStorage.BrainrotModels` and `BrainrotThumb` already renders them. This closes the gap.

## Non-goals

- **No card.** The existing `resultFrame` popup is retired, not decorated.
- **No server changes.** `ThrowResult` already carries every field the reveal needs.
  Nothing in `ServerScriptService` is edited in this phase — the place is shared with
  `yeep1234`, and a client-only change cannot collide with their work.
- **The Robux skip / auto-sell upgrade is NOT built here.** See "Phase 2 hooks" below.
  This spec only guarantees the reveal is shaped so that upgrade is a small addition.
- No new remotes, no new player data fields, no changes to what any control *does*.

## Phase split

The user asked for two things: the reveal, and a purchasable Robux upgrade that skips the
animation and auto-sells a chosen rarity. They chose **"reveal now, upgrade next"**.

Phase 2 is genuinely separate: it needs a product created on the Creator Dashboard (which
Claude cannot do, and which has blocked work on this project before), server-verified
ownership checks, a per-player "which rarities to auto-sell" setting, and a settings UI.
Half of it ("skip the animation") cannot exist until the animation does.

## Reference points in the live code

| Thing | Where | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Catch payload | `ThrowHandler.revealCatch` → `remotes.ThrowResult:FireClient` | Carries `BrainrotName`, `Rarity`, `RarityColor`, `Mutation`, `CashPerSecond`, `Serial`, `Distance`, `Perfect`. Complete for our needs. |
| Old card | `ClientMain`, `remotes.ThrowResult.OnClientEvent` (~line 602) | `resultFrame` + `resultToken`. Retired by this change. |
| World FX | `ClientMain.celebrateCatch` | FOV punch at Rare+, light pillar + camera shake at Epic+. Kept for bands 1–3, suppressed for band 4. |
| 3D thumbnails | `ReplicatedStorage.Modules.BrainrotThumb` | `master(name)` cached stripped model, `add(parent, name, opts)` ViewportFrame with bounding-box-framed camera. |
| UI rarity flair | `ReplicatedStorage.Modules.RarityFX` | Existing vocabulary: halo stroke, shine sweep, sparkles, rainbow cycle. One shared `Heartbeat` driver. |
| 3D mutation FX | `ReplicatedStorage.Modules.MutationFX` | `apply(model, mutationName)` / `clear(host)`. 12 rungs in 4 bands. **World-only.** |
| Tiers | `ReplicatedStorage.Modules.RarityConfig` | 8 tiers, Common → God, each with a `Color`. |
| Mutation colour | `MutationConfig.Color(name)`, `.Rarity(name)` | 12 rungs, Golden(1) → Angel(12). |

### The constraint that shapes the whole design

**ParticleEmitters and `Highlight` do not render inside a `ViewportFrame`.**
`BrainrotThumb` already states this in its own header comment: *"Viewports only draw
BaseParts… Those render nothing."*

`MutationFX` is built entirely from those two instance types. So a viewport reveal
structurally cannot show mutations, and a world reveal can. That is the sole reason the
design is hybrid rather than one render path.

## The ladder

Four bands over the eight tiers, grouped to match how `RarityFX` and `MutationFX` already
band things. Each band adds a **new kind** of effect rather than more of the last — the
rule that made the `MutationFX` and `RarityFX` ladders readable.

| Band | Tiers | Render | Length | Backdrop | Adds |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Common, Uncommon | ViewportFrame, small (~180px) | 1.4s | none | model + name/rarity |
| 2 | Rare, Epic | ViewportFrame, ~280px | 2.0s | 15% dark | coloured halo in tier colour |
| 3 | Legendary, Mythic | ViewportFrame, ~380px | 2.8s | 45% dark | rays behind + sparkles |
| 4 | Secret, God | **real world model** | 3.8s | 80% dark | camera lock, full `MutationFX`, rainbow name |

"n% dark" is a full-screen black `Frame` at `BackgroundTransparency = 1 - n`, fading in over
0.2s and out with the reveal. Stated as opacity because "dim 0.8" read as a transparency
value would mean the opposite of what is intended.

All pixel sizes, durations and dim values are **starting points to be tuned by eye in
Studio**, the way the trees, the font, the terrain palette and the SFX kit were. The
structure is fixed; the numbers are not.

### The spin

One identity across all four bands: **constant angular velocity around world Y**, no
easing, starting from `BrainrotThumb`'s existing front-quarter `DEFAULT_DIR` so the model
faces the player on arrival.

Default **70°/second** — a full turn every ~5.1s. Band 1 therefore shows ~98°, band 4
~266°. Deliberately not "one full turn per band": a shared rate makes every reveal feel
like the same object, which is what "smooth slow spin" asks for. Per-band override allowed
but expected to stay unused.

Driven by a **single connection that exists only while a reveal is playing** and disconnects
on teardown — `RarityFX`'s one-driver pattern, not a connection per reveal.

`RenderStepped`, not `Heartbeat`: band 4 moves the camera, and camera work done on
`Heartbeat` lands a frame late and judders. `RarityFX` uses `Heartbeat` because it only
tints UI, where a frame of latency is invisible.

### Text

Name and rarity only, as floating outlined labels beneath the model. **No panel, no
background** — that is the point of the change. Rarity in `RarityColor`, name in
`UITheme.Camp` ink with `UITheme.inkText` outlining, `UITheme.Font` for the face.

A mutated catch shows the mutation as a name prefix (`Angel Tralalero Tralala`), matching
what `RareCatchClient` already does.

**Band 4's "rainbow" is the rarity label cycling hue**, `Color3.fromHSV((t * 0.3) % 1, 0.82, 1)`
— the same one-property technique `RarityFX` uses for Secret/God tiles. It is called out
because bands 1–3 carry rarity in a static tier colour and there is no card or border in
band 4 for a rainbow to live on.

Distance and cash/s are **dropped**. Distance is already displayed live while the stone
flies; cash/s is visible in the backpack grid.

### Mutations by band

- **Bands 1–3 (viewport):** particles cannot render. The mutation shows as the name prefix
  plus the halo retinted to `MutationConfig.Color(name)` instead of the tier colour.
- **Band 4 (world):** `MutationFX.apply()` runs on the real model — all 12 rungs, real
  lights, sparkles, motes and `Highlight`. This is the payoff for the hybrid, and it lands
  exactly where it matters: Secret and God are the catches where a mutation is most worth seeing.

### Interaction with existing world FX

`celebrateCatch` keeps firing for bands 1–3. For band 4 it is suppressed: the camera is
locked on the model, so the pillar spawned around the player's character would be
off-screen, and a camera shake would fight the lock.

## Architecture

Two new files, one edited file, nothing on the server.

### `ReplicatedStorage.Modules.CatchReveal` (new ModuleScript)

Owns the reveal and nothing else. Knows nothing about remotes, and nothing about Robux.

```
CatchReveal.play(info) -> handle     -- info = {Name, Rarity, RarityColor, Mutation}
handle:skip()                        -- tear down immediately; safe to call twice
CatchReveal.isPlaying() -> boolean
```

A module rather than loose code inside the client script because fusion results, wheel wins
and egg hatches are all plausible future callers of the same reveal, and because it can then
be exercised in isolation from a real throw.

Internal responsibilities: pick the band from `Rarity`, build the UI (dim + viewport +
labels) or the world model + locked camera, run the spin driver, tear everything down.

### `StarterPlayerScripts.CatchRevealClient` (new LocalScript)

Subscribes to `remotes.ThrowResult`, decides whether to reveal, calls `CatchReveal.play`.
Deliberately thin — it is the seam where phase 2 plugs in.

### `ClientMain` (edited)

- Stop showing `resultFrame` on `ThrowResult`. The frame and its styling block are left in
  place but unused, so the change is a one-line revert if the user wants the card back.
- `celebrateCatch` gains an early return for Secret/God (band 4 suppression).

**Collision risk:** `ClientMain` is a shared file the collaborator has live-edited before.
Both edits are small and localised; re-read the file immediately before editing rather than
trusting line numbers from this spec.

## Phase 2 hooks

Two hooks, in two different places, for two different reasons.

**Skip — client-side, and that is correct.** `CatchRevealClient` gets:

```lua
local function shouldReveal(result)  -- phase 2: check gamepass + chosen rarities
    return true
end
```

Skipping an animation is a pure presentation choice. A client lying about it costs nothing,
so the client may own it.

**Auto-sell — server-side, and this is not negotiable.** It belongs in
`ThrowHandler.revealCatch`, where the catch is granted, behind a server-verified
`MarketplaceService:UserOwnsGamePassAsync` check and a server-stored per-player rarity
selection.

A client that can say "sell this catch" can say it about anything, which is a free-money
exploit.

**No server file is touched in this phase, including by comment** — the extension point is
recorded here in the spec, not marked in `ThrowHandler`, so that "nothing on the server"
stays literally true and there is no chance of colliding with the collaborator over a
comment. Recording it explicitly because the two features were requested in one sentence,
and building auto-sell into the reveal would be the natural — and wrong — reading.

## Failure modes

| Failure | Handling |
|---|---|
| No model for that name (`BrainrotThumb.master` returns nil) | Fall back to a text-only reveal: name + rarity, no viewport. A missing model must never cost the player their catch or throw an error. |
| **Camera left locked after band 4** | Restore inside `pcall`, plus a watchdog `task.delay(duration + 3)` that force-restores if teardown never ran. Same belt-and-braces as `ThrowHandler`'s existing flight watchdog. A stuck camera is unrecoverable without rejoining, so it gets two independent guards. |
| A catch lands mid-reveal | Newest wins, token-guarded so a stale teardown cannot kill a newer reveal. Matches the existing `resultToken` behaviour in `ClientMain`. |
| Character dies / resets mid-reveal | Tear down, restore camera, disconnect the driver. |
| Character or camera missing when a reveal starts | Skip the reveal silently. Never error. |
| World model leaks | Client-created so it never replicates to other players. Anchored, `CanCollide = false`, `CanQuery = false`. Explicitly destroyed on teardown, with `Debris:AddItem` as a backstop. |
| `MutationFX.apply` errors on an odd model | `pcall`. The reveal must survive a bad mutation far more than it must show one. |

## Verification

- **All eight tiers.** `ThrowHandler` already has a `forcedCatch` override — force one catch
  per tier and confirm each band renders with the right size, dim and effects.
- **Band 4 with a mutation.** Confirm real `MutationFX` particles appear on the world model —
  this is the specific thing the hybrid exists to deliver, so it must be seen, not assumed.
- **Fallback path.** Force a catch with a name that has no model; confirm text-only and no error.
- **Camera restore.** After every band-4 reveal, and after a mid-reveal `skip()`, and after a
  death during a reveal.
- **Rapid catches.** Two catches close together; confirm the newer reveal survives and the
  older teardown does not kill it.
- **Zero console errors** across the whole sweep.
- **FPS A/B in a single session** — Studio's absolute FPS numbers drift between sessions
  (measured 15.1 and 29.0 minutes apart on an unchanged scene), so only same-session
  comparisons count.

Verification is by looking at the real thing in Studio, not by reading the code back.


===== FILE: docs/specs/2026-07-27-sell-list-and-close-button-design.md =====
# Sell List Thumbnails + Close Button X — Design

**Date:** 2026-07-27
**Status:** Approved (user approved the ladder of changes and the UIStyle decision 2026-07-27)
**Scope:** Client UI only. Zero server, remote, economy or data-schema change.

## Goal

Two small, independent fixes the user asked for:

1. **Show the actual brainrots when selling.** The sell list identifies each brainrot by name and a flat coloured circle. Every other inventory surface in the game now shows a real 3D model.
2. **Make the close button's X visible.** The user's words: *"right now its just a red circle."*

## Non-goals

- No change to what selling *does* — prices, multipliers, the sell remote and its server validation are untouched.
- No restyle of the panels themselves. The close button keeps its position, size, colour and behaviour; only the glyph changes.
- Not a fix for panels that have no close button at all. Every panel in scope already has one; it is merely invisible.

---

## Part 1 — The close button X

### Root cause, established by proof board not by reading

`UITheme.styleClose` sets `btn.Text = "\u{2715}"` (✕, U+2715). **That character does not render in this Roblox build.** The button therefore draws as a bare red circle.

Proved with a live proof board of five candidates on identical plain-red buttons, screenshotted in Play:

| Glyph | Result |
|---|---|
| `\u{2715}` ✕ — **currently shipped** | **blank** |
| `\u{00D7}` × | renders, thin |
| `X` (ASCII) | renders, clean |
| `\u{2716}` ✖ | renders, bold |
| two rotated `Frame`s | renders, thickest — **chosen** |

**An earlier diagnosis was wrong and is worth recording.** `IndexClient:245` carries the comment `-- keep GothamBold from styleClose: FredokaOne has no U+2715 glyph`. That treated the problem as font-specific and "fixed" it by pinning GothamBold. The board was rendered *in GothamBold* and still came out blank, so U+2715 is missing there too and that workaround never worked. **Do not re-fix this by switching fonts.**

A second theory — that `M.gradient`'s `UIGradient` was multiplying the white glyph down to red, a documented trap in this codebase — was also tested and **disproved**: a variant with the glyph on a child `TextLabel`, which a parent gradient cannot touch, was equally blank.

### The change

`UITheme.styleClose` stops setting `Text` and draws the X as **two rotated `Frame`s**. Not a glyph, so it cannot depend on a font or a Roblox version again.

- Bars sized **relative to the button**, so the same code is correct at `UITheme`'s 30px and `UIStyle`'s 34px.
- **Idempotent:** any previously created bars are cleared first, so a second `styleClose` call cannot stack them.
- Bars must not intercept input — the button itself stays the click target.
- Colour stays white against the red fill, matching today's intent.

### Blast radius

`UITheme.styleClose` has **7 call sites covering 8 panels**, all of which inherit the fix with no per-panel edits: `RebirthClient`, `QuestClient` (Goals), `DailyRewardClient`, `FusionClient`, `IndexClient`, `MerchantClient`, and `ClientMain` — the last is one call site in a loop that styles **two** panels, Shop and Sell.

**9 panels in total** are fixed once `UIStyle` is included.

`SeasonClient` goes through **`UIStyle.styleClose`** — the collaborator's separate module, carrying its own copy of the same `"\u{2715}"` bug. The user approved fixing it too, as a self-contained one-function change. It gets its own copy of the bar-drawing rather than a cross-module dependency, because making the collaborator's module depend on ours is an architectural decision that needs their agreement, not a bug fix.

⚠️ `IndexClient:244-245` and `DailyRewardClient` both set `closeBtn.ZIndex = 18` *after* calling `styleClose`, which forces ZIndex 6. The bars must sit above the button at whatever ZIndex the caller later chooses.

**A one-time read of the button's ZIndex at draw time is NOT sufficient** — it would freeze the bars at 7 and strand them *under* the button once a caller raises it to 18, reproducing the exact invisibility being fixed. The bars must **track** the button's ZIndex, via `GetPropertyChangedSignal("ZIndex")`, with the connection cleaned up on redraw. (Corrected 2026-07-27: an earlier draft of this spec said "derive at draw time", which the implementation correctly did not take literally.)

---

## Part 2 — Brainrots in the sell list

`buildSellList` in `ClientMain` builds one `UITheme.accentCard` row per distinct unplaced brainrot. The row's 56px icon tile holds a sunburst backdrop plus a flat 34px circle coloured by rarity.

### The change

Replace the flat circle with a real 3D model via **`BrainrotThumb.add(icon, name, opts)`** — the same shared module the backpack grid and the catch reveal already use. No new machinery.

- The sunburst backdrop tile stays; only the circle is replaced.
- **The tier colour moves to the icon tile's border.** Today the circle is the row's only rarity cue, so replacing it would lose the tier read entirely. Putting rarity on the border is exactly what the backpack grid does, which also makes the two views consistent.
- Row height, layout, ordering, counts, prices and the sell buttons are untouched.

### Why this is cheap

`BrainrotThumb.master(name)` caches one stripped master per name and hands out clones, and the sell list only ever shows distinct *names* (it groups duplicates by name with an `×N` count), so the viewport count is bounded by the number of distinct unplaced brainrots — far below the 58-viewport backpack grid that measured a ~2% FPS cost.

---

## Failure modes

| Failure | Handling |
|---|---|
| **No model for that name** — `BrainrotThumb.master` returns nil. `Maxwell` is the only such entry of 151, but the roster changes. | Fall back to today's flat coloured circle. A missing model must never blank the row or break selling. |
| A row is rebuilt while its viewport exists | `buildSellList` already destroys and rebuilds all child Frames; the viewport dies with its row. No registry to leak. |
| `styleClose` called twice on one button | Bars cleared before redraw; cannot stack. |
| A caller raises the close button's ZIndex after styling (IndexClient does) | Bars derive ZIndex from the button at draw time and sit above it. |

## Verification

Both changes are **visual**, so both are verified by screenshot, not by reading properties back. Two hard-won constraints from the catch-reveal work apply directly:

- Properties written every frame cannot be read back by the tooling — irrelevant here since nothing animates, but the general rule stands: **look at it**.
- Studio must be in Edit mode to install and Play mode to see it.

Checks:
1. Open all **9** panels and confirm a visible X — the 8 on `UITheme` (Rebirth, Goals, Daily, Fusion, Index, Merchant, Shop, Sell) plus Season on `UIStyle`.
2. Confirm each X still *closes* its panel — the bars must not have stolen the click.
3. Open the Sell panel with a mixed inventory and confirm models render, one per distinct name, with the tier colour readable on the border.
4. Confirm the `Maxwell` fallback renders a coloured circle rather than an empty tile.
5. Zero console errors across the sweep.


===== FILE: docs/specs/2026-07-27-wheel-candy-restyle-design.md =====
# Wheel Candy Restyle + Buyable Spins — Design

**Date:** 2026-07-27
**Status:** Approved (user approved art direction, wheel-first ordering, scope and the details-panel decision 2026-07-27)
**Scope:** Phase 1 is client-only. Phases 2–3 add a per-player spin balance and a Robux product.

## Goal

The user's words: *"our wheel looks too basic."* Rebuild the daily spin wheel in the **candy / Pet-Simulator** visual direction supplied in their design handoff, add the information the reference shows (per-segment odds, a details panel), and add buyable extra spins.

## Origin of the art direction

The user supplied `Roblox Brainrot Game UI.zip` — a full design handoff (`design_handoff_brainrot_ui/`) with a README and three HTML mockups built specifically for this game. **Build from v3**, the bright/candy treatment. Plus separate reference screenshots of another game's "Crystal Wheel".

**The handoff is a whole-game UI redesign** — HUD plus eight modal panels. This spec covers **only the wheel**. Two of its panels (egg hatching, gems) describe systems this game does not have and are out of scope entirely. The handoff contains **no wheel**; the wheel references are the user's separate screenshots. The user's note on those: *"They don't need to necessarily be that spiky and popping."*

### The art-direction decision, and the revert path

The handoff's palette (sky blue, white panels, Luckiest Guy) is a **different direction from the cafe restyle** completed days earlier (cream, warm-brown ink, Own a Cafe reference, five stages). The user chose **"go full candy and if we don't like it just revert it back."**

That revert requirement is honoured **by not overwriting anything**:

- Candy lives as a **new `UITheme.Candy` token table plus additive helpers**, beside the existing `Camp`.
- **`Camp` and every current caller are untouched**, so nothing on screen changes except the wheel.
- Reverting phase 1 = reverting `WheelClient`. No global refactor to unpick.

Rolling candy out to the other 12 clients would mean changing how each reads its colours. That is a separate decision to make **after** looking at the wheel, not a speculative refactor now.

## Non-goals

- **No change to `WheelConfig`'s numbers.** Odds, payouts, cooldown and boost values stay exactly as they are. Displayed odds are *derived from* the existing weights so display can never drift from reality.
- No change to the other panels, the cafe world art, or `UITheme.Camp`.
- Not the handoff's HUD, shop, inventory, upgrades, rebirth, gamepasses, daily or hatch panels.
- **The jackpot slot stays flat cash.** Turning it into a random top-tier brainrot pool was considered and explicitly deferred: it collides with Secret mint caps and the vault/tide schedule, and belongs in its own spec.

## Current state

| Slot | Payout | Weight |
|---|---|---|
| SMALL CASH | +$1,000 | 35 |
| BIG CASH | +$10,000 | 25 |
| LUCK BOOST | +30% for 10 min | 15 |
| POWER BOOST | +30% for 10 min | 15 |
| HUGE CASH | +$100,000 | 9 |
| JACKPOT | +$2,500,000 | 1 |

`COOLDOWN` 86400s (24h), `BOOST_MULT` 1.3, `BOOST_TIME` 600s, `TOTAL_WEIGHT` 100 — so weights are already percentages.

- `StarterPlayerScripts.WheelClient` — 557 lines, draws everything. Emoji icons (💵🍀💰🏆💪💎), flat segments, **no pointer**.
- `ServerScriptService.Modules.WheelHandler` — the free daily spin, `Init()` called from `Main`. Phase 2 extends this rather than adding a system.

---

## Phase 1 — restyle (client-only, nothing blocked)

### Tokens

From the handoff's documented set:

| Token | Value |
|---|---|
| Ink / outline | `#10131f`, 6px on every element |
| Panel shell | `#ffffff → #cfe0f5` vertical |
| Chunky shadow | solid offset, **no blur**: `0 6–16px 0 #0a0d16` |
| Corner radius | 24–32 on panels, 14–18 on chips |
| Danger / close | `#ff5c7a → #a3123a` |
| Positive green | `#a3ff4f → #3d9e18` |

The **chunky solid shadow is the load-bearing detail** — it is what makes the mockups read as toy-like and three-dimensional. Roblox has no `box-shadow`, so it is drawn as an offset dark `Frame` behind each element, not a blurred image.

⚠️ **These pixel values come from a 1920-wide web mockup and are starting points, not targets.** A 6px `UIStroke` at Roblox UI scale is heavy, and Roblox strokes render differently from CSS borders. Outline thickness, shadow offset and corner radii all get **tuned by eye against a screenshot**, exactly as the cafe restyle's numbers were. The *relationships* are what must hold: outline thick enough to read as a comic outline, shadow solid and unblurred, radius generous.

Display font: the handoff specifies Luckiest Guy, which Roblox does not have. Nearest available is `FredokaOne`; **`UITheme.Candy` carries its own font token** so the wheel does not depend on `UITheme.Font` (currently `Cartoon`, the cafe face).

### The wheel face

- Six segments in the colours already on each `WheelConfig` slot, heavy black separators, thick outer ring.
- **A pointer at the top.** Its absence is a large part of why the current wheel reads flat — nothing marks where the result lands.
- Each segment shows its **value and its odds** (35% / 25% / 15% / 15% / 9% / 1%), computed as `Weight / TOTAL_WEIGHT`.
- Each segment's emoji sits in a **gradient chip** rather than bare. Swapping to real `IconForge` renders later is a drop-in and needs no layout change.

### The spin

The current spin is the weakest part. Replace with a long **ease-out that decelerates and settles** onto the pointer, followed by a **landing pop** on the winning segment.

⚠️ **The result must stay server-authoritative.** `WheelHandler` decides the outcome; the animation only *displays* it. The client must never pick the landing segment — it must animate *to* the server's answer.

### Details panel

A panel **beside the wheel**, matching the reference's placement rather than a separate screen or a tab — so odds are readable while spinning, which is the whole point. Lists all six slots, each with its icon chip, payout and exact odds, ordered rarest-first so the jackpot reads as the headline. Justified on its own terms: the on-wheel text is small and rotated. Derived from `WheelConfig`, never hardcoded.

On narrow viewports it must not overlap the wheel — the handoff's own responsive rule applies: use `min(px, vw%)`-style sizing rather than fixed widths, and collapse the panel below the wheel rather than letting the two collide.

### Fast Spin toggle

Shortens the spin animation. **Client-local, no schema change** — it resets on rejoin. Persisting a comfort setting is not worth a server data migration.

---

## Phase 2 — buyable spins (builds fully, dormant until phase 3)

### The `ProcessReceipt` hazard — the reason this is designed now

**Roblox permits exactly one `MarketplaceService.ProcessReceipt` callback per game.** Assigning it twice silently breaks the first, and with it every purchase.

A grep confirms **the game currently has none**, so this work would be first and would effectively own it. It is therefore built as a **registry that dispatches by product id**, not as a wheel-specific handler:

- one module owns the single `ProcessReceipt` assignment;
- systems register a handler per product id;
- unknown ids return `NotProcessedYet` so a receipt is never silently eaten.

The catch-reveal skip upgrade is already planned, so this shape pays for itself immediately. (That upgrade is a **gamepass**, which uses `UserOwnsGamePassAsync` and does *not* go through `ProcessReceipt` — but anything consumable after it will.)

### Data

`WheelSpins` added to `PlayerDataManager` defaults with a `Load` migration — the same pattern `DailyStreak`, `Quests`, `QuestDay` and `Rebirths` already use in that file. `PlayerDataManager` is shared with the collaborator, so the change is additive and minimal.

### Rules

- **The server grants spins; the client never asserts one.** A client that can say "give me a spin" can say it repeatedly. Same rule that kept auto-sell server-side in the catch-reveal work.
- Spending a spin and rolling the result both stay inside `WheelHandler`.
- The free daily spin is unchanged and independent of the purchased balance.

### UI

Buy 1 / Buy 3 buttons built and visible, wired to a **placeholder product id**, inert until a real one exists. A clearly-marked constant, following the `SEASONS[1].Starts` dormancy precedent already in this codebase.

---

## Phase 3 — go live

The user creates the developer product on the Creator Dashboard and supplies the id. One constant changes. Nothing else.

## Failure modes

| Failure | Handling |
|---|---|
| Server result arrives late or not at all | The wheel does not begin its final deceleration until the server answers; on timeout it stops neutrally and shows an error rather than landing on a lie. |
| A second `ProcessReceipt` is added later by anyone | The registry owns the only assignment; adding a product means registering, not assigning. Documented at the assignment site. |
| Purchase granted twice (duplicate receipt) | Receipts are keyed and recorded before granting, per Roblox's own guidance. |
| Player leaves mid-spin | Client-side animation only; the grant already happened server-side. |
| Displayed odds drift from real odds | Impossible by construction — both read `WheelConfig.SLOTS[i].Weight`. |
| Candy tokens leak into cafe panels | `Candy` is a separate table; no existing caller reads it. |

## Verification

**Phase 1 is judged by eye, not by assertions** — the same rule the catch-reveal work established after two bugs whose numbers were all correct while the screen was wrong. Screenshots required of: the wheel idle, mid-spin, on a result, the details panel, and Fast Spin on vs off.

Plus:
1. Landed segment matches the server's result across several spins — the animation must never disagree with the grant.
2. Odds shown equal `Weight / TOTAL_WEIGHT` for all six slots.
3. Cooldown display correct when a spin is unavailable.
4. Zero console errors.
5. Phase 2 verified by granting spins server-side directly, since a real purchase cannot be tested without the product.

# Forest Egg Shop + Darrels + Pet System — Design

Date: 2026-07-28 · Approved by: user (chat) · Status: spec for review

## Summary

Wire the dormant EggStall into a real feature: **5 tiered gacha eggs** bought with a new
premium currency (**darrels** 💎), hatching **10 forest-exclusive brainrots** designed by the
user. Ship the full **pet system** (hatch/equip/follow/boost) disabled behind a flag, with
content arriving later. Everything is **world-keyed** — Forest is World 1 of a planned series.

User's stated economy goal: *"harder to progress but still keep players engaged."*

## Decisions made with the user (2026-07-28)

| Question | Decision |
|---|---|
| What hatches | Egg-exclusive brainrots + boost pets (hybrid) |
| Pet slots | 3 equipped free, **6 with a gamepass** (id TBD by user) |
| Content source | User-supplied designs (chart + OBJ); pets designed later by user |
| Brainrot egg currency | Darrels: quests, daily quests, Robux dev products |
| Pet egg currency | Regular cash |
| Egg mechanics | **5 tiered gacha eggs**, published odds, no pity |
| Event window | Forest = World 1 of future multiple worlds; config-keyed, no hard end date |
| Economy scaling | **Rescale chart incomes into existing tier bands** (top-of-band anchors) |
| Architecture | **Approach B** — self-contained subsystem, narrow seams |

## Source art (vendored at `docs/design-handoff/forest-eggs/`)

- `forest-brainrot-chart.html` — user's Claude-designed chart: 10 creatures, names/tiers/prices.
- `forest-brainrots-sprite.png` — extracted 5×2 render sheet (voxel style), build reference.
- `eggs_forest_set.obj` — 10 egg meshes (~5k faces each). **Eggs #6–10 are the forest eggs**
  (Shard / Drip / Horned / Rune / Crown, by decoration groups); #1–5 reserved (likely pet eggs).
- `eggs_forest_set.mtl` — found in Downloads root 2026-07-28, vendored beside the OBJ.
  All 31 referenced materials defined with authored colors. (User also has candy / elemental /
  goof / machine / vault egg sets staged for future worlds — not vendored, not in scope.)

## 1 · Player experience

- EggStall's existing `PromptPart.EggPrompt` ("Open Eggs") opens the **Egg Shop** panel
  (UITheme cafe/candy style). 5 eggs displayed with price and **full odds table always visible**
  (Roblox policy requires published odds for paid random items — mandatory, not optional).
- Darrel balance shown in-panel; a "How do I get darrels?" row points at quests/daily/Robux.
- Hatch: egg model shakes → shard groups separate → creature pops out spinning with the
  RarityFX ladder treatment. Compact (< 4 s), skippable by click.
- Hatched creatures are normal brainrots: pads, income, sell, trade, backpack, Index — with a
  **FOREST EGG** source badge in the Index instead of throw availability.

## 2 · Economy

### Creatures (chart ladder, re-anchored to top-of-band)

|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Cervolino Antlerino | Epic | 800 | Shard |
| 2 | Fanghetto Palunko | Epic | 870 | Shard, Drip |
| 3 | Strigolino Hootini | Epic | 950 | Shard, Drip |

|---|---|---|

| Drip | 85💎 | Fanghetto 34 / Strigolino 36 / Rospino 30 |

### Darrel faucet (harder-but-engaged target: ~10–14💎/day active)

- **3 rotating daily egg-quests** (new, DarrelService-owned; e.g. "skip 25 rocks",
  "catch an Epic+", "collect $50k campfire cash") → 8–12💎/day total.
- **Login-streak milestones** (existing DailyRewardHandler): +5💎 at day 3, +15💎 at day 7.
- **One-time goals** (existing QuestHandler): 20–40💎 on selected milestones.
- **Robux packs** (dev products, ids TBD by user): 80💎 / 180💎 / 400💎 / 1000💎.

## 3 · Architecture (Approach B)

New files, single-purpose, narrow seams:

| Module | Location | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `EggConfig` | ReplicatedStorage.Modules | World registry: `WORLDS.Forest = { Active, Eggs, Creatures }`. Pure data. |
| `EggHandler` | SSS.Modules | Buy → validate → deduct → roll → grant. No yields inside the commit. |
| `DarrelService` | SSS.Modules | Balance/earn/spend, daily egg-quests, streak/goal hooks. |
| `ProductRegistry` | SSS.Modules | **The game's single `ProcessReceipt`**, table-driven; darrel packs first, extensible (wheel spins later). Idempotent via PurchaseId dedupe. |
| `PetConfig` | ReplicatedStorage.Modules | Pet defs + `ENABLED = false` flag. Placeholder until user's pet chart. |
| `PetHandler` | SSS.Modules | Hatch/equip/unequip, follow rigs, boost math. |
| `EggShopClient` | StarterPlayerScripts | Shop panel, odds table, hatch reveal, darrel HUD chip. |

Remotes (new, under `ReplicatedStorage.Remotes`): `EggShopState`, `EggBuy`, `EggResult`,
`PetEquip`, `DarrelUpdate`.

### Integration seams (everything else untouched)

- **BrainrotConfig**: +10 entries with **`Weight = 0`** (the documented load-bearing pattern used
  by Chim/Pete/Maxwell) + `Source = "ForestEgg"`. Throws can never roll them; pads/income/
  sell/trade/index work with zero new code.
- **Grants** go through `BrainrotMover.Give` — inherits the 2026-07-28 trade hardening
  (serials, unique-cap netting, mutation safety). Never through ThrowHandler; discovery and
  mint stats are not inflated (honors ThrowHandler's standing comment).
- **PetHandler.LuckMult(player)** → one multiplier read in ThrowHandler's rollDistance
  (same pattern as RebirthConfig.LuckMult / WeatherLuck). **PetHandler.IncomeMult(player)** →
  one multiplier read in IncomeLoop. These are the only two touches on shared gameplay files.
- **PlayerDataManager schema** (+defaults +nil-migration): `Darrels = 0`, `Pets = {}`,
  `PetSlots = {}`, `EggsOpened = {}`, `DarrelDaily = {}` (quest state), `ReceiptLog = {}`
  (recent PurchaseIds).
- **Main.Init**: register DarrelService, EggHandler, PetHandler, ProductRegistry.

### Pets v1 (shipped disabled)

- Save-side: pet entries `{ Uid, Id, Boost = { Type = "Luck"|"Income", Amount } }`.
- Slots: `SLOTS_FREE = 3`, `SLOTS_PREMIUM = 6` gated on `PET_SLOTS_GAMEPASS_ID` (placeholder 0 ⇒
  premium path inert until the user creates the gamepass).
- Boost stacking: additive within type — `mult = 1 + Σ Amount`.
- Follow rig: ≤10 Massless CanCollide-false parts per pet, AlignPosition hover-follow in
  offset slots behind the character. Perf budget: 6 pets × 6 players ≤ 360 parts worst case.
- `PetConfig.ENABLED = false` hides all pet UI and pet-egg purchases until content lands.
  Pet eggs will use OBJ eggs #1–5 and cost cash (prices TBD with the pet chart).

## 4 · Content build

- **10 creatures**: rebuilt as anchored voxel part-models from the sprite renders (front-3/4
  reference, symmetric completion), ~30–80 parts each, SmoothPlastic, cafe-saturated palette.
  Stored in `ReplicatedStorage.BrainrotModels` (1:1 with config, keeping the invariant).
  Name-collision check against RENAMES keys and live config names at build time (10 new names
  verified unique before insertion).
- **5 egg meshes**: user performs **File → Import 3D** on `eggs_forest_set.obj` once (their
  account, ~30 s). Builder then splits/parents eggs #6–10 into `ReplicatedStorage.EggModels.Forest`
  with shard groups preserved for the hatch animation. If the MTL stays missing, colors are
  authored from material names + the chart's palette.
- Shop display: the 5 eggs replace/augment the 15 static `EggGood` cubes on the stall shelves
  (EggGood cubes stay as ambient decor; real egg models go on the counter).

## 5 · Safety and edge cases

- Rolls are server-side (`Random.new()` per server, never client-influenced).
- Purchase commit is atomic: validate darrels → deduct → roll → Give, **no yields between**;
  Save called after, return-checked with the audit-log pattern from the trade hardening.
- `data.__noSave` sessions cannot buy eggs or receive darrel purchases (item-destruction guard,
  same as trades); Robux receipts for such sessions return `NotProcessedYet` so Roblox retries
  when the profile is healthy.
- `ProcessReceipt` is idempotent: PurchaseId checked against `ReceiptLog` before granting;
  log capped (ring buffer 50).
- If `BrainrotMover.Give` refuses (unique cap): darrels are refunded in the same commit and a
  toast explains why. No partial states.
- Odds shown in UI are generated from `EggConfig` (single source of truth) — display can never
  drift from server behavior.
- Egg quests award via one `DarrelService.Award(player, n, reason)` chokepoint (auditable).

## Out of scope (v1)

- Pet content (user's chart pending), pet-egg pricing, gamepass creation (user, on roblox.com),
  dev-product creation (user), World 2+, pity system (explicitly declined), trading darrels
  (never — currency stays untradeable), CatchReveal integration (egg reveal is its own compact
  animation).

## Open items

1. Gamepass id (+3 pet slots) and 4 dev-product ids (darrel packs) — user creates when ready;
   placeholders keep both paths inert.
2. Pet chart — user supplies later; `PetConfig.ENABLED` stays false until then.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Buying each of the 5 eggs with sufficient darrels hatches a creature from its published
   table; 10k-roll simulation per egg matches odds within ±1.5 pp.
2. Insufficient darrels → refusal toast, no deduction, no grant.
3. Hatched creature places on a pad, earns its exact $/s, sells, trades, and appears in the
   Index with the FOREST EGG badge; throws can never produce it (Weight = 0 verified).
4. Odds table in the shop matches `EggConfig` exactly.
5. Daily egg-quests award darrels once per UTC day; streak/goal hooks award once.
6. `ProcessReceipt` grants exactly once per PurchaseId (double-delivery test passes) and
   returns `NotProcessedYet` for `__noSave` sessions.
7. Pet system: with `ENABLED = false` nothing is visible; flipping it in Studio shows the
   equip UI and a placeholder pet follows with its boost measurably applied (test-only).
8. Zero console errors through a full buy→hatch→place→sell cycle in Play mode.

# Chunky-Cartoon UI Overhaul — Integration Spec (Phase 1)

Date: 2026-07-30 · Status: for user review · Visual authority: `docs/design-handoff/ui-kit/design_handoff_game_ui/` (README.md + tokens.lua + ui_builders.lua + data_schema.lua + states.md + interactive reference). The kit's numbers are FINAL; this spec adds only the game-side integration the kit cannot know.

## User decisions (2026-07-30)

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Currency pills while panel open | HIDE (kit behavior) |
| Scope | Kit's 6 panels + HUD shell only; other surfaces unchanged until Phase 2 |
| Goals mapping | CONSOLIDATE all three quest systems into the one Goals panel |
| Settings "Reset Data" | EXCLUDED — rebirth is the only reset mechanic |
| PNG visual targets | Requested from the design tool; build proceeds from README numbers + interactive reference meanwhile |

Pipeline: browser-rasterize → PNG → CreateAssetAsync upload PILOT (real account assets — natively persistent, unlike EditableMesh place content); fallback = user bulk-import. Rail + currency use real icons Phase 1. Backpack tab icons (pet/charm/egg) + brainrot icon requested from the design tool |

## What ships (Phase 1)

New ScreenGui `GameHUD` (kit's 1350×775 UIScale canvas) containing: currency cluster (top-left: coin pill = Cash, gem pill = Darrels), right-side nav rail (Bag · Pass · Daily · Goals · Index · Settings), and the six kit panels rebuilt to spec.

## Replacement map

| Kit surface | Replaces | Data source (existing, unchanged) |

# game-src — mirrors of Studio scripts (visual system, shipped 2026-07-25)

## Brainrot Forge (2026-09-17) -- how NEW brainrots are made now
- Standard: `docs/brainrot-build-standard.md`. Pipeline spec + plan: `docs/superpowers/{specs,plans}/2026-09-17-brainrot-forge-pilot*.md`.
- `tools/brainrot_forge/` (Python): design scripts -> per-colour baked meshes -> `out/<batch>/<batch>_batch.glb` + `manifest.json` + previews. The user imports the glb via File > Import (Ctrl+M); Roblox's importer turns glTF 180 degrees about Y, so exports are pre-turned (`robloxForward`).
- `BrainrotForge.lua` -> `ServerStorage.BrainrotForge` (build-time assembler), `BrainrotBudget.lua` -> `ServerStorage.BrainrotBudget` (build-time gate). Neither is required by game code. The MCP exec sandbox cannot `require` any module here -- load them with `loadstring(module.Source)()` in Edit mode.
- **Phase 2 (2026-09-17):** the 65 Part-built voxel originals were converted to forge meshes (`python -m brainrot_forge convert`: Studio part dumps -> lossless box bake -> 4 import batches with before/after sheets) and the 43 plot-LOD copies retired; originals and LODs sit in `ServerStorage.AuditBackups.*_PreForge_2026-09-17`. Plan + execution log: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-17-brainrot-forge-conversion.md`.
- WARNING: `BrainrotLooks.lua` / `BrainrotBodyBuilder.lua` / `BrainrotModelFactory.lua` below are DEAD CODE since 2026-07-25 (the roster was replaced the same day; verified 2026-08-28) -- kept as history only.

The live source of truth is Roblox Studio. These are commit-time mirrors:
- BrainrotLooks.lua -> ReplicatedStorage.Modules.BrainrotLooks (213 recipes)
- BrainrotBodyBuilder.lua -> ReplicatedStorage.Modules.BrainrotBodyBuilder

## Sell-list thumbnails + close-button X fix (2026-07-27, design doc: docs/specs/2026-07-27-sell-list-and-close-button-design.md)
Two independent client-UI bug fixes, zero server/remote/economy change.

- UITheme.lua updated: `M.styleClose` no longer sets `btn.Text` (was `"\u{2715}"`, U+2715, which does not render in this Roblox build -- every close button drew as a bare red circle, confirmed by a live 5-candidate proof board). The X is now drawn as two rotated `Frame`s ("CloseXBar"), sized relative to the button (UDim2 Scale, not Offset, so the same code is correct at UITheme's 30px and UIStyle's 34px), white-on-red, idempotent (any previous call's bars are destroyed before redraw). ZIndex is NOT set once at draw time and left alone -- it tracks the button's own ZIndex live via `GetPropertyChangedSignal("ZIndex")`, because MainUI's Global ZIndexBehavior compares ZIndex across the whole tree rather than cascading a parent's Z to its children; `IndexClient` deliberately sets `closeBtn.ZIndex = 18` AFTER calling `styleClose` (which forces ZIndex 6), and a bar frozen at the old Z would end up UNDER the button's own now-higher-Z opaque fill, reproducing the same invisible-X bug in a new form. Verified live: bars tracked 6->7 and 18->19 correctly across that exact sequence. 7 call sites / 9 panels inherit the fix automatically (no per-panel edits): RebirthClient, QuestClient (Goals), DailyRewardClient, FusionClient, IndexClient, MerchantClient, and ClientMain's shared loop (Shop + Sell).
- UIStyle.lua -> ReplicatedStorage.Modules.UIStyle (NEW mirror, first time this file is tracked in game-src/): `UIStyle.styleClose` had its own identical `"\u{2715}"` bug (used only by SeasonClient). Given its own independent copy of the same bar-drawing fix rather than a `require(UITheme)` -- UIStyle is a collaborator's module (see its own header comment), and making it depend on UITheme is an architectural call for them to make, not something a bug fix should decide. User explicitly approved fixing this module too.
- IndexClient: one stale comment corrected (`IndexPatch.txt` ADDENDUM section) -- `-- keep GothamBold from styleClose: FredokaOne has no U+2715 glyph` blamed the font and claimed pinning GothamBold fixed the missing glyph. It never did: the proof board rendered in GothamBold and was still blank, because U+2715 is simply absent from the build, not font-specific. No behavior change, comment only.
- ClientMainSellThumbPatch.txt -> applied to ClientMain (not mirrored as a full file; collaborator-live-edited, same caveat as `ClientMainCatchPatch.txt`): `buildSellList`'s icon tile swaps its flat 34px rarity-coloured circle for a real 3D model via `BrainrotThumb.add(icon, name, opts)` (the same shared module the backpack grid and catch reveal use), sunburst backdrop kept. The tier colour that circle used to carry moves to the icon tile's own border stroke (`UITheme.stroke` in place of the old hardcoded-black `UITheme.ink`), matching how the backpack grid carries rarity on its tile border. Falls back to the old flat circle when `BrainrotThumb.master(name)` returns nil -- `Maxwell` is the only such case of 151 at patch time; verified live that its row shows the coloured circle (with a matching border) rather than an empty tile.
- Verified live in Play mode: all 9 panels' close buttons showed a visible X and still closed on click (Index, Sell, Rebirth, Goals, Daily, Merchant confirmed via real open + real click-to-close; Shop and Fusion confirmed via a briefly forced `Visible = true` since their normal open paths need an owned plot/campfire or are superseded by MerchantClient in current gameplay -- disclosed, then reverted). Sell panel verified with a real mixed 66-name inventory (walked to the stall, pressed E, went through Marco the Buyer's dialogue) showing real spinning-free 3D thumbnails with tier-coloured borders, plus the Maxwell no-model fallback. Console stayed clean throughout. Collaborator `yeep1234` joined the live session partway through verification; only the files listed above were touched.

## Close-button X fix, WheelClient gap (2026-07-27)
The close-button pass above fixed `styleClose` but missed `WheelClient` (the Daily Spin wheel): it builds its close button entirely by hand and never called `styleClose`, so it kept setting `Text = "\u{2715}"` directly. Confirmed live as the ONLY remaining TextButton anywhere in PlayerGui still carrying that literal, rendering at `TextSize = 8` on a 56px button -- the Daily Spin panel is large and front-and-centre, so this was very likely the exact button originally reported broken.

- UITheme.lua updated: the bar-drawing that lived inside `styleClose` as a local `drawCloseX` is now a public `M.closeGlyph(btn)`, and `styleClose` just calls it. Pure extraction -- same body, same behaviour, now reachable by callers that build a close button by hand and can't go through `styleClose` (which would reset size/position/color to the 30px red standard).
- WheelClient.lua -> StarterPlayer.StarterPlayerScripts.WheelClient (first mirror): now requires UITheme and calls `UITheme.closeGlyph(closeBtn)` on its own close button instead of setting `Text`. Deliberately NOT `UITheme.styleClose` -- the button's 56px size, top-right position and red fill are the wheel's own and must not be reset to the 30px standard; the bars size themselves relative to whatever button they're given, so the wheel keeps its own dimensions for free.
- DailyRewardClient.lua -> StarterPlayer.StarterPlayerScripts.DailyRewardClient (first mirror): tidy-up only. Its constructor still passed `Text = "\u{2715}"` before calling `styleClose` -- harmless (styleClose clears `Text` immediately) but a vestigial literal now that the fix is bars-based, removed.
- UIStyle.styleClose untouched, per the existing architecture note above -- it keeps its own independent copy of the bar-drawing rather than depending on UITheme.
- Verified live: walked into the wheel's proximity ring (real auto-open, not a forced `Visible = true`) -- screenshot showed a clean white X on the 56px red button; a real click on the button closed the panel (bars did not steal the click). Full sweep of every ScreenGui in PlayerGui: 98 TextButtons, 0 with `Text == "\u{2715}"`, 10 carrying the bar X (the previous 9 plus WheelUI's, confirmed at its own 56px size rather than the 30px standard -- proof `styleClose` was never called on it). Regression-checked two of the previous 9 post-extraction (DailyUI via its side-rail tile, MainUI.IndexFrame including its ZIndex-set-after-styleClose pattern) -- both still open and close correctly. Console clean throughout.

## Notes / concerns for later tasks

- These are hand-built voxel Part models, deliberately simpler than the ~150 pre-existing
  mesh-imported roster (which use an invisible `RootPart` + imported `Cube`/`Sphere` MeshParts).
  The brief specified this Part-based style explicitly; `BrainrotSpawner` and `BrainrotThumb`
  handle both styles identically (they only care about `PrimaryPart` + bounding box), so no
  compatibility issue.
- Firefly (#8) has a small cosmetic leg-segment seam visible on close zoom; not re-touched further
  given the 2–3 iteration budget and that it doesn't affect silhouette/palette recognition at
  normal camera distance.
- Left-right mirroring of asymmetric features (e.g. the blob's offset eye) was not strictly
  matched against the sprite's exact side — build-time camera angles sometimes made the mirror
  image easier to verify. This has no gameplay or recognizability impact.

## Fix 1 — Horned Egg spikes/horns brightened (post-review)
Review flagged `ForestEgg3`'s 9 `spike_*`/`horn_*` parts as `V≈0.027` — darker than its
own shell (`V≈0.07`), making the egg's signature feature invisible. Fixed on both the
canonical model and its stall clone ("Horned Egg"): original color snapshotted to a
`_EGG_Col` attribute, then `Color = Color3.fromHSV(h, s, 0.30)` applied (same hue/sat,
`V` raised 0.027 → 0.298). 18 parts changed total (9 canonical + 9 clone); no other egg
or the Horned shell touched. Screenshots confirm the horns/spikes now read as a legible
lighter dark-bark tone against the black shell.

## EditableMesh save failure — full native-primitive rebuild (this task)

**Root cause found:** the Task 6 `MeshPart`s (built via `AssetService:CreateEditableMesh()`
+ `CreateMeshPartAsync`, see above) did **not** survive a real cloud save/Studio-restart
cycle. After reopening, all 190 `MeshPart`s across the 5 canonical models and their 5 stall
clones still existed with correct names/positions/`PrimaryPart`/parenting, but every one
rendered as a checkerboard error texture — the editable-mesh geometry itself was gone,
only the container `MeshPart` + transform survived. This confirms the open risk flagged
at the end of Task 6/7 ("EditableMesh persistence across a real place save has not been
verified") landed: **`CreateEditableMesh`/`CreateMeshPartAsync` output is not safe for
anything that needs to survive a save.**

**Fix:** rebuilt all 5 models from scratch as plain native `Part`s — no `EditableMesh`,
no `MeshPart`, no asset upload at all. Each decorative group is now a `Part` with, at
most, a `SpecialMesh` (`MeshType.Sphere`, for "egg"/"ball" groups) or a `CylinderMesh`
(for "rod"/"disc" groups, oriented via `CFrame.Angles` so the mesh's Y-axis follows the
group's longest extent for rods / shortest extent for discs); "block" groups are left as
plain unmeshed `Part`s. `SpecialMesh`/`CylinderMesh` are core built-in Roblox geometry
(not asset-uploaded, not editable-mesh-derived) and do not carry the same save-loss risk.

Built from `docs/design-handoff/forest-eggs/luau_chunks_prim/egg{6..10}_prim1.lua` (one
`execute_luau` call per file, verbatim), staged on `ServerStorage.EggPrimStaging`
(deleted at end of task), normalized (`PrimaryPart` = `shell_body_1`, `ScaleTo`'d to an
absolute bbox height of 2.4 studs, `PivotTo`'d to local origin), then swapped into
`ReplicatedStorage.EggModels.Forest` in place of the broken `MeshPart` models (same
`ForestEgg1..5` names, so `EggShopClient`'s `EggModels.Forest[egg.Model]` lookup and
`EggConfig`'s `Model` fields needed no changes). The 5 broken stall clones on
`Workspace.GameWorld.EggStall.CounterTop` ("Shard Egg" / "Drip Egg" / "Horned Egg" /
"Rune Egg" / "Crown Egg") were destroyed and rebuilt as fresh clones of the new
canonical models at the exact pivots read off the old clones before destroying them;
each got a freshly-built `BillboardGui` price tag matching the original spec exactly
(cream `rgb(247,235,216)` text, ink `rgb(62,34,19)` stroke, `Enum.Font.Cartoon`,
`"<Name>"` / `"<price>💎"`, same `Size`/`StudsOffset`/`AlwaysOnTop` as the originals).

| # | Name | Model | Parts | Height | Price |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Shard Egg | ForestEgg1 | 26 | 2.40 | 60 |
| 2 | Drip Egg | ForestEgg2 | 18 | 2.40 | 85 |

### Fix 2 — Horned Egg spike/horn brightening baked into source (rebuild-proof)

chunk file `luau_chunks_prim/egg8_prim1.lua` directly: all 9 spike_* and horn_* `prim(...)` calls
now pass RGB `(0.208, 0.169, 0.128)` (V≈0.208, same hue/sat as original V≈0.027 dark green) instead

stall "Horned Egg" clone (9 parts) both brightened via `Color3.fromHSV(h, s, 0.30)` and snapshots

## Rerun — band/ring shape fixes (this task)

Re-ran the primitive rebuild from a REGENERATED set of chunk files (same directory,
`luau_chunks_prim/egg{6..10}_prim1.lua`) that changed the mid-shell "stripe" decoration
geometry and added a `ringseg` shape (10-segment ring approximation) plus a `band` shape
(shell-hugging ellipsoid), intended to fix a prior visual bug where wrap decorations
rendered as egg-sized solid slabs and rings rendered as fat discs swallowing the egg.

Destroyed and rebuilt from scratch: canonical `ReplicatedStorage.EggModels.Forest.ForestEgg1..5`
and the 5 `Workspace.GameWorld.EggStall` display clones (pivots read off the old clones before
destroying, preserved exactly: `(-51.925, 9.78/9.6759/9.4988, {-268,-264,-260,-256,-252})`).
The 15 `EggGood` shelf cubes untouched. Ran all 5 regenerated chunk files verbatim via
`execute_luau` — group counts matched the files' own expected totals exactly
(26/18/20/29/97 = 190 total), expanding to 26/18/20/101/205 = 370 actual `Part`s once
`ringseg` groups (8 in Rune, 12 in Crown) each fanned out into 10 sub-parts.

**Visual loop finding: the regenerated chunks did NOT fully fix the bug as shipped.**
First screenshot pass showed the "stripe" groups were still near-full-shell-height blocks
(e.g. Shard's `stripe_2_3` was 0.74×2.37×0.63 against a 1.88×2.40×1.88 shell — 99% of the
shell's own height) that tiled almost the entire circumference, visually reconstituting the
"solid slab" bug. Separately, several `ringseg` groups had tube thickness nearly equal to
their own ring radius (Rune's `ring_1_23`: radius 1.37, tube 1.32; Crown's `ring_1_55`:
radius 0.97, tube 1.02) — i.e. still solid discs, not rings; even the small decorative
`rune_ring_*` symbol loops had tube ≈ radius (near-solid dots instead of visible loops).

**Fix applied directly to both the canonical models and stall clones** (28 `stripe_*` parts,
200 ring-segment parts across all `*ring_*`-named groups): stripe `Size` scaled to
(×0.65 X/Z, ×0.35 Y) around each part's existing center — turns full-height wrap panels into
contained equatorial color patches; every ring segment's tube (`Size.Y`/`Size.Z`, always equal
by construction) reduced to `clamp(tube * 0.3, 0.05, 0.35)`, leaving segment arc-length
(`Size.X`) untouched — turns fat discs into thin bands/loops. `crown_ring_40` (already thin,
tube 0.071) fell under the 0.05 floor and was left essentially unchanged, as intended.

Fix applied to the canonical `ReplicatedStorage` models first, then the 5 stall clones were
destroyed and re-cloned fresh from the fixed canonical models (rather than patching the
first-pass clones separately) so the two stay byte-for-byte identical — avoids the kind of
canonical/clone drift the source chunk files already carry for the Horned Egg brightening fix
(see Concerns below). Re-screenshotted after the fix: wide stall shot plus individual
close-ups on Rune and Crown per the pass bar.

### Per-egg verdicts (screenshot review, 1 fix iteration)
- **Shard Egg (60)** — PASS. Round/egg silhouette, small shard + stud decorations visible on
  the surface, no slabs, tag legible.
- **Drip Egg (85)** — PASS, cleanest of the five. Bright orange egg with visible drip-blob
  decorations and the neck "tape" band; needed no fix (its only large-ish part, `tape_14`, was
  already a properly proportioned thin band).
- **Horned Egg (115)** — PASS. Clean tapered egg silhouette with the two horn nubs and 7 spike
  nubs visible as small protrusions; stripes now blend into the (very dark) shell color rather
  than reading as slabs.
- **Rune Egg (160)** — PASS. Round egg silhouette; close-up confirms the small `rune_ring_*`
  symbol reads clearly as a dashed ring/circle (not a solid dot) after the tube fix; the
  equatorial stripe patches sit on the shell as blocky but contained accents.
- **Crown Egg (220)** — PASS. Dome cap + 7 tan crown points + tan tip nubs read clearly;
  close-up confirms the base collar ring (ex-`ring_1_55`/`ring_2_56`) now reads as a thin green
  band/collar instead of a swallowing blob; hanging chain `link_*` segments visible as dark
  vertical segmented rods near the crown top. The `halo_ring_65` band is present in the
  geometry (tube shrunk 0.356→0.107, same tan hue as the crown points) but is hard to visually

Camera reset to `Enum.CameraType.Fixed` at end of task. Not saved/published, per task
instructions.

### Compat checks
- All 5 canonical models: `PrimaryPart` = a child literally named `shell_body_1`, bbox height

### Concerns
- **The fix was applied to live instances only, not written back into the source chunk files**
  (`luau_chunks_prim/egg{6,8,9,10}_prim1.lua` — egg7/Drip needed no fix). Per the pattern already
  seen in this log (Fix 2, line 193), any future rebuild that re-runs these chunk files verbatim
  will reintroduce the full-height stripe slabs and fat-disc rings. Whoever owns the next
  rebuild should either bake the same `×0.65/×0.35` stripe scale and
  `clamp(tube*0.3, 0.05, 0.35)` ring-tube formula into the generator/chunk files, or re-apply
  this same live-instance fix afterward.
- Several shells (Horned, Rune, Crown to a lesser extent) remain very dark by design (same
  design-verbatim tradeoff noted after Task 6 and in Fix 1/2) — unchanged by this task, still
  worth a design-intent confirmation pass.
- Crown Egg's `halo_ring_65` is geometrically present and correctly thinned but visually blends
  with the crown points' matching tan color at normal camera distance — a distinct color would
  make it read more clearly as a separate "halo" element.

## Design-match pass — video-matched palette + idle animation (this task)

Matched the 5 display models (`Workspace.GameWorld.EggStall` clones + canonical
`ReplicatedStorage.EggModels.Forest.ForestEgg1..5`) against the user's animated design
reference video (49 extracted frames, `f_001.png` front view + `f_010/011/012.png`
overhead ring-angle views). Two parts: **A)** recolor to the design's lit palette,
**B)** a new idle-animation script reproducing the video's ring precession, floating
shards, and hovering crown.

### Part A — recolor

Every changed part's pre-existing color was snapshotted to a `_EGG_Col2` attribute
before overwriting (skipped if the attribute already existed), applied identically to
both the stall clone and the canonical `ForestEgg*` model. 738 parts changed total.
