===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/BrainrotThumb.lua =====
-- BrainrotThumb: shared 3D thumbnail helper.
--
-- Renders a real brainrot model into a ViewportFrame, the way Pet Simulator
-- shows its pets. Two grids need this (the Index and the Backpack) and each was
-- about to grow its own copy of the camera maths, so it lives here once.
--
-- Masters are built ONCE per name and kept UNPARENTED; every viewport gets a
-- CLONE, because a tile dies with its rebuild and would take a shared master
-- down with it.

local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local M = {}

local modelFolder = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("BrainrotModels")
local cache = {}   -- [name] = master Model, or false for "nothing to render"

-- Viewports only draw BaseParts, but a real model also carries emitters,
-- prompts, billboards, sounds and scripts. Those render nothing and make every
-- clone heavier, so the master is stripped once and all clones inherit it.
local function strip(model)
	for _, d in ipairs(model:GetDescendants()) do
		local keep = d:IsA("BasePart") or d:IsA("Model") or d:IsA("Folder")
			or d:IsA("SpecialMesh") or d:IsA("Texture") or d:IsA("Decal")
		if not keep then d:Destroy() end
	end
	return model
end

function M.master(name)
	if cache[name] == nil then
		local real = modelFolder and modelFolder:FindFirstChild(name)
		-- false, not nil: a name with no model must not re-run the lookup on
		-- every rebuild
		cache[name] = real and strip(real:Clone()) or false
	end
	return cache[name] or nil
end

-- front-quarter, slightly above; bodies stand on Y=0 facing -Z
local DEFAULT_DIR = Vector3.new(0.9, 0.45, -1).Unit
M.DEFAULT_DIR = DEFAULT_DIR

-- Where to put a camera so a model of any size fills the frame: the point it
-- looks at, and how far back to stand. Extracted so CatchReveal can ORBIT the
-- camera using the same numbers add() uses to place it once -- two copies of
-- this calculation would drift.
function M.framing(model, fov)
	fov = fov or 30
	local cf, ext = model:GetBoundingBox()
	local dist = math.max(ext.X, ext.Y, ext.Z) / (2 * math.tan(math.rad(fov / 2))) + ext.Z * 0.5
	return cf.Position, dist
end

-- Returns the ViewportFrame, or nil when there is no model for that name, so
-- the caller can fall back to a flat swatch.
function M.add(parent, name, opts)
	local master = M.master(name)
	if not master then return nil end
	opts = opts or {}

	local vp = Instance.new("ViewportFrame")
	vp.Size = opts.size or UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	vp.Position = opts.position or UDim2.fromScale(0, 0)
	vp.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	vp.ZIndex = opts.zIndex or 1
	vp.Parent = parent

	local m = master:Clone()
	if opts.silhouette then
		for _, p in ipairs(m:GetDescendants()) do
			if p:IsA("BasePart") then p.Color = opts.silhouette end
		end
	end
	m.Parent = vp

	-- Frame from the REAL bounding box rather than a constant distance: these
	-- models range from under 5 studs to over 30, so one fixed distance would
	-- crop the big ones and shrink the small ones to a dot.
	local fov = opts.fov or 30
	local centre, dist = M.framing(m, fov)
	local cam = Instance.new("Camera")
	cam.FieldOfView = fov
	cam.CFrame = CFrame.lookAt(centre + (opts.dir or DEFAULT_DIR) * dist, centre)
	cam.Parent = vp
	vp.CurrentCamera = cam

	return vp
end

return M


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/BrainrotWaves.lua =====
-- BrainrotWaves: catchability gate. Since 2026-07-25 this is a thin adapter
-- over SupplySchedule (the Vault & Tide clock) -- kept so its two callers
-- (RarityRoll, IndexClient) never had to change imports, and so the two manual
-- override tables survive as the levers of last resort:
--   FORCE_ON[name] -- always catchable, beats the schedule (never quota-gated)
--   VAULTED[name]  -- never catchable again, beats EVERYTHING incl. FORCE_ON
-- The old quota/spread wave machinery is gone: time-based scheduling replaced
-- it (see docs/specs/2026-07-25-bounded-supply-design.md in the repo).

local SupplySchedule = require(script.Parent.SupplySchedule)
local BrainrotConfig = require(script.Parent.BrainrotConfig)

local M = {}

-- Questline-reward items (BrainrotConfig QuestOnly = true, e.g. Maxwell) are NEVER
-- catchable via a throw -- their only source is the quest grant, which inserts them
-- directly and bypasses the roll. Excluding them here drops them from the roll pool
-- entirely AND makes the Index show them as not-catchable. Static config, so it needs
-- no OverrideKey entry.
M.QUEST_ONLY = {}
for _, e in ipairs(BrainrotConfig) do
	if e.QuestOnly then M.QUEST_ONLY[e.Name] = true end
end

M.FORCE_ON = {
	["Secret Pete"] = true,   -- fixed-odds apex; his gate is LimitedStock's cap
}
M.VAULTED = {}

function M.IsObtainable(name)
	if M.QUEST_ONLY[name] then return false end   -- quest-reward-only: never catchable via throw
	if M.VAULTED[name] then return false end
	if M.FORCE_ON[name] then return true end
	return SupplySchedule.IsObtainable(name)
end

-- Deterministic fingerprint of the override tables, for RarityRoll's pool
-- cache key: an emergency VAULTED flip must invalidate pools NOW, not at the
-- next weekly flip. Sorted, so iteration order can never wobble the string.
function M.OverrideKey()
	local keys = {}
	for n in pairs(M.FORCE_ON) do keys[#keys + 1] = "+" .. n end
	for n in pairs(M.VAULTED) do keys[#keys + 1] = "-" .. n end
	table.sort(keys)
	return table.concat(keys, ";")
end

-- for the Index UI: currently catchable vs total authored
function M.Counts()
	local live = 0
	for _, e in ipairs(BrainrotConfig) do
		if M.IsObtainable(e.Name) then live += 1 end
	end
	return live, #BrainrotConfig
end

return M


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/CatchCinematic/AudioBus.lua =====
--!strict
-- CatchCinematic.AudioBus -- slot-based playback for the cinematic's OWN sounds,
-- plus duck/silence/restore of every OTHER playing Sound in the game (the
-- "ambient" set) so the 0.45s dead-air beat actually reads as dead air.
--
-- Slot resolution: cfg (Config.ASSETS) maps a slot name to either "kit:<name>"
-- (routes through SoundKit.play) or a raw "rbxassetid://..." id (routes through
-- SoundKit.playId). Volume is cfg.VOLUMES[slot] unless opts.volume overrides it.
--
-- Ambient set: every Sound instance found under SoundService or Workspace.SFX
-- (GetDescendants -- both are shallow-and-deep folders of other people's sounds)
-- that IS Playing and is NOT one of ours (identity-checked against _oursSet).
-- Snapshotted ONCE per sound (first time it's seen), original Volume remembered
-- forever until cleanup()/restoreAmbient() lets it go.
--
-- Sound.Volume is NEVER tweened -- every ramp here is a hand-lerp task.spawn
-- loop, matching PostFX's pattern: render-throttle-safe and proven correct,
-- rather than depending on TweenService progress, which read back as stalled
-- during a backgrounded/render-throttled verification session (not a
-- place-wide TweenService defect). duckAmbient/restoreAmbient share a
-- generation counter so the latest call always wins over an in-flight one.
-- silence()/unsilence() are hard,
-- instantaneous cuts (the "dead air" beat must not fade) and operate
-- independently of whatever hand-lerp is mid-flight -- silence() bumps the
-- generation counter to cancel any in-progress duck/restore first, so a lerp
-- from a moment ago can't stomp the hard-cut a frame later.

local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local SoundService = game:GetService("SoundService")
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

local SoundKit = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.SoundKit)

export type AudioBusCfg = { [string]: any }

export type PlayOpts = {
	volume: number?,
	speed: number?,
	range: number?,
	where: (Instance | Vector3)?,
}

type OursEntry = {
	sound: Sound,
	volume: number,
	preSilence: number?,
}

type SnapshotEntry = {
	original: number,
	preSilence: number?,
}

local AudioBus = {}
AudioBus.__index = AudioBus

export type Bus = typeof(setmetatable(
	{} :: {
		_cfg: AudioBusCfg,
		_ours: { OursEntry },
		_oursSet: { [Sound]: boolean },
		_snapshots: { [Sound]: SnapshotEntry },
		_silenced: boolean,
		_gen: number,
		_destroyed: boolean,
	},
	AudioBus
))

function AudioBus.new(cfg: AudioBusCfg): Bus
	local self = setmetatable({
		_cfg = cfg,
		_ours = {} :: { OursEntry },
		_oursSet = {} :: { [Sound]: boolean },
		_snapshots = {} :: { [Sound]: SnapshotEntry },
		_silenced = false,
		_gen = 0,
		_destroyed = false,
	}, AudioBus)
	return (self :: any) :: Bus
end

-- Resolves "kit:<name>" -> SoundKit.play(name, ...) or "rbxassetid://..." ->
-- SoundKit.playId(id, ...). Volume: opts.volume, else cfg.VOLUMES[slot], else
-- 0.5. Returns the Sound (nil if the slot is unknown or SoundKit declined).
function AudioBus:play(slot: string, opts: PlayOpts?): Sound?
	if self._destroyed then
		return nil
	end
	local assetRef = self._cfg[slot]
	if type(assetRef) ~= "string" then
		warn("[AudioBus] unknown slot: " .. tostring(slot))
		return nil
	end

	local volumes = self._cfg.VOLUMES
	local fallbackVol = (type(volumes) == "table" and type(volumes[slot]) == "number") and volumes[slot] or 0.5
	local o = opts or {}
	local volume = (type(o.volume) == "number") and o.volume or fallbackVol
	local playOpts = { volume = volume, speed = o.speed, range = o.range }

	local sound: Sound? = nil
	if assetRef:sub(1, 4) == "kit:" then
		local kitName = assetRef:sub(5)
		local ok, result = pcall(SoundKit.play, kitName, o.where, playOpts)
		if ok then
			sound = result
		else
			warn("[AudioBus] slot '" .. slot .. "' (kit:" .. kitName .. ") errored: " .. tostring(result))
		end
	elseif assetRef:sub(1, 13) == "rbxassetid://" then
		local ok, result = pcall(SoundKit.playId, assetRef, o.where, playOpts)
		if ok then
			sound = result
		else
			warn("[AudioBus] slot '" .. slot .. "' (" .. assetRef .. ") errored: " .. tostring(result))
		end
	else
		warn("[AudioBus] slot '" .. slot .. "' has an unrecognised asset ref: " .. assetRef)
	end

	if sound then
		local entry: OursEntry = { sound = sound, volume = volume, preSilence = nil }
		table.insert(self._ours, entry)
		self._oursSet[sound] = true
		if self._silenced then
			-- Snapshot the sound's REAL current .Volume, not the requested `volume` --
			-- SoundKit.play/playId already scale the requested volume by the player's
			-- global SFX slider (M.SfxScale()), so a player with SFX turned down would
			-- otherwise get unsilenced back to a too-loud, unscaled level.
			entry.preSilence = sound.Volume
			sound.Volume = 0
		end
	end
	return sound
end

-- Adds every currently-playing, not-ours Sound under SoundService/Workspace.SFX
-- to the snapshot set (idempotent -- a Sound already snapshotted keeps its
-- original ORIGINAL volume, never overwritten by a later call).
function AudioBus:_snapshotAmbient()
	local roots: { Instance } = { SoundService }
	local sfx = Workspace:FindFirstChild("SFX")
	if sfx then
		table.insert(roots, sfx)
	end
	for _, root in ipairs(roots) do
		for _, d in ipairs(root:GetDescendants()) do
			if d:IsA("Sound") and d.Playing and not self._oursSet[d] and not self._snapshots[d] then
				self._snapshots[d] = { original = d.Volume, preSilence = nil }
			end
		end
	end
end

-- Hand-lerp every ambient sound toward `toLevel` (a FRACTION 0..1 of that
-- sound's own original volume -- ambient sounds have wildly different authored
-- levels, so a single absolute target would blow some out and mute others) over
-- `seconds`. Supersedes any in-flight duck/restore.
function AudioBus:duckAmbient(toLevel: number, seconds: number)
	if self._destroyed then
		return
	end
	toLevel = math.clamp(toLevel, 0, 1)
	seconds = math.max(seconds, 0.02)
	self:_snapshotAmbient()

	self._gen += 1
	local myGen = self._gen
	local snapshots = self._snapshots

	task.spawn(function()
		local starts: { [Sound]: number } = {}
		for sound in pairs(snapshots) do
			starts[sound] = sound.Volume
		end
		local t0 = os.clock()
		while self._gen == myGen and not self._destroyed do
			local a = math.clamp((os.clock() - t0) / seconds, 0, 1)
			for sound, snap in pairs(snapshots) do
				if sound.Parent then
					local s = starts[sound] or snap.original
					local target = snap.original * toLevel
					sound.Volume = s + (target - s) * a
				end
			end
			if a >= 1 then
				break
			end
			task.wait()
		end
	end)
end

-- Hard-cut OURS to 0 AND the ducked ambient set to 0 -- the 0.45s dead-air beat.
-- Instantaneous, not a lerp. Cancels any in-flight duck/restore first so it
-- can't get overwritten a frame later.
function AudioBus:silence()
	if self._destroyed then
		return
	end
	self._gen += 1
	self._silenced = true
	for sound, snap in pairs(self._snapshots) do
		if sound.Parent then
			snap.preSilence = sound.Volume
			sound.Volume = 0
		end
	end
	for _, entry in ipairs(self._ours) do
		if entry.sound.Parent then
			entry.preSilence = entry.sound.Volume
			entry.sound.Volume = 0
		end
	end
end

-- Hard-cut back to whatever level everything was at the instant BEFORE
-- silence() -- undoes JUST the silence() cut, not a full restore to original
-- (that is restoreAmbient's job).
function AudioBus:unsilence()
	if self._destroyed or not self._silenced then
		return
	end
	self._silenced = false
	for sound, snap in pairs(self._snapshots) do
		if sound.Parent and snap.preSilence then
			sound.Volume = snap.preSilence
		end
		snap.preSilence = nil
	end
	for _, entry in ipairs(self._ours) do
		if entry.sound.Parent and entry.preSilence then
			entry.sound.Volume = entry.preSilence
		end
		entry.preSilence = nil
	end
end

-- Hand-lerp every ambient sound back to its ORIGINAL volume over `seconds`.
-- Supersedes any in-flight duck/restore.
function AudioBus:restoreAmbient(seconds: number)
	if self._destroyed then
		return
	end
	seconds = math.max(seconds, 0.02)
	self._gen += 1
	local myGen = self._gen
	local snapshots = self._snapshots

	task.spawn(function()
		local starts: { [Sound]: number } = {}
		for sound in pairs(snapshots) do
			starts[sound] = sound.Volume
		end
		local t0 = os.clock()
		while self._gen == myGen and not self._destroyed do
			local a = math.clamp((os.clock() - t0) / seconds, 0, 1)
			for sound, snap in pairs(snapshots) do
				if sound.Parent then
					local s = starts[sound] or snap.original
					sound.Volume = s + (snap.original - s) * a
				end
			end
			if a >= 1 then
				break
			end
			task.wait()
		end
	end)
end

-- Stops ours, restores every snapshotted volume -- exactly. Final, idempotent
-- safety net regardless of what duck/silence/restore sequence ran before it.
function AudioBus:cleanup()
	if self._destroyed then
		return
	end
	self._destroyed = true
	self._gen += 1
	for _, entry in ipairs(self._ours) do
		if entry.sound.Parent then
			pcall(function()
				entry.sound:Stop()
			end)
		end
	end
	self._ours = {}
	self._oursSet = {}
	for sound, snap in pairs(self._snapshots) do
		if sound.Parent then
			sound.Volume = snap.original
		end
	end
	self._snapshots = {}
end

return AudioBus


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/CatchCinematic/BrainrotRig.lua =====
--!strict
-- CatchCinematic.BrainrotRig -- the creature. THE MONEY SHOT.
--
-- Clone from ReplicatedStorage.BrainrotModels, neuter (PullCeremony's loop,
-- verbatim, plus Massless -- this rig's clone sits live in world space rather
-- than riding the camera like PullCeremony's does, so it must never contribute
-- mass or collide with anything), scale via MassiveEmergence's exact fit math
-- (reused verbatim, per the brief):
--   hs = clamp(template:GetAttribute("HeightScale") or 1, 0.7, 1.5)
--   fit = min((6.0*hs)/extents.Y, 9.5/max(width,0.01)) * Sizes.Scale(size)
--   model:ScaleTo(model:GetScale() * fit)      -- ScaleTo is ABSOLUTE, always factor-of-original
-- Silhouette colour is MassiveEmergence's, verbatim: Color3.fromRGB(6, 8, 12).
--
-- POSE MATH -- adapted, not copy-pasted, from MassiveEmergence's inline placeAt:
-- MassiveEmergence's placeAt(pos, yaw) is a per-frame RenderStepped closure that
-- rotates the model's CURRENT pivot by `yaw` every call, so the total rotation
-- compounds across frames (fine for a fire-and-forget cutscene, but the OPPOSITE
-- of "setRise(alpha) is a pure function of alpha" -- calling it twice with the
-- same alpha must yield the same pose). So here the pivot/bounding-box-centre
-- offset is captured ONCE at build time (_pivot0/_localOffset, at yaw=0) and
-- every pose call recomputes the model's CFrame from scratch via poseCFrame():
-- pos and yaw both go in, the exact same pivot CFrame comes out, every time.
-- The below/above targets and the quint-ease-out rise curve are MassiveEmergence's
-- own numbers, unchanged.
--
-- Model handling per the brief: all BaseParts Anchored + CanCollide/CanQuery/
-- CanTouch false + Massless; PivotTo for all movement (never welds); ScaleTo is
-- ABSOLUTE (model:GetScale() * factor, never a bare factor).
--
-- .new() calls stageBelow() once at the end of construction, so a rig is ALWAYS
-- fully staged (silhouette-black, sunk below the surface) the instant it exists
-- -- there is no frame where a freshly-cloned model could flash its real colours
-- at some arbitrary ReplicatedStorage-inherited CFrame before the Sequencer gets
-- a chance to pose it. stageBelow() itself stays idempotent/re-callable (the
-- Sequencer's documented staging beat).
--
-- COLOR/SIZE ANIMATION -- HAND-LERPED, NOT TWEENSERVICE, DESPITE THE BRIEF'S
-- "Color is sanctioned" note: TweenService progress read back as stalled during
-- this module's verification session (Studio was backgrounded behind another
-- window and render-throttled at the time -- not a place bug). revealColors()
-- and eyeTwitch() hand-lerp instead (task.spawn stepping loop + task.wait(),
-- the same render-throttle-safe pattern PostFX/AudioBus already use for their
-- own hand-lerped properties) so a reveal never silently depends on the editor
-- window being foregrounded.

local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

local Sizes = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.SizeConfig)

local SILHOUETTE_COLOR = Color3.fromRGB(6, 8, 12)
local EYE_TWITCH_SCALE = 1.15
local EYE_TWITCH_SECONDS = 0.18
local BREACH_ABOVE_FRAC = 1 / 3 -- fraction of model height poking above the surface at breachPose()
local STREAK_MIN_SCALE = 0.03 -- never literally zero -- ScaleTo(0) is undefined behaviour

local BrainrotRig = {}
BrainrotRig.__index = BrainrotRig

export type Rig = typeof(setmetatable(
	{} :: {
		_stage: Folder,
		_name: string,
		_size: string,
		_splashPos: Vector3,
		_model: Model,
		_pivot0: CFrame,
		_localOffset: Vector3,
		_finalExtents: Vector3,
		_belowPos: Vector3,
		_risePos: Vector3,
		_originalColor: { [BasePart]: Color3 },
		_colorsStored: boolean,
		_riseAlpha: number,
		_baseYaw: number,
		_angryEyes: { [BasePart]: { color: Color3, material: Enum.Material } }?,
		_colorGen: number,
		_eyeGen: number,
		_breached: boolean,
		_destroyed: boolean,
	},
	BrainrotRig
))

-- Clone + neuter + fit-scale + parent into stage. Returns nil (all four values)
-- if the model name doesn't exist in BrainrotModels -- the ONE failure path both
-- .new() and swapModel() share, so "no model" fails soft identically either way.
local function buildModel(stage: Folder, name: string, size: string): (Model?, CFrame?, Vector3?, Vector3?)
	local modelFolder = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("BrainrotModels")
	local template = modelFolder and modelFolder:FindFirstChild(name)
	if not template or not template:IsA("Model") then
		return nil, nil, nil, nil
	end

	local model = template:Clone()
	local _, extents = model:GetBoundingBox()
	local hsRaw = template:GetAttribute("HeightScale")
	local hs = math.clamp((typeof(hsRaw) == "number" and hsRaw or 1) :: number, 0.7, 1.5)
	local width = math.max(extents.X, extents.Z)
	local fit = math.min((6.0 * hs) / extents.Y, 9.5 / math.max(width, 0.01)) * Sizes.Scale(size)
	model:ScaleTo(model:GetScale() * fit)

	-- PullCeremony's neuter loop (ReplicatedStorage.Modules.PullCeremony), verbatim,
	-- plus Massless -- see module header.
	for _, d in ipairs(model:GetDescendants()) do
		if d:IsA("BasePart") then
			d.Anchored = true
			d.CanCollide = false
			d.CanQuery = false
			d.CanTouch = false
			d.Massless = true
		elseif d:IsA("Sound") then
			d.Looped = false
			d.Playing = false
		elseif d:IsA("Script") or d:IsA("LocalScript") or d:IsA("ProximityPrompt") or d:IsA("BillboardGui") then
			d:Destroy()
		end
	end

	model.Parent = stage
	local pivot0 = model:GetPivot()
	local cf, finalExtents = model:GetBoundingBox()
	local localOffset = pivot0:PointToObjectSpace(cf.Position)
	return model, pivot0, localOffset, finalExtents
end

-- Pure: same (pivot0, localOffset, pos, yaw) always yields the same CFrame. `pos`
-- is where the model's BOUNDING-BOX CENTRE should land (matches MassiveEmergence's
-- placeAt convention); `yaw` is an ABSOLUTE turn from the model's build-time
-- orientation (pivot0), not an increment on whatever the pivot currently holds.
local function poseCFrame(pivot0: CFrame, localOffset: Vector3, pos: Vector3, yaw: number): CFrame
	local rot = pivot0.Rotation * CFrame.Angles(0, yaw, 0)
	local worldOffset = rot:VectorToWorldSpace(localOffset)
	return CFrame.new(pos - worldOffset) * rot
end

function BrainrotRig.new(stage: Folder, name: string, size: string, splashPos: Vector3): Rig?
	local model, pivot0, localOffset, finalExtents = buildModel(stage, name, size)
	if not model or not pivot0 or not localOffset or not finalExtents then
		return nil
	end

	local self = setmetatable({
		_stage = stage,
		_name = name,
		_size = size,
		_splashPos = splashPos,
		_model = model,
		_pivot0 = pivot0,
		_localOffset = localOffset,
		_finalExtents = finalExtents,
		_belowPos = splashPos - Vector3.new(0, finalExtents.Y * 1.05, 0),
		_risePos = splashPos + Vector3.new(0, finalExtents.Y * 0.5 - finalExtents.Y * 0.08, 0),
		_originalColor = {} :: { [BasePart]: Color3 },
		_colorsStored = false,
		_riseAlpha = 0,
		_baseYaw = 0,
		_angryEyes = nil :: { [BasePart]: { color: Color3, material: Enum.Material } }?,
		_colorGen = 0,
		_eyeGen = 0,
		_breached = false,
		_destroyed = false,
	}, BrainrotRig)
	local rig = (self :: any) :: Rig
	rig:stageBelow()
	return rig
end

function BrainrotRig:_placeAt(pos: Vector3, yaw: number)
	if self._destroyed then
		return
	end
	self._model:PivotTo(poseCFrame(self._pivot0, self._localOffset, pos, self._baseYaw + yaw))
end

-- Silhouette (store colours -- once, idempotently -- then paint rgb(6,8,12)) and
-- pivot fully below splashPos. Safe to call more than once: subsequent calls
-- repaint from the STORED originals (never re-capture already-black colour).
function BrainrotRig:stageBelow()
	if self._destroyed then
		return
	end
	if not self._colorsStored then
		for _, d in ipairs(self._model:GetDescendants()) do
			if d:IsA("BasePart") then
				self._originalColor[d] = d.Color
			end
		end
		self._colorsStored = true
	end
	for part in pairs(self._originalColor) do
		if part.Parent then
			part.Color = SILHOUETTE_COLOR
		end
	end
	self._riseAlpha = 0
	self._breached = false -- back to the initial silhouette state -- not breached (yet)
	self:_placeAt(self._belowPos, 0)
end

-- Pure function of alpha: pivot lerp below->full-rise-height + slow yaw. RETUNED
-- 2026-08-09: MassiveEmergence's quint-ease-out curve and its pi*1.25 total turn
-- are BOTH gone -- the curve is now a sine ease-in-out (the beast crawl) and the
-- turn a 0.6*pi part-turn (the aurafarm turn). See the inline notes below for the
-- owner direction behind each. Still a from-scratch recompute rather than a
-- literal copy of MassiveEmergence's accumulating RenderStepped closure -- see the
-- module header for why.
function BrainrotRig:setRise(alpha: number)
	if self._destroyed then
		return
	end
	alpha = math.clamp(alpha, 0, 1)
	self._riseAlpha = alpha
	-- RETUNED 2026-08-09 (owner feedback: "doesn't emerge slowly like a beast"):
	-- the original quint-ease-OUT burst up fast and settled, which read as a pop.
	-- Sine ease-in-out is the beast crawl -- slow shoulder out of the water, steady
	-- climb, gentle settle. Still pure in alpha.
	local e = 0.5 - 0.5 * math.cos(math.pi * alpha)
	local pos = self._belowPos:Lerp(self._risePos, e)
	-- 0.6*pi (was 1.25*pi): the aurafarm turn -- a slow, unbothered part-turn,
	-- not a runway spin (owner direction 2026-08-09).
	local yaw = alpha * math.pi * 0.6
	self:_placeAt(pos, yaw)
end

-- The setRise alpha whose EASED height equals breachPose's fixed pose, computed
-- from this instance's own numbers so the two can never drift apart. The rise
-- beat starts from here instead of 0 -- without this the creature visibly dunks
-- back underwater after the eruption and re-emerges (the discontinuity behind
-- the owner's "doesn't emerge" note).
function BrainrotRig:breachAlpha(): number
	if self._destroyed then
		return 0
	end
	local breachY = self._splashPos.Y + self._finalExtents.Y * (BREACH_ABOVE_FRAC - 0.5)
	local span = self._risePos.Y - self._belowPos.Y
	if span <= 0 then
		return 0
	end
	local e = math.clamp((breachY - self._belowPos.Y) / span, 0, 1)
	-- invert the sine ease: e = 0.5 - 0.5*cos(pi*a)  ->  a = acos(1 - 2e)/pi
	return math.acos(math.clamp(1 - 2 * e, -1, 1)) / math.pi
end

-- The swapModel guard's WRITER since the v2 retune. The eruption beat now drives
-- the emergence through setRise (0 -> breachAlpha) and never calls breachPose, so
-- _breached had no writer left on the main path and a post-eruption swapModel
-- could have silently rebuilt the creature mid-emergence. The Sequencer marks the
-- breach explicitly here instead, at the instant the dome bursts. Idempotent.
function BrainrotRig:markBreached()
	if self._destroyed then
		return
	end
	self._breached = true
end

-- The eruption instant: head/upper-third above the surface. A fixed pose, not
-- part of the setRise(alpha) timeline (the "rise" beat that follows re-poses via
-- setRise from 0 again -- breachPose is deliberately a separate, discrete beat).
-- OFF THE MAIN PATH since the 2026-08-09 retune: nothing calls it any more (the
-- eruption drives setRise); kept because breachAlpha() is defined against its pose.
function BrainrotRig:breachPose()
	if self._destroyed then
		return
	end
	self._breached = true -- past this point, swapModel is a no-op -- see swapModel's guard
	local centerY = self._splashPos.Y + self._finalExtents.Y * (BREACH_ABOVE_FRAC - 0.5)
	local pos = Vector3.new(self._splashPos.X, centerY, self._splashPos.Z)
	self:_placeAt(pos, 0)
end

-- Hand-lerp stored colours back (see module header: render-throttle-safe,
-- doesn't depend on TweenService progressing). Generation counter so a second
-- revealColors() call cleanly supersedes an in-flight one instead of two loops
-- fighting over the same parts.
function BrainrotRig:revealColors(seconds: number)
	if self._destroyed then
		return
	end
	seconds = math.max(seconds, 0.05)
	self._colorGen += 1
	local myGen = self._colorGen
	local targets = self._originalColor
	local starts: { [BasePart]: Color3 } = {}
	for part in pairs(targets) do
		starts[part] = part.Color
	end

	task.spawn(function()
		local t0 = os.clock()
		while self._colorGen == myGen and not self._destroyed do
			local a = math.clamp((os.clock() - t0) / seconds, 0, 1)
			local e = 1 - (1 - a) ^ 3
			for part, target in pairs(targets) do
				-- angry eyes hold their red through the reveal; calmEyes restores them
				if part.Parent and not (self._angryEyes and self._angryEyes[part]) then
					local s = starts[part] or target
					part.Color = s:Lerp(target, e)
				end
			end
			if a >= 1 then
				break
			end
			task.wait()
		end
	end)
end

function BrainrotRig:_findEyePart(): BasePart?
	if self._destroyed then
		return nil
	end
	for _, d in ipairs(self._model:GetDescendants()) do
		if d:IsA("BasePart") and string.find(string.lower(d.Name), "eye") then
			return d
		end
	end
	return nil
end

-- FACING (owner 2026-08-09: "rise slowly facing the player"): a constant yaw offset
-- applied under every pose, so the rise's slow turn LANDS square on whatever the
-- Sequencer aimed at. Pure state -- the next _placeAt picks it up.
function BrainrotRig:setFacing(baseYaw: number)
	if self._destroyed then
		return
	end
	self._baseYaw = baseYaw
end

-- ANGRY EYES (same owner note): every part whose name contains "eye" goes hot
-- glowing red for the emergence; calmEyes restores the stored originals exactly.
-- Fail-soft: a model with no eye parts is a clean no-op both ways -- and RETURNS
-- FALSE, which is the whole point of the return value: 170 of the 191 models in
-- BrainrotModels have no part named "eye", so on most catches the red never showed
-- at all. The caller needs to know the angry read did not land so it can paint one
-- somewhere the model definitely has (the Sequencer reddens the aura rim instead).
-- Idempotent: a second call re-reports the first call's answer, never re-captures.
function BrainrotRig:angryEyes(): boolean
	if self._destroyed then
		return false
	end
	if self._angryEyes then
		return next(self._angryEyes) ~= nil
	end
	local store: { [BasePart]: { color: Color3, material: Enum.Material } } = {}
	for _, d in ipairs(self._model:GetDescendants()) do
		if d:IsA("BasePart") and string.find(string.lower(d.Name), "eye") then
			store[d] = { color = d.Color, material = d.Material }
			d.Color = Color3.fromRGB(255, 45, 25)
			d.Material = Enum.Material.Neon
		end
	end
	self._angryEyes = store
	return next(store) ~= nil
end

function BrainrotRig:calmEyes()
	local store = self._angryEyes
	if not store then
		return
	end
	self._angryEyes = nil
	for part, orig in pairs(store) do
		if part.Parent then
			part.Color = self._originalColor[part] or orig.color
			part.Material = orig.material
		end
	end
end

-- Briefly hand-lerp an eye part's Size 1.15x and back (see module header: no
-- TweenService in this module). No-op if the model has no part named "eye"
-- (case-insensitive substring match).
function BrainrotRig:eyeTwitch()
	if self._destroyed then
		return
	end
	local eyePart = self:_findEyePart()
	if not eyePart then
		return
	end
	self._eyeGen += 1
	local myGen = self._eyeGen
	local baseSize = eyePart.Size
	local upSize = baseSize * EYE_TWITCH_SCALE
	local half = EYE_TWITCH_SECONDS * 0.5

	task.spawn(function()
		local t0 = os.clock()
		while self._eyeGen == myGen and not self._destroyed and eyePart.Parent do
			local a = math.clamp((os.clock() - t0) / half, 0, 1)
			eyePart.Size = baseSize:Lerp(upSize, a)
			if a >= 1 then
				break
			end
			task.wait()
		end
		if self._eyeGen ~= myGen or self._destroyed or not eyePart.Parent then
			return
		end
		local t1 = os.clock()
		while self._eyeGen == myGen and not self._destroyed and eyePart.Parent do
			local a = math.clamp((os.clock() - t1) / half, 0, 1)
			eyePart.Size = upSize:Lerp(baseSize, a)
			if a >= 1 then
				break
			end
			task.wait()
		end
	end)
end

-- The fitted model's world-space extents, captured once at build time (and refreshed
-- by swapModel). Published because the Sequencer needs them for the hero framing
-- distance, the dread dome radius and WaterFX:erupt's column size -- reaching into
-- _finalExtents from outside was legal (it is in the exported Rig type) but left the
-- geometry contract undocumented.
function BrainrotRig:extents(): Vector3
	return self._finalExtents
end

-- The live clone. WaterFX:cascade needs the Model itself to hang emitters off, and
-- swapModel replaces it, so callers must re-read rather than cache across a swap.
function BrainrotRig:model(): Model
	return self._model
end

-- Current bounding-box top centre -- RockRig's second-bonk target.
function BrainrotRig:headTop(): Vector3
	if self._destroyed then
		return self._splashPos
	end
	local cf, ext = self._model:GetBoundingBox()
	return cf.Position + Vector3.new(0, ext.Y / 2, 0)
end

-- Scale the model down while lerping toward the camera-ray of target2D (a
-- viewport-fraction Vector2, 0..1 on each axis), then hide it. Self-driving
-- (task.spawn stepping loop, per the hard rule -- Model:ScaleTo/PivotTo are not
-- TweenService-able properties regardless). Ends with the model destroyed --
-- "hidden" and "stage empty of it" in one step -- and `done` fired after.
function BrainrotRig:compressAndStreak(target2D: Vector2, seconds: number, done: (() -> ())?)
	if self._destroyed then
		if done then
			task.spawn(done)
		end
		return
	end
	seconds = math.max(seconds, 0.05)
	local model = self._model
	local startPos = model:GetPivot().Position
	local startScale = model:GetScale()
	-- The model's ACTUAL current rotation, not a reconstruction from _riseAlpha:
	-- breachPose() poses at yaw=0 without touching _riseAlpha, so a stale
	-- pivot0/riseAlpha recompute would snap rotation on breach -> compress. Reading
	-- the live pivot is correct regardless of which pose call happened last.
	local lockedRotation = model:GetPivot().Rotation

	local targetPos = startPos
	local cam = Workspace.CurrentCamera
	if cam then
		local vs = cam.ViewportSize
		local sx = math.clamp(target2D.X, 0, 1) * vs.X
		local sy = math.clamp(target2D.Y, 0, 1) * vs.Y
		local ok, ray = pcall(function()
			return cam:ViewportPointToRay(sx, sy)
		end)
		if ok and ray then
			local dist = (startPos - cam.CFrame.Position).Magnitude
			targetPos = ray.Origin + ray.Direction.Unit * dist
		end
	end

	task.spawn(function()
		local t0 = os.clock()
		while not self._destroyed do
			local a = math.clamp((os.clock() - t0) / seconds, 0, 1)
			local e = a * a * a -- cubic ease-in: accelerating streak toward the camera
			local pos = startPos:Lerp(targetPos, e)
			local scaleFactor = math.max(1 - (1 - STREAK_MIN_SCALE) * e, STREAK_MIN_SCALE)
			if model.Parent then
				model:PivotTo(CFrame.new(pos) * lockedRotation)
				pcall(function()
					model:ScaleTo(startScale * scaleFactor)
				end)
			end
			if a >= 1 then
				break
			end
			task.wait()
		end
		if not self._destroyed then
			self._destroyed = true
			self._colorGen += 1
			self._eyeGen += 1
			if model.Parent then
				model:Destroy()
			end
		end
		if done then
			pcall(done)
		end
	end)
end

-- Pre-eruption only: rebuild at the SAME rise alpha (covers the reveal-time
-- fallback swap). ENFORCED, not just documented: a no-op (warn + return false)
-- once breachPose() has run (_breached), so a post-eruption swap can never
-- silently rebuild the creature mid-emergence. Builds the replacement FIRST --
-- if the new name doesn't resolve, the old model is left completely untouched
-- and this returns false. Exactly one model lives in the stage at any time
-- either way.
function BrainrotRig:swapModel(newName: string): boolean
	if self._destroyed then
		return false
	end
	if self._breached then
		warn("[BrainrotRig] swapModel('" .. newName .. "') ignored: already past breachPose()")
		return false
	end
	local newModel, pivot0, localOffset, finalExtents = buildModel(self._stage, newName, self._size)
	if not newModel or not pivot0 or not localOffset or not finalExtents then
		return false
	end

	local oldModel = self._model
	local preservedAlpha = self._riseAlpha

	self._model = newModel
	self._pivot0 = pivot0
	self._localOffset = localOffset
	self._finalExtents = finalExtents
	self._belowPos = self._splashPos - Vector3.new(0, finalExtents.Y * 1.05, 0)
	self._risePos = self._splashPos + Vector3.new(0, finalExtents.Y * 0.5 - finalExtents.Y * 0.08, 0)
	self._name = newName
	self._originalColor = {}
	self._colorsStored = false
	-- The OLD model's eye parts are about to be destroyed: keeping their keys would
	-- leave revealColors skipping dead parts and calmEyes writing to them.
	self._angryEyes = nil

	if oldModel.Parent then
		oldModel:Destroy()
	end

	self:stageBelow() -- paints black + captures colours for the NEW model
	self:setRise(preservedAlpha) -- restore rise progress on the new model
	return true
end

function BrainrotRig:cleanup()
	if self._destroyed then
		return
	end
	self._destroyed = true
	self._colorGen += 1
	self._eyeGen += 1
	if self._model and self._model.Parent then
		self._model:Destroy()
	end
end

return BrainrotRig


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/CatchCinematic/Bridge.lua =====
--!strict
-- CatchCinematic.Bridge -- the handshake between the SERVER's ThrowResult (which
-- carries the authoritative grant) and the client-side cinematic that is already
-- playing by the time it lands. Three parties, one small state machine:
--
--   CinematicClient   arm(payload, secs) -> gen   at flight start, thrower only.
--                                                 nil = refused, run no cinematic.
--                     markFailedFor(gen)          play declined/errored
--   Sequencer         markRunning(gen)            when its conductor binds
--                     result(gen)                 polled per frame for the
--                                                 authoritative name (reveal-time
--                                                 fallbacks can swap the creature)
--                     finish(gen, ok)             exactly once, at teardown
--   CatchRevealClient tryAdopt(result)            "is this catch cinematic-owned?"
--                     onDone(cb)                  "then tell me how it went"
--
-- STATE:  idle --arm--> armed --markRunning--> running --finish--> idle
--         armed/running --markFailedFor / expiry / reset / superseding arm--> idle,
--         and EVERY one of those transitions fires the pending onDone callbacks.
--
-- ============================ THE INVARIANT ============================
-- NO ThrowResult IS EVER SUPPRESSED UNLESS ITS OWN CINEMATIC RAN TO SUCCESS.
-- tryAdopt() returning true is a PROMISE that some onDone will fire; the ordinary
-- reveal is deferred on the strength of it. Three rules keep that promise, and every
-- state transition below is written to preserve them:
--
--   R1  ONE ARM, ONE ADOPTION. An arm that has already taken a result refuses every
--       later one. ThrowResult carries no throw token (it is FireClient'd to the
--       owner and nothing in it identifies the flight), so "this arm is already
--       spoken for" is the ONLY thing separating throw A's result from throw B's
--       when B lands while A's cinematic is still on screen. Without R1, B's result
--       adopts into A's arm, A's cinematic reports success, and B's catch is
--       revealed by nobody. Ordering makes R1 sufficient rather than merely helpful:
--       ThrowHandler clears its one-stone `inFlight` lock only AFTER revealCatch has
--       fired ThrowResult (ThrowHandler ~line 1116), so throw A's ThrowResult always
--       precedes throw B's MassiveCinematic broadcast.
--   R2  A LIVE RUN IS NEVER CLOBBERED. arm() REFUSES while an arm is "running":
--       the caller runs no cinematic for that throw and stages the stock landing
--       instead. Overwriting would strand the running catch's onDone; stealing the
--       slot would break R1.
--   R3  NOTHING VANISHES SILENTLY. Every exit from armed/running goes through
--       settle(), which answers every pending callback exactly once -- including the
--       arm-expiry sweep and reset(), which used to just drop them.
--
-- Generation counter: every arm has an id, and markRunning/result/finish/
-- markFailedFor all no-op unless the id matches the CURRENT arm. That is what stops
-- a stale, debounced or superseded play from tearing down a live arm belonging to a
-- different throw -- the single worst bug this module can have.
--
-- WHY A SEPARATE MODULE: CatchRevealClient must not require the Sequencer, which
-- pulls in CameraRig/WaterFX/HypeUI/... -- every ordinary catch in the game would
-- then depend on the cinematic loading cleanly. This module requires NOTHING, so
-- CatchRevealClient's fail-soft require of it is genuinely cheap. The dependency
-- arrow is one-way: Sequencer -> Bridge, never back.
--
-- ARM EXPIRY: arm() happens at flight start; play() happens TotalTime later. If the
-- scheduler between them dies, a permanently-armed Bridge would swallow the reveal of
-- every future Massive catch, so an arm carries a deadline and fails itself (R3).
-- markRunning() EXTENDS that deadline with the run's own budget, because the arm has
-- to outlive the cinematic: a 4.2s flight armed for flight+cancel+slack would
-- otherwise time out around the eruption beat of a 10.7s cutscene and hand the reveal
-- back to the ordinary path ON TOP of the cinematic still playing it.
--
-- CALLBACKS ARE task.spawn'd, ALWAYS. onDone's callback runs PullCeremony, which
-- BLOCKS for seconds; finish() is called from the Sequencer's render step, and a
-- render step that blocks for seconds freezes the game.

local Bridge = {}

type Result = { [string]: any }

local DEFAULT_ARM_SECONDS = 12

local gen: number = 0
local state: string = "idle" -- "idle" | "armed" | "running"
local armedSize: string? = nil
local armExpiresAt: number = 0
local result: Result? = nil
local doneCbs: { (boolean) -> () } = {}
local lastOk: boolean = false -- outcome of the most recently settled arm

local function clearArm()
	state = "idle"
	armedSize = nil
	armExpiresAt = 0
	result = nil
	doneCbs = {}
end

-- R3's single implementation. Every path out of armed/running calls this.
local function settle(ok: boolean)
	local cbs = doneCbs
	clearArm()
	lastOk = ok == true
	for _, cb in ipairs(cbs) do
		task.spawn(cb, lastOk)
	end
end

-- True while an arm is still live. A timed-out arm is FAILED here (not dropped),
-- so an adopted result is handed back to the ordinary reveal instead of vanishing.
local function armLive(): boolean
	if state == "idle" then
		return false
	end
	if os.clock() > armExpiresAt then
		settle(false)
		return false
	end
	return true
end

-- CinematicClient, thrower only, at flight start. Returns the arm's generation, or
-- NIL when refused (R2) -- a nil return means "run no cinematic for this throw".
function Bridge.arm(payload: { [string]: any }, seconds: number?): number?
	if armLive() then
		if state == "running" then
			return nil -- R2
		end
		settle(false) -- an armed-but-never-played arm being superseded (R3)
	end
	gen += 1
	state = "armed"
	armedSize = (type(payload) == "table" and type(payload.Size) == "string") and payload.Size or nil
	armExpiresAt = os.clock() + math.max(tonumber(seconds) or DEFAULT_ARM_SECONDS, 1)
	result = nil
	doneCbs = {}
	return gen
end

function Bridge.isCurrent(g: number?): boolean
	return type(g) == "number" and g == gen and armLive()
end

-- Sequencer, once its conductor is bound. Promotes armed -> running (so a LATER
-- throw's arm() is refused rather than clobbering it, R2) and pushes the expiry out
-- to cover the run itself -- the caller passes its own wall-clock budget, because the
-- Bridge has no business knowing how long a cut is.
function Bridge.markRunning(g: number?, seconds: number?)
	if type(g) ~= "number" or g ~= gen or state ~= "armed" then
		return
	end
	state = "running"
	local extend = tonumber(seconds)
	if extend then
		armExpiresAt = math.max(armExpiresAt, os.clock() + math.max(extend, 1))
	end
end

-- CatchRevealClient. TRUE means: this catch belongs to a cinematic, do not run the
-- ordinary chain now -- register onDone and let the cinematic decide.
function Bridge.tryAdopt(res: { [string]: any }): boolean
	if not armLive() then
		return false
	end
	if type(res) ~= "table" then
		return false
	end
	-- A size-less result is by definition an ordinary catch, and the size is the one
	-- field the cinematic keys off, so a mismatch is never adopted.
	if res.Size == nil then
		return false
	end
	if armedSize ~= nil and res.Size ~= armedSize then
		return false
	end
	if result ~= nil then
		return false -- R1: this arm is already spoken for
	end
	result = res
	return true
end

-- Sequencer, polled per frame, generation-checked so a stale run can never read a
-- newer throw's grant.
function Bridge.result(g: number?): Result?
	if type(g) == "number" and g == gen then
		return result
	end
	return nil
end

function Bridge.onDone(cb: (boolean) -> ())
	if type(cb) ~= "function" then
		return
	end
	-- Already over (a cinematic that died between tryAdopt and this call): answer
	-- immediately rather than registering a callback nothing will ever fire.
	if state == "idle" then
		task.spawn(cb, lastOk)
		return
	end
	table.insert(doneCbs, cb)
end

-- Sequencer, exactly once per run, with the generation it was handed at play time.
-- ok=false means the cinematic never delivered the reveal (error / death / cancel),
-- which is CatchRevealClient's cue to run the ordinary chain after all.
function Bridge.finish(g: number?, ok: boolean)
	if type(g) ~= "number" or g ~= gen or state == "idle" then
		return
	end
	settle(ok)
end

-- CinematicClient, when ITS OWN play declined or errored before running. Generation-
-- scoped on purpose: a debounced play must never tear down the live arm of the
-- earlier throw whose cinematic is the very thing debouncing it.
function Bridge.markFailedFor(g: number?)
	Bridge.finish(g, false)
end

-- Hard escape hatch (harness teardown, and any future place-level reset). Goes
-- through settle(), so it FAILS a live arm rather than dropping it -- R3 again.
function Bridge.reset()
	if state ~= "idle" then
		settle(false)
	end
	lastOk = false
end

-- Diagnostics only.
function Bridge.debugState(): { [string]: any }
	return {
		gen = gen,
		state = state,
		armedSize = armedSize,
		-- Recomputed WITHOUT armLive(), which settles a stale arm as a side effect --
		-- reading a diagnostic must never change the thing it reports on.
		armLive = state ~= "idle" and os.clock() <= armExpiresAt,
		hasResult = result ~= nil,
		pendingCallbacks = #doneCbs,
		lastOk = lastOk,
	}
end

return Bridge


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/CatchCinematic/CameraRig.lua =====
--!strict
-- CatchCinematic.CameraRig — hand-lerped camera takeover for the Massive catch cinematic.
-- Single per-frame camera writer: the RenderStepped-bound callback below. No TweenService
-- is used on Camera.CFrame or Camera.FieldOfView anywhere in this module — every motion
-- (flyTo/lookHover/orbit/punchFOV/shake) is sampled and applied by hand each frame.
-- ScreenShake (sibling module) owns NO camera writes; it only returns (offset, rollDeg)
-- via the fn installed through setShakeSource, applied here AFTER the base CFrame.
--
-- Wind-down contract: once returnToPlayer() begins a real blend (self._motion.kind ==
-- "returning"), this rig instance is winding down. From that point on: flyTo/lookHover/
-- orbit/punchFOV are no-ops (the wind-down is not interruptible by more motion calls);
-- a second returnToPlayer() call is itself a no-op — the FIRST call's `done` still
-- fires, exactly once, the second call's `done` is never invoked; and takeover() on
-- this same rig instance returns false for as long as it is already active (winding
-- down or not — this also closes the double-save hazard where a second takeover()
-- would overwrite the saved pre-cinematic state with mid-cinematic Scriptable values).
-- restore() is the one abort path out of a wind-down (or out of any active state): it
-- always fires a still-pending returnToPlayer `done` exactly once before returning.

local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

-- A FIXED string, unlike the Sequencer's per-run salted bind name, and deliberately so.
-- A shared BindToRenderStep name is only dangerous when two bindings can be live at
-- once, and two live rigs are impossible here: Sequencer.play refuses to start while a
-- run is active (the `active` debounce), each run builds exactly one CameraRig, and
-- takeover() returns false on an already-active rig instance. One rig, one binding.
local RENDER_BIND_NAME = "CatchCinematicCamera"

export type CameraRigCfg = {
	fovBase: number?,
	fovPunchHi: number?,
	fovPunchSettle: number?,
	fovPunchDur: number?,
	outboundHeight: number?,
	hoverDistMult: number?,
	hoverHeightFrac: number?,
	heroDistMult: number?,
	heroHeightFrac: number?,
	orbitDegrees: number?,
	returnBlendSeconds: number?,
	zoomPunchScale: number?,
}

type SavedCameraState = {
	CameraType: Enum.CameraType,
	CameraSubject: Instance?,
	FieldOfView: number,
	CFrame: CFrame,
}

-- Flat "variant record": one field set covers every motion kind; unused fields stay nil.
-- Each branch in _computeBaseCFrame casts the fields it needs (::) — safe because the
-- fields are always populated together by the constructor for that kind.
type Motion = {
	kind: string, -- "none" | "hold" | "flyTo" | "hover" | "orbit" | "returning"
	cf: CFrame?,
	startCF: CFrame?,
	targetCF: CFrame?,
	duration: number?,
	elapsed: number?,
	easeOutHard: boolean?,
	eye: Vector3?,
	focus: Vector3?,
	startTime: number?,
	seedX: number?,
	seedY: number?,
	seedZ: number?,
	degrees: number?,
	dist: number?,
	height: number?,
	startAngle: number?,
}

type FovPunch = {
	startFOV: number,
	hi: number,
	settle: number,
	duration: number,
	elapsed: number,
}

local CameraRig = {}
CameraRig.__index = CameraRig

export type Rig = typeof(setmetatable(
	{} :: {
		-- Retained only as the documented home of this rig's tunables (Config.CAMERA)
		-- for the Sequencer's own reference — never read internally. Every motion
		-- method below takes explicit per-call numbers instead of silently falling
		-- back to fields in here, so nothing in this module can drift out of sync
		-- with what the Sequencer actually passed for a given beat.
		_cfg: CameraRigCfg,
		_camera: Camera?,
		_active: boolean,
		_bound: boolean,
		_saved: SavedCameraState?,
		_savedOffset: CFrame?,
		_motion: Motion,
		_fovPunch: FovPunch?,
		_shakeSource: (() -> (Vector3, number))?,
		_lastBaseCF: CFrame?,
		_elapsedTime: number,
		_pendingDone: (() -> ())?,
		_pendingFinishSoft: boolean,
	},
	CameraRig
))

local function easeFlyTo(t: number, hard: boolean): number
	t = math.clamp(t, 0, 1)
	if hard then
		-- harder deceleration, no slow start: snap into motion, brake hard at the end.
		return 1 - (1 - t) ^ 7
	end
	-- cubic ease-in first half, quintic ease-out second half.
	if t < 0.5 then
		local u = t * 2
		return 0.5 * (u * u * u)
	else
		local u = (t - 0.5) * 2
		return 0.5 + 0.5 * (1 - (1 - u) ^ 5)
	end
end

local function easeReturnBlend(t: number): number
	t = math.clamp(t, 0, 1)
	return 1 - (1 - t) ^ 5
end

function CameraRig.new(cfg: CameraRigCfg): Rig
	local self = setmetatable({
		_cfg = cfg,
		_camera = nil,
		_active = false,
		_bound = false,
		_saved = nil,
		_savedOffset = nil,
		_motion = { kind = "none" } :: Motion,
		_fovPunch = nil,
		_shakeSource = nil,
		_lastBaseCF = nil,
		_elapsedTime = 0,
		_pendingDone = nil,
		_pendingFinishSoft = false,
	}, CameraRig)
	return self
end

-- True once returnToPlayer() has started a real blend. See the wind-down contract
-- in the module header — this is the single source of truth every guard below reads.
function CameraRig:_isWindingDown(): boolean
	return self._motion.kind == "returning"
end

function CameraRig:_applyRestore(includeCFrame: boolean)
	local cam = self._camera
	local saved = self._saved
	if not cam or not saved then
		return
	end
	cam.CameraType = saved.CameraType
	cam.CameraSubject = saved.CameraSubject
	cam.FieldOfView = saved.FieldOfView
	if includeCFrame then
		-- One-time bookend write (restore/hard-restore only) — not a per-frame writer.
		cam.CFrame = saved.CFrame
	end
end

function CameraRig:takeover(): boolean
	-- Always false while already active — winding down or not. A second takeover()
	-- must never re-save: overwriting self._saved with the current (mid-cinematic,
	-- Scriptable) camera state would permanently lose the real pre-cinematic values
	-- restore() is supposed to hand back.
	if self._active then
		return false
	end

	local cam = workspace.CurrentCamera
	if not cam then
		return false
	end

	self._camera = cam
	-- NEVER save Scriptable as the thing to hand back. Scriptable means some OTHER
	-- script had the camera when we took over (ClientMain's stone-tracking camera is
	-- the one that really does this -- see the CinematicCameraInbound handshake in
	-- CinematicClient, which stops it happening on the real throw path). Whoever it
	-- was, they are not getting it back after a 10.7s cutscene: their render loop is
	-- long gone and their own restore already fired mid-cut. Restoring Scriptable
	-- would leave the player with a frozen camera and no way to recover it short of
	-- rejoining. Custom is the correct terminal state for a cinematic that always
	-- ends by giving the player their camera back, so coerce it here as a last-resort
	-- backstop that no future camera-owning feature can defeat.
	local savedType = cam.CameraType
	local savedSubject: Instance? = cam.CameraSubject
	if savedType == Enum.CameraType.Scriptable then
		warn("[CameraRig] camera was already Scriptable at takeover -- restoring to Custom instead")
		savedType = Enum.CameraType.Custom
		-- A Scriptable owner may also have left CameraSubject nil, and Custom with no
		-- subject is still a dead camera. Only ever done alongside the type coercion --
		-- on the normal path the player's real subject is whatever we found.
		if not savedSubject then
			local plr = Players.LocalPlayer
			local char = plr and plr.Character
			local hum = char and char:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Humanoid")
			if hum then savedSubject = hum end
		end
	end
	self._saved = {
		CameraType = savedType,
		CameraSubject = savedSubject,
		FieldOfView = cam.FieldOfView,
		CFrame = cam.CFrame,
	}

	local player = Players.LocalPlayer
	local character = player and player.Character
	local hrp = (character and character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")) :: BasePart?
	if hrp then
		self._savedOffset = hrp.CFrame:ToObjectSpace(cam.CFrame)
	else
		self._savedOffset = nil
	end

	self._lastBaseCF = cam.CFrame
	self._motion = { kind = "hold", cf = cam.CFrame } :: Motion
	self._fovPunch = nil
	self._shakeSource = nil
	self._elapsedTime = 0
	self._pendingDone = nil
	self._pendingFinishSoft = false

	local typeOk = pcall(function()
		cam.CameraType = Enum.CameraType.Scriptable
	end)
	if not typeOk then
		self._camera = nil
		self._saved = nil
		return false
	end

	local bindOk = pcall(function()
		RunService:BindToRenderStep(RENDER_BIND_NAME, Enum.RenderPriority.Camera.Value + 1, function(dt: number)
			local stepOk, stepErr = pcall(function()
				self:_onRenderStep(dt)
			end)
			if not stepOk then
				warn("[CameraRig] render step error: " .. tostring(stepErr))
			end
		end)
	end)
	if not bindOk then
		pcall(function()
			cam.CameraType = (self._saved :: SavedCameraState).CameraType
		end)
		self._camera = nil
		self._saved = nil
		return false
	end

	self._bound = true
	self._active = true
	return true
end

function CameraRig:flyTo(targetCF: CFrame, seconds: number, easeOutHard: boolean)
	if not self._active or not self._camera or self:_isWindingDown() then
		return
	end
	local startCF = self._lastBaseCF or self._camera.CFrame
	self._motion = {
		kind = "flyTo",
		startCF = startCF,
		targetCF = targetCF,
		duration = math.max(seconds, 1e-3),
		elapsed = 0,
		easeOutHard = easeOutHard,
	} :: Motion
end

function CameraRig:lookHover(eye: Vector3, focus: Vector3)
	if not self._active or not self._camera or self:_isWindingDown() then
		return
	end
	self._motion = {
		kind = "hover",
		eye = eye,
		focus = focus,
		startTime = self._elapsedTime,
		seedX = math.random() * 1000,
		seedY = math.random() * 1000,
		seedZ = math.random() * 1000,
	} :: Motion
end

function CameraRig:orbit(focus: Vector3, degrees: number, seconds: number, dist: number, height: number)
	if not self._active or not self._camera or self:_isWindingDown() then
		return
	end
	local currentCF = self._lastBaseCF or self._camera.CFrame
	local rel = currentCF.Position - focus
	local startAngle = 0
	if rel.Magnitude > 1e-3 then
		startAngle = math.atan2(rel.Z, rel.X)
	end
	self._motion = {
		kind = "orbit",
		focus = focus,
		degrees = degrees,
		duration = math.max(seconds, 1e-3),
		dist = dist,
		height = height,
		elapsed = 0,
		startAngle = startAngle,
	} :: Motion
end

function CameraRig:punchFOV(hi: number, settle: number, seconds: number)
	if not self._active or not self._camera or self:_isWindingDown() then
		return
	end
	self._fovPunch = {
		startFOV = self._camera.FieldOfView,
		hi = hi,
		settle = settle,
		duration = math.max(seconds, 1e-3),
		elapsed = 0,
	}
end

function CameraRig:setShakeSource(fn: (() -> (Vector3, number))?)
	self._shakeSource = fn
end

function CameraRig:returnToPlayer(seconds: number, done: (() -> ())?)
	-- Already winding down: a second returnToPlayer() is a pure no-op. The first
	-- call's motion/done own the wind-down; this call's `done` is deliberately never
	-- invoked (there is nothing for it to observe completing) and nothing here is
	-- touched, so the in-flight blend can't be re-targeted or have its done orphaned.
	if self:_isWindingDown() then
		return
	end

	if not self._active or not self._camera then
		if done then
			pcall(done)
		end
		return
	end

	local player = Players.LocalPlayer
	local character = player and player.Character
	local hrp = (character and character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")) :: BasePart?
	local humanoid = character and character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	local isDead = humanoid ~= nil and humanoid.Health <= 0

	if not hrp or not self._savedOffset or isDead then
		self._pendingDone = done
		self:_finishReturn(true)
		return
	end

	local targetCF = hrp.CFrame * (self._savedOffset :: CFrame)
	self._motion = {
		kind = "returning",
		startCF = self._lastBaseCF or self._camera.CFrame,
		targetCF = targetCF,
		duration = math.max(seconds, 1e-3),
		elapsed = 0,
	} :: Motion
	self._pendingDone = done
end

-- hard=true: full restore incl. CFrame (kill-path / no valid HRP to blend toward).
-- hard=false: CameraType/Subject/FOV only — CFrame was already landed by the render
-- loop's own write this frame (see _onRenderStep), at the blended HRP-relative pose.
function CameraRig:_finishReturn(hard: boolean)
	local done = self._pendingDone
	self._pendingDone = nil

	if hard then
		self:restore()
	else
		pcall(function()
			if self._bound then
				RunService:UnbindFromRenderStep(RENDER_BIND_NAME)
				self._bound = false
			end
			self:_applyRestore(false)
		end)
		self._active = false
		self._shakeSource = nil
		self._motion = { kind = "none" } :: Motion
		self._fovPunch = nil
	end

	if done then
		pcall(done)
	end
end

function CameraRig:restore()
	-- restore() doubles as the abort path (kill-path, or aborting mid-returnToPlayer):
	-- if a returnToPlayer is still in flight, its done must still fire — exactly once,
	-- never silently dropped. Pop it into a local up front (so nothing can read/fire it
	-- twice — in particular the render loop's own _finishReturn can't double-fire it,
	-- since unbinding below guarantees _onRenderStep never runs again), do the actual
	-- restore work, then invoke it last so callers see a fully-restored camera.
	local done = self._pendingDone
	self._pendingDone = nil
	self._pendingFinishSoft = false

	pcall(function()
		if self._bound then
			RunService:UnbindFromRenderStep(RENDER_BIND_NAME)
			self._bound = false
		end
		if self._active then
			self:_applyRestore(true)
		end
	end)
	self._active = false
	self._shakeSource = nil
	self._motion = { kind = "none" } :: Motion
	self._fovPunch = nil

	if done then
		pcall(done)
	end
end

function CameraRig:_updateFOV(dt: number)
	local punch = self._fovPunch
	if not punch then
		return
	end
	local cam = self._camera
	if not cam then
		return
	end
	punch.elapsed += dt
	local t = math.clamp(punch.elapsed / punch.duration, 0, 1)
	local riseFrac = 0.35
	local fov: number
	if t < riseFrac then
		local u = t / riseFrac
		fov = punch.startFOV + (punch.hi - punch.startFOV) * (1 - (1 - u) ^ 3)
	else
		local u = (t - riseFrac) / (1 - riseFrac)
		fov = punch.hi + (punch.settle - punch.hi) * (u * u * (3 - 2 * u))
	end
	cam.FieldOfView = fov
	if t >= 1 then
		self._fovPunch = nil
	end
end

function CameraRig:_computeBaseCFrame(dt: number): CFrame
	local motion = self._motion
	local baseCF: CFrame

	if motion.kind == "hold" then
		baseCF = motion.cf :: CFrame

	elseif motion.kind == "flyTo" then
		local elapsed = (motion.elapsed :: number) + dt
		motion.elapsed = elapsed
		local duration = motion.duration :: number
		local t = math.clamp(elapsed / duration, 0, 1)
		local startCF = motion.startCF :: CFrame
		local targetCF = motion.targetCF :: CFrame
		local alpha = easeFlyTo(t, motion.easeOutHard :: boolean)
		baseCF = startCF:Lerp(targetCF, alpha)
		if t >= 1 then
			self._motion = { kind = "hold", cf = targetCF } :: Motion
		end

	elseif motion.kind == "hover" then
		local eye = motion.eye :: Vector3
		local focus = motion.focus :: Vector3
		local t = self._elapsedTime - (motion.startTime :: number)
		local amp = 0.15
		local dx = math.noise(t * 0.5, motion.seedX :: number) * amp
		local dy = math.noise(t * 0.5, motion.seedY :: number) * amp
		local dz = math.noise(t * 0.5, motion.seedZ :: number) * amp
		baseCF = CFrame.lookAt(eye + Vector3.new(dx, dy, dz), focus)

	elseif motion.kind == "orbit" then
		local elapsed = (motion.elapsed :: number) + dt
		motion.elapsed = elapsed
		local duration = motion.duration :: number
		local t = math.clamp(elapsed / duration, 0, 1)
		local focus = motion.focus :: Vector3
		local degrees = motion.degrees :: number
		local dist = motion.dist :: number
		local height = motion.height :: number
		local startAngle = motion.startAngle :: number
		local angle = startAngle + math.rad(degrees) * t
		local pos = focus + Vector3.new(math.cos(angle) * dist, height, math.sin(angle) * dist)
		baseCF = CFrame.lookAt(pos, focus)

	elseif motion.kind == "returning" then
		local elapsed = (motion.elapsed :: number) + dt
		motion.elapsed = elapsed
		local duration = motion.duration :: number
		local t = math.clamp(elapsed / duration, 0, 1)
		local startCF = motion.startCF :: CFrame
		local targetCF = motion.targetCF :: CFrame
		if t >= 1 then
			baseCF = targetCF
			self._pendingFinishSoft = true
		else
			local alpha = easeReturnBlend(t)
			baseCF = startCF:Lerp(targetCF, alpha)
		end

	else
		baseCF = self._lastBaseCF or (self._camera :: Camera).CFrame
	end

	self._lastBaseCF = baseCF
	return baseCF
end

function CameraRig:_onRenderStep(dt: number)
	if not self._active or not self._camera then
		return
	end

	self._elapsedTime += dt
	local cam = self._camera :: Camera
	self:_updateFOV(dt)

	-- The one and only per-frame Camera.CFrame writer. baseCF comes from whichever
	-- motion state is active (flyTo/hover/orbit/returning/hold); shakeOffset/rollDeg
	-- come from the fn installed via setShakeSource (ScreenShake:sample), applied
	-- strictly AFTER the base CFrame — ScreenShake itself never touches the camera.
	local baseCF = self:_computeBaseCFrame(dt)

	local shakeOffset = Vector3.new()
	local rollDeg = 0
	local source = self._shakeSource
	if source then
		local ok, o, r = pcall(source)
		if ok and typeof(o) == "Vector3" and typeof(r) == "number" then
			shakeOffset = o
			rollDeg = r
		end
	end

	cam.CFrame = baseCF * CFrame.new(shakeOffset) * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, math.rad(rollDeg))

	if self._pendingFinishSoft then
		self._pendingFinishSoft = false
		self:_finishReturn(false)
	end
end

return CameraRig

--!strict
-- CatchCinematic.Config — every tunable for the Massive catch cinematic.
-- DEBUG: set workspace attribute "CinematicTimescale" (number) during Play to
-- rescale every duration live (0.25 = quarter speed); read at sequence start.
local Config = {}

Config.DEBUG_TIMESCALE = 1.0

-- Which sizes trigger the cinematic from a REAL catch. Server reads this too.
-- "full" = 17.9s sequence, "trimmed" = HUGE_TRIM variant, "none" = existing behavior.
-- Huge stays "none" until the owner picks after the side-by-side demo.
Config.SIZES = { Massive = "full", Huge = "none" } :: { [string]: string }

-- After the handoff beat: run the existing PullCeremony too? (comparison pending)
-- Live override for the demo: workspace attribute "CinematicCeremonyAfter" (boolean).
Config.RUN_PULL_CEREMONY_AFTER = false

Config.SPECTATOR_RADIUS = 250          -- studs from EndPos; beyond = ignore entirely
Config.SKIP = { delay = 1.0, holdSeconds = 0.45, exitFadeSeconds = 0.18 }

-- revealCatch can grant NOTHING (player left mid-flight; a vaulted/unique/limited
-- fallback pool came up empty), and then ThrowResult never fires. Seconds from the
-- bonk -- the Sequencer scales it by run.stretch so the deadline always lands at
-- the same PLACE in the cut. The sequencer parks the clock just short of the
-- eruption while it waits, so a late grant delays the creature rather than showing
-- one the player may not own.
-- 3.0 -> 6.0 with the v2 retune (2026-08-09): the eruption moved 3.65 -> 6.35, so a
-- 3.0s deadline expired mid-DREAD and every genuine failure wound down before the
-- suspense had even built. 6.0 has to cover the dread (1.60-5.60) for the wind-down
-- to read at all; it lands in the silence, a hair short of the eruption -- exactly
-- the position the clock-park protects. A real grant arrives within milliseconds of
-- the bonk, so the only thing this costs a genuine failure is a fuller wind-down.
Config.CANCEL_TIMEOUT = 6.0

-- Beat boundaries in seconds from the bonk (t=0 = the final skip contact).
-- RETUNED v2 2026-08-09, owner feedback watching v1 live: "too fast, no suspense,
-- the brainrot doesn't emerge slowly like a beast." Dread 1.6->3.5s, silence
-- 0.45->0.75s, rise 2->5s. Total 10.7 -> 15.9s. The skip prompt covers repeat views.
Config.BEATS = {
	{ name = "bonk",     t0 = 0.00, t1 = 0.35 },
	{ name = "travel",   t0 = 0.35, t1 = 1.60 },
	{ name = "dread",    t0 = 1.60, t1 = 5.60 },  -- 4.0s: the length of the suspense build
	{ name = "silence",  t0 = 5.60, t1 = 6.35 },  -- DO NOT shorten or soften
	{ name = "eruption", t0 = 6.35, t1 = 7.20 },
	{ name = "rise",     t0 = 7.20, t1 = 13.70 },
	{ name = "hype",     t0 = 13.70, t1 = 16.20 },
	{ name = "handoff",  t0 = 16.20, t1 = 17.90 },
}
