--!strict
-- CatchCinematic.Types — shared type definitions for the Massive catch cinematic.
-- Consumed by Sequencer/CinematicClient/ThrowHandler (comment-referenced there).

export type CinematicPayload = {
	UserId: number,
	BrainrotName: string,
	Rarity: string,
	RarityColor: Color3,
	Mutation: string?,
	Size: string,
	RockId: string?,
	RockColor: Color3?,
	EndPos: Vector3,
	SurfaceY: number,
	TotalTime: number,
	NContacts: number,
	SegTime: number,
	Seed: number,
}

return {}


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/CatchCinematic/WaterFX.lua =====
--!strict
-- CatchCinematic.WaterFX -- water-surface effects for the Massive catch cinematic:
-- bonk ripple, glassy-still water, an accelerating dread ripple train, a suction
-- shadow + dip, a taut water dome, the eruption (column + splash + foam), a
-- waterfall cascade off the revealed model, and a fanned godray backdrop.
--
-- Style: reuses ThrowHandler's house ripple recipe verbatim (thin Neon cylinder,
-- rotated flat via CFrame.Angles(0,0,90), TweenService Quad-EaseOut on Size +
-- Transparency -- see ServerScriptService.Modules.ThrowHandler's ripple()/
-- spawnSplash()). Every ring in this module starts at LEAST half-faded
-- (Transparency >= 0.4), never opaque -- a Neon cylinder is a FILLED disc, so an
-- opaque one reads as a solid coin, not a ring.
--
-- TweenService is the one sanctioned animation domain here (BasePart Color/Size/
-- Transparency/CFrame) -- no RenderStepped/Heartbeat loops in this module, even
-- for the "slow rotation" on godrays (see _orbitForever: chained small-arc
-- CFrame tweens, not a per-frame writer). rippleTrain()/suctionAndShadow() are
-- instead driven EXTERNALLY: the caller (Sequencer, or this task's harness)
-- calls them every frame with an advancing `progress`, and this module sets
-- properties directly as a pure function of that progress -- replaying the same
-- progress sequence always reproduces the same state.
--
-- Every part follows ThrowHandler's decorPart pattern: Anchored, CanCollide/
-- CanQuery/CanTouch off, CastShadow off, Locked.
--
-- Randomness: ONLY through the `rng: Random` passed into WaterFX.new (godrays'
-- per-wedge angle/length jitter is the one scatter this module draws). A
-- ParticleEmitter's own per-particle scatter (SpreadAngle, Speed range, etc.) is
-- the ENGINE's internal RNG, not ours, has no override hook, and is left alone --
-- it is not what "all randomness through rng" governs.
--
-- Particle budget: Fx:particleEstimate() is a non-contractual helper (not in the
-- Task 4 interface list, additive only) returning this instance's running total,
-- so the harness/Sequencer can assert
--   sum(Rate * averageLifetime) + one-shot burst counts <= particlesCfg[quality].budget
-- without reverse-engineering live ParticleEmitter state after a fire-and-forget
-- :Emit() burst. It only ever increases (conservative for a budget check).

local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

export type WaterFXCfg = {
	stillWater: boolean?,
	rippleTrainCount: number?,
	rippleMaxRadiusMult: number?,
	rippleAccel: number?,
	suctionDipStuds: number?,
	shadowMaxMult: number?,
	domeHeightFrac: number?,
	domeRiseSeconds: number?,
	columnHeightMult: number?,
	columnSeconds: number?,
	cascadeSeconds: number?,
	debrisBurst: number?,
}

export type ParticlesTierCfg = { mult: number, budget: number }
export type ParticlesCfg = { [string]: ParticlesTierCfg }

local WaterFX = {}
WaterFX.__index = WaterFX

export type Fx = typeof(setmetatable(
	{} :: {
		_cfg: WaterFXCfg,
		_particlesCfg: ParticlesCfg,
		_stage: Folder,
		_surfacePos: Vector3,
		_quality: string,
		_mult: number,
		_budget: number,
		_rng: Random,
		_parts: { Instance },
		_tweens: { Tween },
		_waveSaved: { Size: number, Speed: number }?,
		_particleEstimate: number,
		_rippleTrainSpawned: number,
		_debrisFired: boolean,
		_shadowDisc: BasePart?,
		_dipDisc: BasePart?,
		_dome: BasePart?,
		_destroyed: boolean,
	},
	WaterFX
))

-- Visual constants not owned by Config.WATER (per-effect geometry that isn't a
-- tunable the brief asked for) -- mirrors ThrowHandler's own local constants
-- (SPLASH_TEX etc.), which likewise aren't pulled from a Config table.
local RING_THICKNESS = 0.12
local RING_COLOR = Color3.fromRGB(226, 244, 255)
local BONK_RING_START_D, BONK_RING_END_D, BONK_RING_LIFE = 2.0, 15, 0.55
local DREAD_RING_START_D, DREAD_RING_LIFE = 1.2, 0.9
local BASE_RIPPLE_D = 6
local SHADOW_BASE_D = 6
local SHADOW_TRANSPARENCY_START, SHADOW_TRANSPARENCY_END = 0.5, 0.15
local SURFACE_HUG = 0.03 -- matches ThrowHandler ripple()'s +0.04 "just above water" convention
local SHADOW_COLOR = Color3.fromRGB(8, 10, 14)
local DIP_COLOR = Color3.fromRGB(140, 200, 230)
-- RETUNED 2026-08-09 (owner: "big blue bubble like gum") -- the dome is now a DARK
-- swell, the surface bulging over something enormous, not a bright glass bubble.
local DOME_COLOR = Color3.fromRGB(26, 44, 52)
local DOME_TRANSPARENCY = 0.3
local COLUMN_COLOR = Color3.fromRGB(140, 210, 235)
local COLUMN_CROSS_D_MULT = 0.55 -- cross-section diameter, relative to modelExtents width
local FOAM_TEX = "rbxasset://textures/particles/smoke_main.dds"
local FOAM_BURST_BASE = 70
local MIST_RATE_BASE = 14
local MIST_LIFETIME = 0.55
local CASCADE_TEX = "rbxasset://textures/particles/smoke_main.dds"
local CASCADE_RATE_BASE = 9
local CASCADE_LIFETIME = 0.55
local CASCADE_MAX_PARTS = 3
local GODRAY_COUNT = 5
local GODRAY_COLOR = Color3.fromRGB(255, 250, 220)
local GODRAY_TRANSPARENCY = 0.78
local GODRAY_WIDTH, GODRAY_THICK = 3.2, 0.15
local GODRAY_RADIUS = 6 -- how far each wedge's base sits from the fan's centre pivot
local GODRAY_JITTER_DEG = 8
local GODRAY_LEN_JITTER = 0.3
local GODRAY_TILT_DEG = 12
local GODRAY_SPIN_DEG_PER_SEC = 2.5
local GODRAY_LEG_DEG = 30

local function decorPart(p: BasePart): BasePart
	p.Anchored = true
	p.CanCollide = false
	p.CanQuery = false
	p.CanTouch = false
	p.CastShadow = false
	p.Locked = true
	return p
end

function WaterFX.new(
	cfg: WaterFXCfg,
	particlesCfg: ParticlesCfg,
	stage: Folder,
	surfacePos: Vector3,
	quality: string,
	rng: Random
): Fx
	local tier = particlesCfg[quality] or particlesCfg.high or { mult = 1, budget = math.huge }
	local self = setmetatable({
		_cfg = cfg,
		_particlesCfg = particlesCfg,
		_stage = stage,
		_surfacePos = surfacePos,
		_quality = quality,
		_mult = tier.mult or 1,
		_budget = tier.budget or math.huge,
		_rng = rng,
		_parts = {},
		_tweens = {},
		_waveSaved = nil,
		_particleEstimate = 0,
		_rippleTrainSpawned = 0,
		_debrisFired = false,
		_shadowDisc = nil,
		_dipDisc = nil,
		_dome = nil,
		_destroyed = false,
	}, WaterFX)
	return (self :: any) :: Fx
end

-- Non-contractual: see the module header note on particle-budget verification.
function WaterFX:particleEstimate(): number
	return self._particleEstimate
end

function WaterFX:_ring(pos: Vector3, startD: number, endD: number, life: number, startAlpha: number): BasePart
	local ring = Instance.new("Part")
	ring.Name = "CinematicRipple"
	ring.Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder
	ring.Size = Vector3.new(RING_THICKNESS, startD, startD)
	ring.Material = Enum.Material.Neon
	ring.Color = RING_COLOR
	ring.Transparency = math.max(startAlpha, 0.4)
	ring.CFrame = CFrame.new(pos.X, pos.Y + 0.04, pos.Z) * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, math.rad(90))
	decorPart(ring)
	ring.Parent = self._stage
	table.insert(self._parts, ring)

	local tw = TweenService:Create(
		ring,
		TweenInfo.new(life, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out),
		{ Size = Vector3.new(RING_THICKNESS, endD, endD), Transparency = 1 }
	)
	table.insert(self._tweens, tw)
	tw:Play()
	return ring
end

-- One tiny impact ring -- reuses ThrowHandler's ripple recipe.
function WaterFX:bonkRing()
	self:_ring(self._surfacePos, BONK_RING_START_D, BONK_RING_END_D, BONK_RING_LIFE, 0.5)
end

-- THE THING THE ROCK HITS (owner 2026-08-09: "I don't see the rock visibly hitting
-- something"). A dark back barely breaking the waterline at the strike point: it
-- JOLTS down on impact, holds a beat, then slides back under during the travel.
-- Same lifecycle as every other part here -- stage-parented, tracked, tween-tracked.
function WaterFX:bonkHump(radius: number)
	if self._destroyed then
		return
	end
	radius = math.max(radius or 6, 3)
	local hump = Instance.new("Part")
	hump.Name = "BonkHump"
	hump.Shape = Enum.PartType.Ball
	hump.Material = Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic
	hump.Color = Color3.fromRGB(18, 30, 36)
	-- FULLY OPAQUE, deliberately. This module's own hard-tested finding (see the
	-- suction shadow/dip discs below): a semi-transparent BasePart sitting below this
	-- place's TRUE water top renders completely invisible -- only 0.00 ever draws. The
	-- hump is mostly submerged by design, so 0.05 was the whole back not rendering.
	hump.Transparency = 0
	-- a low back, mostly submerged: wide, flat, only ~15% proud of the surface
	hump.Size = Vector3.new(radius * 2, radius * 0.9, radius * 1.4)
	hump.CFrame = CFrame.new(self._surfacePos - Vector3.new(0, radius * 0.28, 0))
	decorPart(hump)
	hump.Parent = self._stage
	table.insert(self._parts, hump)
	-- Impact jolt, in three tracked tweens: a sharp 0.12s dip, the recovery the
	-- comment always promised (0.3s ease back up by a tenth of the radius -- without
	-- it the back only ever went down, which read as dead weight rather than a living
	-- thing taking a hit), then the sink-away on the existing 0.9s delay, which lands
	-- after the recovery has finished (0.12 + 0.3 < 0.9).
	local dip = TweenService:Create(hump, TweenInfo.new(0.12, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out),
		{ CFrame = hump.CFrame - Vector3.new(0, radius * 0.14, 0) })
	table.insert(self._tweens, dip)
	dip:Play()
	task.delay(0.12, function()
		if self._destroyed or not hump.Parent then
			return
		end
		local back = TweenService:Create(hump, TweenInfo.new(0.3, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out),
			{ CFrame = hump.CFrame + Vector3.new(0, radius * 0.10, 0) })
		table.insert(self._tweens, back)
		back:Play()
	end)
	task.delay(0.9, function()
		if self._destroyed or not hump.Parent then
			return
		end
		-- No Transparency in this tween: fading it out would make it vanish outright on
		-- the first frame off 0 (see the note above the Transparency assignment). It
		-- leaves by sinking, so it sinks far enough (2.2r) to be genuinely gone.
		local sink = TweenService:Create(hump, TweenInfo.new(1.6, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.In),
			{ CFrame = hump.CFrame - Vector3.new(0, radius * 2.2, 0) })
		table.insert(self._tweens, sink)
		sink:Play()
	end)
end

function WaterFX:stillWater()
	if self._cfg.stillWater == false then
		return
	end
	if self._waveSaved then
		return -- already saved -- idempotent, never overwrites the real originals
	end
	local terrain = workspace.Terrain
	self._waveSaved = { Size = terrain.WaterWaveSize, Speed = terrain.WaterWaveSpeed }
	terrain.WaterWaveSize = 0
	terrain.WaterWaveSpeed = 0
end

function WaterFX:_restoreWater()
	if self._waveSaved then
		local terrain = workspace.Terrain
		terrain.WaterWaveSize = self._waveSaved.Size
		terrain.WaterWaveSpeed = self._waveSaved.Speed
		self._waveSaved = nil
	end
end

-- Accelerating concentric ring train: spawn thresholds use exponent 1/rippleAccel
-- so gaps between successive rings SHRINK as progress climbs (dread ramping up).
-- Called every frame with an advancing 0..1 progress; catches up on any threshold
-- crossed between calls (robust to uneven frame timing).
function WaterFX:rippleTrain(progress: number)
	local p = math.clamp(progress, 0, 1)
	local cfg = self._cfg
	local count = math.max(math.floor(cfg.rippleTrainCount or 5), 0)
	local accel = math.max(cfg.rippleAccel or 1.6, 0.1)
	local maxD = BASE_RIPPLE_D * (cfg.rippleMaxRadiusMult or 3.2)

	while self._rippleTrainSpawned < count do
		local i = self._rippleTrainSpawned + 1
		local spawnAt = (i / count) ^ (1 / accel)
		if p < spawnAt then
			break
		end
		self:_ring(self._surfacePos, DREAD_RING_START_D, maxD, DREAD_RING_LIFE, 0.45)
		self._rippleTrainSpawned = i
	end
end

function WaterFX:_emitDebrisBurst()
	local cfg = self._cfg
	local count = math.max(math.floor((cfg.debrisBurst or 24) * self._mult), 0)
	if count <= 0 then
		return
	end
	local host = Instance.new("Part")
	host.Name = "SuctionDebrisHost"
	host.Size = Vector3.new(0.2, 0.2, 0.2)
	host.Transparency = 1
	host.CFrame = CFrame.new(self._surfacePos)
	decorPart(host)
	host.Parent = self._stage
	table.insert(self._parts, host)

	local e = Instance.new("ParticleEmitter")
	e.Name = "SuctionDebris"
	e.Texture = FOAM_TEX
	e.Rate = 0
	e.Lifetime = NumberRange.new(0.3, 0.7)
	e.Speed = NumberRange.new(4, 10)
	e.EmissionDirection = Enum.NormalId.Top
	e.SpreadAngle = Vector2.new(70, 70)
	e.Acceleration = Vector3.new(0, -60, 0)
	e.Size = NumberSequence.new({
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 0.5),
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 0.05),
	})
	e.Color = ColorSequence.new(SHADOW_COLOR:Lerp(Color3.new(1, 1, 1), 0.15))
	e.Transparency = NumberSequence.new({
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 0.2),
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 1),
	})
	e.Parent = host
	e:Emit(count)
	self._particleEstimate += count
end

-- Dark disc growing under the surface + a slight visible dip. Both discs are
-- lazily created once and then updated in place every call -- a pure function of
-- progress, EXCEPT the one-shot debris burst at progress>=0.3 (guarded so it
-- fires exactly once regardless of how many frames straddle that threshold).
function WaterFX:suctionAndShadow(progress: number)
	local p = math.clamp(progress, 0, 1)
	local cfg = self._cfg
	local surf = self._surfacePos

	if not self._shadowDisc then
		local disc = Instance.new("Part")
		disc.Name = "SuctionShadow"
		disc.Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder
		disc.Material = Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic
		decorPart(disc)
		disc.Parent = self._stage
		table.insert(self._parts, disc)
		self._shadowDisc = disc
	end
	if not self._dipDisc then
		local dip = Instance.new("Part")
		dip.Name = "SuctionDip"
		dip.Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder
		dip.Material = Enum.Material.Neon
		decorPart(dip)
		dip.Parent = self._stage
		table.insert(self._parts, dip)
		self._dipDisc = dip
	end

	local shadowMaxMult = cfg.shadowMaxMult or 1.4
	local d = SHADOW_BASE_D + (SHADOW_BASE_D * shadowMaxMult - SHADOW_BASE_D) * p
	local disc = self._shadowDisc :: BasePart
	disc.Size = Vector3.new(0.3, d, d)
	disc.Color = SHADOW_COLOR
	disc.Transparency = SHADOW_TRANSPARENCY_START - (SHADOW_TRANSPARENCY_START - SHADOW_TRANSPARENCY_END) * p
	-- Sits AT the surface (SURFACE_HUG, same convention as ThrowHandler's ripple()
	-- +0.04) rather than literally below it. Hard-tested finding: a semi-transparent
	-- BasePart positioned below this place's TRUE water top renders completely
	-- invisible, on both SmoothPlastic and Neon -- swept Transparency 0.00 to 0.20
	-- at a fixed underwater depth and only 0.00 (fully opaque) ever rendered.
	-- Ripples read as "on the water" for the same reason: they sit a hair ABOVE the
	-- true surface, never below it. So "growing under the surface" is depicted here
	-- as a dark stain spreading ACROSS the surface, not a literal submerged disc.
	disc.CFrame = CFrame.new(surf.X, surf.Y + SURFACE_HUG, surf.Z) * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, math.rad(90))

	local dipStuds = cfg.suctionDipStuds or 1.1
	local dip = self._dipDisc :: BasePart
	local dipD = BASE_RIPPLE_D * 0.9
	dip.Size = Vector3.new(0.15, dipD, dipD)
	dip.Color = DIP_COLOR
	-- Fully opaque -- see the shadow disc's comment above. This one DOES go
	-- genuinely underwater as it lowers, so it needs Transparency 0 to render at
	-- all; reads as a bright sinking whirlpool core rather than a tint, which
	-- still sells "the surface is being pulled down" fine.
	dip.Transparency = 0
	dip.CFrame = CFrame.new(surf.X, surf.Y - dipStuds * p, surf.Z) * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, math.rad(90))

	if not self._debrisFired and p >= 0.3 then
		self._debrisFired = true
		self:_emitDebrisBurst()
	end
end

-- Water-coloured hemisphere (flattened ellipsoid Ball, half-sunk) taut over the
-- silhouette. Only the height grows during the rise -- the footprint (radius) is
-- set once, matching "taut over the silhouette" rather than "swelling outward".
function WaterFX:dome(radius: number)
	if self._dome then
		return
	end
	local cfg = self._cfg
	local heightFrac = cfg.domeHeightFrac or 0.35
	local riseSeconds = cfg.domeRiseSeconds or 0.42

	local ball = Instance.new("Part")
	ball.Name = "SuctionDome"
	ball.Shape = Enum.PartType.Ball
	ball.Material = Enum.Material.Glass
	ball.Color = DOME_COLOR
	ball.Transparency = DOME_TRANSPARENCY
	ball.Size = Vector3.new(radius * 2, 0.2, radius * 2)
	ball.CFrame = CFrame.new(self._surfacePos)
	decorPart(ball)
	ball.Parent = self._stage
	table.insert(self._parts, ball)
	self._dome = ball

	local tw = TweenService:Create(
		ball,
		TweenInfo.new(riseSeconds, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out),
		{ Size = Vector3.new(radius * 2, radius * 2 * heightFrac, radius * 2) }
	)
	table.insert(self._tweens, tw)
	tw:Play()
end

-- Destroys the dome WITH the eruption: a fast outward pop-and-fade, then gone.
function WaterFX:burstDome()
	local ball = self._dome
	if not ball then
		return
	end
	self._dome = nil
	local tw = TweenService:Create(
		ball,
		TweenInfo.new(0.16, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.In),
		{ Size = ball.Size * Vector3.new(1.5, 0.2, 1.5), Transparency = 1 }
	)
	table.insert(self._tweens, tw)
	tw.Completed:Once(function()
		ball:Destroy()
	end)
	tw:Play()
end

-- Vertical column + radial splash ring cascade + one-shot foam sheet. Rates and
-- burst counts scale by this instance's quality mult, same as debrisBurst.
function WaterFX:erupt(modelExtents: Vector3)
	local cfg = self._cfg
	local columnHeight = math.max((cfg.columnHeightMult or 2.6) * modelExtents.Y, 1)
	local columnSeconds = math.max(cfg.columnSeconds or 0.7, 0.05)
	local crossD = math.max(math.max(modelExtents.X, modelExtents.Z) * COLUMN_CROSS_D_MULT, 1)
	local surf = self._surfacePos

	-- Vertical column: same flat-cylinder rotation ThrowHandler's ripple() uses,
	-- just applied to a TALL cylinder (Size.X is the length axis pre-rotation;
	-- CFrame.Angles(0,0,90) always maps it to world Y, regardless of magnitude).
	local column = Instance.new("Part")
	column.Name = "EruptionColumn"
	column.Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder
	column.Material = Enum.Material.Glass
	column.Color = COLUMN_COLOR
	column.Transparency = 0.25
	column.Size = Vector3.new(0.4, crossD, crossD)
	column.CFrame = CFrame.new(surf.X, surf.Y + 0.2, surf.Z) * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, math.rad(90))
	decorPart(column)
	column.Parent = self._stage
	table.insert(self._parts, column)

	local growTw = TweenService:Create(
		column,
		TweenInfo.new(columnSeconds, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out),
		{
			Size = Vector3.new(columnHeight, crossD, crossD),
			CFrame = CFrame.new(surf.X, surf.Y + columnHeight / 2, surf.Z) * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, math.rad(90)),
		}
	)
	table.insert(self._tweens, growTw)
	growTw:Play()
	growTw.Completed:Once(function()
		if not column.Parent then
			return
		end
		local fadeTw = TweenService:Create(
			column,
			TweenInfo.new(columnSeconds * 0.8, Enum.EasingStyle.Sine, Enum.EasingDirection.In),
			{ Transparency = 1, Size = Vector3.new(columnHeight * 0.6, crossD * 0.5, crossD * 0.5) }
		)
		table.insert(self._tweens, fadeTw)
		fadeTw:Play()
	end)

	-- Mist riding the column, auto-disabled after columnSeconds.
	local mistHost = Instance.new("Attachment")
	mistHost.Name = "MistAttach"
	mistHost.Parent = column
	local mist = Instance.new("ParticleEmitter")
	mist.Name = "EruptionMist"
	mist.Texture = FOAM_TEX
	mist.Rate = MIST_RATE_BASE * self._mult
	mist.Lifetime = NumberRange.new(MIST_LIFETIME * 0.7, MIST_LIFETIME)
	mist.Speed = NumberRange.new(2, 6)
	mist.SpreadAngle = Vector2.new(35, 35)
	mist.Size = NumberSequence.new({
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 0.6),
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 1.6),
	})
	mist.Transparency = NumberSequence.new({
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 0.3),
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 1),
	})
	mist.Color = ColorSequence.new(COLUMN_COLOR)
	mist.Parent = mistHost
	self._particleEstimate += mist.Rate * ((MIST_LIFETIME * 0.7 + MIST_LIFETIME) / 2)
	task.delay(columnSeconds, function()
		if mist.Parent then
			mist.Enabled = false
		end
	end)

	-- Radial splash: three cascading rings, ThrowHandler's "big" splash recipe
	-- scaled to the model's own footprint.
	local ringBase = math.max(modelExtents.X, modelExtents.Z) * 1.4
	self:_ring(surf, ringBase * 0.5, ringBase * 1.6, 0.85, 0.45)
	task.delay(0.10, function()
		if not self._destroyed then
			self:_ring(surf, ringBase * 0.4, ringBase * 2.4, 1.1, 0.55)
		end
	end)
	task.delay(0.22, function()
		if not self._destroyed then
			self:_ring(surf, ringBase * 0.3, ringBase * 3.2, 1.45, 0.68)
		end
	end)

	-- Foam sheet: one-shot burst.
	local foamHost = Instance.new("Part")
	foamHost.Name = "EruptionFoamHost"
	foamHost.Size = Vector3.new(0.2, 0.2, 0.2)
	foamHost.Transparency = 1
	foamHost.CFrame = CFrame.new(surf.X, surf.Y + 0.15, surf.Z)
	decorPart(foamHost)
	foamHost.Parent = self._stage
	table.insert(self._parts, foamHost)

	local foam = Instance.new("ParticleEmitter")
	foam.Name = "EruptionFoam"
	foam.Texture = FOAM_TEX
	foam.Rate = 0
	foam.Lifetime = NumberRange.new(0.5, 1.1)
	foam.Speed = NumberRange.new(14, 30)
	foam.EmissionDirection = Enum.NormalId.Top
	foam.SpreadAngle = Vector2.new(60, 60)
	foam.Acceleration = Vector3.new(0, -80, 0)
	foam.Size = NumberSequence.new({
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 1.2),
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 0.1),
	})
	foam.Color = ColorSequence.new(Color3.fromRGB(236, 250, 255))
	foam.Transparency = NumberSequence.new({
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 0.1),
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 1),
	})
	foam.Parent = foamHost
	local foamCount = math.max(math.floor(FOAM_BURST_BASE * self._mult), 1)
	foam:Emit(foamCount)
	self._particleEstimate += foamCount
end

-- Waterfall ParticleEmitters attached to the model's UPPER parts (top 3 by world
-- Y, deterministic by position -- no rng needed for a purely positional choice).
-- Auto-fades: each emitter runs for `seconds` then Enabled=false; already-alive
-- particles finish out their own Transparency ramp naturally.
function WaterFX:cascade(model: Model, seconds: number)
	local parts: { BasePart } = {}
	for _, d in ipairs(model:GetDescendants()) do
		if d:IsA("BasePart") then
			table.insert(parts, d)
		end
	end
	if #parts == 0 then
		return
	end
	table.sort(parts, function(a, b)
		return a.Position.Y > b.Position.Y
	end)

	local n = math.min(CASCADE_MAX_PARTS, #parts)
	for i = 1, n do
		local part = parts[i]
		local emitter = Instance.new("ParticleEmitter")
		emitter.Name = "CinematicCascade"
		emitter.Texture = CASCADE_TEX
		emitter.Rate = CASCADE_RATE_BASE * self._mult
		emitter.Lifetime = NumberRange.new(CASCADE_LIFETIME * 0.7, CASCADE_LIFETIME)
		emitter.Speed = NumberRange.new(2, 5)
		emitter.EmissionDirection = Enum.NormalId.Bottom
		emitter.SpreadAngle = Vector2.new(12, 12)
		emitter.Acceleration = Vector3.new(0, -50, 0)
		emitter.Size = NumberSequence.new({
			NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 0.4),
			NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 0.15),
		})
		emitter.Color = ColorSequence.new(Color3.fromRGB(210, 235, 250))
		emitter.Transparency = NumberSequence.new({
			NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 0.25),
			NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 1),
		})
		emitter.Parent = part
		table.insert(self._parts, emitter)
		self._particleEstimate += emitter.Rate * ((CASCADE_LIFETIME * 0.7 + CASCADE_LIFETIME) / 2)

		task.delay(seconds, function()
			if emitter.Parent then
				emitter.Enabled = false
			end
		end)
	end
end

-- Chains small-arc (GODRAY_LEG_DEG) CFrame tweens around `pivot` forever -- the
-- "slow rotation", built entirely from TweenService (no RenderStepped). Each leg
-- is small enough that the straight-line position Lerp between its two endpoints
-- is visually indistinguishable from the true arc. Stops the instant
-- self._destroyed flips (checked before every new leg is queued).
function WaterFX:_orbitForever(part: BasePart, pivot: Vector3, localOffsetCF: CFrame, startAngleDeg: number, degPerSec: number)
	local function step(angleDeg: number)
		if self._destroyed or not part.Parent then
			return
		end
		local nextAngle = angleDeg + GODRAY_LEG_DEG
		local legSeconds = GODRAY_LEG_DEG / math.max(degPerSec, 0.01)
		local targetCF = CFrame.new(pivot) * CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(nextAngle), 0) * localOffsetCF
		local tw = TweenService:Create(part, TweenInfo.new(legSeconds, Enum.EasingStyle.Linear), { CFrame = targetCF })
		table.insert(self._tweens, tw)
		tw.Completed:Once(function()
			step(nextAngle)
		end)
		tw:Play()
	end
	step(startAngleDeg)
end

-- 5 long translucent Neon wedges (plain Blocks -- WedgePart's taper axis isn't
-- worth the guesswork for a light-shaft silhouette) fanned behind `pos`, slow
-- rotation. Per-wedge angle/length jitter is the ONE rng draw in this module.
function WaterFX:godrays(pos: Vector3, height: number)
	local baseAngle = 360 / GODRAY_COUNT
	for i = 1, GODRAY_COUNT do
		local jitterDeg = (self._rng:NextNumber() - 0.5) * 2 * GODRAY_JITTER_DEG
		local lenMult = 1 + (self._rng:NextNumber() - 0.5) * 2 * GODRAY_LEN_JITTER
		local startAngle = (i - 1) * baseAngle + jitterDeg
		local rayHeight = height * lenMult

		local w = Instance.new("Part")
		w.Name = "Godray"
		w.Shape = Enum.PartType.Block
		w.Material = Enum.Material.Neon
		w.Color = GODRAY_COLOR
		w.Transparency = GODRAY_TRANSPARENCY
		w.Size = Vector3.new(GODRAY_WIDTH, rayHeight, GODRAY_THICK)
		decorPart(w)

		-- Local offset: stood up behind pos at GODRAY_RADIUS studs out, leaning back
		-- slightly. Must clear whatever's at the centre (e.g. erupt()'s column) or
		-- the fan hides behind it -- GODRAY_WIDTH*0.3 (under 1 stud) was PROVEN too
		-- tight in-place: all 5 wedges rendered clustered inside the column's own
		-- ~2.75-stud radius, fully occluded.
		local localOffsetCF = CFrame.new(0, rayHeight / 2, -GODRAY_RADIUS) * CFrame.Angles(math.rad(GODRAY_TILT_DEG), 0, 0)
		w.CFrame = CFrame.new(pos) * CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(startAngle), 0) * localOffsetCF
		w.Parent = self._stage
		table.insert(self._parts, w)

		self:_orbitForever(w, pos, localOffsetCF, startAngle, GODRAY_SPIN_DEG_PER_SEC)
	end
end

-- Destroys everything this instance made, restores Terrain wave props. Sets
-- _destroyed FIRST so any in-flight task.delay/chained-tween callbacks no-op
-- instead of racing new parts into existence after teardown.
function WaterFX:cleanup()
	self._destroyed = true
	for _, tw in ipairs(self._tweens) do
		pcall(function()
			tw:Cancel()
		end)
	end
	self._tweens = {}
	for _, inst in ipairs(self._parts) do
		pcall(function()
			inst:Destroy()
		end)
	end
	self._parts = {}
	self._shadowDisc = nil
	self._dipDisc = nil
	self._dome = nil
	self:_restoreWater()
end

return WaterFX


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/CatchFX.lua =====
-- CatchFX: a world-space burst on the catcher, escalating with rarity.
--
-- Separate from CatchReveal on purpose. CatchReveal owns the screen-space reveal card;
-- this is the thing that happens AROUND YOU, so the two can be tuned (or skipped by the
-- phase-2 upgrade) independently.
--
-- Intensity is one number per tier and every element derives from it, so the ladder
-- cannot end up non-monotonic the way separate hand-tuned entries do. Elements switch on
-- at thresholds rather than scaling from zero -- a Common should be a puff, not a faint
-- version of a God.
--
-- Only sparkles_main and smoke_main resolve as particle textures in this place; anything
-- else renders as nothing, which is why those two do all the work here.
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local Debris = game:GetService("Debris")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local M = {}

local SPARK = "rbxasset://textures/particles/sparkles_main.dds"
local SMOKE = "rbxasset://textures/particles/smoke_main.dds"

-- tier -> intensity. Gaps are deliberate: Legendary is a real step up, Secret another.
local TIER = {
	Common = 1, Uncommon = 2, Rare = 3, Epic = 4,
	Legendary = 5, Mythic = 6, Secret = 7, God = 8,
}

local function attach(part, life)
	Debris:AddItem(part, life)
	return part
end

-- a flat expanding ring on the ground
local function ring(root, colour, size, life, thickness)
	local p = Instance.new("Part")
	p.Name = "CatchFXRing"
	p.Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder
	p.Size = Vector3.new(thickness or 0.4, 2, 2)
	p.CFrame = CFrame.new(root.Position - Vector3.new(0, 2.6, 0)) * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, math.rad(90))
	p.Anchored, p.CanCollide, p.CanQuery, p.CanTouch = true, false, false, false
	p.Material, p.Color = Enum.Material.Neon, colour
	p.Transparency = 0.15
	p.Parent = workspace
	attach(p, life + 0.1)
	TweenService:Create(p, TweenInfo.new(life, Enum.EasingStyle.Quint, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), {
		Size = Vector3.new(thickness or 0.4, size, size),
		Transparency = 1,
	}):Play()
	return p
end

-- a column of light climbing out of the ground
local function beam(root, colour, height, life)
	local p = Instance.new("Part")
	p.Name = "CatchFXBeam"
	p.Size = Vector3.new(2.2, 1, 2.2)
	p.CFrame = CFrame.new(root.Position - Vector3.new(0, 2.4, 0))
	p.Anchored, p.CanCollide, p.CanQuery, p.CanTouch = true, false, false, false
	p.Material, p.Color = Enum.Material.Neon, colour
	p.Transparency = 0.25
	p.Parent = workspace
	attach(p, life + 0.1)
	TweenService:Create(p, TweenInfo.new(life, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), {
		Size = Vector3.new(0.6, height, 0.6),
		CFrame = CFrame.new(root.Position + Vector3.new(0, height / 2 - 2.4, 0)),
		Transparency = 1,
	}):Play()
end

local function sparks(root, colour, count, speed, life, texture, sizeMul)
	local a = Instance.new("Attachment")
	a.Parent = root
	local e = Instance.new("ParticleEmitter")
	e.Texture = texture or SPARK
	e.Color = ColorSequence.new(colour)
	e.LightEmission = 0.8
	e.Lifetime = NumberRange.new(life * 0.5, life)
	e.Speed = NumberRange.new(speed * 0.5, speed)
	e.SpreadAngle = Vector2.new(180, 180)
	e.Acceleration = Vector3.new(0, -18, 0)
	e.Drag = 2
	e.Rotation = NumberRange.new(0, 360)
	e.RotSpeed = NumberRange.new(-180, 180)
	e.Size = NumberSequence.new({
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 1.1 * (sizeMul or 1)),
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 0),
	})
	e.Transparency = NumberSequence.new({
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 0.1),
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 1),
	})
	e.Rate = 0
	e.Parent = a
	e:Emit(count)
	Debris:AddItem(a, life + 0.6)
end

local function flash(root, colour, brightness, range, life)
	local p = Instance.new("Part")
	p.Name = "CatchFXFlash"
	p.Size = Vector3.new(0.2, 0.2, 0.2)
	p.CFrame = CFrame.new(root.Position)
	p.Transparency = 1
	p.Anchored, p.CanCollide, p.CanQuery, p.CanTouch = true, false, false, false
	p.Parent = workspace
	local l = Instance.new("PointLight")
	l.Color, l.Brightness, l.Range = colour, brightness, range
	l.Parent = p
	attach(p, life + 0.1)
	TweenService:Create(l, TweenInfo.new(life, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out),
		{ Brightness = 0 }):Play()
end

-- screen-edge bloom for the top of the ladder only
local function vignette(colour, strength, life)
	local player = Players.LocalPlayer
	local pg = player and player:FindFirstChildOfClass("PlayerGui")
	if not pg then return end
	local gui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
	gui.Name = "CatchFXVignette"
	gui.IgnoreGuiInset = true
	gui.ResetOnSpawn = false
	gui.DisplayOrder = 25
	gui.Parent = pg
	local img = Instance.new("Frame")
	img.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	img.BackgroundColor3 = colour
	img.BackgroundTransparency = 1 - strength
	img.BorderSizePixel = 0
	img.Parent = gui
	local grad = Instance.new("UIGradient")
	grad.Rotation = 90
	grad.Transparency = NumberSequence.new({
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 0.25),
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0.5, 1),
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 0.25),
	})
	grad.Parent = img
	TweenService:Create(img, TweenInfo.new(life, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out),
		{ BackgroundTransparency = 1 }):Play()
	Debris:AddItem(gui, life + 0.2)
end

local function kick(strength)
	local cam = workspace.CurrentCamera
	if not cam then return end
	local t0 = os.clock()
	task.spawn(function()
		while os.clock() - t0 < 0.28 do
			local k = (1 - (os.clock() - t0) / 0.28) * strength
			cam.CFrame = cam.CFrame * CFrame.Angles(
				math.rad((math.random() - 0.5) * k),
				math.rad((math.random() - 0.5) * k), 0)
			task.wait()
		end
	end)
end

-- info = { Rarity = string, Color = Color3?, Mutation = string? }
function M.play(info)
	local player = Players.LocalPlayer
	local char = player and player.Character
	local root = char and char:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	if not root then return end

	local tier = TIER[info and info.Rarity] or 1
	local colour = (info and info.Color) or Color3.fromRGB(255, 236, 170)

	-- every tier gets SOMETHING, but a Common is a puff and nothing more
	sparks(root, colour, 6 + tier * 7, 6 + tier * 3.5, 0.5 + tier * 0.12, nil, 0.6 + tier * 0.09)

	if tier >= 2 then ring(root, colour, 6 + tier * 2.2, 0.45 + tier * 0.05, 0.35) end
	if tier >= 3 then flash(root, colour, 1 + tier * 0.7, 16 + tier * 4, 0.35 + tier * 0.06) end
	if tier >= 4 then
		task.delay(0.09, function()
			if root.Parent then ring(root, colour, 10 + tier * 2.6, 0.5 + tier * 0.05, 0.25) end
		end)
	end
	if tier >= 5 then
		beam(root, colour, 22 + tier * 5, 0.5 + tier * 0.07)
		kick(0.5 + (tier - 5) * 0.45)
	end
	if tier >= 6 then
		-- slow smoke bloom under the sparks: gives the top tiers physical weight
		sparks(root, colour, 10 + tier * 3, 4, 1.1, SMOKE, 3 + tier * 0.5)
	end
	if tier >= 7 then
		vignette(colour, 0.16 + (tier - 7) * 0.1, 0.55)
		-- a second, larger ring a beat later reads as a shockwave rather than a repeat
		task.delay(0.2, function()
			if root.Parent then ring(root, colour, 26 + tier * 4, 0.75, 0.5) end
		end)
	end
	if tier >= 8 then
		task.delay(0.34, function()
			if root.Parent then
				sparks(root, colour, 90, 34, 1.5, nil, 1.5)
				flash(root, colour, 7, 60, 0.7)
			end
		end)
	end
end

M.Tiers = TIER
return M


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/CatchReveal.lua =====
-- CatchReveal: the catch moment.
--
-- When you catch a brainrot, the brainrot ITSELF appears on screen and spins
-- slowly. Four bands over the eight tiers, each adding a NEW KIND of thing
-- rather than more of the last -- the rule that makes the RarityFX and
-- MutationFX ladders readable at a glance:
--
--   1  Common/Uncommon   small viewport, no backdrop
--   2  Rare/Epic         bigger + a coloured halo
--   3  Legendary/Mythic  large + shimmer + sparkles, screen darkened
--   4  Secret/God        a REAL world model, camera locked, full MutationFX
--
-- Why band 4 is not a viewport: ParticleEmitters and Highlight DO NOT RENDER
-- inside a ViewportFrame (BrainrotThumb says as much in its own header), and
-- MutationFX is built entirely from those two. A viewport reveal structurally
-- cannot show a mutation. Secret and God are exactly the catches where a
-- mutation is most worth seeing, so those two get a real model instead.
--
-- This module knows nothing about remotes and nothing about Robux. It is given
-- a catch and it shows it. CatchRevealClient decides whether to call it.

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local BrainrotThumb = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.BrainrotThumb)
local UITheme = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.UITheme)
local Mutations = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.MutationConfig)
local MutationFX = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.MutationFX)

-- "None" and "" both mean no mutation in this codebase; normalise once.
local function mutationOf(info)
	local m = info.Mutation
	if type(m) ~= "string" or m == "" or m == "None" then return nil end
	return m
end

local M = {}

local CF = UITheme.Camp
local player = Players.LocalPlayer

local BAND_OF = {
	Common = 1, Uncommon = 1,
	Rare = 2, Epic = 2,
	Legendary = 3, Mythic = 3,
	Secret = 4, God = 4,
}

-- size    viewport square in px
-- hold    seconds fully on screen, excluding the fades
-- dark    how black the backdrop goes, as OPACITY (0 = no backdrop). For band
--         4 this is the WORLD backdrop Part only -- see fallbackDark below.
-- halo    coloured ring behind the model
-- shimmer seconds per shine sweep, or false
-- sparkle how many twinkles
local SPEC = {
	{ size = 96,  hold = 1.4, dark = 0.00, halo = false, shimmer = false, sparkle = 0 },
	{ size = 120, hold = 2.0, dark = 0.15, halo = true,  shimmer = false, sparkle = 0 },
	{ size = 150, hold = 2.8, dark = 0.60, halo = true,  shimmer = 2.4,   sparkle = 4 },
	-- Band 4 always tries the world path first (buildWorld, below); this row's
	-- size/hold apply to BOTH paths, but dark and fallbackDark are deliberately
	-- separate numbers for two different mechanisms:
	--   dark         the WORLD backdrop, a lit 3D Part (buildWorld, below).
	--   fallbackDark the UI dim Frame used only when the world path is
	--                blocked and this falls back to a viewport instead -- a
	--                flat 2D overlay at the SAME opacity as a lit 3D Part
	--                reads far heavier (verified live: dark's own 0.92 value,
	--                reused for the fallback, nearly erased the persistent
	--                HUD -- the hotbar and top buttons -- which the world
	--                backdrop never touches at all since it only affects the
	--                3D scene), so the fallback earns its own, lower number.
	-- halo/shimmer/sparkle here are unused placeholders -- M.play borrows band
	-- 3's instead, so a fallen-back Secret never reads sparser than a Mythic.
	{ size = 150, hold = 3.8, dark = 0.92, fallbackDark = 0.75, halo = false, shimmer = false, sparkle = 0 },
}

local SPIN = 70     -- degrees per second, identical in every band
local FADE = 0.22   -- seconds, in and out
local FOV  = 30     -- viewport camera, matches BrainrotThumb
-- The reveal now sits at the TOP of the screen, just under the Skip/Shops/Plot bar
-- (StarterGui.MainUI.TabBar: y=12, height 52, in an inset-ignored ScreenGui, so its
-- bottom is ~64px). This is where the holder's TOP edge lands. Both GUIs ignore the
-- GUI inset, so it is a true from-top pixel offset. Tune to taste.
local REVEAL_TOP_Y = 78

-- fixed sparkle spots so a reveal looks composed rather than random
local SPARKLE_AT = {
	Vector2.new(0.14, 0.22), Vector2.new(0.85, 0.28), Vector2.new(0.24, 0.74),
	Vector2.new(0.78, 0.70), Vector2.new(0.50, 0.10),
}

local gui             -- ScreenGui, built on first use
local live            -- the running reveal's record, or nil
local token = 0

local function ensureGui()
	if gui and gui.Parent then return gui end
	gui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
	gui.Name = "CatchRevealUI"
	gui.ResetOnSpawn = false
	gui.IgnoreGuiInset = true
	-- above the rare-catch banner (8) and every panel (9)
	gui.DisplayOrder = 12
	gui.Parent = player:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")
	return gui
end

-- Safe to call twice, and safe after a natural finish. Everything that can
-- outlive the reveal is torn down here and nowhere else, so there is exactly
-- one path out.
local function teardown(rec)
	if not rec or rec.dead then return end
	rec.dead = true
	if rec.conn then rec.conn:Disconnect(); rec.conn = nil end
	if rec.restore then pcall(rec.restore) end
	if rec.root then rec.root:Destroy(); rec.root = nil end
	if live == rec then live = nil end
end

-- The model, framed and spinning. Returns the per-frame updater, or nil when
-- there is no model for that name (caller falls back to text only).
local function buildViewport(rec, spec, info, parent)
	local master = BrainrotThumb.master(info.Name)
	if not master then return nil end

	local vp = Instance.new("ViewportFrame")
	vp.Name = "Model"
	vp.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0)
	vp.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0)
	vp.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(spec.size, spec.size)
	vp.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	vp.ZIndex = 3
	vp.Parent = parent

	local m = master:Clone()
	m.Parent = vp

	-- Frame from the REAL bounding box: these models run from under 5 studs to
	-- over 30, so one fixed distance would crop the big ones and shrink the
	-- small ones to a dot. Shared with BrainrotThumb.add so the grids and the
	-- reveal cannot disagree about how a model is framed.
	local centre, dist = BrainrotThumb.framing(m, FOV)

	local cam = Instance.new("Camera")
	cam.FieldOfView = FOV
	cam.Parent = vp
	vp.CurrentCamera = cam

	rec.viewport = vp

	-- Spin the CAMERA around the model, not the model. Rotating the model would
	-- need its pivot moved to the bounding-box centre first, because on these
	-- packs the PrimaryPart is an arbitrary limb sitting anywhere inside the
	-- body -- it would wobble around an off-centre point. Orbiting the camera
	-- is identical on screen and cannot disturb the model at all.
	local base = BrainrotThumb.DEFAULT_DIR
	return function(t)
		local dir = CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(SPIN) * t, 0) * base
		cam.CFrame = CFrame.lookAt(centre + dir * dist, centre)
	end
end

-- === Band 4: a real model in the world ===
--
-- The camera does NOT move -- it only stops taking input. Moving it risks
-- landing inside terrain or a building, and a reveal that ruins your view is
-- worse than one that is merely close. A black backdrop part behind the model
-- does the darkening, because a full-screen UI dim would darken the model too:
-- UI always renders above the 3D world.
-- Task 5 Step 1b: INVERTED from the original design. The model used to sit
-- BEYOND the character (character distance + clearance), which put the
-- player's own avatar -- and whatever it's wearing -- between the camera and
-- the reveal. Measured on this account: a 7.99x4.77x7.74 Tarantula accessory
-- covered the model's middle, and the backdrop (behind the model) darkened
-- nothing nearer than that, so the takeover never read as a takeover.
--
-- Both the model and the backdrop now sit IN FRONT OF the character instead,
-- each derived from where the character actually is (not a fixed camera-
-- relative offset) for the same reason the original code measured the
-- character rather than hardcoding a distance -- a player who has scrolled
-- their zoom in or out still gets numbers that make sense for where they are:
--   dist         = charDist - MODEL_CLEARANCE     (nearer than the character)
--   backdropDist = charDist - BACKDROP_CLEARANCE  (also nearer, but further
--                  out than the model, so ONE panel hides the avatar and
--                  everything past it at once)
-- MODEL_CLEARANCE > BACKDROP_CLEARANCE by construction, so backdropDist is
-- always further from the camera than dist is -- camera < model < backdrop <
-- character holds for any charDist, not just the default one.
local CHAR_DIST_FALLBACK = 13   -- assumed camera->character distance when there is no character to measure from -- Roblox's default third-person shoulder distance
local MODEL_CLEARANCE    = 7    -- studs the model sits in front of the character (~6 studs from the camera at the default distance)
local BACKDROP_CLEARANCE = 3    -- studs the backdrop sits in front of the character -- less than MODEL_CLEARANCE so it always lands BEHIND the model (~10 studs from the camera at the default distance)
local MIN_MODEL_DIST     = 3    -- floor so the model can never land behind or inside the camera's near plane at a tight zoom
local WORLD_HEIGHT       = 2.6  -- shrunk from 5 for the smaller top-anchored reveal; studs tall when dist == CHAR_DIST_FALLBACK - MODEL_CLEARANCE (6, the default-zoom case); scaled proportionally at other distances so the reveal reads the same size regardless of zoom. Lower than the old 7 because the model is now ~4x closer to the camera than before (6 studs vs ~23), so the same physical height reads much bigger on screen -- verified live: 7 filled the frame edge-to-edge and cropped the creature's own silhouette.
-- Screen-space RAISE for the band-4 world model: shift it UP by this fraction of its
-- camera distance so the reveal sits near the TOP of the screen (under the Skip/Shops
-- bar) rather than dead-centre. Proportional to dist so it reads the same at any zoom;
-- ~0..0.5 keeps it on-screen at a ~70-deg vertical FOV. Tune to taste.
local WORLD_UP_FRAC      = 0.45
local BACKDROP_SIZE      = 400  -- studs square; raised from 260 after a live screenshot showed sky peeking past the top-right corner at the closer ~10-stud backdrop distance -- the corner of a wide viewport reaches slightly further than a naive half-FOV estimate suggests

-- Task 5 final fix wave -- CRITICAL: the model below used to be normalised by
-- HEIGHT ALONE, but it spins continuously about world Y, so its real reach is
-- the horizontal HALF-DIAGONAL of its footprint (0.5*sqrt(X^2+Z^2)) at every
-- instant, not either axis extent alone. That distinction doesn't matter for
-- a static display -- BrainrotSpawner and InventoryHandler both clamp
-- min(height factor, width factor) and that is correct for THEM, because
-- their models never turn -- but nothing here bounded the ROTATING reach at
-- all: the same maths run over every Secret/God model found 6 of 12 sweeping
-- past the backdrop, two of them (Tralalero Tralala and Los Tralaleritos --
-- the tier's two heaviest catch weights) sweeping clean through the camera,
-- at every zoom. These constants are the safety margin added on top of the
-- two hard constraints (sweep < dist; dist + sweep < backdropAt).
local SWEEP_CAM_GAP      = 0.5  -- studs the model's sweep must stay short of the camera
local SWEEP_BACKDROP_GAP = 0.5  -- studs the model's sweep must stay short of the backdrop
local MIN_SWEEP_BUDGET   = 1    -- studs; below this the world path isn't worth it -- bail to viewport (see the charDist guard below)

local function stripScripts(model)
	-- ReplicatedStorage.BrainrotModels is verified 0 scripts today, but this
	-- pack has carried embedded free-model scripts before and they only run
	-- OUTSIDE Studio, so they can never be caught by testing here.
	for _, d in ipairs(model:GetDescendants()) do
		if d:IsA("LuaSourceContainer") then d:Destroy() end
	end
end

-- Rotation-only CFrame that points world -Z at `worldDir`, flattened to the
-- horizontal plane first (Y dropped, then re-normalised). Every rotation
-- buildWorld hands to PivotTo is composed from CFrames built by this
-- function, so every one of them is a pure yaw about world Y -- which is
-- what fixes BOTH the facing bug and the spin-axis bug below: neither the
-- camera's pitch nor its roll can ever enter the model's rotation.
local function flatYawCFrame(worldDir)
	local flat = Vector3.new(worldDir.X, 0, worldDir.Z)
	if flat.Magnitude < 1e-4 then flat = Vector3.new(0, 0, -1) end
	return CFrame.lookAt(Vector3.new(), flat.Unit)
end

-- BrainrotThumb's own front-quarter offset, flattened to a pure yaw (its
-- Y=0.45 "slightly above" component is dropped: this model has to stay
-- UPRIGHT -- see the spin-axis fix below -- so only the horizontal twist can
-- carry over). Computed once at require-time since DEFAULT_DIR never changes.
local DEFAULT_YAW = flatYawCFrame(BrainrotThumb.DEFAULT_DIR)

local function buildWorld(rec, spec, info, fades)
	local cam = workspace.CurrentCamera
	local folder = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("BrainrotModels")
	local src = folder and folder:FindFirstChild(info.Name)
	if not cam or not src then return nil end

	local origin = cam.CFrame

	-- Nearer the camera than the character now, not farther -- see the header
	-- comment above (Task 5 Step 1b). charDist assumes CHAR_DIST_FALLBACK when
	-- there is no character to measure, so the same formula covers both cases.
	local charRoot = player.Character and player.Character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	local charDist = charRoot and (charRoot.Position - origin.Position).Magnitude or CHAR_DIST_FALLBACK

	-- Clamped two ways: never closer to the camera than MIN_MODEL_DIST (the
	-- near-plane floor), and never further out than the character itself even
	-- at an extremely tight zoom -- "nearer than the character" must hold
	-- REGARDLESS of charDist, not just at the default distance.
	-- MIN_MODEL_DIST used to be a floor in name only: math.min(charDist - 1, ...)
	-- was the OUTER call, so whenever charDist - 1 fell below MIN_MODEL_DIST
	-- (charDist < 4) that ceiling silently overrode the floor -- live-recorded
	-- at charDist ~1.8 (Roblox's own camera collision pulling the camera in),
	-- which drove dist, and worldHeight below, both non-positive. Once the
	-- character is this close there is no valid gap left to put a model in at
	-- all, so that regime bails to nil instead of computing a nonsense
	-- distance -- M.play already falls back to the viewport whenever
	-- buildWorld returns nil, the same as a blocked sightline.
	if charDist - 1 < MIN_MODEL_DIST then return nil end
	local dist = math.clamp(charDist - MODEL_CLEARANCE, MIN_MODEL_DIST, charDist - 1)

	-- A second, narrower bail: even once dist clears the floor above, the
	-- backdrop's OWN ceiling (charDist - 0.5, so it never reaches the
	-- character) can end up almost flush against dist, leaving no room for a
	-- sweep budget worth animating -- verified charDist == 4 exactly crushes
	-- every model in the roster to zero height even though neither hard
	-- constraint below is technically violated. Below this, fall back too.
	if (charDist - 0.5) - dist < SWEEP_BACKDROP_GAP + MIN_SWEEP_BUDGET then return nil end

	local spot = origin * CFrame.new(0, dist * WORLD_UP_FRAC, -dist)

	-- Facing + spin axis (Task 5 final fix wave -- two review findings fixed
	-- together since both live in this same rotation).
	--   FACING: a bare `spot` inherits the CAMERA's rotation, and the models
	--   are authored facing -Z, so at t=0 the model's front used to point the
	--   same way the camera looks -- directly AWAY from the camera it's
	--   sitting in front of (measured dot(front, toCamera) == -1.000).
	--   dueCamera is the pure-yaw rotation that faces the model dead at the
	--   camera instead; composing DEFAULT_YAW on top reproduces the SAME
	--   front-quarter angle BrainrotThumb's orbiting camera opens bands 1-3
	--   on (both are pure-Y rotations, so they commute -- only the SUM of the
	--   two yaws matters, not the order).
	--   SPIN AXIS: dueCamera, DEFAULT_YAW and the per-frame spin in poseAt
	--   below are ALL built from flatYawCFrame, i.e. all pure yaw about world
	--   Y -- never the camera's own up vector, which tilts with camera pitch
	--   (measured 5.7 degrees of wobble at 10 degrees of pitch, worse
	--   steeper) and is what the old `spot`-inherited rotation actually spun
	--   the model around.
	local dueCamera = flatYawCFrame(-origin.LookVector)
	local baseRot = dueCamera * DEFAULT_YAW
	local function poseAt(t)
		return CFrame.new(spot.Position) * CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(SPIN) * t, 0) * baseRot
	end

	-- If real, VISIBLE geometry sits between the camera and the reveal spot the
	-- model would be hidden behind it. Rather than shove the camera somewhere it
	-- might not fit, fall back to the viewport path -- a Secret that looks like
	-- a Legendary beats a Secret you cannot see. But in this engine build,
	-- CanCollide=true overrides CanQuery=false for workspace:Raycast, so the
	-- lake's invisible collision walls (CanQuery=false, CanCollide=true, fully
	-- transparent) register as hits despite being nothing a player can see --
	-- measured 37/84 clear across the dock's real stance spots before this
	-- loop, 84/84 after. A fully-transparent hit is not a visual obstruction:
	-- exclude it and cast again, bounded so a stack of invisible parts can't
	-- spin forever. `blocked` starts true and only clears on a genuine no-hit
	-- cast -- measured a maximum of 4 consecutive transparent hits across 168
	-- real casts (cap is 6, so there is headroom), but exhausting the cap
	-- without ever reaching a clean cast must still fail SAFE: an unresolved
	-- line of sight is exactly the kind of obstruction nobody verified, so it
	-- falls back rather than assuming clear.
	local exclude = { player.Character }
	local params = RaycastParams.new()
	params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
	params.FilterDescendantsInstances = exclude
	local blocked = true
	for _ = 1, 6 do
		local hit = workspace:Raycast(origin.Position, (spot.Position - origin.Position), params)
		if not hit then
			blocked = false
			break
		elseif hit.Instance:IsA("BasePart") and hit.Instance.Transparency >= 1 then
			table.insert(exclude, hit.Instance)
			params.FilterDescendantsInstances = exclude
		else
			break
		end
	end
	if blocked then return nil end

	-- Capture savedType and assign rec.restore BEFORE anything is parented or
	-- the camera is touched. If a throw happens anywhere below -- cloning,
	-- scaling, parenting, or the camera assignment itself -- M.play's pcall
	-- calls teardown(rec), which calls rec.restore if one is SET. Assigning it
	-- this early, with rec.worldModel/rec.backdrop nil-checked inside it so it
	-- is safe to call before either exists, closes the window where a throw
	-- could leave the model or backdrop stranded outside rec.root's tree (so
	-- teardown's rec.root:Destroy() can't reach them) or the camera stuck
	-- Scriptable with nothing left to undo it -- unrecoverable without
	-- rejoining.
	local savedType = cam.CameraType
	-- Never save Scriptable as the restore target: if another system (the Massive
	-- catch cinematic) owns the camera right now, restoring Scriptable up to ~9s
	-- later hands back a camera with no writer -- frozen until rejoin. A second
	-- Epic+ catch really can be revealed mid-cut. Custom is the only recoverable
	-- terminal state. Same coercion as CameraRig/MassiveEmergence/ClientMain.
	if savedType == Enum.CameraType.Scriptable then savedType = Enum.CameraType.Custom end
	rec.restore = function()
		if rec.worldModel then rec.worldModel:Destroy(); rec.worldModel = nil end
		if rec.backdrop then rec.backdrop:Destroy(); rec.backdrop = nil end
		local c = workspace.CurrentCamera
		if c then c.CameraType = savedType end
	end

	local m = src:Clone()
	stripScripts(m)
	for _, p in ipairs(m:GetDescendants()) do
		if p:IsA("BasePart") then
			p.Anchored = true
			p.CanCollide = false
			p.CanQuery = false
			p.CanTouch = false
			p.Massless = true
		end
	end

	-- Pivot about the bounding-box centre BEFORE scaling, not after: ScaleTo
	-- scales around the model's CURRENT pivot, and on these packs the
	-- PrimaryPart is an arbitrary limb sitting anywhere inside the body.
	-- Scaling around that off-centre point drags the bounding-box centre along
	-- with it (measured a 3.75-stud shift on a real model) -- pivoting here
	-- first means there is nothing off-centre left to scale around. One
	-- GetBoundingBox call covers both the centre (for the pivot) and the
	-- Y-extent (for the scale factor) since nothing between them moves a part.
	m.PrimaryPart = nil
	local preScale, ext = m:GetBoundingBox()
	m.WorldPivot = CFrame.new(preScale.Position)

	-- WORLD_HEIGHT was tuned to read right when dist is CHAR_DIST_FALLBACK -
	-- MODEL_CLEARANCE (the default-zoom case); scale proportionally at other
	-- distances so the reveal is the same apparent size regardless of zoom.
	local worldHeight = WORLD_HEIGHT * (dist / (CHAR_DIST_FALLBACK - MODEL_CLEARANCE))
	-- Between the model and the character at every distance: always a little
	-- further out than the model, always a little short of the character, so
	-- one panel hides the avatar and the world beyond it at once. Overridden
	-- below, once the model's real footprint is known, if its sweep needs more
	-- room than this default gives it.
	local backdropAt = math.min(charDist - 0.5, math.max(dist + 2, charDist - BACKDROP_CLEARANCE))

	-- ScaleTo is ABSOLUTE. Re-measuring an already-scaled model and calling it
	-- again resets to authored size, so always multiply the CURRENT scale.
	-- `factor` starts as the naive, HEIGHT-ONLY value -- the critical bug, on
	-- its own -- and the sweep clamp below corrects it before it is ever
	-- applied to the model.
	if ext.Y > 0 then
		local factor = worldHeight / ext.Y

		-- The model's real reach while it spins: the half-diagonal of its
		-- horizontal footprint at whatever scale `factor` currently is. A
		-- rotating rectangle's farthest point from its own centre is always its
		-- corner, at every angle, so this bounds the sweep regardless of where
		-- in the spin the model happens to be at any given instant.
		local halfDiag = 0.5 * math.sqrt(ext.X * ext.X + ext.Z * ext.Z)
		local sweep = halfDiag * factor

		-- Reviewer's suggested order, because it costs far less height than
		-- clamping the scale first: PUSH THE BACKDROP OUT to cover this sweep
		-- before touching the scale at all -- ADDING a term to the existing
		-- floor above rather than replacing it, so a model whose sweep already
		-- fits (every "clean" Secret/God at the shipped defaults) gets the exact
		-- same backdropAt as before. Still capped at charDist - 0.5 so the
		-- backdrop can never reach or pass the character.
		backdropAt = math.min(charDist - 0.5, math.max(dist + 2, charDist - BACKDROP_CLEARANCE, dist + sweep + SWEEP_BACKDROP_GAP))

		-- Only NOW clamp the scale, and only if pushing the backdrop out
		-- couldn't fully absorb the sweep (backdropAt hit its charDist - 0.5
		-- ceiling short of what was needed) or the sweep alone already reaches
		-- the camera regardless of the backdrop. maxSweep is always positive
		-- here: dist >= MIN_MODEL_DIST and backdropAt >= dist + 2 by
		-- construction, and the MIN_SWEEP_BUDGET guard above already turned away
		-- the charDist range where that would leave no room at all.
		local maxSweep = math.min(dist - SWEEP_CAM_GAP, backdropAt - dist - SWEEP_BACKDROP_GAP)
		if sweep > maxSweep and halfDiag > 0 then
			factor = math.min(factor, maxSweep / halfDiag)
		end

		m:ScaleTo(m:GetScale() * factor)
	end

	-- Re-measure rather than assume the centre held: cheap, and the per-frame
	-- PivotTo below must be exact. This one CANNOT fold into the call above --
	-- ScaleTo has genuinely moved the parts in between.
	local postScale = m:GetBoundingBox()
	m.WorldPivot = CFrame.new(postScale.Position)

	-- Pose it correctly BEFORE parenting: the spin function returned below
	-- only runs on the next RenderStepped, so without this the clone would
	-- render for one frame at whatever coordinates it was authored at in
	-- BrainrotModels.
	m:PivotTo(poseAt(0))
	m.Parent = workspace          -- client-created: never replicates
	rec.worldModel = m

	-- The payoff for the hybrid. pcall because a bad mutation must never cost
	-- the player the reveal -- showing the creature matters more than tinting it.
	local mut = mutationOf(info)
	if mut then pcall(MutationFX.apply, m, mut) end

	local backdrop = Instance.new("Part")
	backdrop.Name = "CatchRevealBackdrop"
	backdrop.Size = Vector3.new(BACKDROP_SIZE, BACKDROP_SIZE, 1)
	backdrop.CFrame = origin * CFrame.new(0, 0, -backdropAt)
	backdrop.Anchored = true
	backdrop.CanCollide = false
	backdrop.CanQuery = false
	backdrop.CanTouch = false
	backdrop.CastShadow = false
	backdrop.Material = Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic
	backdrop.Color = Color3.new(0, 0, 0)
	backdrop.Transparency = 1
	backdrop.Parent = workspace
	rec.backdrop = backdrop
	-- Fades in alongside everything else (M.play's own fade-in loop, right
	-- after this function returns) and back OUT the same way at teardown --
	-- this used to be tweened in directly, right here, and never registered in
	-- `fades`, so nothing ever tweened it back out: the backdrop (and the
	-- model behind it) snapped to gone in a single frame while the labels were
	-- still mid-fade.
	table.insert(fades, { backdrop, "Transparency", 1 - spec.dark })

	-- Freeze the camera where it already is. rec.restore (above) already knows
	-- how to undo this.
	cam.CameraType = Enum.CameraType.Scriptable
	cam.CFrame = origin

	-- A camera left Scriptable is unrecoverable without rejoining, so it gets a
	-- second, independent guard on top of teardown -- the same belt-and-braces
	-- as ThrowHandler's flight watchdog.
	task.delay(FADE * 2 + spec.hold + 3, function()
		if not rec.dead then teardown(rec) end
	end)

	return function(t)
		if rec.worldModel and rec.worldModel.Parent then
			rec.worldModel:PivotTo(poseAt(t))
		end
	end
end

function M.isPlaying()
	return live ~= nil and not live.dead
end

-- info = { Name, Rarity, RarityColor, Mutation }
-- Returns a handle with :skip(), or nil if nothing could be shown.
function M.play(info)
	if type(info) ~= "table" or type(info.Name) ~= "string" then return nil end

	-- newest wins, matching the resultToken behaviour the old card had
	if live then teardown(live) end
	token += 1
	local myToken = token

	local band = BAND_OF[info.Rarity] or 1
	local spec = SPEC[band]
	local accent = typeof(info.RarityColor) == "Color3" and info.RarityColor
		or Color3.fromRGB(190, 190, 190)

	-- Bands 1-3 are viewports, where ParticleEmitters and Highlight render
	-- nothing, so MutationFX cannot appear. The mutation is carried by the halo
	-- colour and the name prefix instead.
	local mut = mutationOf(info)
	local haloColour = accent
	if mut then
		-- Guarded the same way as MutationFX.apply below: an unknown name or a
		-- future throw inside MutationConfig must never escape M.play's pcall --
		-- the reveal must never be able to block the catch that triggered it.
		local ok, mc = pcall(Mutations.Color, mut)
		if ok and typeof(mc) == "Color3" then haloColour = mc end
	end

	local rec = { dead = false, token = myToken }

	-- Everything below touches live Instances and third-party modules
	-- (BrainrotThumb, UITheme). It all runs inside ONE pcall: rec is reachable
	-- from the instant root is parented below, so no matter how far
	-- construction gets before something throws, teardown(rec) can still find
	-- and destroy whatever was built. Reveal must never be able to break the
	-- catch that triggered it.
	local ok, err = pcall(function()
		local root = Instance.new("Frame")
		root.Name = "Reveal"
		root.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
		root.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		root.ZIndex = 1
		root.Parent = ensureGui()
		rec.root = root

		local fades = {}   -- {inst, prop, to}

		-- Decide the render path FIRST, before any UI flair is built. A world
		-- reveal draws its own backdrop and (Task 3) its own MutationFX, so it
		-- must carry none of the dim/halo/shimmer/sparkle -- and a fallback must
		-- carry band 3's flair, not band 4's own empty placeholders, so a
		-- fallen-back Secret is never sparser than a Mythic. Building the UI
		-- AFTER this decision (rather than building flair, then discovering band
		-- 4 didn't want it) is what makes that possible.
		local spin
		if band == 4 then
			spin = buildWorld(rec, spec, info, fades)
		end

		-- effective is what the REST of this function actually builds from.
		-- World path (spin already set): nothing but the labels. Band-4
		-- fallback: band 4's own size/hold/dark, but band 3's halo/shimmer/
		-- sparkle. Bands 1-3: spec, unchanged.
		local effective = spec
		if spin then
			effective = { size = spec.size, hold = spec.hold, dark = 0,
				halo = false, shimmer = false, sparkle = 0 }
		elseif band == 4 then
			effective = { size = spec.size, hold = spec.hold, dark = spec.fallbackDark,
				halo = SPEC[3].halo, shimmer = SPEC[3].shimmer, sparkle = SPEC[3].sparkle }
		end

		-- backdrop. Stated as OPACITY in SPEC, so invert it here -- "dark 0.8" read
		-- as a transparency would mean the opposite of what is intended.
		if effective.dark > 0 then
			local dim = Instance.new("Frame")
			dim.Name = "Dim"
			dim.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
			dim.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.new(0, 0, 0)
			dim.BackgroundTransparency = 1
			dim.BorderSizePixel = 0
			dim.ZIndex = 1
			dim.Parent = root
			table.insert(fades, { dim, "BackgroundTransparency", 1 - effective.dark })
		end

		local holder = Instance.new("Frame")
		holder.Name = "Holder"
		holder.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0)
		holder.Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0, REVEAL_TOP_Y)   -- top-centre, just under the Skip/Shops/Plot bar
		holder.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(effective.size, effective.size + 92)
		holder.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		holder.ZIndex = 2
		holder.Parent = root

		-- halo: an oversized ring behind the model carrying a coloured stroke
		local haloStroke
		if effective.halo then
			local halo = Instance.new("Frame")
			halo.Name = "Halo"
			halo.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
			halo.Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0, effective.size / 2)
			halo.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(effective.size * 0.86, effective.size * 0.86)
			halo.BackgroundTransparency = 1
			halo.ZIndex = 2
			halo.Parent = holder
			local hc = Instance.new("UICorner")
			hc.CornerRadius = UDim.new(1, 0)
			hc.Parent = halo
			haloStroke = Instance.new("UIStroke")
			haloStroke.Color = haloColour
			haloStroke.Thickness = 6
			haloStroke.Transparency = 1
			haloStroke.LineJoinMode = Enum.LineJoinMode.Round
			haloStroke.Parent = halo
			table.insert(fades, { haloStroke, "Transparency", 0.35 })
		end

		if not spin then
			spin = buildViewport(rec, effective, info, holder)
		end
		if rec.viewport then
			rec.viewport.ImageTransparency = 1
			table.insert(fades, { rec.viewport, "ImageTransparency", 0 })
		end

		-- shimmer lives on its OWN empty frame, never on anything holding text: a
		-- UIGradient tints its parent's glyphs too, which has bitten this codebase.
		local shimmerGrad
		if effective.shimmer then
			local shim = Instance.new("Frame")
			shim.Name = "Shimmer"
			shim.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(effective.size, effective.size)
			shim.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255)
			shim.BackgroundTransparency = 0
			shim.BorderSizePixel = 0
			shim.ZIndex = 4
			shim.Parent = holder
			shimmerGrad = Instance.new("UIGradient")
			shimmerGrad.Rotation = 24
			shimmerGrad.Transparency = NumberSequence.new({
				NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 1),
				NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0.44, 1),
				NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0.50, 0.62),
				NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0.56, 1),
				NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 1),
			})
			shimmerGrad.Parent = shim
		end

		local sparkles = {}
		for i = 1, effective.sparkle do
			local at = SPARKLE_AT[i] or SPARKLE_AT[1]
			local s = Instance.new("TextLabel")
			s.Name = "Sparkle"
			s.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
			s.Position = UDim2.new(at.X, 0, 0, at.Y * effective.size)
			s.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(40, 40)
			s.BackgroundTransparency = 1
			s.Font = UITheme.GlyphFont
			s.Text = "\u{2726}"
			s.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255)
			s.TextSize = 26
			s.TextTransparency = 1
			s.ZIndex = 5
			s.Parent = holder
			sparkles[i] = s
		end

		-- name, then rarity. No panel behind either -- that is the whole point.
		local nameLabel = Instance.new("TextLabel")
		nameLabel.Name = "BrainrotName"
		nameLabel.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0)
		nameLabel.Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0, effective.size + 6)
		nameLabel.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(effective.size + 160, 40)
		nameLabel.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		nameLabel.Font = UITheme.Font
		nameLabel.TextSize = 24
		nameLabel.TextColor3 = CF.onDark
		nameLabel.TextScaled = false
		nameLabel.TextTruncate = Enum.TextTruncate.AtEnd
		nameLabel.Text = mut and (mut .. " " .. info.Name) or info.Name
		nameLabel.TextTransparency = 1
		nameLabel.ZIndex = 6
		nameLabel.Parent = holder
		local nameInk = UITheme.inkText(nameLabel, 3)
		nameInk.Transparency = 1

		local rarityLabel = Instance.new("TextLabel")
		rarityLabel.Name = "Rarity"
		rarityLabel.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0)
		rarityLabel.Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0, effective.size + 48)
		rarityLabel.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(effective.size + 160, 32)
		rarityLabel.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		rarityLabel.Font = UITheme.Font
		rarityLabel.TextSize = 18
		rarityLabel.TextColor3 = accent
		rarityLabel.Text = string.upper(tostring(info.Rarity or "?"))
		rarityLabel.TextTransparency = 1
		rarityLabel.ZIndex = 6
		rarityLabel.Parent = holder
		local rarityInk = UITheme.inkText(rarityLabel, 2.6)
		rarityInk.Transparency = 1

		table.insert(fades, { nameLabel, "TextTransparency", 0 })
		table.insert(fades, { rarityLabel, "TextTransparency", 0 })
		table.insert(fades, { nameInk, "Transparency", 0 })
		table.insert(fades, { rarityInk, "Transparency", 0 })

		-- fade in
		for _, f in ipairs(fades) do
			TweenService:Create(f[1], TweenInfo.new(FADE), { [f[2]] = f[3] }):Play()
		end

		-- One driver for this reveal, disconnected in teardown. Nothing per-frame
		-- survives the reveal.
		local t = 0
		rec.conn = RunService.RenderStepped:Connect(function(dt)
			t += dt
			if spin then spin(t) end
			-- Guarded to [FADE, FADE+hold]: outside that window a TWEEN owns
			-- Transparency (the fade-in below FADE, the fade-out above hold) and
			-- this per-frame set would win the race every single frame, which is
			-- why the halo used to SNAP in instead of fading (known since Task 1).
			-- The phase is shifted so the oscillation's own start (sin = -1, its
			-- trough) lands exactly on 0.35 -- the value the fade-in tween was
			-- already headed to -- so handing off from tween to handler at t=FADE
			-- is seamless instead of jumping to the oscillation's t=0 value.
			if haloStroke and t >= FADE and t <= FADE + effective.hold then
				haloStroke.Transparency = 0.35 + 0.22 * (0.5 + 0.5 * math.sin((t - FADE) * 2.1 - math.pi / 2))
			end
			if shimmerGrad then
				shimmerGrad.Offset = Vector2.new(((t / effective.shimmer) % 1) * 2.6 - 1.3, 0)
			end
			for i = 1, #sparkles do
				local k = 0.5 + 0.5 * math.sin(t * 3.1 + i * 1.9)
				sparkles[i].TextTransparency = 1 - k
				sparkles[i].TextSize = 14 + 14 * k
			end

			-- Band 4's rainbow. There is no card or border in a world reveal for a
			-- cycling colour to live on, so the rarity label carries it -- the same
			-- one-property technique RarityFX uses on Secret/God tiles.
			if band == 4 then
				rarityLabel.TextColor3 = Color3.fromHSV((t * 0.3) % 1, 0.82, 1)
			end
		end)

		live = rec

		-- hold, fade out, tear down
		task.delay(FADE + effective.hold, function()
			if rec.dead or rec.token ~= token then return end
			for _, f in ipairs(fades) do
				local back = (f[2] == "ImageTransparency" or f[2] == "TextTransparency"
					or f[2] == "Transparency" or f[2] == "BackgroundTransparency") and 1 or 0
				TweenService:Create(f[1], TweenInfo.new(FADE), { [f[2]] = back }):Play()
			end
			task.delay(FADE, function()
				if rec.token == token then teardown(rec) end
			end)
		end)
	end)

	if not ok then
		warn(("[CatchReveal] M.play failed while building the reveal -- tearing down: %s"):format(tostring(err)))
		teardown(rec)
		return nil
	end

	return {
		skip = function()
			teardown(rec)
		end,
	}
end

return M


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/DialogueConfig.lua =====
-- DialogueConfig: what the world's NPCs say.
--
-- Keyed by the NpcId attribute on the character model, so an NPC can be moved, renamed
-- or rebuilt without touching its lines. Lines is an ordered list -- talking to someone
-- again advances through it and then holds on the last entry, which is what lets a quest
-- later swap in a different list per stage without changing any of the display code.
--
-- Shared so the client can render a line the instant the server names it, rather than
-- shipping the text over the wire on every interaction.

local DialogueConfig = {}

DialogueConfig.NPCS = {
	Gianluca = {
		Name = "stupid gianluca",
		PromptAction = "Talk",
		-- how long the speech bubble and the on-screen box stay up
		Hold = 5.0,
		Colour = Color3.fromRGB(255, 186, 92),
		Lines = {
			"AAARGGGHHH!!! I CANT FIND MY CHIM!!!",
		},
	},
}

function DialogueConfig.Get(npcId)
	return DialogueConfig.NPCS[npcId]
end

-- index is 1-based and clamps to the last line, so repeat interactions never error and
-- never wrap back to the start
function DialogueConfig.LineAt(npcId, index)
	local e = DialogueConfig.NPCS[npcId]
	if not e or #e.Lines == 0 then return nil end
	return e.Lines[math.clamp(index or 1, 1, #e.Lines)]
end

return DialogueConfig


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/EggConfig.lua =====
-- EggConfig — single source of truth for eggs. The server ROLLS from these
-- tables and the client DISPLAYS them, so shown odds can never drift from
-- real odds (Roblox requires published odds for paid random items).
-- Eggs hatch PETS (EggHandler grants into data.Pets, never onto a plot), so the
-- roll tables name pets and Validate checks them against PetConfig. Until
-- 2026-08-01 they named the ten forest BRAINROTS that were doubling as pets
-- before the real pet art existed, and this required BrainrotConfig instead.
local PetConfig = require(script.Parent.PetConfig)

local M = {}

M.WORLDS = {
	Forest = {
		Active = true,
		DisplayName = "Forest",
		-- Each egg overlaps the next by one or two pets, so spending up never
		-- makes the previous egg's best result unobtainable and every tier has a
		-- cheap-but-unlikely route as well as an expensive-but-likely one.
		-- Weights are per-egg percentages; Validate asserts each row sums to 100.
		Eggs = {
			{ Id = "ForestShard",  Name = "Shard Egg",  Price = 60,  Model = "ForestEgg1",
			  Table = { { "Moss Larva", 45 }, { "Pebble Snout", 33 }, { "Leaf Frog", 22 } } },
			{ Id = "ForestDrip",   Name = "Drip Egg",   Price = 85,  Model = "ForestEgg2",
			  Table = { { "Leaf Frog", 30 }, { "Reed Duck", 34 }, { "Toad Pup", 26 }, { "Acornel", 10 } } },
			{ Id = "ForestHorned", Name = "Horned Egg", Price = 115, Model = "ForestEgg3",
			  Table = { { "Toad Pup", 26 }, { "Acornel", 30 }, { "Sap Snail", 24 }, { "Bramble Bear", 20 } } },
			{ Id = "ForestRune",   Name = "Rune Egg",   Price = 160, Model = "ForestEgg4",
			  Table = { { "Bramble Bear", 28 }, { "Mossback", 30 }, { "Glow Moth", 22 }, { "Hollow Owl", 14 }, { "Vine Coil", 6 } } },
			{ Id = "ForestCrown",  Name = "Crown Egg",  Price = 220, Model = "ForestEgg5",
			  Table = { { "Hollow Owl", 26 }, { "Vine Coil", 26 }, { "Spirit Fawn", 22 }, { "Elder Stag", 20 }, { "Heartwood Guardian", 6 } } },
		},
	},
}

function M.GetWorld(worldId) return M.WORLDS[worldId] end

function M.GetEgg(worldId, eggId)
	local w = M.WORLDS[worldId]
	if not w then return nil end
	for _, egg in ipairs(w.Eggs) do
		if egg.Id == eggId then return egg, w end
	end
	return nil
end

-- Boot-time assert (EggHandler.Init calls it) -- a typo'd pet name must fail
-- loudly at server start, not silently refund a player mid-purchase.
function M.Validate()
	for _, w in pairs(M.WORLDS) do
		for _, egg in ipairs(w.Eggs) do
			local sum = 0
			for _, row in ipairs(egg.Table) do
				assert(PetConfig.IdFor(row[1]), egg.Id .. " references unknown pet: " .. tostring(row[1]))
				sum += row[2]
			end
			assert(sum == 100, egg.Id .. " weights sum to " .. sum .. ", want 100")
		end
	end
	return true
end

-- Every pet that is actually obtainable, for the shop's "where does this drop"
-- copy and for tests that assert the roster and the tables have not drifted.
function M.ObtainablePetIds()
	local ids = {}
	for _, w in pairs(M.WORLDS) do
		for _, egg in ipairs(w.Eggs) do
			for _, row in ipairs(egg.Table) do
				local id = PetConfig.IdFor(row[1])
				if id then ids[id] = true end
			end
		end
	end
	return ids
end

return M

===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/GamepassConfig.lua =====
-- ============================================================================
-- GamepassConfig -- Robux gamepasses (monetization). SHARED so a future shop UI
-- can read names / icons / prices straight from here.
--
-- NOTHING here is surfaced in-game yet: no shop UI, and no purchase prompt fires
-- on its own. This is just the catalog + effect definitions that the server's
-- GamepassService reads.
--
-- >>> TO ACTIVATE A PASS <<<
--   1. Create the pass on the Creator Dashboard:
--        Creations > (this game) > Monetization > Passes > Create a Pass
--   2. Copy its Pass ID.
--   3. Paste it as GamepassId below (replacing the 0).
--   GamepassId == 0 means "not created yet": GamepassService skips the pass
--   entirely (never calls UserOwnsGamePassAsync with a bogus id, never grants its
--   effect) -- same convention as PetConfig.PET_SLOTS_GAMEPASS_ID.
--
-- Effects (read by GamepassService):
--   numbers  -> multipliers, STACKED (product) across all owned passes:
--               CashMult, LuckMult, PowerMult, ChargeMult
--   booleans -> feature flags: AutoCollect, VIP
-- Wiring effects into gameplay is a later step: GamepassService exposes
-- CashMult(player) / LuckMult(player) / HasFlag(player, flag) etc., ready to fold
-- into IncomeLoop / ThrowHandler (which already have LuckMult/IncomeMult seams).
-- ============================================================================
local M = {}

M.List = {
	{ Key = "Cash2x",      GamepassId = 0, Name = "2x Cash",      Icon = "\u{1F4B0}", Desc = "Double all brainrot income",          RobuxPrice = 199, Effects = { CashMult = 2 } },
	{ Key = "Luck2x",      GamepassId = 0, Name = "2x Luck",      Icon = "\u{1F340}", Desc = "Double your rarity luck on throws",    RobuxPrice = 249, Effects = { LuckMult = 2 } },
	{ Key = "SuperArm",    GamepassId = 0, Name = "Super Arm",    Icon = "\u{1F4AA}", Desc = "Skip rocks much farther",             RobuxPrice = 149, Effects = { PowerMult = 2 } },
	{ Key = "FastCharge",  GamepassId = 0, Name = "Fast Charge",  Icon = "\u{26A1}",  Desc = "Charge your throw meter faster",      RobuxPrice = 99,  Effects = { ChargeMult = 1.75 } },
	{ Key = "AutoCollect", GamepassId = 0, Name = "Auto Collect", Icon = "\u{1F9F2}", Desc = "Automatically collect brainrot cash", RobuxPrice = 299, Effects = { AutoCollect = true } },
	{ Key = "VIP",         GamepassId = 0, Name = "VIP",          Icon = "\u{2B50}",  Desc = "1.5x cash & luck, plus a VIP tag",    RobuxPrice = 499, Effects = { CashMult = 1.5, LuckMult = 1.5, VIP = true } },
}

M.ByKey = {}
for _, g in ipairs(M.List) do M.ByKey[g.Key] = g end

-- id -> config (ids are 0 until you fill them in above)
function M.ByGamepassId(id)
