===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/IconForge.lua =====
-- IconForge: Pet-Sim-quality UI icons WITHOUT uploaded assets. Each icon is a
-- tiny primitive MODEL rendered in static ViewportFrames -- which is how Pet
-- Sim's own icons are made (they are 3D renders). Three stacked viewports per
-- icon, all showing clones of the same model:
--   Outline -- ImageColor3 = ink, camera pulled ~10% closer, so the render is a
--             slightly LARGER black silhouette: the chunky cartoon outline.
--   Icon    -- the real render, bright ambient so colours stay candy.
-- No animation anywhere: cameras are fixed, models are anchored. (The rail's
-- old 3D icons were removed for their idle sway, not for being 3D.)

local UITheme = require(script.Parent.UITheme)
local CF = UITheme.Camp

local M = {}

local V = Vector3.new
local RAD = math.rad

--============================= part helpers ================================--
local function P(model, class, size, cf, color, material)
	local part
	if class == "Wedge" then
		part = Instance.new("WedgePart")
	else
		part = Instance.new("Part")
		part.Shape = Enum.PartType[class]
	end
	part.Size = size
	part.CFrame = cf
	part.Color = color
	part.Material = material or Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic
	part.Anchored = true
	part.CanCollide = false
	part.CastShadow = false
	part.TopSurface = Enum.SurfaceType.Smooth
	part.BottomSurface = Enum.SurfaceType.Smooth
	part.Parent = model
	return part
end

-- cylinders lie along X natively; stand them up (Y) or face the camera (Z)
local AXIS = {
	X = CFrame.new(),
	Y = CFrame.Angles(0, 0, RAD(90)),
	Z = CFrame.Angles(0, RAD(90), 0),
}
local function Cyl(model, dia, len, cf, axis, color, material)
	return P(model, "Cylinder", V(len, dia, dia), cf * AXIS[axis], color, material)
end

--=============================== palettes ==================================--
local RED1 = Color3.fromRGB(232, 64, 78)
local RED2 = Color3.fromRGB(196, 44, 58)
local GOLD1 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 199, 44)
local GOLD2 = Color3.fromRGB(226, 158, 22)
local CREAM = Color3.fromRGB(248, 240, 218)
local PAGE = Color3.fromRGB(236, 224, 196)
local TEAL1 = Color3.fromRGB(38, 166, 154)
local TEAL2 = Color3.fromRGB(24, 122, 112)
local WHITE = Color3.fromRGB(245, 245, 245)
local PINE1 = Color3.fromRGB(84, 168, 92)
local PINE2 = Color3.fromRGB(52, 122, 62)
local STONE1 = Color3.fromRGB(148, 160, 172)

--============================ icon model kit ===============================--
-- Every builder returns a Model centred near the origin, FACING +Z (the
-- camera side), roughly 2.2 studs across. Chunky beats detailed: these render
-- at ~64px, so every feature must survive that.
local BUILDERS = {}

BUILDERS.gift = function(model)
	-- box + slightly wider lid + ribbon cross + three-ball bow
	P(model, "Block", V(1.55, 1.15, 1.15), CFrame.new(0, -0.25, 0), RED1)
	P(model, "Block", V(1.8, 0.42, 1.4), CFrame.new(0, 0.42, 0), RED2)
	P(model, "Block", V(0.34, 1.16, 1.17), CFrame.new(0, -0.25, 0.01), GOLD1)  -- front/back ribbon
	P(model, "Block", V(0.36, 0.44, 1.42), CFrame.new(0, 0.42, 0), GOLD2)      -- ribbon over lid
	P(model, "Ball", V(0.42, 0.42, 0.42), CFrame.new(-0.22, 0.75, 0), GOLD1)
	P(model, "Ball", V(0.42, 0.42, 0.42), CFrame.new(0.22, 0.75, 0), GOLD1)
	P(model, "Ball", V(0.3, 0.3, 0.3), CFrame.new(0, 0.82, 0), GOLD2)
end

BUILDERS.target = function(model)
	-- three rings + gold bull + arrow at a jaunty angle
	Cyl(model, 2.15, 0.22, CFrame.new(0, 0, -0.15), "Z", RED1)
	Cyl(model, 1.5, 0.26, CFrame.new(0, 0, -0.1), "Z", WHITE)
	Cyl(model, 0.85, 0.3, CFrame.new(0, 0, -0.05), "Z", RED2)
	P(model, "Ball", V(0.34, 0.34, 0.34), CFrame.new(0, 0, 0.1), GOLD1)
	local shaft = CFrame.new(0.42, 0.42, 0.42) * CFrame.Angles(RAD(-38), RAD(40), 0)
	Cyl(model, 0.11, 1.5, shaft, "Z", CREAM)
	P(model, "Wedge", V(0.1, 0.34, 0.42), shaft * CFrame.new(0, 0.1, 0.72) * CFrame.Angles(RAD(180), 0, 0), RED2)
	P(model, "Wedge", V(0.1, 0.34, 0.42), shaft * CFrame.new(0, -0.1, 0.72) * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, 0), RED2)
end

BUILDERS.star = function(model)
	-- A REAL five-point star: each point is two mirrored wedges forming an
	-- isoceles triangle, planted around a pentagon-ish core. (The first version
	-- was three crossed bars, which renders as a gear/flower, not a star.)
	-- Wedge geometry: a WedgePart's triangular profile lives in its LOCAL YZ
	-- plane (tall edge at -Z, sloping to zero height at +Z), extruded along X.
	-- Rotating +-90 about Y swings that profile into the SCREEN plane and makes
	-- the extrusion the thickness. Two mirrored halves share the tall edge at
	-- x=0, so together they read as one isoceles point. (Rotating about X
	-- instead -- the first attempt -- leaves the profile edge-on: blocky rays.)
	local CORE_R, PH, PW = 0.5, 0.92, 0.62
	for i = 0, 4 do
		local spin = CFrame.Angles(0, 0, RAD(72 * i))
		local center = spin * CFrame.new(0, CORE_R + PH / 2, 0)
		P(model, "Wedge", V(0.3, PH, PW), center * CFrame.new(PW / 2, 0, 0) * CFrame.Angles(0, RAD(90), 0), GOLD1)
		P(model, "Wedge", V(0.3, PH, PW), center * CFrame.new(-PW / 2, 0, 0) * CFrame.Angles(0, RAD(-90), 0), GOLD1)
	end
	Cyl(model, CORE_R * 2.15, 0.3, CFrame.new(0, 0, 0), "Z", GOLD1)
	Cyl(model, CORE_R * 1.5, 0.36, CFrame.new(0, 0, 0.05), "Z", GOLD2)
	P(model, "Ball", V(0.26, 0.26, 0.26), CFrame.new(-0.16, 0.18, 0.2), CREAM)   -- gloss dot
end

BUILDERS.book = function(model)
	-- Open book seen from the FRONT-ABOVE: the pages must present their broad
	-- face to the camera or the whole icon collapses to a sliver. Two page
	-- slabs tilted like an open V, teal covers underneath, spine down the middle.
	local L = CFrame.new(-0.62, 0, -0.02) * CFrame.Angles(RAD(-64), 0, RAD(13))
	local R = CFrame.new(0.62, 0, -0.02) * CFrame.Angles(RAD(-64), 0, RAD(-13))
	P(model, "Block", V(1.32, 1.5, 0.16), L * CFrame.new(0, -0.06, -0.14), TEAL2)   -- covers
	P(model, "Block", V(1.32, 1.5, 0.16), R * CFrame.new(0, -0.06, -0.14), TEAL2)
	P(model, "Block", V(1.22, 1.4, 0.14), L, PAGE)                                  -- page block
	P(model, "Block", V(1.22, 1.4, 0.14), R, PAGE)
	P(model, "Block", V(1.14, 1.3, 0.06), L * CFrame.new(0, 0.02, 0.1), CREAM)      -- top sheet
	P(model, "Block", V(1.14, 1.3, 0.06), R * CFrame.new(0, 0.02, 0.1), CREAM)
	for i = 1, 3 do                                                                 -- text lines
		local y = 0.34 - (i - 1) * 0.3
		P(model, "Block", V(0.72, 0.09, 0.04), L * CFrame.new(-0.04, y, 0.15), TEAL1)
		P(model, "Block", V(0.72, 0.09, 0.04), R * CFrame.new(0.04, y, 0.15), TEAL1)
	end
	P(model, "Block", V(0.2, 1.52, 0.44), CFrame.new(0, -0.1, -0.3) * CFrame.Angles(RAD(-64), 0, 0), TEAL1)  -- spine
end

BUILDERS.trophy = function(model)
	-- cup + flared rim + bowl bottom + stem + two-step base + curled handles
	Cyl(model, 1.1, 0.85, CFrame.new(0, 0.42, 0), "Y", GOLD1)
	Cyl(model, 1.3, 0.16, CFrame.new(0, 0.9, 0), "Y", GOLD2)
	P(model, "Ball", V(1.08, 0.72, 1.08), CFrame.new(0, -0.05, 0), GOLD1)
	Cyl(model, 0.26, 0.5, CFrame.new(0, -0.55, 0), "Y", GOLD2)
	P(model, "Block", V(0.85, 0.2, 0.6), CFrame.new(0, -0.88, 0), GOLD2)
	P(model, "Block", V(1.15, 0.18, 0.8), CFrame.new(0, -1.06, 0), RED2)        -- plinth
	for _, s in ipairs({ -1, 1 }) do
		Cyl(model, 0.15, 0.75, CFrame.new(s * 0.78, 0.45, 0) * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, RAD(-s * 28)), "Y", GOLD2)
		P(model, "Ball", V(0.24, 0.24, 0.24), CFrame.new(s * 0.62, 0.06, 0), GOLD2)
	end
	P(model, "Ball", V(0.3, 0.3, 0.3), CFrame.new(-0.28, 0.55, 0.45), CREAM)    -- gloss dot
end

-- Triangle helper: an isoceles point of height h and base width w, centred on
-- `cf`, standing in the SCREEN plane. Two mirrored wedges sharing their tall
-- edge -- see the note in BUILDERS.star for why the +-90 Y rotation matters.
local function triangle(model, cf, h, w, thick, color)
	P(model, "Wedge", V(thick, h, w / 2), cf * CFrame.new(w / 4, 0, 0) * CFrame.Angles(0, RAD(90), 0), color)
	P(model, "Wedge", V(thick, h, w / 2), cf * CFrame.new(-w / 4, 0, 0) * CFrame.Angles(0, RAD(-90), 0), color)
end

BUILDERS.tent = function(model)
	-- plot: a pine A-frame tent -- big triangle, dark doorway triangle, ground bar
	triangle(model, CFrame.new(0, 0.12, 0), 1.75, 2.05, 0.85, PINE1)
	triangle(model, CFrame.new(0, 0.02, 0.45), 1.35, 1.5, 0.12, PINE2)   -- shaded face
	triangle(model, CFrame.new(0, -0.24, 0.55), 0.85, 0.62, 0.1, CF.ink) -- doorway
	P(model, "Block", V(2.35, 0.2, 1.0), CFrame.new(0, -0.86, 0), PINE2) -- ground
	P(model, "Ball", V(0.16, 0.16, 0.16), CFrame.new(0, 1.05, 0), GOLD1) -- pole finial
end

BUILDERS.bag = function(model)
	-- shops: candy shopping bag, fold-over top, twin handle ARCS, big gold coin.
	-- Handles are three short segments each -- a single straight cylinder read as
	-- a stick and vanished at icon size.
	P(model, "Block", V(1.45, 1.5, 0.85), CFrame.new(0, -0.2, 0), TEAL1)
	P(model, "Block", V(1.56, 0.36, 0.92), CFrame.new(0, 0.63, 0), TEAL2)
	for _, s in ipairs({ -1, 1 }) do
		local hx = s * 0.36
		Cyl(model, 0.13, 0.42, CFrame.new(hx, 0.95, 0) * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, RAD(-s * 34)), "Y", GOLD2)
		Cyl(model, 0.13, 0.34, CFrame.new(s * 0.19, 1.16, 0) * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, RAD(-s * 68)), "Y", GOLD2)
		P(model, "Ball", V(0.14, 0.14, 0.14), CFrame.new(hx, 0.78, 0), GOLD2)
	end
	Cyl(model, 0.72, 0.14, CFrame.new(0.02, -0.24, 0.5), "Z", GOLD1)             -- coin face
	Cyl(model, 0.46, 0.16, CFrame.new(0.02, -0.24, 0.53), "Z", GOLD2)            -- coin inset
end

BUILDERS.stone = function(model)
	-- skip: the stone skipping OFF water -- the splash rings are what make it
	-- read as "skip" rather than "a rock". Stone up-left, three shrinking rings
	-- trailing down-right along the bounce path.
	local LAKE = Color3.fromRGB(86, 176, 214)
	P(model, "Ball", V(1.15, 0.42, 0.95), CFrame.new(-0.32, 0.62, 0) * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, RAD(-16)), STONE1)
	P(model, "Ball", V(0.38, 0.12, 0.3), CFrame.new(-0.45, 0.78, 0.3), WHITE)    -- sheen
	local rings = { { 0.15, -0.28, 1.15 }, { 0.72, -0.6, 0.85 }, { 1.2, -0.85, 0.58 } }
	for _, r in ipairs(rings) do
		Cyl(model, r[3], 0.14, CFrame.new(r[1], r[2], 0) * CFrame.Angles(RAD(74), 0, 0), "Y", LAKE)
		Cyl(model, r[3] * 0.6, 0.16, CFrame.new(r[1], r[2] + 0.02, 0) * CFrame.Angles(RAD(74), 0, 0), "Y", Color3.fromRGB(140, 208, 236))
	end
end

--=============================== mounting ==================================--
-- Camera direction is fixed (three-quarter view from upper right); the DISTANCE
-- is fitted per icon from its real bounding box, so a tall trophy and a wide
-- gift both fill the frame instead of one cropping and the other floating in
-- space. Hand-tuned distances were exactly the bug that cropped the gift.
local CAM_DIR = V(0.42, 0.62, 3).Unit
local FOV = 32
local FIT = 1.28   -- >1 leaves breathing room so the outline pass cannot clip

local function fitDistance(model)
	local _, size = model:GetBoundingBox()
	local radius = math.max(size.X, size.Y, size.Z) * 0.5
	return (radius * FIT) / math.tan(RAD(FOV) * 0.5)
end

local function makeViewport(parent, model, zindex, dist)
	local vp = Instance.new("ViewportFrame")
	vp.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	vp.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	vp.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
	vp.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)
	vp.ZIndex = zindex
	vp.Ambient = Color3.fromRGB(205, 205, 205)
	vp.LightColor = Color3.fromRGB(255, 252, 240)
	vp.LightDirection = V(-0.35, -0.7, -0.45)
	vp.Parent = parent
	local m = model:Clone()
	m.Parent = vp
	local center = model:GetBoundingBox()
	local cam = Instance.new("Camera")
	cam.FieldOfView = FOV
	cam.CFrame = CFrame.lookAt(center.Position + CAM_DIR * dist, center.Position)
	cam.Parent = vp
	vp.CurrentCamera = cam
	return vp
end

-- Mount a finished icon into `parent` (an empty square Frame/button). Returns
-- the holder so callers can scale or hide the whole stack as one thing.
function M.Mount(parent, kind)
	local build = BUILDERS[kind]
	if not build then
		warn("[IconForge] unknown icon kind " .. tostring(kind))
		build = BUILDERS.star
	end
	local model = Instance.new("Model")
	build(model)

	local holder = Instance.new("Frame")
	holder.Name = "ForgedIcon"
	holder.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	holder.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
	holder.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)
	holder.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1.16, 1.16)
	holder.ZIndex = parent.ZIndex or 1
	holder.Parent = parent

	local z = holder.ZIndex
	local dist = fitDistance(model)
	-- (drop shadow removed: on a white sticker card the glyph's own shadow
	-- read as smudge rather than depth. The ink outline below still gives the
	-- silhouette its definition.)
	-- chunky outline: the same render pulled 12% closer, pure ink, so a black
	-- silhouette peeks out evenly around the icon on top of it
	local outline = makeViewport(holder, model, z + 2, dist / 1.12)
	outline.ImageColor3 = CF.ink
	-- the icon itself
	makeViewport(holder, model, z + 3, dist)

	model:Destroy()   -- clones live in the viewports; the master is scaffolding
	return holder
end

return M


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/MassiveEmergence.lua =====
-- MassiveEmergence: the cutscene a SIZE-mutated catch earns.
--
-- Storyboard beats B1-B3 from the approved Catch Ceremony plan, which were designed but
-- never built ("silhouette-in-pillar rise, camera work"). A Huge or Massive is rare enough
-- to deserve the takeover the plan always wanted:
--
--   B1 ANTICIPATION  camera cuts to the water where the stone broke the surface; the lake
--                    glows in the tier colour before anything appears (the Genshin tell)
--   B2 ERUPTION      geyser + ring, screen shake, bass hit
--   B3 THE RISE      the ACTUAL creature rises out of the water as a black silhouette,
--                    turning slowly, then the colours snap on at full height
--
-- It runs IN FRONT of PullCeremony and hands back cleanly, so the existing takeover /
-- odds-climb / stamp all still play afterwards and nothing about them had to change.
--
-- WHY THE REAL MODEL AND NOT A STAND-IN: these are Parts, so a clone costs nothing to
-- silhouette (Color black, then tween back). A ViewportFrame would have been cheaper still
-- but it cannot sit IN the world, and the whole point is that the thing comes out of the
-- actual lake the player just threw into.
--
-- FAILS SOFT EVERYWHERE. No SplashPos, no model, no camera -> return false and the caller
-- carries on to the ordinary reveal. A cutscene must never eat a catch.

local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")
local Debris = game:GetService("Debris")

local Sizes = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.SizeConfig)
local okKit, SoundKit = pcall(function() return require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.SoundKit) end)
if not okKit then SoundKit = nil end

local M = {}

-- Per-size drama. Huge gets a brisk version; Massive gets the full hold.
local BEATS = {
	Huge    = { anticipate = 0.55, erupt = 0.30, rise = 1.10, hold = 0.45, shake = 2.0 },
	Massive = { anticipate = 0.90, erupt = 0.40, rise = 1.90, hold = 0.90, shake = 4.0 },
}

local RISE_EASE = TweenInfo.new(1, Enum.EasingStyle.Quint, Enum.EasingDirection.Out)

local function playSound(name, vol)
	if SoundKit then pcall(SoundKit.play, name, nil, { volume = vol }) end
end

-- a flat expanding ring on the water surface
local function ring(parent, pos, colour, size, life)
	local p = Instance.new("Part")
	p.Anchored = true; p.CanCollide = false; p.CanQuery = false; p.CanTouch = false
	p.Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder
	p.Size = Vector3.new(0.4, 2, 2)
	p.CFrame = CFrame.new(pos) * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, math.rad(90))
	p.Color = colour; p.Material = Enum.Material.Neon
	-- starts already half-faded and dies to nothing: a cylinder is a FILLED disc, so a
	-- solid one reads as a pink pancake on the lake rather than a shockwave ring
	p.Transparency = 0.55
	p.Parent = parent
	TweenService:Create(p, TweenInfo.new(life, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), {
		Size = Vector3.new(0.4, size, size),
		Transparency = 1,
	}):Play()
	Debris:AddItem(p, life + 0.1)
	return p
end

-- the column of light the creature rises inside
local function pillar(parent, pos, colour, height, radius)
	local p = Instance.new("Part")
	p.Anchored = true; p.CanCollide = false; p.CanQuery = false; p.CanTouch = false
	p.Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder
	p.Size = Vector3.new(height, radius, radius)
	p.CFrame = CFrame.new(pos + Vector3.new(0, height / 2, 0)) * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, math.rad(90))
	p.Color = colour; p.Material = Enum.Material.Neon
	p.Transparency = 1
	p.Parent = parent
	return p
end

-- Plays the cutscene. Returns true if it actually ran, false if it declined -- the caller
-- uses that to decide whether to add its own delay before the ordinary reveal.
function M.play(result)
	local size = result and result.Size
	local beats = size and BEATS[size]
	if not beats then return false end

	local splash = result.SplashPos
	if typeof(splash) ~= "Vector3" then return false end

	local template = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("BrainrotModels")
	template = template and template:FindFirstChild(result.Name)
	if not template then return false end

	local cam = Workspace.CurrentCamera
	if not cam then return false end

	local colour = result.RarityColor or Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255)
	local sizeColour = Sizes.Color(size) or colour

	local stage = Instance.new("Folder")
	stage.Name = "MassiveEmergenceStage"
	stage.Parent = Workspace

	-- Build the creature at the size it will actually be, sunk under the surface.
	local model = template:Clone()
	local _, extents = model:GetBoundingBox()
	local hs = math.clamp(template:GetAttribute("HeightScale") or 1, 0.7, 1.5)
	local width = math.max(extents.X, extents.Z)
	local fit = math.min((6.0 * hs) / extents.Y, 9.5 / math.max(width, 0.01)) * Sizes.Scale(size)
	model:ScaleTo(model:GetScale() * fit)
	local _, finalSize = model:GetBoundingBox()

	-- silhouette: remember every colour, then black everything out
	local originalColour = {}
	for _, d in ipairs(model:GetDescendants()) do
		if d:IsA("BasePart") then
			d.Anchored = true; d.CanCollide = false; d.CanQuery = false; d.CanTouch = false
			originalColour[d] = d.Color
			d.Color = Color3.fromRGB(6, 8, 12)
		end
	end
	model.Parent = stage

	local below = splash - Vector3.new(0, finalSize.Y * 1.05, 0)
	local above = splash + Vector3.new(0, finalSize.Y * 0.5 - finalSize.Y * 0.08, 0)
	local function placeAt(pos, yaw)
		local cf, _ = model:GetBoundingBox()
		model:PivotTo(model:GetPivot() * CFrame.Angles(0, yaw, 0) + (pos - cf.Position))
	end
	placeAt(below, 0)

	-- === B1 ANTICIPATION: cut to the water, glow the tier colour before anything shows ===
	-- NEVER hand back Scriptable (2026-08-09). ClientMain's stone-tracking camera holds
	-- CameraType = Scriptable from flight start until landing + 1.4s -- i.e. straight
	-- through the moment this cutscene starts on a real catch. Saving that and restoring
	-- it at the end parks the player in a frozen camera out at the landing point,
	-- permanently, because the tracking camera's own restore already fired mid-cutscene.
	-- Measured on a real forced-Huge throw: camera stranded Scriptable 884 studs away.
	-- The same reveal fabricated with no tracking camera restored fine, which is what
	-- isolated it. Custom is the only correct terminal state: this cutscene always ends
	-- by giving the player their camera back.
	-- ACCEPTED TRADE (parked): if a SECOND Massive's emergence fallback fires while a
	-- Sequencer cut is already running, this forces Custom at the end and cuts the
	-- running cut's last ~6s short. Needs two Massives inside 10.7s, and the terminal
	-- state stays recoverable -- strictly better than the frozen camera it prevents.
	local prevType, prevCF = cam.CameraType, cam.CFrame
	if prevType == Enum.CameraType.Scriptable then
		prevType = Enum.CameraType.Custom
	end
	cam.CameraType = Enum.CameraType.Scriptable
	-- Framed so the creature FILLS the shot. The first cut sat 1.9x its width away and it
	-- read as a small thing in a big lake -- the opposite of the intent.
	local viewDist = math.max(finalSize.X, finalSize.Z) * 1.15 + 10
	local eye = splash + Vector3.new(viewDist * 0.72, finalSize.Y * 0.42 + 4, viewDist * 0.72)
	cam.CFrame = CFrame.lookAt(eye, splash + Vector3.new(0, finalSize.Y * 0.34, 0))

	-- The pillar FRAMES the creature, it must not paint over it. A wide Neon cylinder at
	-- 0.82 washed the whole model in tier colour and buried the silhouette, so it is now
	-- narrower than the body and nearly clear -- read as a shaft of light behind it.
	local glow = pillar(stage, splash, colour, finalSize.Y * 2.2, math.max(finalSize.X, finalSize.Z) * 0.42)
	TweenService:Create(glow, TweenInfo.new(beats.anticipate), { Transparency = 0.93 }):Play()
	ring(stage, splash, colour, math.max(finalSize.X, finalSize.Z) * 1.6, beats.anticipate + 0.2)
	playSound("catchDrama", 0.5)
	task.wait(beats.anticipate)

	-- === B2 ERUPTION: geyser, rings, shake, bass ===
	playSound("catchBigHit", 0.75)
	for i = 1, 3 do
		ring(stage, splash, i % 2 == 0 and sizeColour or colour,
			math.max(finalSize.X, finalSize.Z) * (1.8 + i * 0.9), beats.erupt + 0.5 + i * 0.12)
	end
	local shakeUntil = os.clock() + beats.erupt + beats.rise * 0.5
	local shakeConn
	shakeConn = RunService.RenderStepped:Connect(function()
		if os.clock() > shakeUntil then shakeConn:Disconnect() return end
		local k = beats.shake * 0.06
		cam.CFrame = cam.CFrame * CFrame.new((math.random() - 0.5) * k, (math.random() - 0.5) * k, 0)
	end)
	task.wait(beats.erupt)

	-- === B3 THE RISE: the creature comes out of the water, turning ===
	local t0 = os.clock()
	local riseConn
	riseConn = RunService.RenderStepped:Connect(function()
		local a = math.clamp((os.clock() - t0) / beats.rise, 0, 1)
		-- quint-out: bursts up, then settles
		local e = 1 - (1 - a) ^ 5
		placeAt(below:Lerp(above, e), a * math.pi * 1.25)
		if a >= 1 then riseConn:Disconnect() end
	end)
	task.wait(beats.rise)
	if riseConn.Connected then riseConn:Disconnect() end

	-- colours snap on at full height -- the moment it stops being a shape and becomes a thing
	playSound("catchBigHit", 0.55)
	for part, c in pairs(originalColour) do
		if part.Parent then
			TweenService:Create(part, TweenInfo.new(0.22), { Color = c }):Play()
		end
	end
	TweenService:Create(glow, TweenInfo.new(beats.hold), { Transparency = 1 }):Play()
	task.wait(beats.hold)

	-- hand the camera back exactly as found, then let the ordinary reveal run
	if shakeConn.Connected then shakeConn:Disconnect() end
	cam.CameraType = prevType
	cam.CFrame = prevCF
	stage:Destroy()
	return true
end

return M

===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/MerchantDialog.lua =====
-- MerchantDialog: a small NPC dialogue box shown when you press E at a merchant,
-- right before the shop opens. Reusable across clients.
--   MerchantDialog.Show(npcName, lines, accent, onDone)
-- advances through `lines`; on the last line the button opens the shop by calling
-- onDone(). onDone is dropped if the player LEAVEs or walks away (Hide()).
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local UITheme = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.UITheme)
local CF = UITheme.Camp
local FONT = UITheme.Font
local BODY = Enum.Font.GothamMedium
local player = Players.LocalPlayer

local M = {}
local gui, box, namePlate, nameText, lineText, contBtn, contText
local lines, idx, onDone, anchorPart, finalLabel

local function build()
	if gui and gui.Parent then return end
	gui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
	gui.Name = "MerchantDialogUI"
	gui.ResetOnSpawn = false
	gui.DisplayOrder = 12
	gui.IgnoreGuiInset = true
	gui.Parent = player:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")

	box = Instance.new("Frame")
	box.Name = "DialogBox"
	box.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 1)
	box.Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 1, -150)
	box.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(560, 132)
	box.Visible = false
	box.ZIndex = 10
	box.Parent = gui
	UITheme.campPanel(box)

	-- accent name plate (overhangs the top-left). A UIGradient on the plate does
	-- NOT tint a CHILD label, so the name text stays clean cream.
	namePlate = Instance.new("Frame")
	namePlate.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0, 1)
	namePlate.Position = UDim2.new(0, 20, 0, 14)
	namePlate.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(250, 34)
	namePlate.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255)
	namePlate.BorderSizePixel = 0
	namePlate.ZIndex = 13
	namePlate.Parent = box
	UITheme.corner(namePlate, 9)
	UITheme.ink(namePlate, 3)
	nameText = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	nameText.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	nameText.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	nameText.Font = FONT
	nameText.TextSize = 17
	nameText.TextColor3 = CF.cream
	nameText.ZIndex = 14
	nameText.Parent = namePlate
	UITheme.inkText(nameText, 2.4)

	lineText = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	lineText.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0)
	lineText.Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0, 40)
	lineText.Size = UDim2.new(1, -44, 0, 42)
	lineText.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	lineText.Font = BODY
	lineText.TextSize = 17
	lineText.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255)
	lineText.TextWrapped = true
	lineText.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left
	lineText.TextYAlignment = Enum.TextYAlignment.Top
	lineText.ZIndex = 13
	lineText.Parent = box
	UITheme.inkText(lineText, 1.6)

	contBtn = Instance.new("TextButton")
	contBtn.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(1, 1)
	contBtn.Position = UDim2.new(1, -16, 1, -12)
	contBtn.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(190, 40)
	contBtn.Text = ""
	contBtn.ZIndex = 13
	contBtn.Parent = box
	UITheme.campButton(contBtn, CF.pine1, CF.pine2)
	contText = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	contText.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	contText.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	contText.Font = FONT
	contText.TextSize = 16
	contText.TextColor3 = CF.cream
	contText.ZIndex = 15
	contText.Parent = contBtn
	UITheme.inkText(contText, 2.2)

	local leaveBtn = Instance.new("TextButton")
	leaveBtn.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0, 1)
	leaveBtn.Position = UDim2.new(0, 16, 1, -12)
	leaveBtn.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(120, 40)
	leaveBtn.Text = ""
	leaveBtn.ZIndex = 13
	leaveBtn.Parent = box
	UITheme.campButton(leaveBtn, CF.panelTop, CF.panelBot)
	local leaveText = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	leaveText.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	leaveText.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	leaveText.Font = FONT
	leaveText.TextSize = 15
	leaveText.TextColor3 = CF.muted
	leaveText.Text = "LEAVE"
	leaveText.ZIndex = 15
	leaveText.Parent = leaveBtn
	UITheme.inkText(leaveText, 2)
	leaveBtn.Activated:Connect(function() M.Hide() end)

	-- walk away from the merchant -> dismiss the dialogue
	RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function()
		if not (box and box.Visible and anchorPart) then return end
		local char = player.Character
		local hrp = char and char:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
		if hrp and (hrp.Position - anchorPart.Position).Magnitude > 24 then M.Hide() end
	end)

	contBtn.Activated:Connect(function()
		if not lines then return end
		if idx < #lines then
			idx += 1
			lineText.Text = lines[idx]
			contText.Text = (idx < #lines) and "NEXT \u{25B6}" or finalLabel
		else
			local d = onDone
			M.Hide()
			if d then d() end
		end
	end)
end

function M.Show(npcName, dlgLines, accent, done, anchor, finalTxt)
	build()
	anchorPart = anchor
	finalLabel = finalTxt or "OPEN SHOP \u{25B6}"
	lines = (type(dlgLines) == "table" and #dlgLines > 0) and dlgLines or { "..." }
	idx = 1
	onDone = done
	nameText.Text = npcName or "Merchant"
	UITheme.gradient(namePlate, (accent and accent[1]) or CF.amber1, (accent and accent[2]) or CF.amber2, 90)
	lineText.Text = lines[1]
	contText.Text = (#lines > 1) and "NEXT \u{25B6}" or finalLabel
	box.Visible = true
	local s = box:FindFirstChild("PopScale") or Instance.new("UIScale")
	s.Name = "PopScale"; s.Parent = box; s.Scale = 0.85
	TweenService:Create(s, TweenInfo.new(0.18, Enum.EasingStyle.Back, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), { Scale = 1 }):Play()
end

function M.IsOpen()
	return box ~= nil and box.Visible
end

function M.Hide()
	onDone = nil
	lines = nil
	anchorPart = nil
	if box then box.Visible = false end
end

return M

===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/MutationConfig.lua =====
-- MutationConfig: rare stacking variants that multiply a brainrot's cash/sec.
-- Shared by ThrowHandler (roll), IncomeLoop (multiplier), FusionHandler (ladder)
-- and the client (display).
--
-- ============================ FUSION-ONLY MUTATIONS ============================
-- Rainbow and Glitched are the two most desirable mutations in the game, and as
-- of this change they do NOT drop from a throw at all. `FusionOnly = true` makes
-- Roll() skip them. The only way to get one is to climb the fusion ladder in
-- ServerScriptService.Modules.FusionHandler (5 identical UNPLACED copies of the
-- same brainrot -> 1 copy at the next tier):
--
--     nil -> Golden -> Diamond -> Rainbow -> Glitched      (Glitched is terminal)
--
-- WHY:
--  * Supply. While they dropped natively their supply was unbounded -- anyone
--    who threw long enough eventually got one, so time-at-keyboard rather than
--    effort set the price, and every copy was worth exactly the next. Making
--    them fusion-only turns them into goods CAPPED BY EFFORT: fusing all the
--    way up from plain copies, one Rainbow costs 125 copies of the SAME
--    brainrot (5 -> Golden, 25 -> Diamond, 125 -> Rainbow) and one Glitched
--    costs 625. That is a real, countable price floor a trade can be argued
--    against. Natural Golden (13.5%) and Diamond (5.5%) drops shorten the
--    climb, which is precisely why those two keep their rates -- they are the
--    raw material the ladder eats.
--  * It gives fusion a reason to exist. Before, fusion topped out at Rainbow,
--    which you could also simply find, so the sink was optional flavour that a
--    patient player could ignore. Now it is the ONLY door to the top two tiers,
--    so the duplicate brainrots players already drown in finally have somewhere
--    to go, and every fuse permanently destroys 5 items.
--  * The ceiling still rises with skill, not grind alone: you may only fuse
--    copies of the SAME brainrot, so a Glitched Secret stays a genuinely
--    different achievement from a Glitched common.
--
-- DELIBERATELY NOT DELETED from Mutations.List. Existing player-owned Rainbow
-- and Glitched copies -- and every one fused from here on -- still need Mult(),
-- Color(), Rarity() and the ByName lookup to resolve. Deleting the entries would
-- silently drop those brainrots to x1 cash with no tint. The entries stay; only
-- Roll() changes, declaratively, via the FusionOnly flag.
--
-- Weather is unaffected. Mutations.Events maps each weather event to its OWN
-- mutation (Wet / Sandy / Electric / Frozen / Aurora / Celestial / Demon /
-- Angel); none of those is Rainbow or Glitched, so no live event can force-roll
-- a fusion-only variant. If a future event is ever pointed at one, it would
-- bypass this cap entirely -- don't.
-- ==============================================================================
local Mutations = {}

-- Rarity ladder, weakest to strongest (Rarity = position in that order):
--   1 Gold  2 Diamond  3 Wet  4 Sandy  5 Rainbow  6 Electric
--   7 Frozen  8 Aurora  9 Celestial  10 Glitched  11 Demon  12 Angel
-- The four base variants sit at 1/2/5/10, so their original multipliers
-- (2/5/15/50) are untouched and the event variants interpolate between them.
Mutations.List = {
	{ Name = "Golden",   Rarity = 1,  Mult = 2,  Chance = 0.135,  Color = Color3.fromRGB(255, 215, 60) },
	{ Name = "Diamond",  Rarity = 2,  Mult = 5,  Chance = 0.055,  Color = Color3.fromRGB(120, 230, 255) },
	-- FUSION-ONLY (see the block at the top). Roll() skips any entry flagged
	-- FusionOnly, and Chance is pinned to 0 as a second line of defence so that
	-- code which walks List and forgets the flag still cannot hand one out.
	-- Their natural rates used to be Rainbow 1.45% and Glitched 0.25% per catch.
	{ Name = "Rainbow",  Rarity = 5,  Mult = 15, Chance = 0, FusionOnly = true, Color = Color3.fromRGB(255, 120, 220) },
	{ Name = "Glitched", Rarity = 10, Mult = 50, Chance = 0, FusionOnly = true, Color = Color3.fromRGB(150, 255, 130) },
}

-- Event-exclusive mutations: each can only roll while its own weather event is
-- live, at the fixed chance below. Deliberately kept OUT of Mutations.List so
-- they never appear on an ordinary catch, and so the fusion ladder (which is an
-- explicit map in FusionHandler) is unaffected -- these are terminal rewards.
-- Chance here is CONDITIONAL: the odds while that event is live. It is tuned so
-- the EFFECTIVE per-catch rate falls at every rung of the ladder, Gold down to
-- Angel. The two columns differ a lot because a rare event is live only a sliver
-- of the session -- Shooting Star runs ~3.8% of the time, so Celestial needs a
-- higher in-event chance just to stay commoner than Glitched. The "eff" comment
-- is the real drop rate; the raw Chance column is NOT the ladder.
--
-- These are calibrated against the WeatherHandler cycle: 180s Clear + 20s warning
-- + a 4-7min event (330s avg), so an event is live ~62% of the time. Change any
-- of those durations and these need recomputing, or the ladder breaks.
Mutations.Events = {
	["Fog"]           = { Name = "Wet",       Rarity = 3,  Mult = 7,  Chance = 0.211, Color = Color3.fromRGB(90, 170, 255) },   -- eff 3.50%
	["Sandstorm"]     = { Name = "Sandy",     Rarity = 4,  Mult = 10, Chance = 0.166, Color = Color3.fromRGB(214, 176, 112) },  -- eff 2.30%
	["Thunderstorm"]  = { Name = "Electric",  Rarity = 6,  Mult = 20, Chance = 0.060, Color = Color3.fromRGB(255, 240, 100) },  -- eff 0.70%
	["Blizzard"]      = { Name = "Frozen",    Rarity = 7,  Mult = 26, Chance = 0.063, Color = Color3.fromRGB(172, 236, 255) },  -- eff 0.52%
	["Aurora"]        = { Name = "Aurora",    Rarity = 8,  Mult = 33, Chance = 0.066, Color = Color3.fromRGB(120, 255, 190) },  -- eff 0.40%
	["Shooting Star"] = { Name = "Celestial", Rarity = 9,  Mult = 41, Chance = 0.084, Color = Color3.fromRGB(198, 210, 255) },  -- eff 0.32%
	["Blood Moon"]    = { Name = "Demon",     Rarity = 11, Mult = 70, Chance = 0.051, Color = Color3.fromRGB(220, 48, 48) },    -- eff 0.070%
	["Golden Hour"]   = { Name = "Angel",     Rarity = 12, Mult = 95, Chance = 0.032, Color = Color3.fromRGB(255, 242, 190) },  -- eff 0.018%
}

Mutations.ByName = {}
for _, m in ipairs(Mutations.List) do
	Mutations.ByName[m.Name] = m
end
-- event variants share the same lookup, so Mult()/Color() work for both
for _, m in pairs(Mutations.Events) do
	Mutations.ByName[m.Name] = m
end

-- returns a mutation Name, or nil for an ordinary catch.
-- boost (>1, from weather events) scales the odds of every base variant.
-- eventName (the live weather event) gives that event's own mutation first
-- refusal at its exact listed chance -- boost is NOT applied there, since those
-- odds are already tuned per event and would otherwise double-dip.
-- Entries flagged FusionOnly are skipped entirely: they contribute nothing to
-- the cumulative total, so Golden and Diamond keep their exact absolute odds
-- (no silent re-normalisation) and the leftover probability becomes "no
-- mutation" -- which is the point, that headroom is what fusion now sells.
function Mutations.Roll(boost, eventName)
	local ev = eventName and Mutations.Events[eventName]
	if ev and math.random() < ev.Chance then
		return ev.Name
	end
	boost = boost or 1
	local r = math.random()
	local cum = 0
	for _, m in ipairs(Mutations.List) do
		if not m.FusionOnly then
			cum += math.min(m.Chance * boost, 0.5)
			if r < cum then return m.Name end
		end
	end
	return nil
end

function Mutations.Mult(name)
	local m = name and Mutations.ByName[name]
	return m and m.Mult or 1
end

function Mutations.Color(name)
	local m = name and Mutations.ByName[name]
	return m and m.Color or nil
end

-- position on the rarity ladder (1 = weakest, 12 = strongest); 0 = no mutation
function Mutations.Rarity(name)
	local m = name and Mutations.ByName[name]
	return m and m.Rarity or 0
end

-- every variant, weakest -> strongest; handy for UI listings and sorting
Mutations.Order = {}
for _, m in pairs(Mutations.ByName) do table.insert(Mutations.Order, m) end
table.sort(Mutations.Order, function(a, b) return a.Rarity < b.Rarity end)

return Mutations


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/MutationFX.lua =====
-- MutationFX: the 3D presentation of a mutated brainrot.
--
-- Before this, all twelve mutations rendered IDENTICALLY -- one PointLight plus
-- one sparkle emitter, tinted. A Glitched (x50) looked exactly like a Golden
-- (x2). The economy already has a careful 12-rung rarity ladder in
-- MutationConfig; this makes that ladder visible.
--
-- Everything here is a STATIC instance -- lights, emitters, a Highlight. No
-- per-frame work and no tweens, because these sit on every placed brainrot on
-- every plot in the server and anything per-frame would multiply badly.
--
-- NOTE: it never recolours the model's own parts. Flattening an authored model
-- to one colour erases the thing that makes it recognisable (Pete has 47 parts).
-- The tint is carried by light, particles and a Highlight OUTLINE instead.

local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local Mutations = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.MutationConfig)

local M = {}

local SPARKLE = "rbxasset://textures/particles/sparkles_main.dds"

-- Rarity runs 1 (Golden) .. 12 (Angel). Bands, each adding a NEW kind of effect
-- rather than just more of the last one, so you can read the tier at a glance:
--   1-2   light + sparkles
--   3-6   + a coloured outline around the whole creature
--   7-9   + a faint inner fill and denser, faster sparkles
--   10-12 + rising motes and the brightest light in the game
local function band(r)
	if r >= 10 then return 4
	elseif r >= 7 then return 3
	elseif r >= 3 then return 2
	else return 1 end
end

-- Strip anything a previous call left behind so this is safe to re-apply.
function M.clear(host)
	for _, d in ipairs(host:GetDescendants()) do
		if d.Name == "MutationLight" or d.Name == "MutationAura"
		or d.Name == "MutationMotes" or d.Name == "MutationGlow" then
			d:Destroy()
		end
	end
end

-- model may be a Model or a single BasePart (the placeholder cube).
-- Returns true if anything was applied.
function M.apply(model, mutationName)
	if not mutationName then return false end
	local colour = Mutations.Color(mutationName)
	if not colour then return false end
	local rarity = Mutations.Rarity(mutationName)
	local b = band(rarity)

	local host = model:IsA("BasePart") and model or model.PrimaryPart
	if not host then
		host = model:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("BasePart", true)
	end
	if not host then return false end

	M.clear(model)

	-- how far up the ladder we are, 0..1 -- drives every magnitude below
	local t = math.clamp((rarity - 1) / 11, 0, 1)

	-- Kept deliberately modest. A plot has 16 pads and a server has six plots, so
	-- these can stack to ~96 lights; the old single-value 13/3 washed the whole
	-- base out once more than a couple were mutated. The Highlight below is what
	-- actually carries the colour -- the light is only there to sell it.
	local light = Instance.new("PointLight")
	light.Name = "MutationLight"
	light.Color = colour
	light.Range = 7 + 6 * t
	light.Brightness = 1.0 + 2.6 * t
	light.Parent = host

	local aura = Instance.new("ParticleEmitter")
	aura.Name = "MutationAura"
	aura.Texture = SPARKLE
	aura.Color = ColorSequence.new(colour)
	aura.Rate = 16 + 44 * t
	aura.Lifetime = NumberRange.new(0.6, 1.2 + 0.6 * t)
	aura.Speed = NumberRange.new(0.4, 1.4 + 1.6 * t)
	aura.SpreadAngle = Vector2.new(180, 180)
	aura.Size = NumberSequence.new(0.45 + 0.35 * t)
	aura.Transparency = NumberSequence.new({
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 0.2),
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 1),
	})
	aura.Parent = host

	-- band 2+: outline the whole creature in its mutation colour. A Highlight is
	-- the one way to tint a model without touching its parts' own colours.
	if b >= 2 and not model:IsA("BasePart") then
		local hl = Instance.new("Highlight")
		hl.Name = "MutationGlow"
		hl.FillColor = colour
		hl.OutlineColor = colour
		-- band 2 is outline-only; the fill creeps in higher up the ladder so the
		-- top tiers read as genuinely glowing rather than merely outlined
		hl.FillTransparency = (b >= 3) and (0.86 - 0.22 * t) or 1
		hl.OutlineTransparency = 0
		hl.DepthMode = Enum.HighlightDepthMode.Occluded
		hl.Parent = model
	end

	-- band 4: rising motes, reserved for Glitched / Demon / Angel
	if b >= 4 then
		local motes = Instance.new("ParticleEmitter")
		motes.Name = "MutationMotes"
		motes.Texture = SPARKLE
		motes.Color = ColorSequence.new(colour)
		motes.Rate = 14
		motes.Lifetime = NumberRange.new(1.4, 2.2)
		motes.Speed = NumberRange.new(2.4, 4.0)
		motes.SpreadAngle = Vector2.new(14, 14)
		motes.Acceleration = Vector3.new(0, 3.5, 0)   -- drift upward
		motes.Size = NumberSequence.new({
			NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 0.7),
			NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 0),
		})
		motes.Transparency = NumberSequence.new({
			NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 0.1),
			NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 1),
		})
		motes.Parent = host
	end

	return true
end

return M


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/NumberFormat.lua =====
-- NumberFormat: the ONE abbreviator for player-facing cash.
--
-- Replaces nine near-identical local copies (formatShort x4, formatNumber x4,
-- shorten x1) that had already drifted apart -- %.1fB vs %.2fB, %.0fK vs %.1fK --
-- and all capped at B. A single Secret earning 9.99B/s reaches a trillion in 100
-- seconds, so the missing tiers were about to render live balances as "86400.0B".
--
-- Two deliberate choices:
--  * TRUNCATES, never rounds. Currency must not read higher than it is, and
--    9,999,999,999 has to show as "9.99B" rather than rounding up to "10.00B".
--  * nil/NaN/negative safe. Callers read straight off replicated attributes that
--    can be nil for a frame (see PlotSignClient), and a formatter is the wrong
--    place to throw.

local NumberFormat = {}

-- descending: first threshold that fits wins
local UNITS = {
	{ 1e18, "Qi" },
	{ 1e15, "Qa" },
	{ 1e12, "T"  },
	{ 1e9,  "B"  },
	{ 1e6,  "M"  },
	{ 1e3,  "K"  },
}

-- Truncate to 2 decimals. Done on the DIVIDED value (e.g. 9.999999999) where the
-- magnitude is small, so the multiply cannot lose precision the way it would on
-- the raw 1e10+ input.
local function trunc2(x)
	return math.floor(x * 100) / 100
end

-- 1234 -> "1.23K"   9999999999 -> "9.99B"   8.64e13 -> "86.40T"
function NumberFormat.Short(n)
	if type(n) ~= "number" or n ~= n then return "0" end   -- nil, non-number, NaN
	if n == math.huge then return "\u{221E}" end
	if n == -math.huge then return "-\u{221E}" end

	local sign = n < 0 and "-" or ""
	n = math.abs(n)

	for _, unit in ipairs(UNITS) do
		local threshold, suffix = unit[1], unit[2]
		if n >= threshold then
			return sign .. string.format("%.2f%s", trunc2(n / threshold), suffix)
		end
	end
	return sign .. tostring(math.floor(n))
end

-- "$9.99B" -- the prefix every call site was gluing on by hand
function NumberFormat.Cash(n)
	return "$" .. NumberFormat.Short(n)
end

-- "+9.99B/s" for rate lines. Sub-1000 rates keep a decimal, because most of the
-- roster sits between 1 and 1000 and "+1/s" vs "+1.03/s" is a real difference there.
function NumberFormat.Rate(cps)
	if type(cps) ~= "number" or cps ~= cps then return "+0/s" end
	if cps >= 1000 then return "+" .. NumberFormat.Short(cps) .. "/s" end
	if cps == math.floor(cps) then return "+" .. tostring(math.floor(cps)) .. "/s" end
	return string.format("+%.1f/s", cps)
end

return NumberFormat


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/OfferingConfig.lua =====
-- OfferingConfig: burning a brainrot into the campfire ('Offering') grants a small
-- PERMANENT luck bonus with diminishing returns.
--
-- Why this exists: fusion is the only brainrot sink and it cannot cover Commons
-- (it needs 5 identical name+mutation and stops at the top mutation). Offerings
-- are the sink that scales with the faucet -- every tier can be burned, and the
-- reward is deliberately sub-linear so burning stays worthwhile forever without
-- ever becoming a better luck source than rocks and upgrades.
local M = {}

-- sqrt growth: doubling your offerings does NOT double the bonus
M.PER_OFFERING = 0.010   -- 1% luck per sqrt(offering)
M.MAX_BONUS    = 0.50    -- hard ceiling: +50% luck, reached at 2500 offerings

-- multiplicative luck factor, always >= 1
function M.LuckMult(offerings)
	offerings = tonumber(offerings) or 0
	if offerings <= 0 then return 1 end
	local bonus = math.min(M.PER_OFFERING * math.sqrt(offerings), M.MAX_BONUS)
	return 1 + bonus
end

-- how many more burns until the next visible 1% step (for UI feedback)
function M.NextStepAt(offerings)
	offerings = tonumber(offerings) or 0
	local current = math.floor(M.PER_OFFERING * math.sqrt(offerings) * 100)
	local target = (current + 1) / (M.PER_OFFERING * 100)
	return math.max(1, math.ceil(target * target) - offerings)
end

return M

-- PetConfig (Forest Egg Shop, Task 11) -- pet boosts, slots, gamepass.

PetConfig.SLOTS_FREE = 3

-- === Rarity ladder ============================================================

-- to land under it. Only these four tiers appear in EggConfig's forest tables (Epic x3,

PetConfig.RARITY_BOOSTS = {

	Epic      = { Luck = 1.50, Income = 2.00 },
	Legendary = { Luck = 2.25, Income = 3.50 },

	Epic      = Color3.fromRGB(126, 170, 255),
	Rare      = Color3.fromRGB(120, 214, 168),
}

-- [petId] = { Name, Rarity, Model }. petId is the creature's name with spaces stripped,
-- so a pet record's Id stays stable and readable in a save file.
--
-- NEVER DELETE AN ENTRY. Owned pet records store only Uid + Id; boosts are looked up
-- from here at read time (see PetHandler.boostFor) precisely so a rebalance reaches pets
-- players already own -- but that also means a removed Id turns an owned pet into a
-- boost-less orphan. Retire by dropping it from EggConfig's roll tables instead.
local function pets(rarity, names)
	local t = {}
	for _, n in ipairs(names) do
		t[(n:gsub("%s+", ""))] = { Name = n, Rarity = rarity }
	end
	return t
end

-- RETIRED 2026-08-01, definitions intentionally kept: these ten were the forest
-- BRAINROTS doubling as stand-in pets before the real pet art existed. They are

-- boost-less orphan (see the NEVER DELETE note above).
for rarity, names in pairs({
	Epic      = { "Cervolino Antlerino", "Fanghetto Palunko", "Strigolino Hootini" },
	Legendary = { "Rospino Bavaglio", "Corvacchio Beccarino", "Ceppone Zampalunga" },
	Mythic    = { "Alcione Trombettone", "Lucciolone Pantanini", "Gufocervo Stiltini" },

		PetConfig.Pets[id] = def

-- Id for a creature name, so EggHandler never has to duplicate the strip-spaces rule.
function PetConfig.IdFor(creatureName)
	if typeof(creatureName) ~= "string" then return nil end
	local id = (creatureName:gsub("%s+", ""))
	return PetConfig.Pets[id] and id or nil
end

-- Multipliers for a petId, or a neutral 1x pair if the id is unknown. Callers on the hot
-- throw/income paths must never be able to turn a lookup miss into a 0.
function PetConfig.BoostsFor(petId)
	local def = PetConfig.Pets[petId]
	local b = def and PetConfig.RARITY_BOOSTS[def.Rarity]
	if not b then return 1, 1 end
	return b.Luck or 1, b.Income or 1
end

-- === Follow behaviour =========================================================
-- Read by PetHandler's rig. The bob is what makes an equipped pet read as "happy"
-- rather than as a part being dragged along behind the player.
PetConfig.BOB_HEIGHT = 0.45      -- studs, peak-to-peak above/below the slot height
PetConfig.BOB_PERIOD = 1.6       -- seconds per full up-down cycle
PetConfig.BOB_PHASE_STEP = 0.7   -- radians between slots, so pets don't bob in lockstep
PetConfig.SPIN_PERIOD = 6.0      -- slow idle yaw, seconds per turn

return PetConfig


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/PityConfig.lua =====
-- PityConfig: dry-streak protection for the top tiers. Each throw that REACHES a tier's
-- distance without catching it (or higher) ticks that tier's counter up; once the counter
-- passes Threshold, every further reaching throw gets a big boosted -- never guaranteed --
-- Chance to bump the roll up to that tier. Counters reset when you catch the tier or higher
-- (ThrowHandler.revealCatch). Only the HIGHEST eligible tier fires per throw.
--
-- Ordered low -> high. Tunable: raise Chance for a stronger safety net, raise Threshold to
-- make players wait longer.
return {
	{ Tier = "Legendary", Threshold = 50,  Chance = 0.35 },
	{ Tier = "Mythic",    Threshold = 150, Chance = 0.30 },
	{ Tier = "Secret",    Threshold = 500, Chance = 0.25 },
}

-- 8-point star built from rotated bars, because no image assets are needed
local function makeStar(parent, color)
	local star = Instance.new("Frame")
	star.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
	star.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.44)
	star.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(10, 10)
	star.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	star.Parent = parent
	for i = 0, 3 do
		local bar = Instance.new("Frame")
		bar.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
		bar.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)
		bar.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(i % 2 == 0 and 150 or 96, i % 2 == 0 and 7 or 5)
		bar.Rotation = i * 45
		bar.BackgroundColor3 = color
		bar.BorderSizePixel = 0
		bar.Parent = star
		local g = Instance.new("UIGradient")
		g.Transparency = NumberSequence.new({
			NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 1), NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0.5, 0),
			NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 1),
		})
		g.Parent = bar
	end
	local core = Instance.new("Frame")
	core.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
	core.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)
	core.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(26, 26)
	core.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255)
	core.BorderSizePixel = 0
	core.Parent = star
	local cc = Instance.new("UICorner")
	cc.CornerRadius = UDim.new(1, 0)
	cc.Parent = core
	local scale = Instance.new("UIScale")
	scale.Parent = star
	return star, scale
end

-- result: {Name, Rarity, RarityColor, Mutation, Serial, Exists, OddsN}
function M.play(result)
	local cfg = TIERS[result.Rarity] or TIERS.Common
	activeToken += 1
	local token = activeToken
	local color = result.RarityColor or Color3.fromRGB(255, 216, 77)

	task.spawn(function()
		local g = ensureGui()
		clear()
		local black = nil

		if not cfg.quick then
		-- ===== TAKEOVER =====
		black = Instance.new("Frame")
		black.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
		black.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(4, 4, 8)
		black.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		black.BorderSizePixel = 0
		black.Parent = g
		TweenService:Create(black, TweenInfo.new(0.35), { BackgroundTransparency = 0 }):Play()
		if cfg.drama then SoundKit.play("catchDrama", nil, { volume = VOL_DRAMA }) end
		task.wait(0.38)
		if token ~= activeToken then return end

		local star, starScale = makeStar(black, color)
		starScale.Scale = 0.1
		TweenService:Create(starScale, TweenInfo.new(0.6, Enum.EasingStyle.Back, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), { Scale = 1 }):Play()
		task.spawn(function()
			local t0 = os.clock()
			while token == activeToken and star.Parent do
				local dt = os.clock() - t0
				star.Rotation = dt * 24
				starScale.Scale = 1 + 0.08 * math.sin(dt * 3)
				task.wait()
			end
		end)
		for i = 1, 10 do
			local d = Instance.new("Frame")
			d.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(3, 3)
			d.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.08 + (i * 0.09) % 0.85, 1.05)
			d.BackgroundColor3 = color
			d.BackgroundTransparency = 0.45
			d.BorderSizePixel = 0
			d.Parent = black
			TweenService:Create(d, TweenInfo.new(3 + (i % 3), Enum.EasingStyle.Linear), {
				Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.08 + (i * 0.09) % 0.85, -0.1),
				BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			}):Play()
		end
		SoundKit.play("catchSparkle", nil, { volume = VOL_SHIMMER })
		task.wait(cfg.hold)
		if token ~= activeToken then return end

		-- ===== CLIMB =====
		local counter = label(black, "1 / 2", 96, Color3.fromRGB(255, 216, 77), 8)
		counter.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
		counter.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.72)
		local cScale = Instance.new("UIScale")
		cScale.Parent = counter
		local target = math.max(2, result.OddsN or 100)
		local steps = 6
		for s = 1, steps do
			if token ~= activeToken then return end
			local v = math.max(2, math.floor(target ^ (s / steps)))
			counter.Text = "1 / " .. comma(v)
			cScale.Scale = 1.25
			TweenService:Create(cScale, TweenInfo.new(0.12, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), { Scale = 1 }):Play()
			SoundKit.play("catchSparkle", nil, { volume = VOL_TICK })
			task.wait(cfg.climb / steps)
		end
		counter.Text = "1 / " .. comma(target)
		task.wait(0.25)
		if token ~= activeToken then return end
		end -- not cfg.quick

		-- ===== BURST =====
		-- THE TIER LEAD. Skipped only when the caller already played this exact
		-- cue (CatchRevealClient.playTierCue does, for non-broadcast tiers) --
		-- without that check, wiring the bottom three here would double every
		-- Common/Uncommon/Rare catch against a cue that already sounds correct.
		-- Nil flag = nobody else played one, so this carries it alone: safe
		-- whichever reveal system survives.
		local tierVol = CATCH_VOLUME[result.Rarity] or 0.25
		if not result.TierCuePlayed then
			SoundKit.play(CATCH_SOUND[result.Rarity] or "catchLegend", nil, { volume = tierVol })
		end
		-- THE CREATURE'S OWN VOICE, layered rather than replacing: the tier sound
		-- says how rare, the voice says who. Scaled to 0.8 of the tier lead so it
		-- always sits UNDER it -- a flat value would drown a Common's 0.13 while
		-- vanishing under a God's 0.54. Absent/empty VoiceId returns nil and
		-- costs one comparison, which is the state of all 161 today.
		SoundKit.playId(result.VoiceId, nil, { volume = tierVol * VOICE_REVEAL_MULT })
		if not cfg.quick then
			SoundKit.play("catchBigHit", nil, { volume = VOL_BIGHIT })
		end
		local flash = Instance.new("Frame")
		flash.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
		flash.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255)
		flash.BackgroundTransparency = cfg.quick and 0.35 or 0
		flash.BorderSizePixel = 0
		flash.Parent = g
		for i = 1, cfg.shards do
			local sh = Instance.new("Frame")
			sh.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
			sh.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)
			sh.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(8, 60)
			sh.Rotation = i * (360 / cfg.shards)
			sh.BackgroundColor3 = color
			sh.BorderSizePixel = 0
			sh.ZIndex = 3
			sh.Parent = g
			local a = math.rad(sh.Rotation - 90)
			TweenService:Create(sh, TweenInfo.new(0.55, Enum.EasingStyle.Quart, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), {
				Position = UDim2.new(0.5 + 0.75 * math.cos(a), 0, 0.5 + 0.75 * math.sin(a), 0),
				Size = UDim2.fromOffset(4, 160),
				BackgroundTransparency = 1,
			}):Play()
		end
		TweenService:Create(flash, TweenInfo.new(cfg.quick and 0.3 or 0.5), { BackgroundTransparency = 1 }):Play()
		if black then
			TweenService:Create(black, TweenInfo.new(0.4), { BackgroundTransparency = 1 }):Play()
		end
		task.wait(cfg.quick and 0.18 or 0.42)
		if token ~= activeToken then return end
		clear()

		-- ===== HANDOFF: GIANT REAL MODEL in the world, camera-locked =====
		-- Viewports render no particles, no Highlight, no real lighting -- which
		-- is exactly why a card reveal feels fake after this buildup. So the
		-- ceremony shows the ACTUAL model, big, floating in front of the camera,
		-- with confetti and (when present) its real mutation aura. Falls back to
		-- the old CatchReveal card only if the model folder has no entry.
		local revealModel = nil
		local modelFolder = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("BrainrotModels")
		local master = modelFolder and modelFolder:FindFirstChild(result.Name)
		if master then
			revealModel = master:Clone()
			for _, d in ipairs(revealModel:GetDescendants()) do
				if d:IsA("BasePart") then
					d.Anchored = true
					d.CanCollide = false
					d.CanQuery = false
					d.CanTouch = false
				elseif d:IsA("Sound") then
					-- KEPT, not destroyed: stripping these also stripped any voice
					-- line shipped inside a model. But a clone must never be able
					-- to make noise on its own, so each one is neutered: a model
					-- shipping a Looped + Playing Sound would otherwise drone for
					-- the whole reveal and, worse, keep going if anything ever
					-- leaked the clone. Looped=false bounds it to one play, and
					-- Playing=false means only code that explicitly asks gets audio.
					-- The clone is Destroyed on teardown regardless, which is the
					-- backstop.
					d.Looped = false
					d.Playing = false
				elseif d:IsA("Script") or d:IsA("LocalScript")
					or d:IsA("ProximityPrompt") or d:IsA("BillboardGui") then
					d:Destroy()
				end
			end
			local cam = workspace.CurrentCamera
			local _, ext = revealModel:GetBoundingBox()
			local radius = math.max(ext.X, ext.Y, ext.Z)
			-- distance so the model fills ~70% of the vertical FOV
			local dist = radius / (2 * math.tan(math.rad(cam.FieldOfView / 2)) * 0.7)
			revealModel.Parent = cam
			local spinConn
			local t0 = os.clock()
			spinConn = RunService.RenderStepped:Connect(function()
				if token ~= activeToken or not revealModel.Parent then
					spinConn:Disconnect()
					if revealModel.Parent then revealModel:Destroy() end
					return
				end
				local dt = os.clock() - t0
				local c = workspace.CurrentCamera
				local base = c.CFrame * CFrame.new(0, -0.06 * radius + 0.05 * radius * math.sin(dt * 2), -dist)
				revealModel:PivotTo(base * CFrame.Angles(0, dt * 0.9, 0))
			end)
			-- tier glow + confetti, on the model itself so it moves with it
			local host = revealModel:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("BasePart", true)
			if host then
				local hl = Instance.new("Highlight")
				hl.FillTransparency = 1
				hl.OutlineColor = color
				hl.OutlineTransparency = 0.15
				hl.Parent = revealModel
				local confetti = Instance.new("ParticleEmitter")
				confetti.Texture = "rbxasset://textures/particles/sparkles_main.dds"
				confetti.Color = ColorSequence.new({
					ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0, color),
					ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(1, Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255)),
				})
				confetti.Size = NumberSequence.new({
					NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, radius * 0.06),
					NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, radius * 0.02),
				})
				confetti.Speed = NumberRange.new(radius * 0.6, radius * 1.3)
				confetti.SpreadAngle = Vector2.new(180, 180)
				confetti.Lifetime = NumberRange.new(0.8, 1.6)
				confetti.Rate = 0
				confetti.Parent = host
				confetti:Emit(cfg.quick and 28 or 70)
				if result.Mutation and result.Mutation ~= "" and result.Mutation ~= "None" then
					pcall(MutationFX.apply, revealModel, result.Mutation)
				end
			end
		else
			pcall(CatchReveal.play, result)
		end

		-- ===== STAMP overlay =====
		local stamp = Instance.new("Frame")
		stamp.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0)
		stamp.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.06)
		stamp.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(10, 10)
		stamp.AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.XY
		stamp.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		stamp.Parent = g
		local list = Instance.new("UIListLayout")
		list.HorizontalAlignment = Enum.HorizontalAlignment.Center
		list.Padding = UDim.new(0, 2)
		list.SortOrder = Enum.SortOrder.LayoutOrder
		list.Parent = stamp
		local nameL = label(stamp, string.upper(result.Name or "?"), 58, Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255), 6)
		nameL.LayoutOrder = 1
		local tierL = label(stamp, string.upper(result.Rarity or ""), 30, color, 4)
		tierL.LayoutOrder = 2
		if result.Serial then
			local ex = result.Exists and (" · ONLY " .. tostring(result.Exists) .. " EXIST") or ""
			label(stamp, "#" .. tostring(result.Serial) .. ex, 24, Color3.fromRGB(255, 216, 77), 3).LayoutOrder = 3
		end
		if result.OddsN and not cfg.quick then
			label(stamp, "1 in " .. comma(result.OddsN) .. " of its tier", 18, Color3.fromRGB(200, 208, 200), 2.5).LayoutOrder = 4
		end
		local sScale = Instance.new("UIScale")
		sScale.Scale = 2.6
		sScale.Parent = stamp
		TweenService:Create(sScale, TweenInfo.new(0.28, Enum.EasingStyle.Back, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), { Scale = 1 }):Play()

		local dismissed = false
		local conn
		conn = UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(function(input, processed)
			if processed then return end
			if input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1
				or input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.Touch then
				dismissed = true
			end
		end)
		local held = 0
		local holdMax = cfg.quick and 1.4 or 3.2
		while held < holdMax and not dismissed and token == activeToken do
			task.wait(0.1)
			held += 0.1
		end
		conn:Disconnect()
		if token ~= activeToken then return end
		for _, d in ipairs(stamp:GetDescendants()) do
			if d:IsA("TextLabel") then
				TweenService:Create(d, TweenInfo.new(0.3), { TextTransparency = 1, TextStrokeTransparency = 1 }):Play()
			elseif d:IsA("UIStroke") then
				TweenService:Create(d, TweenInfo.new(0.3), { Transparency = 1 }):Play()
			end
		end
		task.wait(0.32)
		if token == activeToken then
			if revealModel and revealModel.Parent then revealModel:Destroy() end
			clear()
		end
	end)
end

return M

===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/RarityCurve.lua =====
-- RarityCurve: probabilistic rarity. DISTANCE unlocks higher tiers and shifts the odds
-- toward them; LUCK shifts them further; higher tiers are geometrically rarer and nothing
-- is guaranteed. Shared so ThrowHandler (the real roll) and LuckHUDClient (the displayed
-- odds) read IDENTICAL numbers -- change a tunable here and both move together.
--
-- God (Secret Pete) is NOT part of the curve: he is an independent FixedChance handled in
-- RarityRoll.PickInTier. The curve tops out at Secret; ThrowHandler gives Pete his shot by
-- routing a top-of-curve roll through PickInTier(GodIndex).
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local RarityConfig = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.RarityConfig)

local RarityCurve = {}

-- === TUNABLES (retune difficulty here) ===
RarityCurve.TIER_STEP = 0.40        -- each higher tier's base weight is this x the previous. LOWER = rarer top tiers.
RarityCurve.RAMP = 160              -- studs for a tier to fade from 0 -> full weight past its unlock distance
RarityCurve.LUCK_INFLUENCE = 0.18   -- how strongly access-luck shifts the curve toward higher tiers

-- The curve covers the distance-banded tiers (Common..Secret). God has an infinite band
-- (MaxDistance == huge) and is excluded. Each tier's unlock distance = its MinDistance,
-- read from RarityConfig so the curve tracks the roster automatically.
local UNLOCK = {}
local TOP = 0
for i, t in ipairs(RarityConfig) do
	if t.MaxDistance ~= math.huge then
		UNLOCK[i] = t.MinDistance
		TOP = i
	end
end
RarityCurve.TopTier = TOP        -- highest tier index the curve can roll (Secret)
RarityCurve.GodIndex = TOP + 1   -- God's index, for Pete's independent FixedChance shot

-- Per-tier weights at a distance + access luck. Weight 0 means that tier is not unlocked.
function RarityCurve.Weights(distance, accessLuck)
	local lf = 1 + (math.max(accessLuck or 1, 1) - 1) * RarityCurve.LUCK_INFLUENCE
	local w = {}
	for i = 1, TOP do
		if distance < UNLOCK[i] then
			w[i] = 0
		else
			local ramp = math.clamp((distance - UNLOCK[i]) / RarityCurve.RAMP, 0, 1)
			w[i] = ramp * (RarityCurve.TIER_STEP ^ (i - 1)) * (lf ^ (i - 1))
		end
	end
	return w
end

-- Normalized probability per tier (index 1..TopTier). For the luck HUD.
function RarityCurve.Probabilities(distance, accessLuck)
	local w = RarityCurve.Weights(distance, accessLuck)
	local sum = 0
	for i = 1, TOP do sum += w[i] end
	local p = {}
	for i = 1, TOP do p[i] = (sum > 0) and (w[i] / sum) or 0 end
	if sum <= 0 then p[1] = 1 end   -- thrown nowhere: treat as Common
	return p
end

-- Roll a tier INDEX (1..TopTier) from the weighted distribution.
function RarityCurve.RollTierIndex(distance, accessLuck)
	local w = RarityCurve.Weights(distance, accessLuck)
	local sum = 0
	for i = 1, TOP do sum += w[i] end
	if sum <= 0 then return 1 end
	local r = math.random() * sum
	local c = 0
	for i = 1, TOP do
		c += w[i]
		if r <= c then return i end
	end
	return TOP
end

return RarityCurve


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/RarityFX.lua =====
-- RarityFX: escalating "this one is special" treatment for inventory tiles.
--
-- The point is CONTRAST. Common and Uncommon deliberately get NOTHING -- if every
-- tile shimmered, none would read as rare. Effects start at Rare and pile up, so
-- the good stuff announces itself across a dense grid.
--
-- ONE Heartbeat drives every tile. Per-tile connections would mean ~60 live
-- connections on a full backpack; this is a single loop over a registry that drops
-- entries as soon as their tile is destroyed, so a rebuild cleans itself up.

local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local M = {}

-- glow    = stroke transparency at rest (LOWER is stronger)
-- shimmer = seconds per sweep across the tile, or false
-- sparkle = how many twinkles
-- rainbow = hue cycles per second on the border, or false
-- The ladder adds ONE new kind of effect per step, so you can tell tiers apart at
-- a glance rather than just "more sparkly":
--     Rare/Epic  faint coloured rim, nothing moving
--     Legendary  + a shine sweep
--     Mythic     + sparkles
--     Secret/God + a cycling rainbow border
-- Tuned against a real end-game backpack, where 48 of 58 tiles were Rare or
-- better: starting the moving effects at Rare made almost everything shimmer,
-- which defeated the whole point.
local SPEC = {
	Common    = false,
	Uncommon  = false,
	Rare      = { glow = 0.72, shimmer = false, sparkle = 0, rainbow = false },
	Epic      = { glow = 0.60, shimmer = false, sparkle = 0, rainbow = false },
	Legendary = { glow = 0.42, shimmer = 3.0,   sparkle = 0, rainbow = false },
	Mythic    = { glow = 0.30, shimmer = 2.3,   sparkle = 3, rainbow = false },
	Secret    = { glow = 0.20, shimmer = 1.8,   sparkle = 4, rainbow = 0.22 },
	God       = { glow = 0.12, shimmer = 1.3,   sparkle = 5, rainbow = 0.45 },
}

-- fixed spots so a tile looks the same on every rebuild instead of jittering
local SPARKLE_AT = {
	Vector2.new(0.16, 0.20), Vector2.new(0.82, 0.30), Vector2.new(0.30, 0.68),
	Vector2.new(0.72, 0.62), Vector2.new(0.50, 0.14),
}

local active, conn, clock = {}, nil, 0

local function ensureDriver()
	if conn then return end
	conn = RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(dt)
		clock += dt
		for i = #active, 1, -1 do
			local e = active[i]
			if not e.root.Parent then
				table.remove(active, i)      -- tile destroyed by a rebuild
			else
				e.update(clock)
			end
		end
		if #active == 0 then conn:Disconnect(); conn = nil end
	end)
end

-- Drop every registered tile. The driver sheds them anyway once the instances are
-- destroyed; this just avoids a frame of animating corpses.
function M.reset()
	table.clear(active)
end

function M.tiers() return SPEC end

-- outer = the coloured border frame, inner = the card's content frame.
-- phase spreads the animation so a grid does not pulse in lockstep.
function M.attach(outer, inner, tierName, accent, phase)
	local spec = SPEC[tierName]
	if not spec then return false end
	phase = phase or 0

	local parts = {}

	-- halo: a slightly oversized frame BEHIND the tile carrying a coloured stroke.
	-- It sits in the grid's cell padding, so it costs no layout room.
	local glow = Instance.new("Frame")
	glow.Name = "RarityGlow"
	glow.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
	glow.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)
	glow.Size = UDim2.new(1, 8, 1, 8)
	glow.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	glow.ZIndex = (outer.ZIndex or 1) - 1
	glow.Parent = outer
	local gc = Instance.new("UICorner"); gc.CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, 16); gc.Parent = glow
	local gs = Instance.new("UIStroke")
	gs.Color = accent
	gs.Thickness = 4
	gs.Transparency = spec.glow
	gs.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Border
	gs.LineJoinMode = Enum.LineJoinMode.Round
	gs.Parent = glow
	parts.glow = gs

	-- shine sweep. The gradient lives on its OWN empty frame, never on anything
	-- holding text -- a UIGradient tints its parent's glyphs too, which has bitten
	-- this codebase before.
	if spec.shimmer then
		local shim = Instance.new("Frame")
		shim.Name = "Shimmer"
		shim.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
		shim.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255)
		shim.BorderSizePixel = 0
		shim.ZIndex = 15   -- above the 3D render (14), below value/name text (16)
		shim.Parent = inner
		local shc = Instance.new("UICorner"); shc.CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, 10); shc.Parent = shim
		local sg = Instance.new("UIGradient")
		sg.Rotation = 24
		sg.Transparency = NumberSequence.new({
			NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 1),
			NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0.44, 1),
			NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0.50, 0.55),
			NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0.56, 1),
			NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 1),
		})
		sg.Parent = shim
		parts.shimmer = sg
	end

	local sparkleCount = spec.sparkle or 0
	for i = 1, sparkleCount do
		local at = SPARKLE_AT[i] or SPARKLE_AT[1]
		local s = Instance.new("TextLabel")
		s.Name = "Sparkle"
		s.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
		s.Position = UDim2.fromScale(at.X, at.Y)
		s.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(18, 18)
		s.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		s.Font = Enum.Font.GothamBold
		s.Text = "\u{2726}"
		s.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255)
		s.TextSize = 13
		s.ZIndex = 17
		s.Parent = inner
		parts[i] = s
	end

	active[#active + 1] = {
		root = outer,
		update = function(t)
			local tt = t + phase
			parts.glow.Transparency = spec.glow + 0.18 * (0.5 + 0.5 * math.sin(tt * 2.1))
			if parts.shimmer then
				parts.shimmer.Offset = Vector2.new(((tt / spec.shimmer) % 1) * 2.6 - 1.3, 0)
			end
			for i = 1, sparkleCount do
				local s = parts[i]
				if s then
					local k = 0.5 + 0.5 * math.sin(tt * 3.1 + i * 1.9)
					s.TextTransparency = 1 - k
					s.TextSize = 9 + 7 * k
				end
			end
			if spec.rainbow then
				-- the border itself cycles: unmistakable at a glance in a full grid
				outer.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromHSV((tt * spec.rainbow) % 1, 0.82, 1)
			end
		end,
	}
	ensureDriver()
	return true
end

return M


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/RebirthConfig.lua =====
-- RebirthConfig: prestige curves shared by RebirthHandler, IncomeLoop, ThrowHandler.
local RebirthConfig = {}

-- ===================== RETUNED ALONGSIDE THE ROCK LADDER =====================
-- The old cost was 1,000,000 x 1.8^n. Against 12 pads of Mythic brainrots that first
-- rebirth was EIGHT AND A HALF SECONDS of income, and the 1.8 growth never caught up
-- with a ~5.8x-per-tier income curve, so rebirth stopped being a decision.
--
-- The other half of this is RebirthHandler: rebirth wipes OwnedRocks back to Pebble.
-- That used to cost ~2.6M to rebuild; with the reworked RockConfig the full ladder is
-- ~725M, so the rock wipe is now the dominant sacrifice and the cash price has to sit
-- in the same order of magnitude or the gate is meaningless.
--
-- Payout was raised with it. At +10% per rebirth, giving up ~725M of rocks bought so
-- little that rebirthing was close to a trap; +15% keeps the loop worth entering. The
-- old comment claimed "the value is in rebirthing often" -- that is no longer the
-- shape of it. Rebirth is now an occasional milestone that replays the rock ladder,
-- which is exactly what makes the longer ladder worth having built.
--
-- Brainrots and their placements still survive, so income does NOT collapse on
-- rebirth: placed brainrots keep producing at their tier. What you lose is your cash
-- and your ability to CATCH high tiers until the rocks are rebought.

-- cash needed to perform the NEXT rebirth, given the current rebirth count
function RebirthConfig.Cost(rebirths)
	return math.floor(100000000 * (2.0 ^ (rebirths or 0)))
end

-- permanent money multiplier (+15% per rebirth)
function RebirthConfig.IncomeMult(rebirths)
	return 1 + 0.15 * (rebirths or 0)
end

-- permanent luck multiplier -- feeds the mutation-odds boost, NOT tier access
-- (ThrowHandler deliberately excludes rebirth luck from tier access) (+7% per rebirth)
function RebirthConfig.LuckMult(rebirths)
	return 1 + 0.07 * (rebirths or 0)
end

-- permanent throw power -- scales how far a skip goes (+7% per rebirth)
function RebirthConfig.PowerMult(rebirths)
	return 1 + 0.07 * (rebirths or 0)
end

return RebirthConfig

-- RockConfig: the progression ladder. 21 rocks -- the top 7 are end-game "cosmic"
-- rocks past BrainrotCore, all pinned at the 900m reach cap, that sell pure LUCK.
-- Buying is SEQUENTIAL: ShopHandler requires you to own the previous rock first, and
-- MerchantClient shows the shop in pages. Order below = ladder order; keep it ascending.
--
-- ============================ HOW A ROCK GATES A TIER ============================
-- MaxDistance ONLY matters where it crosses a RarityConfig band edge. The edges are
--
--     Common 0 | Uncommon 100 | Rare 220 | Epic 360 | Legendary 500 |
--     Mythic 640 | Secret 780 | God 900
--
-- so a rock reaching 150 and one reaching 200 both roll Uncommon and nothing else.
-- Extra reach INSIDE a band buys literally nothing. That is why this ladder
-- alternates what each purchase sells:
--
--   REACH rocks unlock a higher tier band AND raise your odds inside it.
--   LUCK  rocks raise Luck instead. Luck now shifts the whole RarityCurve toward the
--         top (ReplicatedStorage.Modules.RarityCurve) -- distance no longer GUARANTEES
--         a tier, it weights the odds, so both reach and luck pull their weight.
--
-- The shop row already prints "Up to Nm - x luck" (MerchantClient), so a LUCK rock
-- reads as an upgrade rather than looking like a no-op purchase.
--
-- Under the RarityCurve, Luck has a SMOOTH (un-clamped) effect on the odds, so the
-- end-game LUCK rocks below stay meaningful all the way up. Do not over-inflate them:
-- luck also multiplies with the Lucky Charm upgrade, Offerings and the Maxwell pet, so
-- the product climbs fast -- the top rock plus maxed upgrades is what the Secret odds
-- are tuned around.
--
-- ============================== WHY THESE PRICES ==============================
-- Tier income grows ~5.8x per band (weighted-average cash/sec over obtainable
-- names). The old ladder grew prices only ~4.6x per band, so every gate was CHEAPER
-- in real terms than the last and progression accelerated: time-to-next-rock fell
-- 59s -> 49 -> 34 -> 30 -> 25 -> 21 and the whole ladder was under 4 minutes.
--
-- Prices now step ~3.2x per rock, i.e. ~10.4x per band against ~5.8x income, so each
-- band takes ~1.8x longer than the one before. Full ladder on bare 12-pad income is
-- ~1.3 hours instead of 3.9 minutes, and the curve finally rises.
--
-- The short-then-long rhythm within a band is deliberate: crossing a band edge is a
-- ~6x income jump, so the LUCK rock right after it lands quickly as a reward, then
-- the next REACH rock is the real climb.
--
-- ============================== DO NOT RENAME IDS ==============================
-- data.OwnedRocks and data.EquippedRock are keyed by Id string. ThrowHandler line
-- ~343 falls back to `rockById["Pebble"]` when an Id is missing, so deleting or
-- renaming an entry does not error -- it SILENTLY demotes every owner of that rock
-- to Pebble. All 8 original Ids are preserved below for exactly that reason; the 6
-- new rocks are inserted around them. Add, never rename.
return {
