===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/RockDesign.lua =====
--[[ ==========================================================================
RockDesign -- the single source of truth for what every rock LOOKS like.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
There were three copies of this data before: a private ROCK_DESIGN in
ThrowHandler (8 of 14 rocks), a ROCK_PREVIEW in MerchantClient (14, but
different shapes and materials from the thrown rock), and nothing at all for
Rocco's shelf. A rock could therefore look like three different objects
depending on whether you were buying it, throwing it, or looking at it.

Now: ById holds the base spec, and Build(id) returns a detailed multi-part
Model used by the shop preview, the shelf display and the thrown rock alike.

Colour lives in RockConfig next to Price/Luck (balance data). This module is
presentation only. Keyed by RockConfig Id, which is never renamed.

Build() is DETERMINISTIC -- the chip layout is driven by a seed derived from the
rock's Id, so the same rock is always the same rock, in every surface.
========================================================================== ]]

local V = Vector3.new
local Mat = Enum.Material
local Shape = Enum.PartType

local RockDesign = {}

RockDesign.Default = {
	Shape = Shape.Block, Size = V(2.2, 0.4, 1.5), Material = Mat.Slate,
	Reflectance = 0, Archetype = "rough",
}

-- Archetypes drive the DETAIL pass in Build():
--   rough   chipped angular stone      smooth  water-worn, few soft bumps
--   crystal jutting facets             metal   flat facets + bright specks
--   core    neon heart + orbiting shards
RockDesign.ById = {
	Pebble            = { Shape = Shape.Block, Size = V(1.8, 0.8, 1.4),  Material = Mat.Pebble,        Reflectance = 0,    Archetype = "rough"   },
	SmoothStone       = { Shape = Shape.Ball,  Size = V(2.0, 1.2, 1.6),  Material = Mat.SmoothPlastic, Reflectance = 0.05, Archetype = "smooth"  },
	FlatSkipper       = { Shape = Shape.Block, Size = V(2.4, 0.35, 1.8), Material = Mat.Slate,         Reflectance = 0,    Archetype = "smooth"  },
	SlateDisc         = { Shape = Shape.Block, Size = V(2.6, 0.28, 2.1), Material = Mat.Slate,         Reflectance = 0.05, Archetype = "smooth"  },
	GraniteChunk      = { Shape = Shape.Block, Size = V(1.9, 1.3, 1.7),  Material = Mat.Granite,       Reflectance = 0,    Archetype = "rough"   },
	RiverGlass        = { Shape = Shape.Block, Size = V(2.1, 0.5, 1.7),  Material = Mat.Glass,         Reflectance = 0.45, Archetype = "smooth"  },
	ObsidianShard     = { Shape = Shape.Block, Size = V(2.6, 0.5, 1.0),  Material = Mat.Glass,         Reflectance = 0.3,  Archetype = "crystal" },
	BasaltPlate       = { Shape = Shape.Block, Size = V(2.5, 0.6, 2.0),  Material = Mat.Basalt,        Reflectance = 0,    Archetype = "rough"   },
	MeteoriteFragment = { Shape = Shape.Block, Size = V(1.9, 1.4, 1.8),  Material = Mat.Rock,          Reflectance = 0,    Archetype = "rough"   },
	StarcastIron      = { Shape = Shape.Block, Size = V(2.0, 1.0, 1.6),  Material = Mat.Metal,         Reflectance = 0.35, Archetype = "metal"   },
	GoldenRock        = { Shape = Shape.Ball,  Size = V(1.9, 1.5, 1.7),  Material = Mat.Metal,         Reflectance = 0.4,  Archetype = "metal"   },
	PrismaticGeode    = { Shape = Shape.Ball,  Size = V(1.8, 1.7, 1.8),  Material = Mat.Glass,         Reflectance = 0.5,  Archetype = "crystal" },
	VoidstoneShard    = { Shape = Shape.Block, Size = V(2.4, 0.6, 1.1),  Material = Mat.Glass,         Reflectance = 0.2,  Archetype = "crystal" },
	BrainrotCore      = { Shape = Shape.Ball,  Size = V(1.9, 1.9, 1.9),  Material = Mat.Neon,          Reflectance = 0,    Archetype = "core"    },
}

function RockDesign.For(id)
	return RockDesign.ById[id] or RockDesign.Default
end

local function seedOf(id)
	local n = 0
	for i = 1, #id do n = (n * 31 + string.byte(id, i)) % 2147483647 end
	return n
end

local function newPart(parent, name, size, cf, colour, material, reflectance, shape)
	local p = Instance.new("Part")
	p.Name, p.Size, p.CFrame, p.Color = name, size, cf, colour
	p.Material = material
	p.Reflectance = reflectance or 0
	if shape then p.Shape = shape end
	p.Anchored, p.CanCollide, p.CanQuery, p.CastShadow = true, false, false, false
	p.TopSurface, p.BottomSurface = Enum.SurfaceType.Smooth, Enum.SurfaceType.Smooth
	p.Parent = parent
	return p
end

-- Evenly spread directions (Fibonacci sphere) instead of pure random. Random
-- directions clustered -- an early build put all three swells on the +X side and
-- left the stone visibly lopsided.
local GOLDEN = math.pi * (3 - math.sqrt(5))
local function spreadDir(i, n, rng)
	local y = 1 - (i - 0.5) / n * 2
	local r = math.sqrt(math.max(0, 1 - y * y))
	local t = GOLDEN * i + rng:NextNumber(-0.25, 0.25)
	return Vector3.new(math.cos(t) * r, y * rng:NextNumber(0.75, 1.0), math.sin(t) * r).Unit
end

local function onSurface(size, dir, inset)
	return Vector3.new(dir.X * size.X / 2, dir.Y * size.Y / 2, dir.Z * size.Z / 2) * (inset or 1)
end

--[[ True axis-aligned size of a built rock.
	Model:GetBoundingBox() is NOT reliable here: for Ball parts it reports the
	inscribed extent, and measured 1.59 wide on a stone whose core alone is 2.0.
	Callers that fit a rock into a shelf cell must use this instead. ]]
function RockDesign.Extents(model)
	local lo = Vector3.new(math.huge, math.huge, math.huge)
	local hi = -lo
	for _, p in ipairs(model:GetDescendants()) do
		if p:IsA("BasePart") then
			local cf, s = p.CFrame, p.Size
			local R, U, L = cf.RightVector, cf.UpVector, cf.LookVector
			local e = Vector3.new(
				math.abs(R.X) * s.X / 2 + math.abs(U.X) * s.Y / 2 + math.abs(L.X) * s.Z / 2,
				math.abs(R.Y) * s.X / 2 + math.abs(U.Y) * s.Y / 2 + math.abs(L.Y) * s.Z / 2,
				math.abs(R.Z) * s.X / 2 + math.abs(U.Z) * s.Y / 2 + math.abs(L.Z) * s.Z / 2)
			lo = Vector3.new(math.min(lo.X, cf.X - e.X), math.min(lo.Y, cf.Y - e.Y), math.min(lo.Z, cf.Z - e.Z))
			hi = Vector3.new(math.max(hi.X, cf.X + e.X), math.max(hi.Y, cf.Y + e.Y), math.max(hi.Z, cf.Z + e.Z))
		end
	end
	return hi - lo, (hi + lo) / 2
end

--[[ Build(id, colour) -> Model
	Core is the PrimaryPart and carries the base spec. Detail parts are kept well
	under the core's size and half-buried in its surface, so they add texture
	without inflating the silhouette or turning the rock lopsided. ]]
function RockDesign.Build(id, colour)
	local spec = RockDesign.For(id)
	colour = colour or Color3.fromRGB(120, 120, 120)
	local rng = Random.new(seedOf(id or "rock"))

	local model = Instance.new("Model")
	model.Name = id or "Rock"
	local core = newPart(model, "Core", spec.Size, CFrame.new(), colour,
		spec.Material, spec.Reflectance, spec.Shape)
	model.PrimaryPart = core

	local dark  = colour:Lerp(Color3.fromRGB(0, 0, 0), 0.32)
	local light = colour:Lerp(Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255), 0.28)
	local md = math.min(spec.Size.X, spec.Size.Y, spec.Size.Z)
	local A = spec.Archetype or "rough"
	local function spin() return CFrame.Angles(rng:NextNumber(0, 6.28), rng:NextNumber(0, 6.28), rng:NextNumber(0, 6.28)) end

	if A == "rough" then
		for i = 1, 7 do
			local s = md * rng:NextNumber(0.20, 0.34)
			newPart(model, "Chip" .. i,
				Vector3.new(s, s * rng:NextNumber(0.65, 1.05), s * rng:NextNumber(0.75, 1.15)),
				CFrame.new(onSurface(spec.Size, spreadDir(i, 7, rng), 0.80)) * spin(),
				(i % 2 == 0) and dark or light, spec.Material, spec.Reflectance)
		end
	elseif A == "smooth" then
		for i = 1, 4 do
			local s = md * rng:NextNumber(0.28, 0.42)
			newPart(model, "Swell" .. i, Vector3.new(s * 1.6, s * 0.8, s * 1.35),
				CFrame.new(onSurface(spec.Size, spreadDir(i, 4, rng), 0.62)) * CFrame.Angles(0, rng:NextNumber(0, 6.28), 0),
				light, spec.Material, spec.Reflectance, Enum.PartType.Ball)
		end
		newPart(model, "Sheen", Vector3.new(spec.Size.X * 0.5, spec.Size.Y * 0.26, spec.Size.Z * 0.34),
			CFrame.new(0, spec.Size.Y * 0.30, 0), light, spec.Material,
			math.max(spec.Reflectance, 0.16), Enum.PartType.Ball)
	elseif A == "crystal" then
		for i = 1, 6 do
			local len = md * rng:NextNumber(0.75, 1.25)
			newPart(model, "Facet" .. i, Vector3.new(md * 0.28, len, md * 0.24),
				CFrame.new(onSurface(spec.Size, spreadDir(i, 6, rng), 0.55))
					* CFrame.Angles(rng:NextNumber(-0.9, 0.9), rng:NextNumber(0, 6.28), rng:NextNumber(-0.9, 0.9)),
				(i % 2 == 0) and light or dark, spec.Material, math.max(spec.Reflectance, 0.25))
		end
	elseif A == "metal" then
		for i = 1, 6 do
			local s = md * rng:NextNumber(0.30, 0.48)
			newPart(model, "Facet" .. i, Vector3.new(s, s * 0.26, s * rng:NextNumber(0.85, 1.2)),
				CFrame.new(onSurface(spec.Size, spreadDir(i, 6, rng), 0.78)) * spin(),
				light, spec.Material, math.min(0.6, spec.Reflectance + 0.2))
		end
		for i = 1, 3 do
			local s = md * 0.11
			newPart(model, "Speck" .. i, Vector3.new(s, s, s),
				CFrame.new(onSurface(spec.Size, spreadDir(i * 2, 6, rng), 0.9)),
				light, Mat.Foil, 0.5, Enum.PartType.Ball)
		end
	elseif A == "core" then
		local halo = newPart(model, "Halo", spec.Size * 1.12, CFrame.new(),
			colour:Lerp(Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255), 0.5), Mat.Neon, 0, Enum.PartType.Ball)
		halo.Transparency = 0.72
		for i = 1, 7 do
			local s = md * rng:NextNumber(0.13, 0.22)
			newPart(model, "Frag" .. i, Vector3.new(s, s * 1.8, s * 0.7),
				CFrame.new(onSurface(spec.Size, spreadDir(i, 7, rng), 0.86)) * spin(),
				colour:Lerp(Color3.fromRGB(0, 0, 0), 0.55), Mat.SmoothPlastic, 0.1)
		end
	end

	return model
end

return RockDesign


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/SeasonConfig.lua =====
-- SeasonConfig: daily-quest pool + season pass tiers. Shared by SeasonPassHandler
-- (progress/awards) and SeasonClient (display). Quests rotate daily (UTC), same
-- 3 for every player. Free track only for now — premium track needs a gamepass id.
local M = {}

-- Event names fired by SeasonPassHandler.Notify
M.QuestPool = {
	{ Id = "Throw20",  Name = "Skip 20 rocks",             Icon = "\u{1FAA8}", Event = "Throw",      Target = 20, XP = 100 },
	{ Id = "Throw50",  Name = "Skip 50 rocks",             Icon = "\u{1FAA8}", Event = "Throw",      Target = 50, XP = 250 },
	{ Id = "Perfect5", Name = "Land 5 PERFECT skips",     Icon = "\u{2B50}", Event = "Perfect",    Target = 5,  XP = 150 },
	{ Id = "Rare3",    Name = "Catch 3 Rare or better",    Icon = "\u{1F48E}", Event = "RareCatch",  Target = 3,  XP = 150 },
	{ Id = "Epic1",    Name = "Catch an Epic or better",   Icon = "\u{1F52E}", Event = "EpicCatch",  Target = 1,  XP = 200 },
	{ Id = "Fuse1",    Name = "Fuse at the campfire",      Icon = "\u{1F525}", Event = "Fuse",       Target = 1,  XP = 200 },
	{ Id = "Daily1",   Name = "Claim the daily reward",    Icon = "\u{1F381}", Event = "DailyClaim", Target = 1,  XP = 50 },
}

M.PoolById = {}
for _, q in ipairs(M.QuestPool) do M.PoolById[q.Id] = q end

-- same 3 quests for everyone on a given UTC day
function M.QuestsForDay(day)
	local rng = Random.new(day)
	local pool = table.clone(M.QuestPool)
	for i = #pool, 2, -1 do
		local j = rng:NextInteger(1, i)
		pool[i], pool[j] = pool[j], pool[i]
	end
	return { pool[1], pool[2], pool[3] }
end

-- 25 tiers, 250 XP each; cash escalates with milestone spikes every 5th tier
M.XP_PER_TIER = 250
M.Tiers = {}
for i = 1, 25 do
	local cash = math.floor(800 * (1.38 ^ (i - 1)) / 100 + 0.5) * 100
	if i % 5 == 0 then cash = cash * 2 end
	M.Tiers[i] = { XP = M.XP_PER_TIER, Cash = cash, Milestone = i % 5 == 0 }
end

-- cumulative XP needed to unlock tier i
function M.ThresholdFor(i)
	return i * M.XP_PER_TIER
end

return M

-- SideRail: the left button rail -- sticker cards, matching the reference art.
--
-- HISTORY, because this has flipped once already:
--   2026-07-25  "just the icon itself" -- plates removed, icons left free-floating
--               as 3D IconForge renders behind a heavy ink outline.
--   2026-07-26  reference image reverses it. Each slot is a sticker again: white
--               card + coloured ribbon banner + corner badge, no drop shadow, and
--               a flat emoji glyph instead of the 3D render. Built to match
--               UIStyle.sticker exactly so this rail and the nav rail on the
--               right read as ONE art style.
--
-- The handle contract has never changed across any of it:
--   { button, setReady(on), setBadge(kind, n) }   -- so no caller edits, ever.
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local player = Players.LocalPlayer

-- Round 2: reuse the SAME shared theme module the Trade/Booth/Season surfaces use.
local UIStyle = require(script.Parent.UIStyle)
local PAL = UIStyle.Palette

-- Campfire palette (UITheme.Camp) supplies the ink for glyph outlines, shadows
-- and badge rims -- the only framing a free-floating icon still has.
local UITheme = require(script.Parent.UITheme)
local CF = UITheme.Camp

local OUTLINE = CF.ink   -- warm campfire black (was a cool navy) behind every glyph
local WHITE = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255)
local BADGE_RED = Color3.fromRGB(235, 64, 52)
local BADGE_GOLD = Color3.fromRGB(255, 194, 26)

-- (per-tile accent plumbing removed with the plates: callers still pass
-- hueTop/hueBottom harmlessly, but a free-floating glyph has no face to tint --
-- the emoji brings its own colour)

local SideRail = {}

-- ===== idle motion: REMOVED =====
-- The old sway rocked each 3D icon +/-14 degrees every Heartbeat via math.sin
-- -- that was the "shaky" tell the user called out. Icons are flat 2D now and
-- sit perfectly still; ALL motion is hover/press only. No idle driver remains.
-- (idle-sway Heartbeat driver + `spinning` registry deleted -- icons are static)

-- ===== floating rail singleton =====
local railFrame
local function getRail()
	if railFrame and railFrame.Parent then return railFrame end
	local pg = player:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")
	local sg = pg:FindFirstChild("SideRailUI")
	if not sg then
		sg = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
		sg.Name = "SideRailUI"
		sg.ResetOnSpawn = false
		sg.DisplayOrder = 6
		pcall(function() sg.ScreenInsets = Enum.ScreenInsets.CoreUISafeInsets end)
		sg.Parent = pg
	end
	railFrame = sg:FindFirstChild("LeftRail")
	if not railFrame then
		railFrame = Instance.new("Frame")
		railFrame.Name = "LeftRail"
		railFrame.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		railFrame.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0, 0.5)
		railFrame.Position = UDim2.new(0, 18, 0.42, 0)
		railFrame.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(76, 10)
		railFrame.AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y
		railFrame.Parent = sg
		local list = Instance.new("UIListLayout")
		list.FillDirection = Enum.FillDirection.Vertical
		list.HorizontalAlignment = Enum.HorizontalAlignment.Center
		list.SortOrder = Enum.SortOrder.LayoutOrder
		list.Padding = UDim.new(0, 12)
		list.Parent = railFrame
		local scale = Instance.new("UIScale")
		scale.Parent = railFrame
		local cam = workspace.CurrentCamera
		local function upd() if cam then scale.Scale = math.clamp(cam.ViewportSize.Y / 900, 0.8, 1.25) end end
		upd()
		if cam then cam:GetPropertyChangedSignal("ViewportSize"):Connect(upd) end
	end
	-- OFF-SCREEN MUST NOT ANIMATE, whoever hid it. GameHUDClient hides this
	-- frame directly rather than going through updateRailVisibility, so hooking
	-- only our own path missed that case entirely (verified: the suspend never
	-- fired while the rail was folded). Watching the frame's own Visible, plus
	-- the ScreenGui's Enabled, catches every hider including future ones.
	return railFrame
end

-- (3D icon builders removed -- rail icons are flat 2D glyphs now)

-- ===== vector icons =====
-- Escape hatch for slots the emoji set serves badly. The system emoji font
-- draws U+1F381 as an orange lump that does not read as a present at rail size,
-- and no other codepoint is a gift, so Daily is drawn from flat shapes instead.
-- Same visual language as the emoji (flat, saturated, no outline) -- just built
-- rather than typed. A slot with a builder here uses it; everything else falls
-- through to glyphFor().
local VECTOR_ICONS = {}

function VECTOR_ICONS.Daily(parent, z)
	local BOX_LIGHT = Color3.fromRGB(255, 86, 96)
	local BOX_DARK  = Color3.fromRGB(214, 38, 62)
	local GOLD      = Color3.fromRGB(255, 202, 64)

	local function piece(name, colour, anchor, pos, size, zi, radiusScale)
		local f = Instance.new("Frame")
		f.Name = name
		f.AnchorPoint = anchor
		f.Position = pos
		f.Size = size
		f.BackgroundColor3 = colour
		f.BorderSizePixel = 0
		f.ZIndex = zi
		f.Parent = parent
		local c = Instance.new("UICorner")
		c.CornerRadius = UDim.new(radiusScale or 0.12, 0)
		c.Parent = f
		return f
	end

	-- bows first so the lid overlaps their base
	piece("BowL", GOLD, Vector2.new(1, 1), UDim2.fromScale(0.54, 0.28), UDim2.fromScale(0.34, 0.26), z, 1)
	piece("BowR", GOLD, Vector2.new(0, 1), UDim2.fromScale(0.46, 0.28), UDim2.fromScale(0.34, 0.26), z, 1)
	-- body, then the lid sitting proud of it
	piece("Box", BOX_DARK,  Vector2.new(0.5, 0), UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.46), UDim2.fromScale(0.84, 0.48), z + 1, 0.10)
	piece("Lid", BOX_LIGHT, Vector2.new(0.5, 0), UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.26), UDim2.fromScale(1.00, 0.22), z + 2, 0.20)
	-- ribbon runs over lid and body, knot covers where the bows meet
	piece("RibbonV", GOLD, Vector2.new(0.5, 0), UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.26), UDim2.fromScale(0.17, 0.68), z + 3, 0.30)
	piece("Knot",    GOLD, Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5), UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.28), UDim2.fromScale(0.22, 0.22), z + 4, 1)
end

-- ===== icon glyphs =====
-- Keyed by slot NAME rather than iconKind: the kinds were named after the old
-- 3D primitives ("bag", "star") and several described the feature poorly.
-- Backpack in particular rendered as a lidded bin and read as a bin, which is
-- what prompted this pass.
--
-- Deliberately no duplicates: Skip on the right rail already owns the dartboard,
-- so Goals takes a clipboard rather than a second target.
local NAME_GLYPHS = {
	Daily    = "\u{1F381}",   -- wrapped gift
	Goals    = "\u{1F4CB}",   -- clipboard
	Backpack = "\u{1F392}",   -- school satchel: the clearest backpack in the set
	Rebirth  = "\u{2B50}",    -- star
	Index    = "\u{1F4D6}",   -- open book
	Season   = "\u{1F3C6}",   -- trophy
}
-- fallback for any future slot that has no name mapping
local KIND_GLYPHS = {
	gift = "\u{1F381}", target = "\u{1F3AF}", star = "\u{2B50}",
	book = "\u{1F4D6}", trophy = "\u{1F3C6}", bag = "\u{1F392}",
}
local function glyphFor(cfg)
	return cfg.glyph
		or NAME_GLYPHS[cfg.name or ""]
		or KIND_GLYPHS[cfg.iconKind or ""]
		or "\u{2B50}"
end

-- ===== tile factory =====
-- 2026-07-26: the plate is BACK, by user reference image. The previous pass
-- stripped tiles down to a free-floating glyph ("just the icon itself"); the
-- new reference is explicitly the opposite -- a white illustration card with a
-- bold coloured ribbon banner under it, red alert bubble on the corner. That
-- sticker shape is now the whole UI's language (see UIStyle.sticker).
--
-- Callers are UNCHANGED: every one of them already passed name / hueTop /
-- hueBottom, which previously went nowhere ("a free-floating glyph has no face
-- to tint"). Those now drive the ribbon label and its gradient, so the six
-- existing rail buttons pick up the new look without a single call-site edit.
--
-- Handle contract is also unchanged: { button, setReady, setBadge }.
-- ===================== CLAIM PULSE ARBITRATION =====================
-- Every rail client calls setReady on its own tile with no knowledge of the
-- others, so four could breathe at once. Six pulsing buttons reads as noise
-- rather than as a reward, so the decision is made HERE, centrally, where the
-- full set is visible -- no call site changes.
--
-- <= PULSE_MAX claimable: they all pulse.
-- >  PULSE_MAX: only the highest-priority one pulses. The rest keep a STATIC
--    glow, so nothing stops advertising that it is claimable -- it just stops
--    competing for attention.
-- ONE shared driver for every claim pulse, matching the convention
-- UIKit.Builders already uses for its rainbow ring ("ONE Heartbeat total, a
-- registry pruned when the instance is gone") rather than a loop per element.
--
-- Why not a tween, given the round asked for tweens: measured in this place, a
-- TweenService tween on BackgroundTransparency does not run -- the property sits
-- at whatever it was last set to. Frame.Size tweens fine (it drives the quest
-- bar), so this is property-specific, not a broken TweenService. UIScale.Scale,
-- NumberValue.Value and Sound.Volume behave the same way. One registry-driven
-- Heartbeat for the whole rail keeps the cost bounded and, critically, still
-- lets every pulse be stopped dead when the rail folds away.
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
local pulseSet, pulseConn = {}, nil

-- Effective visibility: every GuiObject ancestor Visible, and the ScreenGui
-- Enabled. A hidden ANCESTOR is what folding the rail actually does.
local function isShown(inst)
	local node = inst
	while node and node ~= game do
		if node:IsA("GuiObject") and not node.Visible then return false end
		if node:IsA("ScreenGui") then return node.Enabled end
		node = node.Parent
	end
	return true
end

local function ensurePulseDriver()
	if pulseConn then return end
	pulseConn = RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function()
		local t = os.clock()
		local live = false
		for glow, spec in pairs(pulseSet) do
			if not glow.Parent then
				pulseSet[glow] = nil                 -- gone for good
			else
				live = true
				-- OFF-SCREEN DOES NO WORK. Visibility is decided HERE, per frame,
				-- rather than by hooking whoever hides the rail: GameHUDClient
				-- hides LeftRail directly while SideRail hides it too, and
				-- hooking both made them fight and flip-flop (observed live --
				-- the pulse was cleared several times a second and never showed).
				-- Asking the instance is self-correcting and cannot disagree.
				if glow.Visible and glow:IsDescendantOf(game) and isShown(glow) then
					local a = (math.sin(t * (2 * math.pi / spec.period)) + 1) * 0.5
					glow.BackgroundTransparency = spec.rest + (spec.peak - spec.rest) * a
				elseif glow.BackgroundTransparency ~= spec.rest then
					glow.BackgroundTransparency = spec.rest   -- park it, once
				end
			end
		end
		if not live then
			pulseConn:Disconnect()
			pulseConn = nil
		end
	end)
end

local PULSE_MAX = 3
local CLAIM_PRIORITY = { Daily = 1, Season = 2, Goals = 3, Rebirth = 4 }
local readyTiles = {}   -- [tileName] = { setPulse = fn, ready = bool, legacyGlow = Frame }

-- U3 port: GameHUDClient hides LeftRail permanently, so a claim cue painted on
-- these tiles animates something the player never sees. The visible nav rail
-- attaches a per-button halo here; from then on every claim paint for that
-- tile name lands on the halo instead. Reporters are untouched -- the handle
-- contract does not change.
local REST_ALPHA, PULSE_ALPHA, PULSE_PERIOD = 0.35, 0.62, 1.1
local claimSurfaces = {}   -- [tileName] = GuiObject on the visible rail
local badgeSurfaces = {}   -- [tileName] = fn(kind, n) painting the visible badge

local function arbitrateClaims()
	local ready = {}
	for name, entry in pairs(readyTiles) do
		if entry.ready then ready[#ready + 1] = name end
	end
	table.sort(ready, function(a, b)
		return (CLAIM_PRIORITY[a] or 99) < (CLAIM_PRIORITY[b] or 99)
	end)
	local onlyTop = #ready > PULSE_MAX
	for i, name in ipairs(ready) do
		readyTiles[name].setPulse(not onlyTop or i == 1)
	end
end

-- The visible rail calls this once per button it wants claim cues on. Safe in
-- any order relative to MakeTile: attaching re-applies the tile's current
-- ready state to the new surface, and a tile made later routes to the surface
-- through claimTarget() on its next paint.
function SideRail.attachClaimSurface(name, glow)
	claimSurfaces[name] = glow
	local entry = readyTiles[name]
	if entry then
		-- the legacy glow may still be registered with the pulse driver; retire it
		if entry.legacyGlow then
			pulseSet[entry.legacyGlow] = nil
		end
		glow.Visible = entry.ready == true
		glow.BackgroundTransparency = REST_ALPHA
		arbitrateClaims()
	else
		glow.Visible = false
	end
end

-- Badge twin of attachClaimSurface: the visible rail hands us a paint
-- function (kind, n), and every handle.setBadge for that tile name routes
-- there instead of the hidden tile's own bubble. The last badge is replayed
-- on attach, so a reporter that painted before the HUD rail finished
-- building loses nothing.
function SideRail.attachBadgeSurface(name, paint)
	badgeSurfaces[name] = paint
	local entry = readyTiles[name]
	if entry and entry.lastBadgeKind then
		paint(entry.lastBadgeKind, entry.lastBadgeN)
	end
end

-- Called when the rail folds away behind an open panel. Off-screen elements
-- must not keep animating, and the loops are CANCELLED rather than hidden --
-- a paused-but-live tween is exactly the orphan this is meant to avoid.



function SideRail.MakeTile(cfg)
	local rail = getRail()
	local W, CARD_H, RIBBON_H, OVERLAP = 72, 64, 26, 9

	local accentDark = cfg.hueBottom or PAL.Gold.dark
	local accent = {
		light   = cfg.hueTop or PAL.Gold.light,
		dark    = accentDark,
		outline = accentDark:Lerp(Color3.fromRGB(0, 0, 0), 0.55),
	}

	local slot = Instance.new("Frame")
	slot.Name = (cfg.name or "Rail") .. "Slot"
	slot.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	slot.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(W, CARD_H + RIBBON_H - OVERLAP)
	slot.LayoutOrder = cfg.layoutOrder or 1
	slot.ClipsDescendants = false
	slot.Parent = rail

	-- invisible hit surface covering card + ribbon
	local tile = Instance.new("ImageButton")
	tile.Name = "Tile"
	tile.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
	tile.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)
	tile.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	tile.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	tile.AutoButtonColor = false
	tile.ClipsDescendants = false
	tile.ZIndex = 2
	tile.Parent = slot
	local uiscale = Instance.new("UIScale"); uiscale.Parent = tile

	-- 1. (no drop shadow -- cards sit flat; the white keyline does the work)

	-- 2. white illustration card
	local card = Instance.new("Frame")
	card.Name = "StickerCard"
	card.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0)
	card.Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0, 0)
	card.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(W - 6, CARD_H)
	card.BackgroundColor3 = WHITE
	card.BorderSizePixel = 0
	card.ClipsDescendants = false
	card.ZIndex = 3
	card.Parent = tile
	Instance.new("UICorner", card).CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, 16)
	UIStyle.gradient(card, { light = WHITE, dark = Color3.fromRGB(238, 240, 248) })
	UIStyle.stroke(card, WHITE, 3.5)

	-- 3. claim cue: soft gold halo, behind the icon, inside the card
	local readyGlow = Instance.new("Frame")
	readyGlow.Name = "ReadyGlow"
	readyGlow.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
	readyGlow.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)
	readyGlow.Size = UDim2.fromScale(0.92, 0.92)
	readyGlow.BackgroundColor3 = PAL.Gold.light
	readyGlow.BackgroundTransparency = 0.35
	readyGlow.BorderSizePixel = 0
	readyGlow.Visible = false
	readyGlow.ZIndex = 4
	readyGlow.Parent = card
	Instance.new("UICorner", readyGlow).CornerRadius = UDim.new(1, 0)

	-- 4. the glyph -- a flat emoji, built EXACTLY like UIStyle.sticker builds
	-- the nav cards on the right, so the two rails read as one art style.
	--
	-- This replaces IconForge, which rendered 3D primitives into stacked
	-- ViewportFrames behind a heavy ink silhouette. That technique was built for
	-- free-floating icons against the world; sitting on a white card it made the
	-- left rail look darker and blockier than the right one.
	local icon = Instance.new("Frame")
	icon.Name = "StickerIcon"
	icon.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
	icon.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.44)
	icon.Size = UDim2.fromScale(0.68, 0.68)
	icon.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	icon.ZIndex = 5
	icon.Parent = card
	-- keep it square whatever the card does, so a drawn icon never skews
	local ratio = Instance.new("UIAspectRatioConstraint")
	ratio.AspectRatio = 1
	ratio.Parent = icon

	local drawn = VECTOR_ICONS[cfg.name or ""]
	if drawn then
		drawn(icon, 5)
	else
		local glyph = Instance.new("TextLabel")
		glyph.Name = "Glyph"
		glyph.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
		glyph.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		glyph.ZIndex = 5
		glyph.Font = UIStyle.Fonts.Title
		glyph.TextScaled = true
		glyph.TextColor3 = WHITE      -- emoji carry their own colour; this is only a fallback
		glyph.Text = glyphFor(cfg)
		glyph.Parent = icon
		-- emoji must not be re-coloured or outlined by the game-wide UIPolish sweep
		glyph:SetAttribute("NoPolish", true)
	end

	-- 5. ribbon banner -- wider than the card, overlapping its foot
	local ribbon = Instance.new("Frame")
	ribbon.Name = "StickerRibbon"
	ribbon.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 1)
	ribbon.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 1)
	ribbon.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(W, RIBBON_H)
	ribbon.BackgroundColor3 = accent.light
	ribbon.BorderSizePixel = 0
	ribbon.ZIndex = 9
	ribbon.Parent = tile
	Instance.new("UICorner", ribbon).CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, 9)
	UIStyle.gradient(ribbon, accent)
	UIStyle.stroke(ribbon, WHITE, 3)

	local word = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	word.Name = "StickerLabel"
	word.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
	word.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)
	word.Size = UDim2.new(1, -8, 1, -6)
	word.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	word.Text = string.upper(cfg.label or cfg.name or "")
	word.TextScaled = true
	word.ZIndex = 10
	word.Parent = ribbon
	UIStyle.bubbleText(word, accent)
	local cap = Instance.new("UITextSizeConstraint")
	cap.MaxTextSize = 17
	cap.Parent = word

	-- 6. badge (top-right of the card)
	local badge = Instance.new("Frame")
	badge.Name = "Badge"
	badge.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(1, 0)
	badge.Position = UDim2.new(1, 4, 0, -4)
	badge.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(22, 22)
	badge.BackgroundColor3 = BADGE_RED
	badge.BorderSizePixel = 0
	badge.Visible = false
	badge.ZIndex = 11
	badge.Parent = card
	Instance.new("UICorner", badge).CornerRadius = UDim.new(1, 0)
	-- white rim, matching the sticker keyline (was campfire ink)
	local bstroke = Instance.new("UIStroke")
	bstroke.Thickness = 2.5; bstroke.Color = WHITE; bstroke.Parent = badge
	local blabel = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	blabel.BackgroundTransparency = 1; blabel.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	blabel.Font = UIStyle.Fonts.Title; blabel.TextColor3 = WHITE; blabel.TextScaled = true
	blabel.Text = "!"; blabel.ZIndex = 12; blabel.Parent = badge
	UIStyle.bubbleText(blabel, OUTLINE)
	local bpad = Instance.new("UIPadding")
	bpad.PaddingTop = UDim.new(0, 3); bpad.PaddingBottom = UDim.new(0, 3)
	bpad.PaddingLeft = UDim.new(0, 3); bpad.PaddingRight = UDim.new(0, 3); bpad.Parent = blabel
	local bscale = Instance.new("UIScale"); bscale.Parent = badge

	-- ===== interaction juice =====
	local cur
	local function to(s, t, style, dir)
		if cur then cur:Cancel() end
		cur = TweenService:Create(uiscale, TweenInfo.new(t, style or Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, dir or Enum.EasingDirection.Out), { Scale = s })
		cur:Play()
	end
	tile.MouseEnter:Connect(function() to(1.08, 0.12) end)
	tile.MouseLeave:Connect(function() to(1.0, 0.22, Enum.EasingStyle.Back) end)
	tile.MouseButton1Down:Connect(function() to(0.9, 0.08) end)
	tile.MouseButton1Up:Connect(function() to(1.08, 0.22, Enum.EasingStyle.Back) end)

	-- ===== handle =====
	local handle = { button = tile }
	-- alive pass #1: the claim halo pops in once, then BREATHES until cleared.
	-- 1.6 is UIKit.Tokens' T.tween.pulsePeriod (SideRail deliberately imports no
	-- Tokens); the loop mirrors UIKit.Builders.claimRing exactly.
	-- APPEARS BY FADE, not by pop. The old pop tweened a UIScale, and a
	-- TweenService tween on UIScale.Scale does not run in this place (probed
	-- live: the scale sits at whatever it was set to). A transparency fade is
	-- both what the spec asks for and a GuiObject property, which does tween.
	local key = cfg.name or tostring(slot)
	-- claim paints land on the visible rail's halo once one is attached for
	-- this name (see attachClaimSurface); until then, the legacy readyGlow.
	local function claimTarget()
		return claimSurfaces[key] or readyGlow
	end
	local function setPulse(on)
		local glow = claimTarget()
		if on then
			pulseSet[glow] = { rest = REST_ALPHA, peak = PULSE_ALPHA, period = PULSE_PERIOD }
			ensurePulseDriver()
		else
			pulseSet[glow] = nil                       -- deregistered, not merely paused
			if glow.Visible then
				glow.BackgroundTransparency = REST_ALPHA  -- static, still claimable
			end
		end
	end
	readyTiles[key] = { setPulse = setPulse, ready = false, legacyGlow = readyGlow }

	function handle.setReady(on)
		local entry = readyTiles[key]
		local glow = claimTarget()
		if on == true then
			if not glow.Visible then
				glow.Visible = true
				glow.BackgroundTransparency = REST_ALPHA   -- appears at rest, no pop
			end
			if entry then entry.ready = true end
		else
			setPulse(false)
			glow.BackgroundTransparency = REST_ALPHA
			glow.Visible = false
			if entry then entry.ready = false end
		end
		arbitrateClaims()
	end
	-- alive pass #5: a visible badge whose text CHANGES re-pops (1.25 -> 1);
	-- rapid updates retarget by cancelling the previous tween, never stacking.
	local badgeTween = nil
	function handle.setBadge(kind, n)
		kind = kind or "none"
		-- memo + route: once the visible rail attaches a badge surface it owns
		-- this tile's badge paint; the memo makes a late attach lossless
		local entry = readyTiles[key]
		if entry then entry.lastBadgeKind, entry.lastBadgeN = kind, n end
		local paint = badgeSurfaces[key]
		if paint then paint(kind, n); return end
		if kind == "none" then badge.Visible = false; return end
		local wasVisible = badge.Visible
		local oldText = blabel.Text
		badge.Visible = true
		if kind == "dot" then
			blabel.Text = ""; badge.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(15, 15); badge.BackgroundColor3 = BADGE_RED
		elseif kind == "count" then
			blabel.Text = (n and n > 99) and "99+" or tostring(n or 0); badge.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(22, 22); badge.BackgroundColor3 = BADGE_RED
		elseif kind == "alert" then
			blabel.Text = "!"; badge.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(22, 22); badge.BackgroundColor3 = BADGE_GOLD
		end
		if not wasVisible then
			if badgeTween then badgeTween:Cancel() end
			bscale.Scale = 0
			badgeTween = TweenService:Create(bscale, TweenInfo.new(0.35, Enum.EasingStyle.Back, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), { Scale = 1 })
			badgeTween:Play()
		elseif blabel.Text ~= oldText then
			if badgeTween then badgeTween:Cancel() end
			bscale.Scale = 1.25
			badgeTween = TweenService:Create(bscale, TweenInfo.new(0.25, Enum.EasingStyle.Back, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), { Scale = 1 })
			badgeTween:Play()
		end
	end
	return handle
end

-- ===== single-open coordination =====
-- Rail panels registered here close one another, so only ONE is open at a time.
-- We watch each panel's Visible; when one turns on, the rest turn off. Works no
-- matter how a client toggles it (a raw Visible flag, or UIStyle.popIn which also
-- sets Visible). Hiding the others via Visible=false is enough for every panel.
local railPanels = {}


-- The rail sits at DisplayOrder 6, above every panel, and its cards are wide
-- enough to cover a panel's left-hand column (the Index grid lost a whole
-- column of tiles behind it). Rather than pad every panel, the rail simply
-- gets out of the way: it hides while any registered panel is open and comes
-- back when the last one closes.
local function updateRailVisibility()
	if not (railFrame and railFrame.Parent) then return end
	local anyOpen = false
	for panel in pairs(railPanels) do
		if panel.Parent and panel.Visible then anyOpen = true break end
	end
	railFrame.Visible = not anyOpen
	-- the quest tracker hugs the right edge and overlaps open panels the same
	-- way the rail does, so it folds away with the rail and returns with it
	local pg = player:FindFirstChild("PlayerGui")
	local qt = pg and pg:FindFirstChild("QuestTrackerUI")
	if qt then qt.Enabled = not anyOpen end
end

function SideRail.registerPanel(frame)
	if not frame or railPanels[frame] then return frame end
	railPanels[frame] = true
	frame:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Visible"):Connect(function()
		if frame.Visible then
			for other in pairs(railPanels) do
				if other ~= frame and other.Parent and other.Visible then
					other.Visible = false
				end
			end
		end
		updateRailVisibility()
	end)
	updateRailVisibility()
	return frame
end

return SideRail


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/SoundKit.lua =====
-- SoundKit: every sound effect in the game, in one place.
--
-- Before this there was no audio layer at all -- three stock rbxasset sounds
-- scattered across three scripts, no Sound instances saved, nothing in
-- SoundService. Sounds are declared here BY NAME so a call site never carries
-- an asset id, and changing a sound is a one-line edit instead of a hunt.
--
-- Every id below was verified to actually LOAD in this experience before being
-- added. Roblox gates third-party audio and an unusable id fails SILENTLY --
-- no error, just no sound -- so "it looked right in the code" proves nothing.

local SoundService = game:GetService("SoundService")
local Debris = game:GetService("Debris")
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local ContentProvider = game:GetService("ContentProvider")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")   -- M.loop's stop fade

local M = {}

-- UIKIT (Task 10): per-category volume state, driven by the Settings
-- panel's AUDIO sliders (SettingsPanel -> M.SetCategoryVolume). `sfx` scales
-- every M.play() call (see the Volume line inside M.play below); `music` has
-- no player of its own to scale YET -- this game has no ambient/background
-- music system at all today (SoundService was confirmed to have ZERO
-- children outside what M.play() clones in-and-out, live, before this
-- change) -- so `vol.music` is stored for a future SoundService.Music folder
-- to be scaled by (SetCategoryVolume nil-guards that lookup below), and
-- simply has no audible effect yet. Not a bug: the seam is forward-compatible.
local vol = { music = 0.7, sfx = 1 }

-- Long-lived sounds (music tracks, ambient loops) are NOT M.play() clones, so the
-- sfx multiply inside M.play cannot reach them. Their owners register here and
-- re-apply their own base * scale whenever the slider moves.
local musicListeners = {}
function M.OnMusicVolume(fn)
	if type(fn) ~= "function" then return end
	table.insert(musicListeners, fn)
	pcall(fn, vol.music)   -- fire immediately so a late-loading owner starts correct
end
function M.MusicScale() return vol.music end
function M.SfxScale() return vol.sfx end

-- Same seam for SFX. M.play multiplies vol.sfx into every clone it makes, but a
-- long-lived loop (the lake bed, WheelClient's persistent sounds) is never a
-- clone, so it would ignore the SFX slider entirely without this.
local sfxListeners = {}
function M.OnSfxVolume(fn)
	if type(fn) ~= "function" then return end
	table.insert(sfxListeners, fn)
	pcall(fn, vol.sfx)
end

-- category: "music" | "sfx". v is clamped to 0..1 regardless of input.
function M.SetCategoryVolume(category, v)
	if type(v) ~= "number" or v ~= v then
		warn("[SoundKit] SetCategoryVolume: not a number: " .. tostring(v))
		return
	end
	v = math.clamp(v, 0, 1)
	if category == "music" then
		vol.music = v
		-- MULTIPLIER, not an absolute level. This used to do `s.Volume = v`,
		-- which had two bugs: a 0.5 slider forced every track to 0.5 when
		-- MusicClient's tuned base is 0.15 (3.3x too loud), and because
		-- MusicClient builds a NEW Sound per track, the next track came back at
		-- 0.15 and the setting silently reverted. Each long-lived Sound now
		-- carries its authored level as a BaseVolume attribute and is scaled
		-- against it, so the slider is proportional and idempotent.
		local musicFolder = SoundService:FindFirstChild("Music")
		if musicFolder then
			for _, snd in ipairs(musicFolder:GetChildren()) do
				if snd:IsA("Sound") then
					local base = snd:GetAttribute("BaseVolume")
					if base then snd.Volume = base * v end
				end
			end
		end
		-- Owners that fade their own sounds (MusicClient tweens Volume) cannot be
		-- driven by the loop above -- a tween in flight would overwrite it. They
		-- register here instead and re-apply against their own base.
		for _, fn in ipairs(musicListeners) do
			pcall(fn, v)
		end
	elseif category == "sfx" then
		vol.sfx = v
		for _, fn in ipairs(sfxListeners) do
			pcall(fn, v)
		end
	else
		warn("[SoundKit] SetCategoryVolume: unknown category: " .. tostring(category))
	end
end

-- One template per sound, parented to SoundService so the asset resolves once
-- for the session instead of on every play.
local templates = {}
local function template(name)
	local id = M.Ids[name]
	if not id then
		warn("[SoundKit] unknown sound: " .. tostring(name))
		return nil
	end
	local t = templates[name]
	if not t or not t.Parent then
		t = Instance.new("Sound")
		t.Name = "tpl_" .. name
		t.SoundId = id
		t.Volume = 0
		t.Parent = SoundService
		templates[name] = t
	end
	return t
end

-- Warm every template up front so the first catch of a session is not silent
-- while the asset streams in.
-- Builds every template so the SoundId resolves once per session. This alone is
-- NOT a preload: it creates the instances but never asks the engine to fetch the
-- assets, which is why M.play below has to floor its cleanup delay at
-- math.max(TimeLength, 3) -- TimeLength reads 0 until the asset actually lands.
--
-- ContentProvider:PreloadAsync YIELDS (seconds, over the network), so it is
-- spawned rather than run inline: a caller must never block its own startup on
-- audio. Client-only -- the server has no reason to fetch audio bytes.
function M.preload()
	for name in pairs(M.Ids) do template(name) end
	if not RunService:IsClient() then return end
	if M._preloading or M._preloaded then return end
	M._preloading = true
	task.spawn(function()
		local list = {}
		for name in pairs(M.Ids) do
			local t = templates[name]
			if t then table.insert(list, t) end
		end
		local ok, err = pcall(function()
			ContentProvider:PreloadAsync(list)
		end)
		M._preloading = false
		M._preloaded = ok
		if not ok then
			warn("[SoundKit] PreloadAsync failed: " .. tostring(err))
		end
	end)
end

-- where: nil for a flat 2D sound (UI, or something that happened to YOU),
--        a BasePart or Vector3 to place it in the world so distance applies.
-- opts:  volume, speed, range
function M.play(name, where, opts)
	local t = template(name)
	if not t then return nil end
	opts = opts or {}

	local s = t:Clone()
	s.Name = name
	-- 0.5 was too hot across the board -- feedback was "loud rings". Call sites
	-- should still pass an explicit volume; this default is for quiet incidentals.
	-- UIKIT (Task 10): scaled by the Settings panel's Sound FX slider
	-- (vol.sfx, default 1 = no change) -- every M.play() call site in the
	-- game routes through here, so this one multiply covers all of them.
	s.Volume = (opts.volume or 0.25) * vol.sfx
	s.PlaybackSpeed = opts.speed or 1

	-- TimeLength is 0 until the asset loads, so the cleanup delay needs a floor
	-- or a clone can be destroyed before it has made a sound.
	local life = math.max(t.TimeLength, 3) + 0.5

	if typeof(where) == "Instance" and where:IsA("BasePart") then
		s.RollOffMaxDistance = opts.range or 90
		s.Parent = where
	elseif typeof(where) == "Vector3" then
		local anchor = Instance.new("Part")
		anchor.Anchored = true
		anchor.CanCollide = false
		anchor.CanQuery = false
		anchor.Transparency = 1
		anchor.Size = Vector3.one
		anchor.CFrame = CFrame.new(where)
		anchor.Parent = workspace
		s.RollOffMaxDistance = opts.range or 90
		s.Parent = anchor
		Debris:AddItem(anchor, life)
	else
		s.Parent = SoundService
	end

	s:Play()
	Debris:AddItem(s, life)
	return s
end

-- LOOPS. M.play is fire-and-forget with a Debris lifetime, which is wrong for a
-- charge bed: it must survive an arbitrarily long hold and then stop on command.
-- Same template/clone/volume-scaling path as M.play, so the Settings SFX slider
-- still governs it -- this is a second play SHAPE, not a second audio layer.
--
-- Returns a handle: :setSpeed(n) to drive pitch, :stop(fade) to fade and destroy.
-- stop() is idempotent, so a caller may call it from several teardown paths.
function M.loop(name, opts)
	local t = template(name)
	if not t then return nil end
	opts = opts or {}

	local s = t:Clone()
	s.Name = name .. "_loop"
	s.Looped = true
	s.Volume = (opts.volume or 0.2) * vol.sfx
	s.PlaybackSpeed = opts.speed or 1
	s.Parent = SoundService     -- 2D: this is happening to YOU, not somewhere
	s:Play()

	local handle = { sound = s }
	local stopped = false
	function handle:setSpeed(n)
		if stopped or not s.Parent then return end
		if type(n) ~= "number" or n ~= n then return end
		s.PlaybackSpeed = n
	end
	function handle:stop(fade)
		if stopped then return end
		stopped = true
		if not s.Parent then return end
		fade = fade or 0
		if fade <= 0 then
			s:Destroy()
			return
		end
		TweenService:Create(s, TweenInfo.new(fade), { Volume = 0 }):Play()
		Debris:AddItem(s, fade + 0.05)   -- destroyed even if the tween is interrupted
	end
	return handle
end

-- Play an ARBITRARY asset id, for content-authored audio that cannot live in
-- M.Ids -- specifically BrainrotConfig.VoiceId, which is one id per creature and
-- would mean 161 entries in a table that exists to be a curated palette.
--
-- Deliberately NOT a new volume category: voices are sound effects, so they take
-- vol.sfx exactly like every M.play clone, and the existing SFX slider governs
-- them with no new plumbing.
--
-- Returns the Sound, or nil for a nil/empty id -- so a creature with no VoiceId
-- costs one comparison and nothing else.
function M.playId(assetId, where, opts)
	if type(assetId) ~= "string" or assetId == "" then return nil end
	opts = opts or {}

	local s = Instance.new("Sound")
	s.Name = "voice"
	s.SoundId = assetId
	s.Volume = (opts.volume or 0.25) * vol.sfx
	s.PlaybackSpeed = opts.speed or 1
	s.Looped = false   -- never: a voice line is a one-shot by definition

	-- TimeLength is 0 until the asset resolves, so the cleanup floor mirrors
	-- M.play's. An id that never loads is destroyed on the floor and is silent.
	local life = math.max(s.TimeLength, 4) + 0.5

	if typeof(where) == "Instance" and where:IsA("BasePart") then
		s.RollOffMaxDistance = opts.range or 90
		s.RollOffMode = Enum.RollOffMode.InverseTapered
		s.Parent = where
	else
		s.Parent = SoundService
	end

	s:Play()
	Debris:AddItem(s, life)
	return s
end

return M


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/SupplySchedule.lua =====
-- SupplySchedule: the single source of truth for WHEN each brainrot is catchable.
-- Clock-pure: everything derives from server-synced UTC time + this authored
-- config, so every server and every client independently agrees with no
-- DataStore and no publish.
--   Common/Uncommon: always live.
--   Rare/Epic:       "the Tide" -- a permanent per-name A/B split; even
--                    week-index -> A live, odd -> B. Every name is live at
--                    least every other week, and players can plan around it.
--   Legendary/Mythic: "the Vault" -- seasons retire authored batches forever
--                    (a season's Retire list leaves when the NEXT season
--                    starts, so the whole season is the last-chance window).
--   Secret:          always live but hard-capped (LimitedStock owns the
--                    counts; CAPPED below only tells the UI which names to badge).
-- PRE-LAUNCH DORMANCY: until SEASONS[1].Starts the schedule is inert -- no
-- tide, no countdowns, everything catchable. The game is not public yet, and
-- nothing may retire before the public could ever catch it.
-- Ownership is NEVER gated here: this module answers "can it be CAUGHT now",
-- nothing else.

local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
local BrainrotConfig = require(script.Parent.BrainrotConfig)

local M = {}

local WEEK = 604800

M.SEASONS = {
	{
		-- SET THIS WHEN YOU LAUNCH: the real go-live Monday 00:00 UTC. Until
		-- then it is a far-future placeholder and the whole schedule is DORMANT.
		Starts = 1798761600, -- PLACEHOLDER: 2027-01-01 00:00 UTC
		-- mid-ladder picks, so neither a tier's weakest nor its apex leaves first
		Retire = { "Los Bombinitos", "Los Tacoritas", "Extinct Matteo" },
		Debut = {},
	},
	{
		-- keep exactly 8 weeks (4838400s) after Season 1 when moving the date
		Starts = 1803600000, -- PLACEHOLDER: Season 1 + 8 weeks
		Retire = {},
		Debut = {},
	},
}

-- Names with a hard mint cap (LimitedStock.MAX must list exactly these).
-- Duplicated here as a name SET only, because this module is shared and the
-- counts live server-side.
-- Must stay in exact lockstep with LimitedStock.MAX (a Studio test asserts it).
M.CAPPED = {
	["Secret Pete"] = true,
	["Tralalero Tralala"] = true, ["Los Tralaleritos"] = true,
	["La Vacca Saturno Saturnita"] = true, ["Las Vaquitas Saturnitas"] = true,
	["La Grande Combinasion"] = true, ["Los Combinasionas"] = true,
	["Matteo"] = true, ["Odin Din Din Dun"] = true,
	["Secret Lucky Block"] = true, ["Brainrot God Lucky Block"] = true,
	["Admin Lucky Block"] = true,
}

local TIDE = { Rare = true, Epic = true }

--============================ injectable clock ==============================--
-- Server-synchronised UNIX time on BOTH peers. os.time() on a client reads the
-- DEVICE clock, which players can skew by minutes -- the Index would then
-- disagree with the server near every boundary. GetServerTimeNow is epoch-based
-- and synced for clients, and equals wall time on the server.
local function realNow()
	return workspace:GetServerTimeNow()
end
local now = realNow
-- Studio-only: tests step the clock across week and season boundaries instead
-- of waiting eight weeks. A nil fn restores the real clock.
function M.SetClock(fn)
	if RunService:IsStudio() then
		now = fn or realNow
	end
end

--=============================== authored maps ==============================--
local entryByName = {}
for _, e in ipairs(BrainrotConfig) do
	entryByName[e.Name] = e
end

local debutSeasonOf = {}   -- [name] = season index it debuts in
local retireSeasonOf = {}  -- [name] = season index whose END retires it
for k, season in ipairs(M.SEASONS) do
	for _, n in ipairs(season.Debut) do debutSeasonOf[n] = k end
	for _, n in ipairs(season.Retire) do retireSeasonOf[n] = k end
end

-- A retire list needs a NEXT season to define when it triggers; the final
-- authored season's Retire can never fire. Loud, because silently-immortal
-- "retirements" would be a lie in the Index.
if #M.SEASONS[#M.SEASONS].Retire > 0 then
	warn("[SupplySchedule] the final season's Retire list can never trigger -- author the next season row")
end

--============================== time helpers ================================--
local function seasonIndexAt(t)
	local idx = 1
	for k, season in ipairs(M.SEASONS) do
		if t >= season.Starts then idx = k end
	end
	return idx
end

-- A season "has ended" only when a NEXT season exists and has started; the
-- final authored season never ends (the schedule holds its final state).
local function seasonEndedAt(k, t)
	local nextSeason = M.SEASONS[k + 1]
	return nextSeason ~= nil and t >= nextSeason.Starts
end

local function weekIndexAt(t)
	return math.max(0, math.floor((t - M.SEASONS[1].Starts) / WEEK))
end

--================================ the tide ==================================--
-- Split membership is PER-NAME and PERMANENT, from a hash of the name alone.
-- Two rejected alternatives, both review-killed:
--   * per-season reshuffle -- at every season boundary ~half the away names
--     land away AGAIN (14 straight days), breaking the "live at least every
--     other week" guarantee and falsifying every RETURNS timestamp;
--   * positional shuffle over the roster -- appending ONE config entry moves
--     EXISTING names between sets mid-week.
-- djb2 folded mod a prime (the exact shape MintRegistry already ships): every
-- intermediate stays far below 2^53, so double math is exact and the answer is
-- identical on every client and server, forever.
local function inSetA(name)
	local h = 5381
	for i = 1, #name do
		h = (h * 33 + string.byte(name, i)) % 4294967291
	end
	return h % 2 == 0
end

--================================ public API ================================--

-- status, changeAt. Precedence: unreleased > vaulted > retiring > away >
-- capped > live. Sold-out is deliberately NOT a status here: this module is
-- clock-pure and shared; sold-out truth lives server-side in LimitedStock.
function M.StatusOf(name)
	local entry = entryByName[name]
	if not entry then return nil, nil end
	local t = now()
	local curIdx = seasonIndexAt(t)

	local debutIdx = debutSeasonOf[name]
	if debutIdx and t < M.SEASONS[debutIdx].Starts then
		return "unreleased", M.SEASONS[debutIdx].Starts
	end

	-- Pre-launch dormancy: until Season 1's authored start, the schedule is
	-- inert -- no tide, no countdowns, everything catchable (caps still shown).
	-- Sits AFTER the unreleased check so future debuts stay hidden pre-launch.
	if t < M.SEASONS[1].Starts then
		return M.CAPPED[name] and "capped" or "live", nil
	end

	local retireIdx = retireSeasonOf[name]
	if retireIdx then
		if seasonEndedAt(retireIdx, t) then
			return "vaulted", M.SEASONS[retireIdx + 1].Starts
		end
		if retireIdx == curIdx and M.SEASONS[curIdx + 1] then
			return "retiring", M.SEASONS[curIdx + 1].Starts
		end
	end

	if TIDE[entry.Rarity] then
		local wk = weekIndexAt(t)
		local wantA = (wk % 2 == 0)
		-- With a permanent split, "next flip" is always the true return time.
		if inSetA(name) ~= wantA then
			return "away", M.SEASONS[1].Starts + (wk + 1) * WEEK
		end
	end

	if M.CAPPED[name] then
		return "capped", nil
	end
	return "live", nil
end

function M.IsObtainable(name)
	local status = M.StatusOf(name)
	return status == "live" or status == "capped" or status == "retiring"
end

-- Unix time of the next instant ANY availability can change: the sooner of the
-- next tide flip and the next season boundary. For countdown UI.
function M.NextChange()
	local t = now()
	local nextFlip = M.SEASONS[1].Starts + (weekIndexAt(t) + 1) * WEEK
	for _, season in ipairs(M.SEASONS) do
		if season.Starts > t and season.Starts < nextFlip then
			nextFlip = season.Starts
		end
	end
	return nextFlip
end

-- Changes exactly when the answer of IsObtainable can change. RarityRoll keys
-- its pool cache on this so pools rebuild at boundaries and never in between.
function M.PeriodKey()
	local t = now()
	if t < M.SEASONS[1].Starts then return "pre" end
	return seasonIndexAt(t) .. ":" .. weekIndexAt(t) % 2
end

-- live, total -- for the Index header.
function M.Counts()
	local live = 0
	for _, e in ipairs(BrainrotConfig) do
		if M.IsObtainable(e.Name) then live += 1 end
	end
	return live, #BrainrotConfig
end

return M

===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/UIKit/Builders.lua =====
--!strict
-- ui_builders.lua — the five primitives this style needs, so panels stay short.
-- Reproduces: thick outline, hard offset shadow, vertical gradient, top gloss,
-- bottom shade, stroked display text, inset track.
--
-- local UI = require(script.Parent.ui_builders)
-- local panel = UI.panel(parent, UDim2.fromOffset(960, 566))
-- local btn   = UI.button(panel, "Claim", "green", UDim2.fromOffset(136, 60))

local T = require(script.Parent.Tokens)
-- SoundKit is a LEAF (requires no module) and UIKit is never required server-side,
-- so this cannot cycle. Same SfxWired attribute key UITheme/UIStyle use, so a button
-- built here and restyled elsewhere still gets exactly ONE click connection.
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
local SoundKit = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("Modules"):WaitForChild("SoundKit"))
local CLICK_VOLUME = 0.12
local function wireClick(btn: GuiButton, soundName: string?)
	if not RunService:IsClient() then return end
	if btn:GetAttribute("SfxWired") then return end
	btn:SetAttribute("SfxWired", true)
	btn.MouseButton1Click:Connect(function()
		pcall(SoundKit.play, soundName or "uiClick", nil, { volume = CLICK_VOLUME })
	end)
end

local UI = {}

function UI.corner(parent: Instance, radius: number): UICorner
	local c = Instance.new("UICorner")
	c.CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, radius)
	c.Parent = parent
	return c
end

function UI.stroke(parent: Instance, thickness: number?): UIStroke
	local s = Instance.new("UIStroke")
	s.Thickness = thickness or T.stroke.control
	s.Color = T.color.outline
	s.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Border
	s.LineJoinMode = Enum.LineJoinMode.Round
	s.Parent = parent
	return s
end

function UI.gradient(parent: Instance, colorSequence: ColorSequence): UIGradient
	local g = Instance.new("UIGradient")
	g.Color = colorSequence
	g.Rotation = 90 -- top -> bottom
	g.Parent = parent
	return g
end

--[[ GLOSS AND SHADE ARE RETIRED (2026-08-06, user call).

This used to draw a white strip along the top edge of a surface and a dark strip
along the bottom, on all 68 elements that pass through here. Because both were
full-width and pinned flush to the edge, on a rounded host they overhung the
curve and rendered as pale bars sitting proud of the shape -- worst on the
currency pills, which are stadiums ~37px round while the gloss was a 6px strip
whose own corner clamped to 3px.

I first fixed that by clipping both strips to the host's silhouette, which did
work. The user's call on seeing it was that the banding itself is the problem,
not where its edges land -- so the strips are gone rather than contained. The
surfaces keep their UIGradient, which is what actually gives them their form.

Every caller that looks the strips up by name guards with `if gloss then` -- the
cash pill, the egg shop's open button, toasts, the throw frame and button, the
rail's legacy sweep. Checked all six; they simply skip now.
]]
function UI.gloss(frame: GuiObject, _radius: number?, _lightAlpha: number?)
	-- Nothing is drawn. See the note above.
	--
	-- Still a FUNCTION, not deleted: 20 scripts call it, and it now does the
	-- useful job of TAKING DOWN strips on any instance that already has them --
	-- a reused element, or one built before this change.
	for _, n in ipairs({ "GlossClip", "Gloss", "Shade" }) do
		local old = frame:FindFirstChild(n)
		if old then old:Destroy() end
	end
end

-- The hard cartoon shadow: a copy of the shape, outline-coloured, pushed down Y.
-- Returns the wrapper you should parent siblings to; `frame` stays the visual surface.
function UI.hardShadow(frame: GuiObject, offsetY: number, radius: number): Frame
	local sh = Instance.new("Frame")
	sh.Name = "HardShadow"
	sh.Size = frame.Size
	sh.Position = frame.Position + UDim2.fromOffset(0, offsetY)
	sh.AnchorPoint = frame.AnchorPoint
	sh.BackgroundColor3 = T.color.outline
	sh.BorderSizePixel = 0
	sh.ZIndex = frame.ZIndex - 1
	sh.Parent = frame.Parent
	UI.corner(sh, radius)

	-- FIX F2 (2026-07-30 fix wave): shadow FOLLOWS its frame. UI.button (and
	-- every panel) calls UI.hardShadow at creation time, before the caller
	-- repositions the frame (the mandatory two-step pattern: `local f = ...;
	-- f.Position = ...` set AFTER construction) -- so the shadow captured
	-- above at the frame's creation-time Position/AnchorPoint would otherwise
	-- be stranded wherever `frame` originally sat, visible as a dark offset
	-- block under every panel's close button, the Pass quests button, and the
	-- Goals/Settings segment buttons. Three connections per shadow is fine --
	-- shadows are few. No double-offset risk: sh.Position is already set to
	-- frame.Position + offset above, so if Position never changes these
	-- handlers simply never fire and the initial value stands untouched.
	frame:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Position"):Connect(function()
		sh.Position = frame.Position + UDim2.fromOffset(0, offsetY)
	end)
	frame:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AnchorPoint"):Connect(function()
		sh.AnchorPoint = frame.AnchorPoint
	end)
	frame.Destroying:Connect(function()
		sh:Destroy()
	end)

	return sh
end

-- Display text. `styleKey` indexes T.text.
-- LemonPop 2026-08-13: the stroke follows the FILL, not the style spec alone
-- -- light type (white/gold, i.e. sitting on a dark or saturated ground)
-- keeps the heavy outline; dark ink (the light-surface default) carries
-- itself unstroked. Luminance decides, same trick as UITheme.campButton.
local function lum(c: Color3): number
	return 0.2126 * c.R + 0.7152 * c.G + 0.0722 * c.B
end
function UI.label(parent: Instance, text: string, styleKey: string, color: Color3?): TextLabel
	local spec = T.text[styleKey]
	local l = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	l.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	l.Text = text
	l.TextColor3 = color or T.color.white
	l.TextSize = spec[1]
	l.FontFace = if styleKey == "meta" then T.font.ui else T.font.display
	l.RichText = false
	l.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left
	l.AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.XY
	l.Parent = parent
	if spec[2] > 0 and lum(l.TextColor3) > 0.5 then
		local s = Instance.new("UIStroke")
		s.Thickness = spec[2]
		s.Color = T.color.outline
		s.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Contextual
		s.LineJoinMode = Enum.LineJoinMode.Round
		s.Parent = l
	end
	return l
end

-- Panel / card surface. kind: "panel" | "subPanel" | "row" | "slot" | "tab" | "track"
-- LemonPop: the kit's light grounds; every other kind is treated as dark/saturated
local LIGHT_KINDS = {
	panel = true, subPanel = true, slot = true, window = true, cream = true,
	freeCard = true, lockBadge = true, knob = true, passCard = true,
}
function UI.surface(parent: Instance, size: UDim2, kind: string, radius: number?, strokeW: number?): Frame
	local f = Instance.new("Frame")
	f.Size = size
	f.BackgroundColor3 = T.color.white
	f.BorderSizePixel = 0
	f.Parent = parent
	local r = radius or T.radius.panel
	UI.corner(f, r)
	UI.gradient(f, T.gradient[kind])
	UI.stroke(f, strokeW or T.stroke.panel)
	-- LemonPop 2026-08-13: any surface that is not one of the kit's LIGHT
	-- grounds is dark or saturated (rows, tracks, tabs, the red header, and
	-- the action-gradient kinds panels use for header bars) -- tag it once and
	-- UIPolish gives every label inside the white stroked on-dark treatment;
	-- light surfaces default to dark unstroked ink.
	if not LIGHT_KINDS[kind] then
		f:SetAttribute("PolishOnDark", true)
	end
	return f
end

function UI.panel(parent: Instance, size: UDim2): Frame
	local f = UI.surface(parent, size, "panel", T.radius.panel, T.stroke.panel)
	UI.hardShadow(f, T.shadowOffset.panel, T.radius.panel)
	local p = Instance.new("UIPadding")
	p.PaddingTop = UDim.new(0, T.pad.panel)
	p.PaddingBottom = UDim.new(0, T.pad.panel)
	p.PaddingLeft = UDim.new(0, T.pad.panel)
	p.PaddingRight = UDim.new(0, T.pad.panel)
	p.Parent = f
	return f
end

-- variant: "gold" | "goldSmall" | "green" | "purple" | "red" | "blue" | "disabled" | "tab"
function UI.button(parent: Instance, text: string, variant: string, size: UDim2, styleKey: string?): TextButton
	local b = Instance.new("TextButton")
	b.Size = size
	b.Text = ""
	b.AutoButtonColor = false
	b.BackgroundColor3 = T.color.white
	b.BorderSizePixel = 0
	b.Active = variant ~= "disabled"
	b.Parent = parent
	-- LemonPop 2026-08-13: action gradients are saturated grounds -- their
	-- labels keep the white stroked treatment (see UIPolish PolishOnDark)
	b:SetAttribute("PolishOnDark", true)
	UI.corner(b, T.radius.control)
	UI.gradient(b, T.gradient[variant])
	UI.stroke(b, T.stroke.control)
	if variant ~= "disabled" then
		UI.gloss(b, T.radius.control)
		UI.hardShadow(b, T.shadowOffset.control, T.radius.control)
	end
	local l = UI.label(b, text, styleKey or "buttonM",
		if variant == "disabled" then T.color.textDisabled else T.color.white)
	l.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	l.AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.None
	l.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Center
	l.ZIndex = 3

	-- hover / press
	-- Rest position captured LAZILY (state machine below), not at creation:
	-- UI.button doesn't take a position parameter, so every caller's mandatory
	-- pattern is `local btn = UI.button(...); btn.Position = ...` -- set AFTER
	-- this function returns. Capturing `b.Position` here (as this used to do)
	-- froze `base` at the TextButton default (0,0) before the caller ever
	-- repositioned it, so the first hover/press tween dragged the button back
	-- toward (0,0)-ish. Instead: capture `rest` on first MouseEnter, by which
	-- point the caller has always already set the real Position. Same fix as
	-- GameHUDClient's nav-rail basePos() (~line 528).
	-- Known limitation: if a caller repositions the button again WHILE it is
	-- already hovered/pressed, `rest` is not invalidated (no cheap way to
	-- detect external repositioning) -- that one tween will animate off the
	-- stale `rest` instead of the new position. Considered acceptable: no
	-- caller in this codebase repositions buttons post-hover today.
	local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
	local rest = nil
	local hovered, pressed = false, false
	if variant ~= "disabled" then
		b.MouseEnter:Connect(function()
			if not hovered and not pressed then
				rest = b.Position
			end
			hovered = true
			TweenService:Create(b, T.tween.hover, { Position = rest - UDim2.fromOffset(0, 2) }):Play()
		end)
		b.MouseLeave:Connect(function()
			hovered = false
			TweenService:Create(b, T.tween.hover, { Position = rest }):Play()
		end)
		b.MouseButton1Down:Connect(function()
			pressed = true
			TweenService:Create(b, T.tween.press, { Position = rest + UDim2.fromOffset(0, 2) }):Play()
		end)
		b.MouseButton1Up:Connect(function()
			pressed = false
			TweenService:Create(b, T.tween.press, {
				Position = if hovered then rest - UDim2.fromOffset(0, 2) else rest,
			}):Play()
		end)
	end
	-- disabled variants stay silent: a dead control that clicks reads as a bug
	if variant ~= "disabled" then wireClick(b, "uiClick") end
	return b
end

-- Inset progress track + fill. Returns (track, fill). Drive with UI.setFill.
function UI.track(parent: Instance, size: UDim2, fillVariant: string, radius: number?): (Frame, Frame)
	local r = radius or T.radius.inner
	local t = UI.surface(parent, size, "track", r, T.stroke.control)
	t.ClipsDescendants = true

	local inset = Instance.new("Frame") -- inner top shadow
	inset.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 4)
	inset.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.new(0, 0, 0)
	inset.BackgroundTransparency = 0.45
	inset.BorderSizePixel = 0
	inset.ZIndex = 2
	inset.Parent = t

	local fill = Instance.new("Frame")
	fill.Size = UDim2.new(0, 0, 1, 0)
	fill.BackgroundColor3 = T.color.white
	fill.BorderSizePixel = 0
	fill.ZIndex = 1
	fill.Parent = t
	UI.corner(fill, r)
	UI.gradient(fill, T.gradient[fillVariant])
	return t, fill
end

function UI.setFill(fill: Frame, pct: number, animate: boolean?)
	local goal = UDim2.new(math.clamp(pct, 0, 1), 0, 1, 0)
	if animate then
		game:GetService("TweenService"):Create(fill, T.tween.bar, { Size = goal }):Play()
	else
		fill.Size = goal
	end
end

-- 4px inner rarity frame + inner glow. rarity: "common" | "rare" | "epic" | "legend"
function UI.rarityFrame(slot: GuiObject, rarity: string): Frame

------------------------------------------------------------------- additions
-- README-specified builders, missing from the vendored kit file. Same shared-
-- driver convention as ReplicatedStorage.Modules.RarityFX: ONE Heartbeat total,
-- a registry pruned when the instance is gone, instead of a connection per ring.

local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local ringActive, ringConn, ringClock = {}, nil, 0

local function ensureRingDriver()
	if ringConn then return end
	ringConn = RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(dt)
		ringClock += dt
		for i = #ringActive, 1, -1 do
			local e = ringActive[i]
			if not e.ring.Parent then
				table.remove(ringActive, i) -- ring destroyed by a rebuild/close
			else
				e.gradient.Rotation = (ringClock / 6 * 360 + e.phase) % 360
			end
		end
		if #ringActive == 0 then ringConn:Disconnect(); ringConn = nil end
	end)
end

-- Rainbow cycling ring around `card`. No texture asset exists yet, so this is a
-- Frame + UIStroke + UIGradient fallback (an ImageLabel ring texture can replace
-- it later without changing the call site). Rotation sweeps 0->360 over 6s.
function UI.rainbowRing(card: GuiObject, radius: number?): Frame
	local ring = Instance.new("Frame")
	ring.Name = "RainbowRing"
	ring.Size = UDim2.new(1, 10, 1, 10)
	ring.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(-5, -5)
	ring.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	ring.ZIndex = (card.ZIndex or 1) + 1
	ring.Parent = card
	UI.corner(ring, radius or T.radius.control)

	local stroke = Instance.new("UIStroke")
	stroke.Thickness = 5
	stroke.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Border
	stroke.LineJoinMode = Enum.LineJoinMode.Round
	stroke.Parent = ring

	local gradient = Instance.new("UIGradient")
	gradient.Color = ColorSequence.new({
		ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0,    T.hex("#FF5252")),
		ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0.25, T.hex("#FFB200")),
		ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0.5,  T.hex("#7CE04A")),
		ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0.75, T.hex("#3FA9F5")),
		ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(1,    T.hex("#A855F7")),
	})
	gradient.Parent = stroke

	ringActive[#ringActive + 1] = { ring = ring, gradient = gradient, phase = 0 }
	ensureRingDriver()
	return ring
end

	return b
end

-- Small pill tag on a card corner. variant: "EQUIPPED" | "GRAND" | "NEW".
local RIBBON_VARIANT = {
	EQUIPPED = "green",
	GRAND = "purple",
	NEW = "red",
}

function UI.ribbon(parent: Instance, text: string, variant: string): Frame
	local grad = RIBBON_VARIANT[variant] or "green"
	local r = Instance.new("Frame")
	r.Name = "Ribbon"
	r.AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.X
	r.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(0, 24)
	r.BackgroundColor3 = T.color.white
	r.BorderSizePixel = 0
	r.ZIndex = 10
	r.Parent = parent
	r:SetAttribute("PolishOnDark", true) -- LemonPop: ribbon gradients = saturated grounds, white stroked label
	UI.corner(r, T.radius.chip)
	UI.gradient(r, T.gradient[grad])
	UI.stroke(r, T.stroke.chip)

	local pad = Instance.new("UIPadding")
	pad.PaddingLeft = UDim.new(0, 10)
	pad.PaddingRight = UDim.new(0, 10)
	pad.Parent = r

	local l = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	l.Name = "Text"
	l.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	l.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	l.Text = text
	l.TextColor3 = T.color.white
	l.TextSize = T.text.chip[1]
	l.FontFace = T.font.ui
	l.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Center
	l.TextYAlignment = Enum.TextYAlignment.Center
	l.ZIndex = 11
	l.Parent = r
	if T.text.chip[2] > 0 then
		local s = Instance.new("UIStroke")
		s.Thickness = T.text.chip[2]
		s.Color = T.color.outline
		s.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Contextual
		s.Parent = l
	end

	return r
end

return UI


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/UIKit/IconArt.lua =====
--!strict
--[[ =========================================================================
IconArt -- the design kit's nav icons, rebuilt from Roblox GUI primitives.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
WHY THIS EXISTS. The kit ships each icon as an SVG (docs/design-handoff/
ui-kit/design_handoff_game_ui/icons/*.svg) plus a 512px PNG. Turning those
PNGs into Roblox image assets is still a pending user step -- and
AssetService:CreateAssetAsync is not available in this Studio session -- so
until real asset ids exist the rail would show empty slots. Rather than a
placeholder, this module redraws the SAME artwork out of Frames, straight
from the SVG geometry, so the rail matches captures/hud.png today.

The SHAPES table below is a transcription of those SVGs, in SVG user units,
in paint order. When real ids do land, nothing here needs deleting: the rail
prefers T.icons[id] whenever it is a non-empty string and only falls back to
IconArt.draw.

HOW THE KIT DRAWS. Every icon SVG paints twice. Pass 1 repeats each shape in
#16170F with stroke-width 9 (16/17 on stroked paths), which fattens it by 4.5
units on every side and produces the chunky dark keyline the style depends on.
Pass 2 paints the same shapes in colour on top. draw() reproduces exactly
that: every shape flagged `outline` is drawn once expanded by EXPAND in
keyline black, then all shapes are drawn again in colour. Doing it as a
separate pass -- rather than a UIStroke per shape -- is what keeps the keyline
on the icon's OUTER silhouette instead of drawing a seam between every pair of
touching shapes (e.g. the bag's flap against its body).

COORDINATES. Every icon uses viewBox "-5 -5 74 74": the drawable area spans
-5..69 on both axes, so a coordinate maps to pixels as (v + 5) * size / 74.
Y grows downward, matching both SVG and Roblox.
========================================================================= ]]

local IconArt = {}

local VB_MIN = -5   -- viewBox origin on both axes
local VB_SPAN = 74  -- viewBox width/height
local EXPAND = 4.5  -- half the kit's stroke-width 9 keyline, in SVG units
local KEYLINE = Color3.fromHex("#16170F")

--[[ Shape types the renderer understands:
  rect   x, y, w, h, r          -- r = corner radius, 0 = square
  circle cx, cy, radius
  bar    x1, y1, x2, y2, t      -- straight stroked segment, round caps
  arch   x1, x2, yTop, yBottom, t -- upside-down U, e.g. the bag handle
  star   cx, cy, outerRadius    -- 5-pointed star (drawn as a glyph)
Shared optional fields:
  rot / pivotX / pivotY   degrees clockwise, about a point (SVG rotate(a px py));
                          without a pivot the shape spins about its own centre
  fill                    flat colour
  gradTop / gradBottom    vertical gradient (used instead of fill)
  gradFixed               keep the gradient vertical on screen even though the
                          shape is rotated. Needed when the rotation is OUR
                          implementation detail rather than the kit's: the kit
                          rotates a gradient along with its shape (the pass
                          ticket), but a diamond we happen to build out of a
                          rotated square must still shade top-to-bottom.
  strokeColor/strokeWidth an inner stroke the COLOURED shape itself carries
  opacity                 0..1, default 1
  clip {x1,y1,x2,y2}      render inside this window -- how a rect gets two
                          rounded and two square corners, as several kit paths do
  outline                 true if the shape had a pass-1 dark duplicate
]]
