---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
local function rotAbout(pivotX: number, pivotY: number, x: number, y: number, deg: number): (number, number)
	if deg == 0 then return x, y end
	local rad = math.rad(deg)
	local c, s = math.cos(rad), math.sin(rad)
	local dx, dy = x - pivotX, y - pivotY
	-- y grows downward here, so this is a clockwise rotation for positive deg --
	-- matching both SVG's rotate() and Roblox's GuiObject.Rotation.
	return pivotX + dx * c - dy * s, pivotY + dx * s + dy * c
end

local function corner(inst: GuiObject, radiusPx: number)
	local c = Instance.new("UICorner")
	c.CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, math.max(radiusPx, 0))
	c.Parent = inst
end

local function paint(f: GuiObject, sh, dark: boolean, scale: number)
	if dark then
		f.BackgroundColor3 = KEYLINE
		f.BackgroundTransparency = 0
		return
	end
	if sh.gradTop and sh.gradBottom then
		f.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
		local g = Instance.new("UIGradient")
		g.Color = ColorSequence.new(Color3.fromHex(sh.gradTop), Color3.fromHex(sh.gradBottom))
		-- 90 = top -> bottom. A UIGradient rotates with its frame, which is what
		-- the kit wants for a rotated shape -- unless the rotation is ours, in
		-- which case cancel it back out.
		g.Rotation = if sh.gradFixed then 90 - (sh.rot or 0) else 90
		g.Parent = f
	else
		f.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromHex(sh.fill or "#FFFFFF")
	end
	if sh.opacity then
		f.BackgroundTransparency = 1 - sh.opacity
	end
	if sh.strokeColor and sh.strokeWidth then
		local st = Instance.new("UIStroke")
		st.Color = Color3.fromHex(sh.strokeColor)
		-- SVG centres a stroke on the edge; UIStroke draws it entirely outside,
		-- so half the nominal width reproduces the outer half we can see.
		st.Thickness = math.max(sh.strokeWidth * 0.5 * scale, 1)
		st.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Border
		st.LineJoinMode = Enum.LineJoinMode.Round
		st.Parent = f
	end
end

---------------------------------------------------------------- renderer
-- Draws one shape. `e` is the outward expansion in SVG units: EXPAND for the
-- keyline pass, 0 for the colour pass.
local function drawShape(root: GuiObject, scale: number, sh, e: number, dark: boolean, z: number)
	local function px(v: number): number return (v - VB_MIN) * scale end
	local function len(v: number): number return v * scale end

	-- A clipped shape lives inside its own ClipsDescendants frame, so positions
	-- inside it are relative to that frame's top-left.
	local host, ox, oy = root, 0, 0
	local function openClip(x1: number, y1: number, x2: number, y2: number)
		local c = Instance.new("Frame")
		c.Name = "Clip"
		c.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		c.BorderSizePixel = 0
		c.ClipsDescendants = true
		c.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(px(x1), px(y1))
		c.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(len(x2 - x1), len(y2 - y1))
		c.ZIndex = z
		c.Parent = root
		host, ox, oy = c, px(x1), px(y1)
	end

	if sh.clip then
		-- widen the window with the shape, so the keyline pass is not shaved
		openClip(sh.clip[1] - e, sh.clip[2] - e, sh.clip[3] + e, sh.clip[4] + e)
	end

	local function place(cx: number, cy: number, w: number, h: number, rot: number): Frame
		local f = Instance.new("Frame")
		f.BorderSizePixel = 0
		f.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5) -- Rotation pivots on the anchor, so centre it
		f.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(px(cx) - ox, px(cy) - oy)
		f.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(len(w), len(h))
		f.Rotation = rot
		f.ZIndex = z
		f.Parent = host
		return f
	end

	local kind = sh.type

	if kind == "rect" then
		local x, y = sh.x - e, sh.y - e
		local w, h = sh.w + 2 * e, sh.h + 2 * e
		local cx, cy = x + w * 0.5, y + h * 0.5
		local rot = sh.rot or 0
		if sh.pivotX then
			cx, cy = rotAbout(sh.pivotX, sh.pivotY, cx, cy, rot)
		end
		local f = place(cx, cy, w, h, rot)
		local r = sh.r or 0
		if r > 0 then corner(f, len(r + e)) end
		paint(f, sh, dark, scale)

	elseif kind == "circle" then
		local radius = sh.radius + e
		local f = place(sh.cx, sh.cy, radius * 2, radius * 2, 0)
		corner(f, len(radius))
		paint(f, sh, dark, scale)

	elseif kind == "bar" then
		local t = sh.t + 2 * e
		local dx, dy = sh.x2 - sh.x1, sh.y2 - sh.y1
		local length = math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy)
		-- round caps overhang each end by t/2, so the capsule is length + t long
		local f = place((sh.x1 + sh.x2) * 0.5, (sh.y1 + sh.y2) * 0.5, length + t, t, math.deg(math.atan2(dy, dx)))
		corner(f, len(t * 0.5))
		paint(f, sh, dark, scale)

	elseif kind == "arch" then
		-- An upside-down U: a capsule outline whose bottom half is clipped away.
		-- The ring is inset by t/2 so its OUTSIDE-drawn UIStroke lands centred on
		-- the path, the way an SVG stroke would.
		local t = sh.t + 2 * e
		local ringX, ringW = sh.x1 + t * 0.5, (sh.x2 - sh.x1) - t
		local ringTop = sh.yTop + t * 0.5
		local ringH = 2 * (sh.yBottom - ringTop)
		if ringW > 0 and ringH > 0 then
			local saveHost, saveOx, saveOy = host, ox, oy
			openClip(sh.x1 - t * 0.5, sh.yTop - t * 0.5, sh.x2 + t * 0.5, sh.yBottom)
			local ring = Instance.new("Frame")
			ring.BorderSizePixel = 0
			ring.BackgroundTransparency = 1
			ring.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(px(ringX) - ox, px(ringTop) - oy)
			ring.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(len(ringW), len(ringH))
			ring.ZIndex = z
			ring.Parent = host
			corner(ring, len(math.min(ringW, ringH) * 0.5))
			local st = Instance.new("UIStroke")
			st.Color = dark and KEYLINE or Color3.fromHex(sh.fill or "#FFFFFF")
			st.Thickness = math.max(len(t), 1)
			st.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Border
			st.LineJoinMode = Enum.LineJoinMode.Round
			st.Parent = ring
			host, ox, oy = saveHost, saveOx, saveOy
		end

	elseif kind == "star" then
		-- No polygon primitive in Roblox GUI, so the star is a glyph. The keyline
		-- pass draws a larger black star behind the gold one, which reads as the
		-- same outline the other shapes get.
		local radius = sh.outerRadius + e
		local cx, cy = sh.cx, sh.cy
		local rot = sh.rot or 0
		if sh.pivotX then
			cx, cy = rotAbout(sh.pivotX, sh.pivotY, cx, cy, rot)
		end
		local l = Instance.new("TextLabel")
		l.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		l.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
		l.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(px(cx) - ox, px(cy) - oy)
		l.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(len(radius * 2), len(radius * 2))
		l.Rotation = rot
		l.Text = "\u{2605}" -- BLACK STAR: a plain dingbat, not an emoji
		l.TextScaled = true
		l.RichText = false
		l.TextColor3 = if dark then KEYLINE else Color3.fromHex(sh.gradTop or sh.fill or "#FFFFFF")
		l.ZIndex = z
		l.Parent = host
		if not dark and sh.gradTop and sh.gradBottom then
			local g = Instance.new("UIGradient")
			g.Color = ColorSequence.new(Color3.fromHex(sh.gradTop), Color3.fromHex(sh.gradBottom))
			g.Rotation = 90
			g.Parent = l
		end
	end
end

--[[ Draws `name` into `parent` at `size` px square, based at ZIndex `zBase`.
Returns the container Frame, or nil for an unknown name. The container is
inert -- transparent, no input -- so callers keep owning hit-testing. ]]
function IconArt.draw(parent: GuiObject, name: string, size: number, zBase: number): Frame?
	local shapes = IconArt.SHAPES[name]
	if not shapes then return nil end

	local scale = size / VB_SPAN
	local root = Instance.new("Frame")
	root.Name = "IconArt_" .. name
	root.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	root.BorderSizePixel = 0
	root.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(size, size)
	root.ZIndex = zBase
	root.Parent = parent

	-- pass 1: the dark keyline, every outlined shape fattened by EXPAND
	for _, sh in ipairs(shapes) do
		if sh.outline then
			drawShape(root, scale, sh, EXPAND, true, zBase + 1)
		end
	end
	-- pass 2: colour, in the kit's paint order (later shapes above earlier ones)
	for i, sh in ipairs(shapes) do
		drawShape(root, scale, sh, 0, false, zBase + 1 + i)
	end

	return root
end

function IconArt.has(name: string): boolean
	return IconArt.SHAPES[name] ~= nil
end

return IconArt

-- UIStroke thickness for a given text size (4px at 46-52, 3 at 26-40, 2 below)
function S.strokeFor(textSize: number): number

--!strict
-- tokens.lua — design tokens for the chunky cartoon HUD.
-- Design canvas: 1350 x 775. All numbers are offset px at that canvas size.

local T = {}

local function hex(h: string): Color3
	return Color3.fromHex(h)
end

-- Two- or three-stop vertical gradient (top -> bottom). Use with UIGradient (Rotation = 90).
local function seq(stops: { { pos: number, hex: string } }): ColorSequence
	local kp = {}
	for i, s in ipairs(stops) do
		table.insert(kp, ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(s.pos, hex(s.hex)))
	end
	return ColorSequence.new(kp)
end

T.hex = hex

===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ReplicatedStorage/Modules/UIStyle.lua =====
--[[
UIStyle — bubbly "cartoony simulator" theme for the Trading Center surfaces
============================================================================
Used by: TradeClient (green), BoothClient (teal), SeasonClient (purple).
NOT used by ClientMain / shop / sell menus — those keep UITheme, untouched.

STYLE GUIDE (read me before styling anything new!)
--------------------------------------------------
* Shapes: everything rounded. Panels corner 18, cards/buttons corner 12,
  pills for money amounts. -> UIStyle.corner / UIStyle.pill
* Outlines: thick dark Border-mode UIStroke on everything. Panels 6px,
  buttons/cards 3px. -> UIStyle.stroke
* Color: saturated vertical gradients, light on top -> dark on bottom.
  One accent per surface:
      Trade  = green,   Booth = teal,   Season = purple,
      Gold   = ONLY for cash / price / reward amounts (any surface),
      Red    = destructive (cancel / decline / remove / close),
      Grey   = neutral or disabled, Locked = dark desaturated locked state.
  Cream is the card body color; Ink is the dark text color used on cream.
* Text: chunky white FredokaOne (Fonts.Title) for titles + button labels,
  GothamBold (Fonts.Body) for small body text and dense numbers. EVERY
  white text that sits on a gradient MUST get a Contextual UIStroke via
  UIStyle.bubbleText — white-on-light with no outline is invisible (this
  bit us before; do not skip it).
* Motion: panels pop in/out (popIn/popOut), buttons scale on hover AND
  press (attachHoverPress). Never rely on hover alone — mobile has none.

All helpers are idempotent: re-calling one on the same instance updates
the existing named child instead of duplicating it. Canonical child names:
  "UIStyleCorner", "UIStyleStrokeBorder" (Border mode),
  "UIStyleStrokeText" (Contextual mode), "UIStyleGradient",
  "UIStyleScale" (panel root scale), "PressScale" (button hover/press).
Border vs text strokes are distinguished by ApplyStrokeMode AND by name.
]]

local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
-- SoundKit is a LEAF (it requires no module of its own), and UIStyle is never
-- required server-side, so this top-level require cannot cycle. UITheme requires
-- it lazily instead only because UITheme loads on the server too.
local SoundKit = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("Modules"):WaitForChild("SoundKit"))

local UIStyle = {}

-- CLICK AUDIO. Deliberately the SAME "SfxWired" attribute key UITheme.wireClick
-- uses: a button that passes through constructors in BOTH modules (or is styled
-- and then wired directly) can only ever get ONE connection, so it can never
-- double-click. Volume matches UITheme's existing 0.12 so every button in the
-- game sits at one level.
local CLICK_VOLUME = 0.12
local function wireClick(btn, soundName)
	if not RunService:IsClient() then return end
	if typeof(btn) ~= "Instance" or not btn:IsA("GuiButton") then return end
	if btn:GetAttribute("SfxWired") then return end
	btn:SetAttribute("SfxWired", true)
	btn.MouseButton1Click:Connect(function()
		pcall(SoundKit.play, soundName or "uiClick", nil, { volume = CLICK_VOLUME })
	end)
end
UIStyle._wireClick = wireClick

local function C(r, g, b) return Color3.fromRGB(r, g, b) end

UIStyle.Palette = {
	Gold   = { light = C(255, 200, 60),  dark = C(240, 150, 25),  outline = C(140, 80, 10) },
	Trade  = { light = C(120, 225, 120), dark = C(40, 170, 70),   outline = C(20, 95, 45) },
	Booth  = { light = C(95, 220, 220),  dark = C(30, 160, 175),  outline = C(15, 90, 105) },
	Season = { light = C(190, 140, 255), dark = C(125, 70, 220),  outline = C(70, 35, 130) },
	-- support accents (additions beyond the core four):
	Red    = { light = C(255, 120, 105), dark = C(220, 60, 55),   outline = C(130, 25, 20) },
	Grey   = { light = C(205, 210, 220), dark = C(145, 152, 166), outline = C(70, 76, 88) },
	Locked = { light = C(120, 126, 140), dark = C(78, 84, 98),    outline = C(42, 46, 56) },
	Cream  = C(255, 248, 235),
	Ink    = C(45, 35, 25),
	White  = C(255, 255, 255),
}
UIStyle.Fonts = { Title = Enum.Font.FredokaOne, Body = Enum.Font.GothamBold }

local P = UIStyle.Palette

-- soft cream gradient used for card bodies
local CARD = { light = P.Cream, dark = C(240, 226, 202) }

-- one active tween per animated instance; a new tween cancels the old one
-- (kv-weak so destroyed rows don't pile up dead entries)
local activeTweens = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "kv" })
local function playTween(target, info, goal)
	local old = activeTweens[target]
	if old then old:Cancel() end
	local tween = TweenService:Create(target, info, goal)
	activeTweens[target] = tween
	tween:Play()
	return tween
end

local function findChild(parent, name, className)
	local child = parent:FindFirstChild(name)
	if child and child:IsA(className) then return child end
	return nil
end

-- accepts an accent table ({light, dark, outline}) or a raw Color3
local function outlineColorOf(accent)
	if typeof(accent) == "Color3" then return accent end
	if type(accent) == "table" and accent.outline then return accent.outline end
	return P.Ink
end

function UIStyle.corner(gui, px)
	local c = findChild(gui, "UIStyleCorner", "UICorner")
	if not c then
		c = Instance.new("UICorner")
		c.Name = "UIStyleCorner"
		c.Parent = gui
	end
	c.CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, px or 12)
	return c
end

function UIStyle.pill(gui)
	local c = UIStyle.corner(gui)
	c.CornerRadius = UDim.new(0.5, 0)
	return c
end

function UIStyle.stroke(gui, accent, thickness)
	local s = findChild(gui, "UIStyleStrokeBorder", "UIStroke")
	if not s then
		s = Instance.new("UIStroke")
		s.Name = "UIStyleStrokeBorder"
		s.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Border
		s.LineJoinMode = Enum.LineJoinMode.Round
		s.Parent = gui
	end
	s.Color = outlineColorOf(accent)
	s.Thickness = thickness or 3
	s.Transparency = 0
	return s
end

function UIStyle.gradient(gui, accent)
	local g = findChild(gui, "UIStyleGradient", "UIGradient")
	if not g then
		g = Instance.new("UIGradient")
		g.Name = "UIStyleGradient"
		g.Parent = gui
	end
	g.Rotation = 90
	g.Color = ColorSequence.new(accent.light, accent.dark)
	return g
end

-- chunky cartoon text: white + dark Contextual outline. bodyFont = true
-- keeps GothamBold for dense/small text; default is FredokaOne.
function UIStyle.bubbleText(label, accent, bodyFont)
	label.Font = bodyFont and UIStyle.Fonts.Body or UIStyle.Fonts.Title
	label.TextColor3 = P.White
	local s = findChild(label, "UIStyleStrokeText", "UIStroke")
	if not s then
		s = Instance.new("UIStroke")
		s.Name = "UIStyleStrokeText"
		s.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Contextual
		s.LineJoinMode = Enum.LineJoinMode.Round
		s.Parent = label
	end
	s.Color = outlineColorOf(accent)
	s.Thickness = bodyFont and 2 or 2.5
	s.Transparency = 0
	return s
end

local function clampedScale()
	local cam = workspace.CurrentCamera
	local y = cam and cam.ViewportSize.Y or 900
	if y <= 1 then y = 900 end -- viewport not ready yet
	return math.clamp(y / 900, 0.8, 1.25)
end

local function rootScale(panel)
	local sc = findChild(panel, "UIStyleScale", "UIScale")
	if not sc then
		sc = Instance.new("UIScale")
		sc.Name = "UIStyleScale"
		sc.Parent = panel
	end
	return sc
end

function UIStyle.stylePanel(frame, accent)
	frame.BackgroundColor3 = P.White
	frame.BackgroundTransparency = 0
	frame.BorderSizePixel = 0
	UIStyle.corner(frame, 18)
	UIStyle.gradient(frame, accent)
	UIStyle.stroke(frame, accent, 6)
	local base = clampedScale()
	frame:SetAttribute("UIStyleBaseScale", base)
	rootScale(frame).Scale = base
	return frame
end

function UIStyle.styleHeader(frame, accent, text)
	frame.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0)
	frame.Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0, 8)
	frame.Size = UDim2.new(1, -18, 0, 40)
	frame.BackgroundColor3 = P.White
	frame.BackgroundTransparency = 0
	frame.BorderSizePixel = 0
	UIStyle.corner(frame, 12)
	-- darker banner (dark -> outline shade) so the white title pops
	local g = findChild(frame, "UIStyleGradient", "UIGradient")
	if not g then
		g = Instance.new("UIGradient")
		g.Name = "UIStyleGradient"
		g.Parent = frame
	end
	g.Rotation = 90
	g.Color = ColorSequence.new(accent.dark, accent.outline)
	UIStyle.stroke(frame, accent, 3)
	if frame:IsA("TextLabel") or frame:IsA("TextButton") then
		if text then frame.Text = text end
		frame.TextSize = 20
		UIStyle.bubbleText(frame, accent)
	end
	return frame
end

-- safe to re-call on the same button for per-state recolor
function UIStyle.styleButton(btn, accent)
	btn.BackgroundColor3 = P.White
	btn.BackgroundTransparency = 0
	btn.BorderSizePixel = 0
	btn.AutoButtonColor = false
	UIStyle.corner(btn, 12)
	UIStyle.gradient(btn, accent)
	UIStyle.stroke(btn, accent, 3)
	if btn:IsA("TextButton") then
		UIStyle.bubbleText(btn, accent)
	end
	wireClick(btn, "uiClick")
	return btn
end

-- row/card: soft cream body + accent outline
function UIStyle.styleCard(frame, accent)
	frame.BackgroundColor3 = P.White
	frame.BackgroundTransparency = 0
	frame.BorderSizePixel = 0
	UIStyle.corner(frame, 12)
	UIStyle.stroke(frame, accent, 3)
	UIStyle.gradient(frame, CARD)
	return frame
end

-- gold pill treatment for any cash / price / reward amount text
function UIStyle.goldAmount(label)
	label.BackgroundColor3 = P.White
	label.BackgroundTransparency = 0
	label.BorderSizePixel = 0
	UIStyle.pill(label)
	UIStyle.gradient(label, P.Gold)
	UIStyle.stroke(label, P.Gold, 2)
	UIStyle.bubbleText(label, P.Gold, true)
	return label
end

-- Bars are children of btn, so Position/Size stay relative to it for free.
-- ZIndex needs live tracking: this codebase's ScreenGuis often use Global
-- ZIndexBehavior, which compares ZIndex across the WHOLE tree instead of
-- cascading a parent's Z to its children, so a caller that raises btn.ZIndex
-- after styling would otherwise strand the bars at their old Z and let the
-- button's own opaque fill repaint over them. This is its own copy of
-- UITheme's identical helper -- kept local rather than a cross-module
-- require, since making this module depend on UITheme is a bigger call than
-- a bug fix.
local closeXSignals = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
local function drawCloseX(btn)
	local oldConn = closeXSignals[btn]
	if oldConn then oldConn:Disconnect() end
	for _, c in ipairs(btn:GetChildren()) do
		if c.Name == "CloseXBar" then c:Destroy() end
	end

	local bars = {}
	for _, rot in ipairs({ 45, -45 }) do
		local bar = Instance.new("Frame")
		bar.Name = "CloseXBar"
		bar.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
		bar.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)
		bar.Size = UDim2.new(0.64, 0, 0.16, 0)
		bar.Rotation = rot
		bar.BackgroundColor3 = P.White
		bar.BorderSizePixel = 0
		bar.Parent = btn
		bars[#bars + 1] = bar
	end

	local function sync()
		for _, bar in ipairs(bars) do bar.ZIndex = btn.ZIndex + 1 end
	end
	sync()
	closeXSignals[btn] = btn:GetPropertyChangedSignal("ZIndex"):Connect(sync)
end

-- red round close button, top-right of its panel
function UIStyle.styleClose(btn)
	btn.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(1, 0)
	btn.Position = UDim2.new(1, -12, 0, 12)
	btn.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(34, 34)
	btn.Text = ""
	btn.ZIndex = 6
	-- wire the CLOSE voice first: styleButton below would otherwise claim this
	-- button for the generic uiClick via the shared SfxWired guard
	wireClick(btn, "panelClose")
	UIStyle.styleButton(btn, P.Red)
	UIStyle.pill(btn)
	drawCloseX(btn)
	return btn
end

-- hover 1.06 / press 0.92 scale feedback. Wires BOTH hover and press paths
-- (touch fires the mouse-button events; hover alone would strand mobile).
-- Pass enabled = false to only ensure the inert PressScale child exists
-- (disabled/locked buttons: present for consistency, no feedback).
-- Never double-connects: wiring is guarded by an attribute.
function UIStyle.attachHoverPress(btn, enabled)
	local ps = findChild(btn, "PressScale", "UIScale")
	if not ps then
		ps = Instance.new("UIScale")
		ps.Name = "PressScale"
		ps.Parent = btn
	end
	if enabled == false then return ps end
	if btn:GetAttribute("UIStyleHoverWired") then return ps end
	btn:SetAttribute("UIStyleHoverWired", true)
	local hovering = false
	local function to(target, dur)
		playTween(ps, TweenInfo.new(dur, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), { Scale = target })
	end
	btn.MouseEnter:Connect(function()
		hovering = true
		to(1.06, 0.12)
	end)
	btn.MouseLeave:Connect(function()
		hovering = false
		to(1, 0.12)
	end)
	btn.MouseButton1Down:Connect(function()
		to(0.92, 0.08)
	end)
	btn.MouseButton1Up:Connect(function()
		to(hovering and 1.06 or 1, 0.08)
	end)
	return ps
end

-- pop-open: 0.65 -> full scale, 0.25s Back/Out. Sets Visible = true itself.
function UIStyle.popIn(panelRoot)
	local base = panelRoot:GetAttribute("UIStyleBaseScale") or 1
	local sc = rootScale(panelRoot)
	panelRoot.Visible = true
	pcall(SoundKit.play, "panelOpen", nil, { volume = CLICK_VOLUME })
	sc.Scale = base * 0.65
	playTween(sc, TweenInfo.new(0.25, Enum.EasingStyle.Back, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), { Scale = base })
end

-- pop-closed: 0.15s Quad/In shrink, THEN hides the panel and calls cb.
-- If a popIn interrupts, the tween is cancelled and Visible stays true.
function UIStyle.popOut(panelRoot, cb)
	pcall(SoundKit.play, "panelClose", nil, { volume = CLICK_VOLUME })
	local base = panelRoot:GetAttribute("UIStyleBaseScale") or 1
	local sc = rootScale(panelRoot)
	local tween = playTween(sc, TweenInfo.new(0.15, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.In), { Scale = base * 0.65 })
	tween.Completed:Connect(function(playbackState)
		if playbackState == Enum.PlaybackState.Completed then
			panelRoot.Visible = false
			sc.Scale = base
			if cb then cb() end
		end
	end)
end

-- ============================================================================
-- Pet-Sim "clean plate" -- turns `root` into a single raised, SOLID plated
-- clickable: a dark saturated accent RIM (root itself), a fully-opaque
-- low-contrast FACE inset + nudged up, exactly ONE soft top GLOSS, and a
-- centered iconHolder to drop a flat 2D icon into. No 3D, no stacked
-- medallions, no idle motion -- the plate is perfectly still; hover/press
-- juice is the caller's job.
--
-- Idempotent: reuses children by canonical Name, so re-calling it (e.g. to
-- recolor for a ready/locked state) never duplicates layers or strokes.
--   root  = the GuiObject you pass in (ImageButton/Frame) -> rim + input surface
--   Face  = "PlateFace"       solid, clips its own children to the rounded rect
--   Gloss = "PlateGloss"      one white sheen, transparency gradient 0.55 -> 1
--   Icon  = "PlateIconHolder" transparent holder, centered, ~64% of the face
--   Shadow= "PlateShadow"     behind root (skipped when opts.shadow == false)
-- Returns { root, face, gloss, iconHolder, shadow }.
local PLATE_BLACK = C(15, 18, 24)
local function plateEnsure(parent, name, className)
	local c = parent:FindFirstChild(name)
	if not (c and c:IsA(className)) then
		if c then c:Destroy() end
		c = Instance.new(className)
		c.Name = name
		c.Parent = parent
	end
	return c
end
local function plateCorner(gui, scale)
	local c = plateEnsure(gui, "PlateCorner", "UICorner")
	c.CornerRadius = UDim.new(scale, 0)
	return c
end
local function normalizeAccent(accent)
	if type(accent) == "table" and accent.light and accent.dark then
		return { light = accent.light, dark = accent.dark, outline = accent.outline or accent.dark }
	end
	if typeof(accent) == "Color3" then
		return { light = accent, dark = accent:Lerp(PLATE_BLACK, 0.35), outline = accent:Lerp(PLATE_BLACK, 0.6) }
	end
	return P.Grey
end

function UIStyle.plate(root, accent, opts)
	opts = opts or {}
	accent = normalizeAccent(accent)
	local cScale    = opts.corner    or 0.20  -- corner radius as a fraction of the short side
	local glossFrac = opts.gloss     or 0.44  -- gloss covers the top 44% of the face
	local faceIn    = opts.faceInset or 0.86  -- face size as a fraction of the rim
	local faceLift  = opts.faceLift  or 0.03  -- nudge the face up so the bottom rim reads thicker

	-- RIM (the root itself): dark saturated accent + thick round outline stroke.
	root.BackgroundColor3 = accent.dark
	root.BackgroundTransparency = 0
	root.BorderSizePixel = 0
	if root:IsA("GuiButton") then root.AutoButtonColor = false end
	plateCorner(root, cScale)
	UIStyle.stroke(root, accent, opts.strokeThickness or 3)

	-- FACE: solid, low-contrast vertical gradient; clips gloss/icon to its round.
	local face = plateEnsure(root, "PlateFace", "Frame")
	face.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
	face.Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0.5 - faceLift, 0)
	face.Size = UDim2.fromScale(faceIn, faceIn)
	face.BackgroundColor3 = accent.light
	face.BackgroundTransparency = 0
	face.BorderSizePixel = 0
	face.ClipsDescendants = true
	face.ZIndex = (root.ZIndex or 1) + 1
	plateCorner(face, cScale)
	local fg = plateEnsure(face, "PlateFaceGradient", "UIGradient")
	fg.Rotation = 90
	fg.Color = ColorSequence.new(accent.light:Lerp(P.White, 0.15), accent.light:Lerp(PLATE_BLACK, 0.12))

	-- GLOSS: one white top sheen fading out downward (never a hard bar).
	local gloss = plateEnsure(face, "PlateGloss", "Frame")
	gloss.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0)
	gloss.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0)
	gloss.Size = UDim2.fromScale(0.92, glossFrac)
	gloss.BackgroundColor3 = P.White
	gloss.BorderSizePixel = 0
	gloss.ZIndex = face.ZIndex + 1
	plateCorner(gloss, cScale)
	local gg = plateEnsure(gloss, "PlateGlossGradient", "UIGradient")
	gg.Rotation = 90
	gg.Transparency = NumberSequence.new({ NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 0.55), NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 1) })

	-- ICON HOLDER: centered transparent slot for a flat 2D icon.
	local iconHolder = plateEnsure(face, "PlateIconHolder", "Frame")
	iconHolder.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
	iconHolder.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)
	iconHolder.Size = UDim2.fromScale(0.64, 0.64)
	iconHolder.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	iconHolder.ZIndex = gloss.ZIndex + 1

	-- SHADOW behind the rim (one only; skip when the caller supplies its own).
	local shadow
	if opts.shadow ~= false and root.Parent then
		shadow = plateEnsure(root.Parent, "PlateShadow", "Frame")
		shadow.AnchorPoint = root.AnchorPoint
		shadow.Position = root.Position + UDim2.fromOffset(0, opts.shadowDrop or 5)
		shadow.Size = root.Size
		shadow.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(8, 10, 16)
		shadow.BackgroundTransparency = 0.6
		shadow.BorderSizePixel = 0
		shadow.ZIndex = (root.ZIndex or 1) - 1
		plateCorner(shadow, cScale)
	end

	wireClick(root, "uiClick")   -- no-ops when the plate root is a Frame, not a button
	return { root = root, face = face, gloss = gloss, iconHolder = iconHolder, shadow = shadow }
end

--[[ ==========================================================================
STICKER RAIL  (the colourful side-menu look)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
UIStyle.sticker(btn, opts) turns a TextButton into a "sticker" menu entry:
a white illustration card, a saturated ribbon banner across its foot, and
an optional red "!" alert bubble clipped to the top-right corner.

	opts = {
		accent = UIStyle.Palette.Trade,   -- ribbon colour (table or Color3)
		label  = "shop",                  -- ribbon word; upper-cased for you
		glyph  = "\u{1F6D2}",             -- emoji drawn on the card
		image  = "rbxassetid://123",      -- optional; wins over glyph
		badge  = true,                    -- show the red "!" bubble
	}

Every piece is white-outlined rather than dark-outlined -- that white keyline
against the world is what makes these read as stickers instead of as panels.
The ribbon word keeps a dark Contextual stroke so white-on-yellow still reads.

Idempotent like the rest of this module: re-calling updates the existing
children instead of stacking new ones. Canonical child names:
	StickerCard / StickerIcon / StickerRibbon / StickerBadge
========================================================================== ]]
function UIStyle.sticker(btn, opts)
	opts = opts or {}
	local accent = normalizeAccent(opts.accent or P.Gold)
	local z = btn.ZIndex or 1

	btn.AutoButtonColor = false
	btn.BackgroundTransparency = 1     -- still fully hit-testable
	btn.BorderSizePixel = 0
	btn.ClipsDescendants = false       -- ribbon + badge overhang the button
	btn.Text = ""

	local function ensure(parent, name, class)
		local c = parent:FindFirstChild(name)
		if c and not c:IsA(class) then c:Destroy(); c = nil end
		if not c then
			c = Instance.new(class)
			c.Name = name
			c.Parent = parent
		end
		return c
	end

	-- 1. NO SHADOW. The cards read cleaner sitting flat against the world --
	-- the white keyline alone is enough separation. Cleared here too so a
	-- hot-reload over an older build does not leave an orphan slab behind.
	local staleShadow = btn:FindFirstChild("StickerShadow")
	if staleShadow then staleShadow:Destroy() end

	-- 2. CARD - the white illustration plate
	local card = ensure(btn, "StickerCard", "Frame")
	card.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0)
	card.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0)
	card.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, -22)
	card.BackgroundColor3 = P.White
	card.BorderSizePixel = 0
	card.ZIndex = z + 1
	UIStyle.corner(card, 18)
	UIStyle.gradient(card, { light = P.White, dark = C(238, 240, 248) })
	UIStyle.stroke(card, P.White, 3.5)

	-- 3. ICON - emoji by default, ImageLabel when opts.image is given
	local wantImage = opts.image ~= nil
	local old = card:FindFirstChild("StickerIcon")
	if old and ((wantImage and not old:IsA("ImageLabel")) or (not wantImage and not old:IsA("TextLabel"))) then
		old:Destroy()
	end
	local icon = ensure(card, "StickerIcon", wantImage and "ImageLabel" or "TextLabel")
	icon.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
	icon.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.44)
	icon.Size = UDim2.fromScale(0.68, 0.68)
	icon.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	icon.ZIndex = z + 2
	if wantImage then
		icon.Image = opts.image
		icon.ScaleType = Enum.ScaleType.Fit
	else
		icon.Text = opts.glyph or "\u{2B50}"
		icon.Font = UIStyle.Fonts.Title
		icon.TextScaled = true
		icon.TextColor3 = P.White
	end

	-- 4. RIBBON - the banner; wider than the card so it reads as a wrap
	local ribbon = ensure(btn, "StickerRibbon", "Frame")
	ribbon.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 1)
	ribbon.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 1)
	ribbon.Size = UDim2.new(1, 12, 0, 36)
	ribbon.BackgroundColor3 = accent.light
	ribbon.BorderSizePixel = 0
	ribbon.ZIndex = z + 3
	UIStyle.corner(ribbon, 11)
	UIStyle.gradient(ribbon, accent)
	UIStyle.stroke(ribbon, P.White, 3.5)

	local word = ensure(ribbon, "StickerLabel", "TextLabel")
	word.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
	word.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)
	word.Size = UDim2.new(1, -12, 1, -8)
	word.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	word.ZIndex = z + 4
	word.Text = string.upper(opts.label or btn.Name)
	word.TextScaled = true
	UIStyle.bubbleText(word, accent)
	local wc = word:FindFirstChild("UIStyleTextSize")
	if not wc then
		wc = Instance.new("UITextSizeConstraint")
		wc.Name = "UIStyleTextSize"
		wc.Parent = word
	end
	wc.MaxTextSize = 26

	-- 5. BADGE - red "!" bubble, hangs off the card's top-right corner
	local badge = ensure(btn, "StickerBadge", "Frame")
	badge.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
	badge.Position = UDim2.new(1, -4, 0, 4)
	badge.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(30, 30)
	badge.BackgroundColor3 = P.Red.light
	badge.BorderSizePixel = 0
	badge.ZIndex = z + 5
	badge.Visible = opts.badge == true
	UIStyle.pill(badge)
	UIStyle.gradient(badge, P.Red)
	UIStyle.stroke(badge, P.White, 3)

	local bang = ensure(badge, "StickerBang", "TextLabel")
	bang.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
	bang.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.46)
	bang.Size = UDim2.fromScale(0.9, 0.8)
	bang.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	bang.ZIndex = z + 6
	bang.Text = "!"
	bang.TextScaled = true
	UIStyle.bubbleText(bang, P.Red)

	UIStyle.attachHoverPress(btn)
	wireClick(btn, "uiClick")
	return { card = card, icon = icon, ribbon = ribbon, label = word, badge = badge }
end

-- Show/hide the red "!" on a button already passed through UIStyle.sticker.
function UIStyle.stickerBadge(btn, on)
	local badge = btn:FindFirstChild("StickerBadge")
	if badge then badge.Visible = on and true or false end
end

return UIStyle

	blue1 = Color3.fromRGB(96, 182, 255), blue2 = Color3.fromRGB(30, 127, 219),

	hudGold1 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 216, 96), hudGold2 = Color3.fromRGB(238, 148, 24),

	cashText = Color3.fromRGB(126, 255, 148),

M.Palette = P

-- Central click SFX wiring. Idempotent via the SfxWired attribute: -- SFX2
-- campButton/styleButton are deliberately RE-CALLED on the same button for -- SFX2
-- state swaps, so without the guard every restyle would stack another connect. -- SFX2
-- SoundKit is required lazily inside pcall (UITheme loads very early on both -- SFX2
-- client AND server, so an eager top-level require risks load-order cycles). -- SFX2
local function wireClick(btn, soundName) -- SFX2
	if not game:GetService("RunService"):IsClient() then return end -- SFX2
	if not btn:IsA("GuiButton") then return end -- SFX2
	if btn:GetAttribute("SfxWired") then return end -- SFX2
	btn:SetAttribute("SfxWired", true) -- SFX2
	btn.MouseButton1Click:Connect(function() -- SFX2
		local ok, kit = pcall(function() -- SFX2
			return require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("Modules"):WaitForChild("SoundKit")) -- SFX2
		end) -- SFX2
		if ok and kit then pcall(kit.play, soundName, nil, { volume = 0.12 }) end -- SFX2
	end) -- SFX2
end -- SFX2

function M.corner(o, r)
	local c = o:FindFirstChildOfClass("UICorner") or Instance.new("UICorner")
	c.CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, r or 12); c.Parent = o; return c
end

function M.stroke(o, color, thick, transp)
	local s = Instance.new("UIStroke")
	s.Color = color or P.outline; s.Thickness = thick or 2; s.Transparency = transp or 0
	s.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Border; s.LineJoinMode = Enum.LineJoinMode.Round; s.Parent = o; return s
end

function M.gradient(o, cTop, cBot, rot)
	local g = o:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIGradient") or Instance.new("UIGradient")
	g.Rotation = rot or 90; g.Color = ColorSequence.new(cTop, cBot); g.Parent = o; return g
end

-- soft white gloss strip over the top of an element (no text underneath)
function M.gloss(o, radius, topTransparency)
	local gl = Instance.new("Frame")
	gl.Name = "Gloss"; gl.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0); gl.Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0, 2)
	gl.Size = UDim2.new(1, -6, 0.44, 0); gl.BackgroundColor3 = P.white; gl.BorderSizePixel = 0
	gl.ZIndex = (o.ZIndex or 1) + 1; gl.Parent = o
	local c = Instance.new("UICorner"); c.CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, radius or 8); c.Parent = gl
	local g = Instance.new("UIGradient"); g.Rotation = 90
	g.Transparency = NumberSequence.new({ NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, topTransparency or 0.5), NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 1) }); g.Parent = gl
	return gl
end

-- glossy rounded medallion chip (used for shop rock / sell rarity swatch)
function M.medallion(parent, size, pos, color)
	local m = Instance.new("Frame")
	m.Size = size; m.Position = pos; m.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0, 0.5)
	m.BackgroundColor3 = color; m.BorderSizePixel = 0; m.Parent = parent
	M.corner(m, 10)
	M.stroke(m, P.white, 1.5, 0.5)
	M.gloss(m, 8)
	return m
end

-- idempotent premium action button (safe to re-call to change color per state)
function M.styleButton(btn, cTop, cBot)
	btn.AutoButtonColor = true
	btn.BackgroundColor3 = P.white
	btn.TextColor3 = P.white
	btn.Font = Enum.Font.GothamBold
	btn.BorderSizePixel = 0
	M.corner(btn, 9)
	M.gradient(btn, cTop, cBot, 90)
	local hasBorder, hasText = false, false
	for _, s in ipairs(btn:GetChildren()) do
		if s:IsA("UIStroke") then
			if s.ApplyStrokeMode == Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Contextual then hasText = true else hasBorder = true end
		end
	end
	if not hasBorder then M.stroke(btn, P.outline, 2) end
	if not hasText then
		local ts = Instance.new("UIStroke")
		ts.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Contextual
		ts.Color = Color3.fromRGB(28, 32, 42); ts.Thickness = 2; ts.Transparency = 0.1; ts.Parent = btn
	end
	wireClick(btn, "uiClick") -- SFX2
end

function M.stylePanel(frame)
	frame.BackgroundColor3 = P.white
	frame.BackgroundTransparency = 0.03
	M.corner(frame, 16)
	if not frame:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIGradient") then M.gradient(frame, P.panelTop, P.panelBot, 90) end
	if not frame:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIStroke") then M.stroke(frame, P.outline, 2.5) end
end

function M.styleHeader(titleLabel, accentTop, accentBot)
	titleLabel.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0)
	titleLabel.Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0, 9)
	titleLabel.Size = UDim2.new(1, -18, 0, 40)
	titleLabel.BackgroundColor3 = P.white
	titleLabel.BackgroundTransparency = 0
	titleLabel.Font = Enum.Font.GothamBlack
	titleLabel.TextColor3 = P.white
	titleLabel.TextSize = 19
	titleLabel.BorderSizePixel = 0
	M.corner(titleLabel, 12)
	M.gradient(titleLabel, accentTop, accentBot, 90)
	if not titleLabel:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIStroke") then M.stroke(titleLabel, P.outline, 2) end
	local ts = Instance.new("UIStroke")
	ts.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Contextual; ts.Color = Color3.fromRGB(20, 22, 28); ts.Thickness = 1.6; ts.Transparency = 0.3; ts.Parent = titleLabel
end

-- Bars are children of btn, so Position/Size stay relative to it for free.
-- ZIndex needs live tracking: MainUI's Global ZIndexBehavior compares ZIndex
-- across the WHOLE tree instead of cascading a parent's Z to its children, so
-- a caller raising btn.ZIndex after styling (IndexClient does, deliberately)
-- would otherwise strand the bars at their old Z and let the button's own
-- opaque fill repaint over them.
--
-- Public: styleClose calls this, but so does anything that builds its own
-- close button by hand and can't go through styleClose (e.g. WheelClient's
-- oversized 56px Daily Spin close button, whose size/position/color are
-- deliberate and must not be reset to the 30px standard).
local closeXSignals = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
function M.closeGlyph(btn)
	local oldConn = closeXSignals[btn]
	if oldConn then oldConn:Disconnect() end
	for _, c in ipairs(btn:GetChildren()) do
		if c.Name == "CloseXBar" then c:Destroy() end
	end

	local bars = {}
	for _, rot in ipairs({ 45, -45 }) do
		local bar = Instance.new("Frame")
		bar.Name = "CloseXBar"
		bar.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
		bar.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)
		bar.Size = UDim2.new(0.64, 0, 0.16, 0)
		bar.Rotation = rot
		bar.BackgroundColor3 = P.white
		bar.BorderSizePixel = 0
		bar.Parent = btn
		bars[#bars + 1] = bar
	end

	local function sync()
		for _, bar in ipairs(bars) do bar.ZIndex = btn.ZIndex + 1 end
	end
	sync()
	closeXSignals[btn] = btn:GetPropertyChangedSignal("ZIndex"):Connect(sync)
end

function M.styleClose(btn)
	btn.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(1, 0)
	btn.Position = UDim2.new(1, -13, 0, 13)
	btn.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(30, 30)
	btn.BackgroundColor3 = P.white
	btn.Text = ""
	btn.AutoButtonColor = true
	btn.BorderSizePixel = 0
	btn.ZIndex = 6
	M.corner(btn, 15)
	M.gradient(btn, P.red1, P.red2, 90)
	if not btn:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIStroke") then M.stroke(btn, P.outline, 2) end
	M.closeGlyph(btn)
	wireClick(btn, "panelClose") -- SFX2
end

-- ===================================================================
-- CAMPFIRE style pack (v2 look): chunky black outlines, sunburst icon
-- backdrops, carved-wood ribbon headers, per-card accent colours.
-- Warm lake-and-campfire palette instead of the old cool navy.
-- ===================================================================
local CF = {
	-- CAFE palette. Panels are cream and the ink is dark BROWN, never black.
	ink      = Color3.fromRGB(62, 34, 19),     -- outline on every shape AND glyph
	panelTop = Color3.fromRGB(250, 240, 224),  -- cream panel body
	panelBot = Color3.fromRGB(238, 224, 200),
	cardTop  = Color3.fromRGB(245, 220, 192),  -- card cream
	cardBot  = Color3.fromRGB(231, 203, 170),
	-- `cream` and `muted` are TEXT colours, and the panel under them just went
	-- from dark green to cream -- so they invert to dark brown. Roughly 58 call
	-- sites across 12 client scripts read these two, which is exactly why the
	-- swap happens here instead of in every script.
	cream    = Color3.fromRGB(62, 34, 19),
	muted    = Color3.fromRGB(138, 108, 82),
	-- for glyphs/fills that sit on a DARK or saturated surface (header bar,
	-- accent buttons) where dark-on-dark would disappear
	onDark   = Color3.fromRGB(255, 246, 228),
	wood1    = Color3.fromRGB(205, 132, 58),   -- warm-brown header bar
	wood2    = Color3.fromRGB(178, 104, 40),
	locked1  = Color3.fromRGB(214, 198, 176),  -- disabled / locked button fill
	locked2  = Color3.fromRGB(186, 168, 146),
	-- per-card accents
	amber1 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 200, 96),  amber2 = Color3.fromRGB(232, 138, 34),
	ember1 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 152, 82),  ember2 = Color3.fromRGB(214, 80, 40),
	pine1  = Color3.fromRGB(146, 214, 122), pine2  = Color3.fromRGB(54, 140, 76),
	lake1  = Color3.fromRGB(126, 216, 224), lake2  = Color3.fromRGB(36, 138, 166),
	berry1 = Color3.fromRGB(226, 150, 226), berry2 = Color3.fromRGB(146, 68, 168),
}
M.Camp = CF

-- the bubbly cafe face, picked off the Stage 5 proof board
M.Font = Enum.Font.Cartoon

-- decorative dingbats (✦, arrows) -- the theme face above may not carry these
-- glyphs, so anything ornamental rather than body text draws from here instead
M.GlyphFont = Enum.Font.GothamBold

local function lum(c) return 0.2126 * c.R + 0.7152 * c.G + 0.0722 * c.B end

-- heavy black outline (the single biggest reason this style pops)
function M.ink(o, thick)
	local s = Instance.new("UIStroke")
	s.Color = CF.ink; s.Thickness = thick or 3; s.Transparency = 0
	s.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Border
	s.LineJoinMode = Enum.LineJoinMode.Round
	s.Parent = o
	return s
end

-- black outline around TEXT glyphs
function M.inkText(o, thick)
	local s = Instance.new("UIStroke")
	s.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Contextual
	s.Color = CF.ink; s.Thickness = thick or 2.4; s.Transparency = 0
	s.Parent = o
	return s
end

-- radial sunburst rays behind an icon; rays pivot on their AnchorPoint at the centre
function M.sunburst(parent, color, rays, baseTop, baseBot)
	rays = rays or 12
	local holder = Instance.new("Frame")
	holder.Name = "Sunburst"
	holder.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	holder.BackgroundColor3 = P.white
	holder.BorderSizePixel = 0
	holder.ClipsDescendants = true
	holder.ZIndex = (parent.ZIndex or 1)
	holder.Parent = parent
	M.corner(holder, 10)
	-- Cafe look: the radial rays are RETIRED. The base is always the light card
	-- cream now -- callers pass their old dark base colours (e.g. cardBot/ink),
	-- which on the cafe palette would render a dark tile, so they're ignored.
	M.gradient(holder, CF.cardTop, CF.cardBot, 90)
	-- One flat accent wash replaces the rays, keeping each caller's "one accent
	-- per card" read. It is still NAMED "Ray" on purpose: RareCatchClient walks
	-- the burst's children and retints anything called "Ray" to show the tier
	-- colour, so that per-tier read keeps working with no change at the call site.
	local wash = holder:FindFirstChild("Ray") or Instance.new("Frame")
	wash.Name = "Ray"
	wash.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	wash.BackgroundColor3 = color
	wash.BackgroundTransparency = 0.58
	wash.BorderSizePixel = 0
	wash.ZIndex = holder.ZIndex
	wash.Parent = holder
	M.corner(wash, 10)
	return holder
end

-- derive a card interior from an accent hue so each card reads in its OWN
-- colour instead of a uniform cream -- this is what makes the cards pop.
-- Cafe version: PALE tinted cream. The body text on these cards is now dark
-- brown, so the old deep jewel-tone interior would swallow it whole.
function M.accentFill(accent)
	local h, s = accent:ToHSV()
	local top = Color3.fromHSV(h, math.min(s * 0.30, 1), 0.98)
	local bot = Color3.fromHSV(h, math.min(s * 0.46, 1), 0.90)
	return top, bot
end

-- card with an accent border + black outline. returns the INNER content frame.
-- the interior is tinted toward `accent` so each card reads as its own colour.
function M.accentCard(parent, accent, radius)
	local outer = Instance.new("Frame")
	outer.BackgroundColor3 = accent
	outer.BorderSizePixel = 0
	outer.Parent = parent
	M.corner(outer, radius or 14)
	M.ink(outer, 3)
	local inner = Instance.new("Frame")
	inner.Name = "Content"
	inner.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
	inner.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)
	inner.Size = UDim2.new(1, -7, 1, -7)
	inner.BackgroundColor3 = P.white
	inner.BorderSizePixel = 0
	inner.ZIndex = (outer.ZIndex or 1) + 1
	inner.Parent = outer
	M.corner(inner, (radius or 14) - 3)
	local fillTop, fillBot = M.accentFill(accent)
	M.gradient(inner, fillTop, fillBot, 90)
	return inner, outer
end

-- carved-wood banner that overhangs the top of a panel
function M.ribbon(parent, text, widthScale)
	local holder = Instance.new("Frame")
	holder.Name = "Ribbon"
	holder.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0)
	holder.Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0, -22)
	holder.Size = UDim2.new(widthScale or 0.74, 0, 0, 58)
	holder.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	holder.ZIndex = (parent.ZIndex or 1) + 4
	holder.Parent = parent
	for _, side in ipairs({ -1, 1 }) do
		local tab = Instance.new("Frame")
		tab.Name = "Tab"
		tab.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
		tab.Position = UDim2.new(side < 0 and 0 or 1, side * 16, 0.5, 7)
		tab.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(58, 42)
		tab.Rotation = side * 8
		tab.BackgroundColor3 = P.white
		tab.BorderSizePixel = 0
		tab.ZIndex = holder.ZIndex
		tab.Parent = holder
		M.corner(tab, 8)
		M.gradient(tab, CF.wood2, CF.ink, 90)
		M.ink(tab, 3)
	end
	local plank = Instance.new("Frame")
	plank.Name = "Plank"
	plank.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	plank.BackgroundColor3 = P.white
	plank.BorderSizePixel = 0
	plank.ZIndex = holder.ZIndex + 1
	plank.Parent = holder
	M.corner(plank, 12)
	M.gradient(plank, CF.wood1, CF.wood2, 90)
	M.ink(plank, 3.5)
	M.gloss(plank, 10, 0.86)   -- keep the sheen subtle or the wood washes out to beige
	local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	label.Name = "Title"
	label.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	label.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	label.Font = M.Font
	label.TextScaled = false
	label.TextSize = 30
	label.TextColor3 = CF.onDark
	label.Text = text or ""
	label.ZIndex = holder.ZIndex + 3
	label.Parent = holder
	M.inkText(label, 3.2)
	return holder, label
end

-- Solid warm-brown header bar: the cafe alternative to M.ribbon's carved plank.
-- Sits flush across the top of a panel instead of overhanging it.
function M.headerBar(parent, text, height)
	local bar = Instance.new("Frame")
	bar.Name = "HeaderBar"
	bar.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0)
	bar.Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0, 0)
	bar.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, height or 52)
	bar.BackgroundColor3 = P.white
	bar.BorderSizePixel = 0
	bar.ZIndex = (parent.ZIndex or 1) + 2
	bar.Parent = parent
	M.corner(bar, 16)
	M.gradient(bar, CF.wood1, CF.wood2, 90)
	M.ink(bar, 3)
	local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	label.Name = "Title"
	label.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	label.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	label.Font = M.Font
	label.TextSize = 26
	label.TextColor3 = CF.onDark
	label.Text = text or ""
	label.ZIndex = bar.ZIndex + 1
	label.Parent = bar
	M.inkText(label, 2.6)
	return bar, label
end

-- cream panel body for the cafe look
function M.campPanel(frame)
	frame.BackgroundColor3 = P.white
	frame.BackgroundTransparency = 0
	frame.BorderSizePixel = 0
	M.corner(frame, 18)
	M.gradient(frame, CF.panelTop, CF.panelBot, 90)
	M.ink(frame, 4)
end

-- big chunky price/action pill
function M.campButton(btn, cTop, cBot)
	btn.BackgroundColor3 = P.white
	btn.BorderSizePixel = 0
	btn.AutoButtonColor = true
	btn.Font = M.Font
	-- campButton gradient/locked-state audit (the spec asked for this sweep).
	-- A UIGradient on a TextButton multiplies its TEXT as well as its background,
	-- so NEITHER a light nor a dark label survives on fill colour alone. What
	-- actually carries legibility is the thick dark-brown glyph outline applied
	-- below -- light glyphs + heavy ink outline is the reference look on the
	-- saturated buttons. Dark ink is only correct on a genuinely PALE fill
	-- (locked/disabled, or the cream panel colours), where a light label would
	-- vanish and the outline would be all that's left.
	btn.TextColor3 = ((lum(cTop) + lum(cBot)) * 0.5 > 0.70) and CF.ink or CF.onDark
	M.corner(btn, 10)
	M.setColors(btn, cTop, cBot)
	if not btn:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIStroke") then M.ink(btn, 3) end
	local hasText = false
	for _, s in ipairs(btn:GetChildren()) do
		if s:IsA("UIStroke") and s.ApplyStrokeMode == Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Contextual then hasText = true end
	end
	if not hasText then M.inkText(btn, 2.6) end
	wireClick(btn, "uiClick") -- SFX2
end

-- swap an already-styled element's gradient colors (state changes)
function M.setColors(o, cTop, cBot)
	local g = o:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIGradient")
	if g then g.Color = ColorSequence.new(cTop, cBot) else M.gradient(o, cTop, cBot, 90) end
end

-- vibrant HUD button: bright gradient + gloss shine + chunky dark outline + outlined bold text
function M.styleHudButton(btn, cTop, cBot, radius)
	radius = radius or 12
	btn.BackgroundColor3 = P.white
	btn.BackgroundTransparency = 0
	btn.BorderSizePixel = 0
	btn.AutoButtonColor = true
	btn.Font = Enum.Font.GothamBlack
	btn.TextColor3 = P.white
	M.corner(btn, radius)
	M.setColors(btn, cTop, cBot)
	local border, textStroke
	for _, s in ipairs(btn:GetChildren()) do
		if s:IsA("UIStroke") then
			if s.ApplyStrokeMode == Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Contextual then textStroke = s else border = s end
		end
	end
	border = border or M.stroke(btn, P.outline, 3)
	border.Color = P.outline; border.Thickness = 3; border.Transparency = 0
	if not textStroke then
		textStroke = Instance.new("UIStroke")
		textStroke.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Contextual
		textStroke.Parent = btn
	end
	textStroke.Color = Color3.fromRGB(20, 24, 32); textStroke.Thickness = 2; textStroke.Transparency = 0.1
	if not btn:FindFirstChild("Gloss") then M.gloss(btn, math.max(radius - 3, 4), 0.72) end
	wireClick(btn, "uiClick") -- SFX2
	return btn
end

-- dark glossy chip (cash counter, throw panel) with an accent rim
function M.styleHudChip(frame, radius, accent, accentTransparency)
	radius = radius or 12
	frame.BackgroundColor3 = P.white
	frame.BackgroundTransparency = 0
	frame.BorderSizePixel = 0
	M.corner(frame, radius)
	M.setColors(frame, P.hudDark1, P.hudDark2)
	local border
	for _, s in ipairs(frame:GetChildren()) do
		if s:IsA("UIStroke") and s.ApplyStrokeMode ~= Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Contextual then border = s end
	end
	border = border or M.stroke(frame, accent or P.hudGold1, 2.5)
	border.Color = accent or P.hudGold1
	border.Thickness = 2.5
	border.Transparency = accentTransparency or 0.15
	if not frame:FindFirstChild("Gloss") then M.gloss(frame, math.max(radius - 3, 4), 0.82) end
	return frame
end

-- ===================================================================
-- CANDY style pack (2026-07-27). A SECOND palette living beside Camp,
-- from the user's design handoff (docs/design-handoff, build from v3):
-- bright Pet-Sim treatment -- white panels, comic-thick ink outlines,
-- and hard unblurred offset shadows.
--
-- Deliberately ADDITIVE. Camp and all 12 of its callers are untouched,
-- so nothing on screen changes until something opts in. That is what
-- makes reverting this a one-file revert rather than unpicking the
-- five-stage cafe restyle.
-- ===================================================================
local CANDY = {
	ink       = Color3.fromRGB(16, 19, 31),      -- #10131f, on everything
	panelTop  = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255),
	panelBot  = Color3.fromRGB(207, 224, 245),   -- #cfe0f5
	shadow    = Color3.fromRGB(10, 13, 22),      -- #0a0d16, SOLID, never blurred
	green1    = Color3.fromRGB(163, 255, 79),
	green2    = Color3.fromRGB(61, 158, 24),
	red1      = Color3.fromRGB(255, 92, 122),
	red2      = Color3.fromRGB(163, 18, 58),
	gold1     = Color3.fromRGB(255, 230, 128),
	gold2     = Color3.fromRGB(224, 140, 0),
	onDark    = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255),
	-- The handoff specifies Luckiest Guy, which Roblox does not have.
	-- FredokaOne is the nearest chunky rounded face. Kept HERE rather than
	-- on M.Font so the cafe face (Cartoon) is unaffected.
	font      = Enum.Font.FredokaOne,
	radius    = 26,    -- panels; chips use ~16
	-- Task 4 tune-by-eye: 4 (itself already reduced from the handoff's 6) still
	-- read heavy at Roblox scale once the whole wheel was on screen together --
	-- particularly stacked up on the small chips/rows, where a 4px border on a
	-- ~44px chip is proportionally thick. 3 keeps the "comic outline" read
	-- (relationship that must hold, per the spec) without looking like a slab.
	stroke    = 3,
}
M.Candy = CANDY

-- The detail that makes the reference read as a toy: a HARD offset shadow,
-- no blur. Drawn as a plain Frame behind the object, matching its corner
-- radius. Parented to the object's PARENT (not the object) so it cannot be
-- clipped by ClipsDescendants and cannot inherit a gradient.
function M.candyShadow(o, offsetY, radius)
	offsetY = offsetY or 8
	local sh = Instance.new("Frame")
	sh.Name = "CandyShadow"
	sh.BackgroundColor3 = CANDY.shadow
	sh.BorderSizePixel = 0
	sh.Size = o.Size
	sh.Position = o.Position + UDim2.fromOffset(0, offsetY)
	sh.AnchorPoint = o.AnchorPoint
	sh.ZIndex = math.max(1, o.ZIndex - 1)
	sh.Parent = o.Parent
	local c = Instance.new("UICorner")
	c.CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, radius or CANDY.radius)
	c.Parent = sh
	return sh
end

function M.candyPanel(f, radius)
	f.BackgroundColor3 = CANDY.panelTop
	f.BorderSizePixel = 0
	M.corner(f, radius or CANDY.radius)
	M.gradient(f, CANDY.panelTop, CANDY.panelBot, 90)
	local s = Instance.new("UIStroke")
	s.Color = CANDY.ink
	s.Thickness = CANDY.stroke
	s.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Border
	s.LineJoinMode = Enum.LineJoinMode.Round
	s.Parent = f
	return f
end

function M.candyButton(b, c1, c2, radius)
	b.BackgroundColor3 = c1
	b.BorderSizePixel = 0
	b.AutoButtonColor = true
	b.TextColor3 = CANDY.onDark
	b.Font = CANDY.font
	M.corner(b, radius or 18)
	M.gradient(b, c1, c2, 90)
	local s = Instance.new("UIStroke")
	s.Color = CANDY.ink
	s.Thickness = CANDY.stroke
	s.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Border
	s.LineJoinMode = Enum.LineJoinMode.Round
	s.Parent = b
	-- a gradient multiplies TEXT as well as background and multiply can only
	-- darken, so a light label needs its own ink outline to survive. NOT
	-- M.inkText -- that shared helper hardcodes Camp's warm-brown ink (CF.ink),
	-- so a candy button's text outline would pick up the cafe's colour instead
	-- of candy's own near-black. Built by hand here so it stays on CANDY.ink.
	local ts = Instance.new("UIStroke")
	ts.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Contextual
	ts.Color = CANDY.ink
	ts.Thickness = 2.5
	ts.Parent = b
	wireClick(b, "uiClick") -- SFX2
	return b
end

-- ===================================================================
-- BAZAAR style pack: dark stall-shop look (totem/gem shop reference).
-- Deliberately ADDITIVE, same as Candy above -- nothing else on screen
-- changes until a shop script opts in by calling these instead of
-- accentCard/campPanel/campButton.
-- ===================================================================
-- 2026-08-13 LEMONPOP RETINT (spec §3b "every shop"): the dark stall goes
-- lemon-cream -- light window, warm outline, ONE red header per shop window
-- (the per-shop bronze/green/pink header identities collapse into the red,
-- deliberate). Old values inline. Text colours below assume the pack's
-- builders now set NoPolish and follow the light/dark rule themselves.
local BZ = {
	ink        = Color3.fromRGB(36, 31, 20),    -- #241F14 (was 10,13,19)
	panelTop   = Color3.fromRGB(255, 251, 226), -- #FFFBE2 (was dark 38,46,60)
	panelBot   = Color3.fromRGB(255, 217, 119), -- #FFD977 (was 19,23,32)
	panelEdge  = Color3.fromRGB(36, 31, 20),    -- #241F14 (was 7,9,13)
	header1    = Color3.fromRGB(255, 107, 92),  -- #FF6B5C the ONE red (was cyan 126,219,255)
	header2    = Color3.fromRGB(216, 52, 44),   -- #D8342C (was 26,138,214)
	close1     = Color3.fromRGB(255, 107, 107), -- #FF6B6B (was 255,100,100)
	close2     = Color3.fromRGB(216, 62, 62),   -- #D83E3E (was 204,32,32)
	notice     = Color3.fromRGB(194, 65, 12),   -- #C2410C accent ink on light (was salmon 255,122,96)
	cardTop    = Color3.fromRGB(255, 246, 207), -- #FFF6CF subPanel (was 35,43,56)
	cardBot    = Color3.fromRGB(247, 201, 92),  -- #F7C95C (was 23,28,38)
	cardEdge   = Color3.fromRGB(36, 31, 20),    -- #241F14 (was 12,16,22)
	iconTop    = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255), -- #FFFFFF light art well (was 48,57,74)
	iconBot    = Color3.fromRGB(255, 244, 217), -- #FFF4D9 (was 27,32,43)

	desc       = Color3.fromRGB(51, 38, 26),    -- #33261A ink on light (was 224,230,240)
	muted      = Color3.fromRGB(122, 106, 82),  -- #7A6A52 (was 150,158,174)
	stock      = Color3.fromRGB(216, 52, 44),   -- #D8342C warning red that reads on cream (was 255,92,92)

	cash2      = Color3.fromRGB(79, 180, 46),   -- #4FB42E (was 92,194,40)

	gem2       = Color3.fromRGB(224, 138, 12),  -- #E08A0C (was 222,120,18)
	white      = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255),
	rivetTop   = Color3.fromRGB(194, 168, 120), -- #C2A878 brass on cream (was 90,100,118)
	rivetBot   = Color3.fromRGB(138, 115, 80),  -- #8A7350 (was 30,35,46)
	rowAltTop  = Color3.fromRGB(255, 242, 192), -- #FFF2C0 alt stripe (was 31,38,50)
	rowAltBot  = Color3.fromRGB(242, 193, 84),  -- #F2C154 (was 19,23,32)
	shadow     = Color3.fromRGB(36, 31, 20),    -- #241F14 warm hard shadow (was 6,7,10)
	-- per-shop header identity RETIRED under LemonPop's one-red-header rule --
	-- keys kept so call sites don't change, all resolve to the red
	-- (was rock 255,199,120/197,122,32; sell 168,236,130/58,168,76; egg 255,156,214/188,72,172)
	rockHeader1 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 107, 92), rockHeader2 = Color3.fromRGB(216, 52, 44),
	sellHeader1 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 107, 92), sellHeader2 = Color3.fromRGB(216, 52, 44),
	eggHeader1  = Color3.fromRGB(255, 107, 92), eggHeader2  = Color3.fromRGB(216, 52, 44),

M.Bazaar = BZ
M.BazaarFont = Enum.Font.FredokaOne

local function bzStroke(o, color, thick)
	local s = Instance.new("UIStroke")
	s.Color = color; s.Thickness = thick or 2
	s.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Border
	s.LineJoinMode = Enum.LineJoinMode.Round
	s.Parent = o
	return s
end

local function bzTextStroke(o, thick)
	local s = Instance.new("UIStroke")
	s.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Contextual
	s.Color = BZ.ink; s.Thickness = thick or 2; s.Transparency = 0.1
	s.Parent = o
	return s
end

-- hard, unblurred offset shadow -- same technique as candyShadow, but on BZ.shadow.
-- Idempotent per SOURCE OBJECT via a weak map (same pattern as closeXSignals
-- above): re-calling this for the same `o` updates its existing shadow instead
-- of stacking a new one, which matters because bazaarPanel/Header/Close/Pill
-- can legitimately be re-called on the same instance (state restyles).
local bzShadowMap = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
local function bzShadow(o, offsetY, radius)
	local sh = bzShadowMap[o]
	if not sh or not sh.Parent then
		sh = Instance.new("Frame")
		sh.Name = "BazaarShadow"
		sh.BackgroundColor3 = BZ.shadow
		sh.BorderSizePixel = 0
		sh.Parent = o.Parent
		local c = Instance.new("UICorner")
		c.CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, radius or 12)
		c.Parent = sh
		bzShadowMap[o] = sh
		-- The shadow is a SIBLING of `o` -- it has to sit BEHIND the panel, so it
		-- cannot be a child of it -- which means hiding `o` does NOT hide this.
		-- Everything else below is copied from `o` (Size/Position/AnchorPoint/
		-- ZIndex); Visible was the one property never linked, so a closed panel
		-- left its shadow on screen as an opaque near-black rounded rectangle at
		-- the panel's exact size and position. Found live: MerchantFrame hidden
		-- but its 680x620 shadow still drawn, reading as a big black square
		-- mid-screen, with the Rock and Sell shops' 440x400 shadows orphaned
		-- underneath it. Same failure UI.hardShadow has -- see the Bug D2 note in
		-- GameHUDClient, which solved it with a wrapper Frame; this builder is
		-- called on frames it does not own, so it links the property instead.
		o:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Visible"):Connect(function()
			sh.Visible = o.Visible
		end)
	end
	-- Mirrored on every call, not only from the signal above: bazaarPanel and
	-- friends are re-called on state restyles, which can land while the panel is
	-- already hidden, and a fresh shadow must not flash back on.
	sh.Visible = o.Visible
	sh.Size = o.Size
	sh.Position = o.Position + UDim2.fromOffset(0, offsetY or 5)
	sh.AnchorPoint = o.AnchorPoint
	sh.ZIndex = math.max(1, o.ZIndex - 1)
	return sh
end

-- small stud/rivet, the "bolted-together market stall" detail on panel corners
local function bzRivet(parent, x, y, z)
	local r = Instance.new("Frame")
	r.Name = "Rivet"
	r.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
	r.Position = UDim2.new(0, x, 0, y)
	r.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(9, 9)
	r.BackgroundColor3 = BZ.rivetTop
	r.BorderSizePixel = 0
	r.ZIndex = z
	r.Parent = parent
	M.corner(r, 5)
	M.gradient(r, BZ.rivetTop, BZ.rivetBot, 90)
	bzStroke(r, BZ.panelEdge, 1.5)
	return r
end

-- dark gradient panel body, used for the whole shop window. Chunkier than the
-- first pass: thicker outline, a hard offset shadow behind the whole panel,
-- and four corner rivets so it reads as a bolted-together market stall rather
-- than a flat generic dark rectangle.
function M.bazaarPanel(frame, radius)
	radius = radius or 18
	frame.BackgroundColor3 = BZ.panelTop
	frame.BackgroundTransparency = 0
	frame.BorderSizePixel = 0
	M.corner(frame, radius)
	M.gradient(frame, BZ.panelTop, BZ.panelBot, 90)
	if not frame:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIStroke") then bzStroke(frame, BZ.panelEdge, 4) end
	bzShadow(frame, 7, radius)
	if not frame:FindFirstChild("Rivet") then
		local w, h = frame.AbsoluteSize.X, frame.AbsoluteSize.Y
		-- fallback offsets for the very first frame (AbsoluteSize not resolved yet)
		if w == 0 then w, h = 440, 400 end
		bzRivet(frame, 16, 16, frame.ZIndex + 3)
		bzRivet(frame, w - 16, 16, frame.ZIndex + 3)
		bzRivet(frame, 16, h - 16, frame.ZIndex + 3)
		bzRivet(frame, w - 16, h - 16, frame.ZIndex + 3)
	end
	return frame
end

-- inset title bar with an optional leading glyph, e.g. "\u{1F4E6}". Pass
-- accentTop/accentBot to give a shop its OWN identity colour (rock shop
-- bronze, sell green, egg pink) instead of every panel sharing one cyan --
-- omit them and it falls back to the original cyan.
function M.bazaarHeader(parent, text, iconGlyph, accentTop, accentBot)
	local bar = Instance.new("Frame")
	bar.Name = "BazaarHeader"
	bar.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0)
	bar.Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0, 10)
	bar.Size = UDim2.new(1, -58, 0, 44)
	bar.BackgroundColor3 = BZ.white
	bar.BorderSizePixel = 0
	bar.ZIndex = (parent.ZIndex or 1) + 2
	bar.Parent = parent
	M.corner(bar, 12)
	M.gradient(bar, accentTop or BZ.header1, accentBot or BZ.header2, 90)
	bzStroke(bar, BZ.panelEdge, 3)
	bzShadow(bar, 4, 12)

	if iconGlyph then
		local icon = Instance.new("TextLabel")
		icon.Name = "Icon"
		icon.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0, 0.5)
		icon.Position = UDim2.new(0, 8, 0.5, 0)
		icon.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(30, 30)
		icon.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		icon.Font = Enum.Font.GothamBold
		icon.Text = iconGlyph
		icon.TextSize = 24
		icon.ZIndex = bar.ZIndex + 1
		icon.Parent = bar
	end

	local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	label.Name = "Title"
	label.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0, 0.5)
	label.Position = UDim2.new(0, iconGlyph and 42 or 14, 0.5, 0)
	label.Size = UDim2.new(1, (iconGlyph and -52 or -24), 1, 0)
	label.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	label.Font = M.BazaarFont
	label.Text = text or ""
	label.TextColor3 = BZ.white -- red header = dark ground: white + stroke stays
	label.TextSize = 21
	label.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left
	label.TextTruncate = Enum.TextTruncate.AtEnd
	label.ZIndex = bar.ZIndex + 1
	label:SetAttribute("NoPolish", true) -- LemonPop: the pack governs its own text
	label.Parent = bar
	bzTextStroke(label, 2)
	return bar, label
end

-- one dark bordered item row; caller fills in icon/title/desc/pills. Rows
-- alternate between two close shades (odd/even, counted off existing
-- siblings) so a long list reads as a striped stall shelf instead of one
-- undifferentiated dark slab -- purely cosmetic, no call site needs to change.
function M.bazaarRow(parent, height)
	local existing = 0
	for _, c in ipairs(parent:GetChildren()) do
		if c:IsA("Frame") and c.Name == "Row" then existing += 1 end
	end
	local top, bot = BZ.cardTop, BZ.cardBot
	if existing % 2 == 1 then top, bot = BZ.rowAltTop, BZ.rowAltBot end

	local row = Instance.new("Frame")
	row.Name = "Row"
	row.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, height or 96)
	row.BackgroundColor3 = top
	row.BorderSizePixel = 0
	row.Parent = parent
	M.corner(row, 12)
	M.gradient(row, top, bot, 90)
	bzStroke(row, BZ.cardEdge, 3)
	return row
end
