-- is already in memory -- a flaky read must never blank a working index.
local function loadAll()
	if not storeReady() then return end
	local fresh = {}
	for shard = 1, NUM_SHARDS do
		local ok, result = pcall(function()
			return store:GetAsync(shardName(shard))
		end)
		if not ok then
			noteFailure("load", result)
			return
		end
		if type(result) == "table" then
			for key, list in pairs(mergeShard(result, nil)) do
				fresh[key] = list
			end
		end
	end
	noteSuccess()
	index = fresh
	applyPending() -- observations not yet written are still ours to report
end

local function requeue(key, list)
	local dest = pending[key]
	if not dest then
		dest = {}
		pending[key] = dest
	end
	for _, o in ipairs(list) do
		if #dest < MAX_OBS_PER_ITEM then
			table.insert(dest, o)
			pendingCount += 1
		end
	end
end

local function flush()
	if pendingCount == 0 or not storeReady() then return end

	-- Detach BEFORE the first yield. UpdateAsync yields, and a sale landing
	-- during that yield must go into a fresh queue, not into the table the
	-- transform is already reading (and that we are about to clear).
	local outgoing = pending
	pending = {}
	pendingCount = 0

	local byShard = {}
	for key, list in pairs(outgoing) do
		local shard = shardOf(key)
		local bucket = byShard[shard]
		if not bucket then
			bucket = {}
			byShard[shard] = bucket
		end
		bucket[key] = list
	end

	for shard, adds in pairs(byShard) do
		local merged
		local ok, err = pcall(function()
			store:UpdateAsync(shardName(shard), function(old)
				merged = mergeShard(old, adds)
				return merged
			end)
		end)
		if ok and merged then
			noteSuccess()
			-- The merged shard is the freshest view we have of these items: it
			-- also contains sales other servers wrote since our last read.
			for key, list in pairs(merged) do
				index[key] = list
			end
		else
			noteFailure("flush", err)
			for key, list in pairs(adds) do
				requeue(key, list) -- try again next cycle; still readable in memory meanwhile
			end
		end
	end
end

-- One lock so a periodic flush and a periodic reload can never interleave and
-- half-overwrite each other, and so nothing in here can ever throw at a caller.
local function guarded(fn)
	if busy then return false end
	busy = true
	local ok, err = pcall(fn)
	busy = false
	if not ok then
		warn("[PriceIndex] " .. tostring(err))
	end
	return true
end

-- Logs one completed sale. Returns true if it was accepted as an observation.
-- NEVER YIELDS: it only touches memory, so it is safe to call from inside a
-- no-yield critical section such as the booth buy path.
function PriceIndex.RecordSale(name, mutation, price, buyerUserId, sellerUserId)
	if type(name) ~= "string" or name == "" then return false end
	if mutation ~= nil and type(mutation) ~= "string" then return false end

	price = tonumber(price)
	if not price or price ~= price or price == math.huge then return false end
	price = math.floor(price)
	if price < 1 or price > MAX_PRICE then return false end

	if type(buyerUserId) ~= "number" or buyerUserId ~= buyerUserId then return false end
	if type(sellerUserId) ~= "number" or sellerUserId ~= sellerUserId then return false end
	buyerUserId, sellerUserId = math.floor(buyerUserId), math.floor(sellerUserId)
	-- "selling to yourself" is wash trading in its simplest form, not a price
	if buyerUserId == sellerUserId then return false end

	local key = itemKey(name, mutation)
	local now = os.time()
	local obs = { T = now, P = price, B = buyerUserId, S = sellerUserId }

	local list = index[key]
	if not list then
		list = {}
		index[key] = list
	end
	-- oldest first, so everything that has aged out sits at the front
	while #list > 0 and list[1].T < now - WINDOW do
		table.remove(list, 1)
	end
	-- past the per-pair cap the extra rows are dead weight: Get() collapses a
	-- pair to a single vote anyway, so storing more only feeds a wash-trader's
	-- ability to bloat the shard.
	if countPair(list, pairKey(buyerUserId, sellerUserId)) >= MAX_PER_PAIR then
		return false
	end
	table.insert(list, obs)
	while #list > MAX_OBS_PER_ITEM do
		table.remove(list, 1)
	end

	local queue = pending[key]
	if not queue then
		queue = {}
		pending[key] = queue
	end
	table.insert(queue, obs)
	pendingCount += 1
	return true
end

-- Returns median, sampleCount for the last 7 days.
-- Returns nil, sampleCount while the sample is below MIN_SAMPLES -- the count is
-- still handed back so a UI can honestly say "3 of 5 sales needed" rather than
-- inventing a price. Never yields.
function PriceIndex.Get(name, mutation)
	if type(name) ~= "string" then return nil, 0 end
	if mutation ~= nil and type(mutation) ~= "string" then return nil, 0 end

	local list = index[itemKey(name, mutation)]
	if not list then return nil, 0 end

	local cutoff = os.time() - WINDOW
	local live = {}
	for _, o in ipairs(list) do
		if o.T >= cutoff then
			table.insert(live, o)
		end
	end
	table.sort(live, function(a, b) return a.T < b.T end)

	-- One vote per counterparty pair, and it is their EARLIEST trade. Keeping
	-- the earliest rather than the latest matters: it means a pair cannot keep
	-- re-trading to steer the value of the single vote they are allowed.
	local seen, prices = {}, {}
	for _, o in ipairs(live) do
		local pk = pairKey(o.B, o.S)
		if not seen[pk] then
			seen[pk] = true
			table.insert(prices, o.P)
		end
	end

	local n = #prices
	if n < MIN_SAMPLES then
		return nil, n
	end

	table.sort(prices)
	local mid = math.floor(n / 2)
	local median
	if n % 2 == 1 then
		median = prices[mid + 1]
	else
		median = (prices[mid] + prices[mid + 1]) / 2
	end
	return math.floor(median + 0.5), n
end

function PriceIndex.Init()
	-- Non-blocking on purpose: Main runs every Init() in sequence, so a cold
	-- DataStore read must not hold up the rest of the server's boot. Until the
	-- first load lands Get() reports "not enough data", which is already the
	-- right answer for a server that has not seen any sales yet.
	--
	-- Flush and reload share ONE coroutine so they can never overlap.
	task.spawn(function()
		guarded(loadAll)
		local sinceRefresh = 0
		while true do
			task.wait(FLUSH_SECONDS)
			guarded(flush)
			sinceRefresh += FLUSH_SECONDS
			if sinceRefresh >= REFRESH_SECONDS then
				sinceRefresh = 0
				guarded(loadAll)
			end
		end
	end)

	game:BindToClose(function()
		local waited = 0
		while busy and waited < 5 do
			task.wait(0.1)
			waited += 0.1
		end
		guarded(flush) -- don't lose the last few sales on shutdown
	end)

	print(("PriceIndex online (%d-day median, min %d sales)"):format(PriceIndex.WindowDays, MIN_SAMPLES))
end

return PriceIndex


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ServerScriptService/Modules/ProductRegistry.lua =====
local MarketplaceService = game:GetService("MarketplaceService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local PDM = require(script.Parent.PlayerDataManager)
local DarrelService = require(script.Parent.DarrelService)

local M = {}
local PRODUCTS = {}  -- [productId] = { Type, Amount }

function M.Register(productId, def)
	if productId == 0 then return end  -- placeholder: inert until the user creates real ids
	assert(PRODUCTS[productId] == nil, "duplicate product id " .. productId)
	PRODUCTS[productId] = def
end

local function grant(player, data, def)
	if def.Type == "Darrels" then
		-- Award returns false (never throws post-mutation) on invalid amounts. A
		-- false must NOT reach the ReceiptLog: once a PurchaseId is logged, the
		-- dedupe branch answers PurchaseGranted forever with nothing credited.
		return DarrelService.Award(player, def.Amount, "robux:" .. tostring(def.Amount)) == true
	end
	return false
end

-- The actual receipt-processing logic, kept as a standalone function so it can
-- be unit-tested (and reused by Task 12's idempotence test) without going
-- through MarketplaceService. M.Init() assigns THIS SAME function to
-- MarketplaceService.ProcessReceipt -- see the comment there for why that
-- assignment must never be duplicated anywhere else in the game.
function M.ProcessReceipt(info)
	local player = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(info.PlayerId)
	if not player then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
	local data = PDM.Get(player)
	if not data or data.__noSave then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end

	local key = tostring(info.PurchaseId)
	if table.find(data.ReceiptLog, key) then
		-- grant already in memory; only confirm once it has persisted at least once
		local saved = PDM.Save(player)
		if saved then
			return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted
		else
			return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet
		end
	end
	local def = PRODUCTS[info.ProductId]
	if not def then
		warn("[ProductRegistry] unknown product id " .. tostring(info.ProductId))
		return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet
	end
	-- pcall is defense-in-depth only: grant implementations must never throw
	-- AFTER mutating data, because a caught failure returns NotProcessedYet on
	-- the assumption nothing was granted. DarrelService.Award upholds this by
	-- pcall'ing its own post-mutation notify path.
	local ok, granted = pcall(grant, player, data, def)
	if not ok then
		warn("[ProductRegistry] grant threw for product " .. tostring(info.ProductId) .. ": " .. tostring(granted))
	end
	if not ok or granted ~= true then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
	table.insert(data.ReceiptLog, key)
	if #data.ReceiptLog > 50 then table.remove(data.ReceiptLog, 1) end
	local saved = PDM.Save(player)
	if not saved then
		-- Grant + log are in-memory only. If this session never saves, both the
		-- darrels AND the log entry vanish together -- a Roblox retry next session
		-- re-grants correctly. So NotProcessedYet is safe AND self-consistent.
		return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet
	end
	return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted
end

function M.Init()
	-- Roblox allows exactly ONE ProcessReceipt per game. This is it. Add new
	-- purchasables via M.Register, never a second assignment.
	MarketplaceService.ProcessReceipt = M.ProcessReceipt

	-- Darrel packs (user creates dev products on roblox.com, then replaces these zeros):
	local PACK_IDS = { 0, 0, 0, 0 }           -- <- fill with real dev product ids
	local PACK_AMOUNTS = { 80, 180, 400, 1000 }
	for i, id in ipairs(PACK_IDS) do
		M.Register(id, { Type = "Darrels", Amount = PACK_AMOUNTS[i] })
	end
end

return M


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ServerScriptService/Modules/QuestHandler.lua =====
-- QuestHandler: a Goals board of one-time milestone rewards. Fully data-driven
-- (polls player data), so it needs no hooks into the throw/sell/plot handlers.
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local ServerScriptService = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")

local PlayerDataManager = require(ServerScriptService.Modules.PlayerDataManager)
local BrainrotConfig = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.BrainrotConfig)
local remotes = ReplicatedStorage.Remotes

local RARITY_ORDER = { Common = 1, Uncommon = 2, Rare = 3, Epic = 4, Legendary = 5, Mythic = 6, Secret = 7, God = 8 }
local rarityByName = {}
for _, b in ipairs(BrainrotConfig) do rarityByName[b.Name] = b.Rarity end

-- data helpers
local function bestRarity(data)
	local best = 0
	for _, e in ipairs(data.Brainrots) do
		best = math.max(best, RARITY_ORDER[rarityByName[e.Name] or "Common"] or 1)
	end
	return best
end
local function totalBrainrots(data) return #data.Brainrots end
local function filledPads(data)
	local n = 0
	for _, e in ipairs(data.Brainrots) do if e.PadIndex then n += 1 end end
	return n
end
local function maxDupe(data)
	local counts, m = {}, 0
	for _, e in ipairs(data.Brainrots) do
		counts[e.Name] = (counts[e.Name] or 0) + 1
		m = math.max(m, counts[e.Name])
	end
	return m
end

-- ordered goal list (id, description, reward, met(data))
-- Every goal now carries cur(data) + target alongside met(). The protocol could
-- previously only say yes/no, so "fill 10 plot spots" transmitted Met = false
-- whether you had 0 or 9 -- there was nothing a progress bar could read.
--
-- met() is KEPT and still authoritative for claiming: cur/target are for display
-- only, so a display bug can never hand out a reward. The two agree by
-- construction (met is cur >= target) but claim never consults cur.
local QUESTS = {
	{ id = "uncommon",  desc = "Catch an Uncommon+ brainrot", reward = 1500,  target = 2,
	  cur = bestRarity,      met = function(d) return bestRarity(d) >= 2 end },
	{ id = "own5",      desc = "Own 5 brainrots",             reward = 4000,  target = 5,
	  cur = totalBrainrots,  met = function(d) return totalBrainrots(d) >= 5 end },
	{ id = "cash25k",   desc = "Reach $25,000 cash",          reward = 6000,  target = 25000,
	  cur = function(d) return d.Cash end,   met = function(d) return d.Cash >= 25000 end },
	{ id = "rare",      desc = "Catch a Rare+ brainrot",      reward = 10000, target = 3,
	  cur = bestRarity,      met = function(d) return bestRarity(d) >= 3 end },
	{ id = "dupe3",     desc = "Own 3 of the same brainrot",  reward = 8000,  target = 3,
	  cur = maxDupe,         met = function(d) return maxDupe(d) >= 3 end },
	{ id = "pads10",    desc = "Fill 10 plot spots",          reward = 18000, target = 10,
	  cur = filledPads,      met = function(d) return filledPads(d) >= 10 end },
	{ id = "epic",      desc = "Catch an Epic+ brainrot",     reward = 30000, target = 4,
	  cur = bestRarity,      met = function(d) return bestRarity(d) >= 4 end },
	{ id = "cash250k",  desc = "Reach $250,000 cash",         reward = 40000, target = 250000,
	  cur = function(d) return d.Cash end,   met = function(d) return d.Cash >= 250000 end },
	{ id = "legendary", desc = "Catch a Legendary+ brainrot", reward = 75000, target = 5,
	  cur = bestRarity,      met = function(d) return bestRarity(d) >= 5 end },
	{ id = "mythic",    desc = "Catch a Mythic+ brainrot",    reward = 200000,target = 6,
	  cur = bestRarity,      met = function(d) return bestRarity(d) >= 6 end },
}

local QuestHandler = {}

function QuestHandler.SendState(player)
	local data = PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
	if not data then return end
	local list = {}
	for _, q in ipairs(QUESTS) do
		-- Cur is clamped to Target for display so a bar can never overfill (you can
		-- hold $9m against a $25k goal). Met stays exactly as it was -- everything
		-- already reading this payload is unaffected.
		local target = q.target or 1
		local cur = math.clamp(tonumber(q.cur and q.cur(data)) or 0, 0, target)
		list[#list + 1] = {
			Id = q.id, Desc = q.desc, Reward = q.reward,
			Met = q.met(data) == true,
			Claimed = data.Quests[q.id] == true,
			Cur = cur, Target = target,
		}
	end
	remotes.QuestState:FireClient(player, list)
end

local function claim(player, questId)
	if typeof(questId) ~= "string" then return end
	local data = PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
	if not data then return end
	local quest
	for _, q in ipairs(QUESTS) do if q.id == questId then quest = q break end end
	if not quest then return end
	if data.Quests[questId] then return end        -- already claimed
	if not quest.met(data) then return end          -- goal not reached
	data.Quests[questId] = true
	PlayerDataManager.GrantCash(data, quest.reward)
	PlayerDataManager.PushUpdate(player)
	QuestHandler.SendState(player)
end

function QuestHandler.Init()
	remotes.QuestClaim.OnServerEvent:Connect(claim)

	local function onJoin(player)
		task.spawn(function()
			local tries = 0
			while not PlayerDataManager.Get(player) and tries < 60 do task.wait(0.1); tries += 1 end
			if PlayerDataManager.Get(player) then
				task.wait(1)
				QuestHandler.SendState(player)
			end
		end)
	end
	Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onJoin)
	for _, p in ipairs(Players:GetPlayers()) do onJoin(p) end

	-- refresh 'Met' flags periodically as players progress
	task.spawn(function()
		while true do
			task.wait(3)
			for _, p in ipairs(Players:GetPlayers()) do QuestHandler.SendState(p) end
		end
	end)

	print("QuestHandler online")
end

return QuestHandler


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ServerScriptService/Modules/RarityRoll.lua =====
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local RarityConfig = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.RarityConfig)
local BrainrotConfig = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.BrainrotConfig)
local Waves = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.BrainrotWaves)
local SupplySchedule = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.SupplySchedule)
local LimitedStock = require(script.Parent.LimitedStock)

-- Pools are CACHED, not static: availability changes over time (weekly tide
-- flips, seasonal retirements), when a capped name sells out, and when the
-- emergency override tables flip. The cache key captures exactly those inputs,
-- so pools rebuild at boundaries and never in between -- a per-throw scan over
-- 214 entries stays off the hot path.
local poolsByTier, totalByTier, fixedByTier
local currentKey = nil

local function poolKey()
	-- OverrideKey folds in the FORCE_ON/VAULTED emergency levers so a runtime
	-- flip rebuilds pools immediately instead of hiding until the next boundary.
	local key = SupplySchedule.PeriodKey() .. "#" .. Waves.OverrideKey()
	-- SoldOut is stale-tolerant (<=60s) and never yields, so folding it into the
	-- key costs a dozen table lookups. TryClaim at reveal time stays the authority.
	local sold = {}
	for name in pairs(LimitedStock.MAX) do
		if LimitedStock.SoldOut(name) then
			sold[#sold + 1] = name
		end
	end
	table.sort(sold)
	return key .. "|" .. table.concat(sold, "|")
end

local function rebuildPools()
	poolsByTier, totalByTier, fixedByTier = {}, {}, {}
	for _, entry in ipairs(BrainrotConfig) do
		if Waves.IsObtainable(entry.Name) and not LimitedStock.SoldOut(entry.Name) then
			if entry.FixedChance then
				local f = fixedByTier[entry.Rarity]
				if not f then f = {}; fixedByTier[entry.Rarity] = f end
				f[#f + 1] = entry
			else
				local p = poolsByTier[entry.Rarity]
				if not p then p = {}; poolsByTier[entry.Rarity] = p end
				p[#p + 1] = entry
				totalByTier[entry.Rarity] = (totalByTier[entry.Rarity] or 0) + entry.Weight
			end
		end
	end
end

local function ensurePools()
	local key = poolKey()
	if key ~= currentKey then
		currentKey = key
		rebuildPools()
	end
end
ensurePools()

-- A weighted entry's odds are Weight / (live tier total), so they move whenever a
-- wave changes which names are live. FixedChance entries are rolled on their own,
-- BEFORE the pool, so "1 in 100,000 Secret rolls" stays literally true across every
-- future wave. Their Weight is never summed and never used.
-- SoldOut is the cheap non-yielding pre-check, so an exhausted item stops costing a
-- roll. It can be stale; the authoritative reservation happens at reveal time in
-- ThrowHandler, which is also the only place allowed to yield.
local function rollFixed(tierName)
	local fixed = fixedByTier[tierName]
	if not fixed then return nil end
	for _, entry in ipairs(fixed) do
		if not LimitedStock.SoldOut(entry.Name) and math.random() < entry.FixedChance then
			return entry
		end
	end
	return nil
end

local RarityRoll = {}

function RarityRoll.TierForDistance(distance)
	for _, tier in ipairs(RarityConfig) do
		if distance >= tier.MinDistance and distance < tier.MaxDistance then
			return tier
		end
	end
	return RarityConfig[#RarityConfig]
end

-- Index of the tier a RAW distance reaches (no luck). The equipped rock decides
-- your reach; luck buys promotions on top (see ThrowHandler).
function RarityRoll.TierIndexForDistance(distance)
	for i = #RarityConfig, 1, -1 do
		if distance >= RarityConfig[i].MinDistance then return i end
	end
	return 1
end

-- Weighted pick within one tier, restricted to the CURRENTLY OBTAINABLE names,
-- after giving that tier's fixed-odds entries their independent roll.
-- Never returns a nil entry: an empty tier falls back down to the nearest tier
-- that has any, so a bad quota can never hand a player a nil catch.
-- skipFixed: used by the reveal-time fallback, when a limited item was rolled but its
-- last slot had already gone to another server. Re-rolls an ordinary catch for the tier.
function RarityRoll.PickInTier(tierIndex, skipFixed)
	ensurePools()
	tierIndex = math.clamp(tierIndex, 1, #RarityConfig)
	for i = tierIndex, 1, -1 do
		local tier = RarityConfig[i]
		local jackpot = not skipFixed and rollFixed(tier.Name) or nil
		if jackpot then return jackpot, tier end
		local pool = poolsByTier[tier.Name]
		local totalWeight = totalByTier[tier.Name]
		if pool and #pool > 0 and totalWeight and totalWeight > 0 then
			local roll = math.random() * totalWeight
			local cumulative = 0
			for _, entry in ipairs(pool) do
				cumulative += entry.Weight
				if roll <= cumulative then return entry, tier end
			end
			return pool[#pool], tier
		end
	end
	return nil, RarityConfig[1]
end

function RarityRoll.RollForDistance(distance)
	local tier = RarityRoll.TierForDistance(distance)
	local pool = {}
	local totalWeight = 0
	for _, entry in ipairs(BrainrotConfig) do
		if entry.Rarity == tier.Name then
			table.insert(pool, entry)
			totalWeight += entry.Weight
		end
	end
	if #pool == 0 then return nil, tier end
	if totalWeight <= 0 then return nil, tier end

	local roll = math.random() * totalWeight
	local cumulative = 0
	for _, entry in ipairs(pool) do
		cumulative += entry.Weight
		if roll <= cumulative then
			return entry, tier
		end
	end
	return pool[#pool], tier
end

return RarityRoll


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ServerScriptService/Modules/RebirthHandler.lua =====
-- RebirthHandler: prestige. Wipes CASH and your ROCK collection only -- brainrots
-- and their plot placements are kept -- in exchange for a small permanent stack of
-- money / luck / throw-power (applied in IncomeLoop + ThrowHandler via RebirthConfig).
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local ServerScriptService = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")

local PlayerDataManager = require(ServerScriptService.Modules.PlayerDataManager)
local MaxwellQuest = require(ServerScriptService.Modules.MaxwellQuest)
local RebirthConfig = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.RebirthConfig)
local remotes = ReplicatedStorage.Remotes

local RebirthHandler = {}

function RebirthHandler.SendState(player)
	local data = PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
	if not data then return end
	local r = data.Rebirths or 0
	remotes.RebirthState:FireClient(player, {
		Rebirths = r,
		Cost = RebirthConfig.Cost(r),
		IncomeMult = RebirthConfig.IncomeMult(r),
		LuckMult = RebirthConfig.LuckMult(r),
		PowerMult = RebirthConfig.PowerMult(r),
		NextIncomeMult = RebirthConfig.IncomeMult(r + 1),
		NextLuckMult = RebirthConfig.LuckMult(r + 1),
		NextPowerMult = RebirthConfig.PowerMult(r + 1),
		CanAfford = data.Cash >= RebirthConfig.Cost(r),
	})
end

local function doRebirth(player)
	local data = PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
	if not data then return end
	local r = data.Rebirths or 0
	local cost = RebirthConfig.Cost(r)
	local result = remotes:FindFirstChild("PurchaseResult")
	if data.Cash < cost then
		if result then result:FireClient(player, { Success = false, Message = "Not enough cash to rebirth." }) end
		RebirthHandler.SendState(player)
		return
	end

	-- the prestige sacrifice: cash and the rock collection, nothing else.
	-- Brainrots stay exactly where they are, still placed and still earning.
	data.Cash = 0
	data.OwnedRocks = { Pebble = true }
	data.EquippedRock = "Pebble"
	data.Rebirths = r + 1

	PlayerDataManager.PushUpdate(player)
	RebirthHandler.SendState(player)
	-- Maxwell's step 2 is "reach Rebirth 15"; let his questline react to the new total.
	pcall(MaxwellQuest.NotifyRebirth, player)
	if result then
		result:FireClient(player, { Success = true, Message = "\u{2B50} Rebirth " .. data.Rebirths .. "! Permanent boost unlocked." })
	end
end

function RebirthHandler.Init()
	remotes.RebirthRequest.OnServerEvent:Connect(doRebirth)

	local function onJoin(player)
		task.spawn(function()
			local tries = 0
			while not PlayerDataManager.Get(player) and tries < 60 do task.wait(0.1); tries += 1 end
			if PlayerDataManager.Get(player) then task.wait(1); RebirthHandler.SendState(player) end
		end)
	end
	Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onJoin)
	for _, p in ipairs(Players:GetPlayers()) do onJoin(p) end

	-- refresh CanAfford as cash grows
	task.spawn(function()
		while true do
			task.wait(3)
			for _, p in ipairs(Players:GetPlayers()) do RebirthHandler.SendState(p) end
		end
	end)

	print("RebirthHandler online")
end

return RebirthHandler


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ServerScriptService/Modules/SeasonPassHandler.lua =====
-- SeasonPassHandler: daily quests feed Season XP; XP unlocks a 25-tier reward track.
-- Other handlers report events via SeasonPassHandler.Notify / NotifyCatch (additive hooks).
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local ServerScriptService = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")

local PlayerDataManager = require(ServerScriptService.Modules.PlayerDataManager)
local SeasonConfig = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.SeasonConfig)
local RarityConfig = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.RarityConfig)

local remotes = ReplicatedStorage.Remotes

local rarityIndexByName = {}
for i, tier in ipairs(RarityConfig) do rarityIndexByName[tier.Name] = i end

local SeasonPassHandler = {}

local function currentDay()
	return math.floor(os.time() / 86400)
end

-- reset quest progress when the UTC day rolls over
local function ensureDay(data)
	local today = currentDay()
	if data.SeasonQuestDay ~= today then
		data.SeasonQuestDay = today
		data.SeasonQuests = {}
	end
	return today
end

function SeasonPassHandler.SendState(player)
	local data = PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
	if not data then return end
	local today = ensureDay(data)
	local questIds, progress = {}, {}
	for _, def in ipairs(SeasonConfig.QuestsForDay(today)) do
		table.insert(questIds, def.Id)
		local q = data.SeasonQuests[def.Id]
		progress[def.Id] = { P = q and q.P or 0, D = q and q.D or false }
	end
	remotes.SeasonState:FireClient(player, {
		XP = data.SeasonXP or 0,
		Claimed = data.SeasonClaimed or {},
		QuestIds = questIds,
		Progress = progress,
		Day = today,
	})
end

function SeasonPassHandler.Notify(player, event, n)
	local data = PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
	if not data then return end
	local today = ensureDay(data)
	local changed = false
	for _, def in ipairs(SeasonConfig.QuestsForDay(today)) do
		if def.Event == event then
			local q = data.SeasonQuests[def.Id]
			if not q then q = { P = 0, D = false }; data.SeasonQuests[def.Id] = q end
			if not q.D then
				q.P = math.min(q.P + (n or 1), def.Target)
				if q.P >= def.Target then
					q.D = true
					data.SeasonXP = (data.SeasonXP or 0) + def.XP
				end
				changed = true
			end
		end
	end
	if changed then
		SeasonPassHandler.SendState(player)
	end
end

-- Rare = index 3+, Epic = index 4+ (both quests can progress from one catch)
function SeasonPassHandler.NotifyCatch(player, tierName)
	local idx = rarityIndexByName[tierName]
	if not idx then return end
	if idx >= 3 then SeasonPassHandler.Notify(player, "RareCatch", 1) end
	if idx >= 4 then SeasonPassHandler.Notify(player, "EpicCatch", 1) end
end

local function claimTier(player, tier)
	local data = PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
	if not data then return end
	if typeof(tier) ~= "number" or tier ~= math.floor(tier) then return end
	local def = SeasonConfig.Tiers[tier]
	if not def then return end
	data.SeasonClaimed = data.SeasonClaimed or {}
	local key = tostring(tier) -- datastore-safe key
	if data.SeasonClaimed[key] then return end
	if (data.SeasonXP or 0) < SeasonConfig.ThresholdFor(tier) then return end
	data.SeasonClaimed[key] = true
	PlayerDataManager.GrantCash(data, def.Cash)
	PlayerDataManager.PushUpdate(player)
	SeasonPassHandler.SendState(player)
end

function SeasonPassHandler.Init()
	remotes.SeasonClaim.OnServerEvent:Connect(claimTier)
	-- client asks for state once its UI is listening
	remotes.SeasonState.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player)
		SeasonPassHandler.SendState(player)
	end)
	print("SeasonPassHandler online")
end

return SeasonPassHandler


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ServerScriptService/Modules/SellHandler.lua =====
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local ServerScriptService = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")

local PlayerDataManager = require(ServerScriptService.Modules.PlayerDataManager)
local InventoryHandler = require(ServerScriptService.Modules.InventoryHandler)
local MintRegistry = require(ServerScriptService.Modules.MintRegistry)
local BrainrotConfig = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.BrainrotConfig)
local Mutations = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.MutationConfig)

local SELL_MULTIPLIER = 40

local cashPerSecondByName = {}
local rarityByName = {}
for _, entry in ipairs(BrainrotConfig) do
	cashPerSecondByName[entry.Name] = entry.CashPerSecond
	rarityByName[entry.Name] = entry.Rarity
end

local remotes = ReplicatedStorage.Remotes

local SellHandler = {}

function SellHandler.Init()
	remotes.SellBrainrot.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, payload)
		local data = PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
		if not data then return end
		if typeof(payload) ~= "table" or typeof(payload.Name) ~= "string" then return end

		local cashPerSecond = cashPerSecondByName[payload.Name]
		if not cashPerSecond then
			remotes.SellResult:FireClient(player, { Success = false, Message = "Unknown brainrot." })
			return
		end

		local sellValueEach = cashPerSecond * SELL_MULTIPLIER
		local mode = payload.Mode == "All" and "All" or "One"

		-- Only brainrots sitting in the inventory can be sold. A placed one is
		-- earning on the base and must be picked up first (hold E on it), which
		-- is what clears its PadIndex. This also means selling never has to tear
		-- down a pad model -- if it is sellable, there is no model to remove.
		--
		-- WHICH copies sell:
		--   One: the LEAST valuable unplaced copy (smallest Mutations.Mult) - the
		--        same rule BrainrotMover.Take uses, so selling a plain copy can
		--        never silently eat your Golden one.
		--   All: every unplaced PLAIN copy; mutated copies are skipped unless the
		--        client explicitly opts in with payload.IncludeMutated == true.
		local sellIndex = {}
		if mode == "All" then
			local includeMutated = payload.IncludeMutated == true
			for i, entry in ipairs(data.Brainrots) do
				if entry.Name == payload.Name and entry.PadIndex == nil
					and (includeMutated or entry.Mutation == nil) then
					sellIndex[i] = true
				end
			end
		else
			local bestIndex, bestMult
			for i, entry in ipairs(data.Brainrots) do
				if entry.Name == payload.Name and entry.PadIndex == nil then
					local mult = Mutations.Mult(entry.Mutation)
					if not bestMult or mult < bestMult then
						bestIndex, bestMult = i, mult
					end
				end
			end
			if bestIndex then sellIndex[bestIndex] = true end
		end

		local totalSold, placedSkipped = 0, 0
		local remaining = {}
		for i, entry in ipairs(data.Brainrots) do
			if sellIndex[i] then
				totalSold += 1
				PlayerDataManager.DrainPending(player, entry, data)
				-- sold copies are destroyed for good: record the burn so the
				-- registry's live "exists" counts stay honest (gated on IsTracked,
				-- the same rule the mint side uses).
				if MintRegistry.IsTracked(rarityByName[entry.Name], entry.Mutation) then
					pcall(MintRegistry.Burn, entry.Name, entry.Mutation, 1)
				end
			else
				if entry.Name == payload.Name and entry.PadIndex then placedSkipped += 1 end
				table.insert(remaining, entry)
			end
		end
		data.Brainrots = remaining

		if totalSold == 0 then
			local msg = placedSkipped > 0
				and ("That " .. payload.Name .. " is on your base \u{2014} pick it up first (hold E on it).")
				or ("You don't own any " .. payload.Name .. ".")
			remotes.SellResult:FireClient(player, { Success = false, Message = msg })
			return
		end

		local totalValue = totalSold * sellValueEach
		PlayerDataManager.GrantCash(data, totalValue)

		remotes.SellResult:FireClient(player, {
			Success = true,
			Message = "Sold " .. totalSold .. "x " .. payload.Name .. " for $" .. totalValue,
			Amount = totalValue,
		})

		-- the sold entries are gone from data; rebuild the Backpack so their Tools
		-- go with them. Without this the tool lingers and the brainrot still looks
		-- like it is in the inventory.
		InventoryHandler.SyncBackpack(player)
		PlayerDataManager.PushUpdate(player)
	end)
end

return SellHandler


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ServerScriptService/Modules/SessionLock.lua =====
-- SessionLock: makes a profile owned by exactly one live server at a time.
--
-- WHY THIS EXISTS. World 2 is moving to its own Place in this universe, so a player
-- will cross servers mid-session. Both places read the same DataStore key, and the
-- destination server can finish its load BEFORE the origin server's save lands. The
-- player then arrives as their older self while everything they spent still exists --
-- that is the classic cross-place duplication bug, and with trading, booth sales and
-- a price index it would poison the economy rather than just inconvenience one player.
--
-- The fix is to make the read and the claim ONE transaction. Everything here goes
-- through UpdateAsync on the same key PlayerDataManager uses, because a lock kept
-- anywhere else can always disagree with the profile it is supposed to be guarding.
--
-- Returning nil from an UpdateAsync transform cancels the write. That is how a claim
-- refuses without touching the stored profile.
local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")

local M = {}

-- MUST match PlayerDataManager exactly, or the lock guards nothing.
local STORE_NAME = "BrainrotSkip_PlayerData_v1"
local KEY_PREFIX = "Player_"
local store = DataStoreService:GetDataStore(STORE_NAME)

local JOB = game.JobId ~= "" and game.JobId or ("studio-" .. tostring(os.clock()))
local PLACE = game.PlaceId

-- A server that crashes never releases its lock, so a lock has to be able to die of
-- old age. 90s is comfortably longer than the 30s heartbeat: a live server always
-- refreshes well inside the window, a dead one is reclaimable within a minute and a half.
local STALE_AFTER = 90
local HEARTBEAT = 30
local CLAIM_TRIES = 6
local CLAIM_WAIT = 2

local function key(userId) return KEY_PREFIX .. userId end
local function held(sess)
	return sess and sess.job and sess.job ~= JOB and (os.time() - (sess.t or 0)) < STALE_AFTER
end

M.owned = {}          -- [userId] = true while this server holds the lock

-- Claim the profile and return it in the same transaction.
-- Returns: data, status   where status is "ok" | "new" | "locked" | "error"
-- On "locked" or "error" the caller MUST treat the session as read-only.
function M.Claim(userId)
	local out, status
	for attempt = 1, CLAIM_TRIES do
		local ok, err = pcall(function()
			store:UpdateAsync(key(userId), function(oldData)
				if oldData and held(oldData.__session) then
					status = "locked"
					return nil                       -- cancel: someone else is live on this profile
				end
				local d = oldData
				if d == nil then
					status = "new"
					d = { __sessionNew = true }      -- marker only; caller supplies real defaults
				else
					status = "ok"
				end
				d.__session = { job = JOB, t = os.time(), place = PLACE }
				out = d
				return d
			end)
		end)
		if ok and status ~= "locked" then
			M.owned[userId] = true
			return out, status
		end
		if not ok then
			status = "error"
			warn(("[SessionLock] claim error for %d: %s"):format(userId, tostring(err)))
		end
		if attempt < CLAIM_TRIES then task.wait(CLAIM_WAIT) end
	end
	return nil, status or "error"
end

-- Write the profile, but only while we still hold the lock. If another server has
-- taken it we are the stale session and writing would roll their progress back.
function M.Save(userId, data)
	if not data or data.__noSave then return false end
	local wrote = false
	for attempt = 1, 3 do
		local ok, err = pcall(function()
			store:UpdateAsync(key(userId), function(oldData)
				if oldData and held(oldData.__session) then
					return nil                       -- lock stolen: refuse, do not clobber
				end
				data.__session = { job = JOB, t = os.time(), place = PLACE }
				wrote = true
				return data
			end)
		end)
		if ok then return wrote end
		if attempt == 3 then
			warn(("[SessionLock] save FAILED for %d: %s"):format(userId, tostring(err)))
		else
			task.wait(0.4 * attempt)
		end
	end
	return false
end

-- Final write + hand the profile back. Call this BEFORE TeleportAsync, and await it,
-- so the destination server's Claim finds an unlocked profile with current data.
function M.Release(userId, data)
	local released = false
	local ok, err = pcall(function()
		store:UpdateAsync(key(userId), function(oldData)
			if oldData and held(oldData.__session) then return nil end
			local d = data or oldData
			if not d then return nil end
			if not d.__noSave then
				d.__session = nil                    -- unlocked, ready for the next server
				released = true
				return d
			end
			return nil
		end)
	end)
	if not ok then
		warn(("[SessionLock] release error for %d: %s"):format(userId, tostring(err)))
	end
	M.owned[userId] = nil
	return released
end

-- Keeps our locks from ageing out while the player is still here. Cheap: one
-- UpdateAsync per player per 30s, well inside DataStore budgets.
function M.StartHeartbeat(getData)
	task.spawn(function()
		while true do
			task.wait(HEARTBEAT)
			for userId in pairs(M.owned) do
				local data = getData and getData(userId)
				if data and not data.__noSave then
					pcall(function()
						store:UpdateAsync(key(userId), function(oldData)
							if oldData and held(oldData.__session) then return nil end
							local d = oldData or data
							d.__session = { job = JOB, t = os.time(), place = PLACE }
							return d
						end)
					end)
				end
			end
		end
	end)
end

-- SHUTDOWN. Without this, a server that stops (including Studio's Stop button, which
-- does fire BindToClose) leaves its locks looking live for the full stale window, and the
-- next session to load that profile gets a read-only one. In Studio that is every single
-- Stop -> Play cycle, because JobId is empty there so each run counts as a new server.
--
-- Roblox gives BindToClose up to 30s; releasing N profiles is N UpdateAsync calls, so this
-- comfortably fits for any realistic server size.
function M.ReleaseAll(getData)
	local ids = {}
	for userId in pairs(M.owned) do table.insert(ids, userId) end
	for _, userId in ipairs(ids) do
		local data = getData and getData(userId)
		pcall(M.Release, userId, data)
	end
	return #ids
end

M.JobId = JOB
M.StaleAfter = STALE_AFTER
return M


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ServerScriptService/Modules/SettingsService.lua =====
-- SettingsService: validates and persists the Settings panel's preferences
-- (kit README §3.3) into data.Settings. ONE remote: SettingsSave (RemoteEvent,
-- client->server, fire-and-forget -- see GameHUDPanels.SettingsPanel's
-- slider/segmented/toggle wiring). Self-heals the remote under
-- ReplicatedStorage.Remotes on Init() rather than assuming it was hand-built
-- in Studio, same spirit as this file's own creation.
--
-- WHITELIST DISCIPLINE: the keys the kit's Settings panel writes (music, sfx,
-- quality, fastSpin, hideOwnBanners, cinematicReducedMotion, cinematicLowQuality,
-- skipReveal), plus the two HUD collapses
-- (navHidden, questsHidden) documented at their branch below. Anything else in the
-- payload is silently dropped (warn + skip that ONE key -- a malformed or
-- hostile client sending {Cash=999} alongside a legit {music=0.5} must not
-- lose the legit half of the update, and must never be able to touch a
-- field outside data.Settings). Numeric fields (music/sfx) are CLAMPED into
-- [0,1] rather than rejected outright -- an out-of-range value is still a
-- real intent ("turn it up/down"), so clamping preserves the direction
-- instead of discarding the whole update. quality and the booleans
-- (fastSpin/hideOwnBanners) are type+enum checked and dropped (not
-- coerced) on mismatch. skipReveal is a TABLE of {TierName = bool} --
-- rebuilt against the RarityConfig tier whitelist rather than trusted,
-- and replaced whole on every write (the panel always sends all chips).
-- (v1 note: a single boolean `skipAnimations` shipped briefly on
-- 2026-08-04 and was superseded the same day by per-rarity skipReveal;
-- the old field may linger inertly in old saves, and the panel migrates
-- it client-side to all-rarities-on.)
--
-- QUALITY ENUM DEVIATION: the task brief spells this enum
-- {"Low","Med","High"}, but StarterPlayerScripts.GameHUDClient's own
-- ctx.state.settings default (shipped Task 3, already live/committed) is
-- `quality = "Medium"`, and the kit's own settings.png capture labels the
-- middle button "Medium" in full. Validating against "Med" would reject
-- that pre-existing default the instant a client round-trips it, so this
-- module validates "Medium" (not "Med") for consistency with what Task 3
-- already shipped and what the kit literally shows on screen. Documented
-- deviation; see task-10-report.md.
--
-- REDEEM CODE: the kit's Settings footer also draws a "Redeem Code" button,
-- and the task brief asks for a stub RemoteFunction named "RedeemCode" here
-- that always answers `false, "Invalid code"`. That name is NOT free --
-- ReplicatedStorage.Remotes.RedeemCode already exists, as a RemoteEvent,
-- wired end-to-end to a REAL promo-code system (ServerScriptService.Modules.
-- DailyRewardHandler.redeemCode + ServerScriptService.Modules.CodeConfig's 4
-- live codes), already used by the legacy DailyRewardClient UI. A second
-- same-named instance would make every `remotes.RedeemCode` lookup in the
-- game ambiguous, and a permanently-failing stub would be a real regression
-- for a player who types a genuine code into the NEW panel instead of the
-- old one. SettingsPanel therefore fires the EXISTING RedeemCode remote
-- directly -- nothing added here. Documented deviation; see
-- task-10-report.md.

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local ServerScriptService = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")
local PlayerDataManager = require(ServerScriptService.Modules.PlayerDataManager)
local RarityConfig = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Modules"):WaitForChild("RarityConfig"))

local remotes = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Remotes")

local QUALITY_VALUES = { Low = true, Medium = true, High = true }

local SettingsService = {}

-- RATE LIMIT WITHOUT LOSING INTENT. At most one applied write per player per
-- window; anything arriving inside the window is COALESCED into a pending payload
-- and flushed when the window expires, rather than dropped.
--
-- This used to be a bare `return` on the debounce, and with a single settings panel
-- that was invisible: you cannot drag two sliders at once. Two independent HUD
-- collapse buttons broke it immediately (2026-08-07) -- press HIDE UI and the quest
-- toggle in quick succession and the second one applies on screen, fires, and is
-- thrown away, so the client shows one thing and the save holds another. The player
-- finds out on their next join, when the HUD comes back wrong.
--
-- Coalescing keeps the real protection (a client firing in a loop still cannot make
-- us apply+push in a loop) while honouring the last value for every key it sent.
local SAVE_WINDOW = 0.5
local lastSave = {}  -- [player] = os.clock() of the last APPLIED write
local pending = {}   -- [player] = merged payload awaiting flush (nil = none scheduled)

local function clamp01(n)
	if type(n) ~= "number" or n ~= n then
		return nil -- reject NaN/non-numbers outright, nothing sane to clamp
	end
	return math.clamp(n, 0, 1)
end

-- Validates ONE payload table against the whitelist. Returns a NEW table
-- containing only the keys that passed (clamped/typed) -- never mutates
-- `tbl`. Exposed so the fresh-clone whitelist probe (task brief Step 5) can
-- call it directly on a fabricated table without touching a live player:
-- rejects {Cash=999}, accepts {music=0.5}, clamps {sfx=99}->1.
function SettingsService._Validate(tbl)
	local out = {}
	if type(tbl) ~= "table" then
		return out
	end
	for key, value in pairs(tbl) do
		if key == "music" or key == "sfx" then
			local v = clamp01(value)
			if v then
				out[key] = v
			else
				warn("[SettingsService] dropped invalid " .. key .. ": " .. tostring(value))
			end
		elseif key == "quality" then
			if type(value) == "string" and QUALITY_VALUES[value] then
				out.quality = value
			else
				warn("[SettingsService] dropped invalid quality: " .. tostring(value))
			end
		-- navHidden / questsHidden (2026-08-07): the two independent HUD collapses.
		-- navHidden folds the rail and the teleport tabs; questsHidden folds the quest
		-- bar and tracker. They live in Settings rather than their own save fields so
		-- they ride the same validated round trip as every other preference -- and this
		-- whitelist is why it matters: an unlisted key is dropped with a warning, so a
		-- setting not named here silently never persists.
		--
		-- (An earlier single "hudHidden" key is deliberately NOT listed. It hid the
		-- currency and luck too, which is no longer wanted; any profile still carrying
		-- it simply keeps a value nothing reads.)
		elseif key == "fastSpin" or key == "hideOwnBanners"
			or key == "navHidden" or key == "questsHidden"
			-- cinematicReducedMotion / cinematicLowQuality (task 8, Massive Catch
			-- Cinematic): SettingsPanel's two new toggle rows, same shape as
			-- fastSpin/hideOwnBanners -- a live player Attribute write plus this
			-- validated round trip so the preference survives a rejoin.
			or key == "cinematicReducedMotion" or key == "cinematicLowQuality" then
			if type(value) == "boolean" then
				out[key] = value
			else
				warn("[SettingsService] dropped invalid " .. key .. ": " .. tostring(value))
			end
		elseif key == "skipReveal" then
			if type(value) == "table" then
				local t = {}
				for _, tier in ipairs(RarityConfig) do
					if type(value[tier.Name]) == "boolean" then t[tier.Name] = value[tier.Name] end
				end
				out.skipReveal = t
			else
				warn("[SettingsService] dropped invalid skipReveal: " .. tostring(value))
			end
		else
			warn("[SettingsService] dropped unknown key: " .. tostring(key))
		end
	end
	return out
end

-- Validates + merges directly into `data.Settings` (creating it if absent).
-- Returns the validated subset that was actually written, so the caller can
-- tell "nothing survived validation" (empty table) from "wrote something".
-- Exposed for the round-trip probe: a fabricated `{Settings = {}}` data
-- table in, a mixed valid/invalid payload, and data.Settings only carries
-- the valid half afterward.
function SettingsService._Apply(data, tbl)
	local valid = SettingsService._Validate(tbl)
	if next(valid) == nil then
		return valid
	end
	data.Settings = data.Settings or {}
	for k, v in pairs(valid) do
		data.Settings[k] = v
	end
	return valid
end

local function applyNow(player, tbl)
	local data = PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
	if not data then
		return
	end
	local valid = SettingsService._Apply(data, tbl)
	if next(valid) ~= nil then
		-- Echoes data.Settings back via DataUpdated -- SettingsPanel's own
		-- top-level listener re-applies it, closing the round trip.
		PlayerDataManager.PushUpdate(player)
	end
end

local function onSettingsSave(player, tbl)
	if type(tbl) ~= "table" then return end
	local now = os.clock()
	local last = lastSave[player]

	if last and now - last < SAVE_WINDOW then
		local queued = pending[player]
		if queued then
			-- A flush is already scheduled; fold this payload into it. Later keys win,
			-- which is what someone mashing one toggle expects: the last press sticks.
			for k, v in pairs(tbl) do queued[k] = v end
			return
		end
		-- Copy rather than keep the client's table: it is the one reference we hold
		-- across a yield, and _Validate must stay the thing that decides its contents.
		queued = {}
		for k, v in pairs(tbl) do queued[k] = v end
		pending[player] = queued

		task.delay(SAVE_WINDOW - (now - last), function()
			local payload = pending[player]
			pending[player] = nil
			-- Parent check: they may have left during the wait, and writing into a
			-- profile that is already being released is worse than losing a preference
			-- for someone who is gone.
			if payload and player.Parent then
				lastSave[player] = os.clock()
				applyNow(player, payload)
			end
		end)
		return
	end

	lastSave[player] = now
	applyNow(player, tbl)
end

function SettingsService.Init()
	local save = remotes:FindFirstChild("SettingsSave")
	if not save then
		save = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
		save.Name = "SettingsSave"
		save.Parent = remotes
	end
	save.OnServerEvent:Connect(onSettingsSave)
	Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(p)
		lastSave[p] = nil
		pending[p] = nil
	end)
	print("SettingsService online")
end

return SettingsService


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ServerScriptService/Modules/ShopHandler.lua =====
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local ServerScriptService = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")

local PlayerDataManager = require(ServerScriptService.Modules.PlayerDataManager)
local RockConfig = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.RockConfig)

local rockById = {}
local rockIndexById = {}
for i, rock in ipairs(RockConfig) do
	rockById[rock.Id] = rock
	rockIndexById[rock.Id] = i   -- ladder position, for the sequential-unlock check
end

local remotes = ReplicatedStorage.Remotes

local ShopHandler = {}

function ShopHandler.Init()
	remotes.BuyRock.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, rockId)
		local data = PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
		if not data then return end
		local rock = rockById[rockId]
		if not rock then
			remotes.PurchaseResult:FireClient(player, { Success = false, Message = "Unknown rock." })
			return
		end
		if data.OwnedRocks[rockId] then
			remotes.PurchaseResult:FireClient(player, { Success = false, Message = "Already owned." })
			return
		end
		-- SEQUENTIAL UNLOCK: you must own the previous rock in the ladder before buying this
		-- one. Authoritative here; MerchantClient also greys out locked rocks for clarity.
		local idx = rockIndexById[rockId]
		if idx and idx > 1 then
			local prev = RockConfig[idx - 1]
			if not data.OwnedRocks[prev.Id] then
				remotes.PurchaseResult:FireClient(player, { Success = false, Message = "Unlock the " .. prev.Id .. " first!" })
				return
			end
		end
		if data.Cash < rock.Price then
			remotes.PurchaseResult:FireClient(player, { Success = false, Message = "Not enough Cash." })
			return
		end

		data.Cash -= rock.Price
		data.OwnedRocks[rockId] = true
		data.EquippedRock = rockId

		remotes.PurchaseResult:FireClient(player, { Success = true, Message = "Bought and equipped " .. rockId .. "!" })
		PlayerDataManager.PushUpdate(player)
	end)

	remotes.EquipRock.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, rockId)
		local data = PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
		if not data then return end
		if not data.OwnedRocks[rockId] then
			remotes.PurchaseResult:FireClient(player, { Success = false, Message = "You don't own that rock." })
			return
		end
		data.EquippedRock = rockId
		remotes.PurchaseResult:FireClient(player, { Success = true, Message = "Equipped " .. rockId .. "!" })
		PlayerDataManager.PushUpdate(player)
	end)
end

return ShopHandler

-- COSMETIC MODULE, DELIBERATELY A SOFT DEPENDENCY. This is the core throw loop, and a

		.. "); catch cutscenes are disabled for this server")

-- Each rock's own thrown look now lives in ReplicatedStorage.Modules.RockDesign
-- so Rocco's shelf display and the thrown rock cannot drift apart. The private
-- table this replaces only covered the 8 original Ids, so the 6 later rocks all
-- threw as the same generic slate block.

local raritySignFolder = Workspace:WaitForChild("GameWorld")

--============================ SKIP SURFACES =============================--
-- THERE ARE TWO SKIP AREAS NOW. The hub lake is open water at y 1.5; the Frozen
-- Tundra's is a solid sea-ice plane at y 1999, 8000 studs away. Everything a throw
-- draws -- the skip path, the splashes, the ripples, the settle pose -- used to be
-- pinned to the hub's single WATER_Y, so a stone thrown in the tundra skipped along
-- an invisible plane two thousand studs beneath the ice.
--
-- A skip area is any BasePart named ThrowZone under GameWorld. It carries its own
-- surface height and the Z its skip path starts at as attributes, so a third one is a
-- build-time job with no edit here. Defaults are the hub's old constants, which means
-- a zone authored without attributes still behaves exactly as before.
local DEFAULT_SURFACE_Y = 1.5
local DEFAULT_SKIP_START_Z = 28

local function surfaceYOf(zone)
	return (zone and zone:GetAttribute("SurfaceY")) or DEFAULT_SURFACE_Y
end

local function skipStartZOf(zone)
	return (zone and zone:GetAttribute("SkipStartZ")) or DEFAULT_SKIP_START_Z
end

-- Cached rather than walked per throw: GameWorld has tens of thousands of descendants
-- and this would otherwise run on every skip, every splash.
-- DOES THIS WORLD HAVE ANYTHING TO CATCH AT ALL (2026-08-07).
-- World 2's roster (BrainrotConfigTundra) is deliberately EMPTY pending real content,
-- and an empty pool makes RarityRoll.PickInTier return nil for every tier -- so a throw
-- there falls into the "empty tier" abandon below. To the player that is indistinguishable
-- from the game swallowing the throw: the bar charges, PERFECT lands, and then nothing
-- happens until the client's ~6.7s watchdog frees the bar.
--
-- Publishing the answer as an ATTRIBUTE ON THE DOCK lets the client refuse BEFORE the
-- charge and say why. No remote needed: attributes on workspace parts replicate on their
-- own, and the flag re-derives itself whenever the zone list is rebuilt -- so the day the
-- tundra roster is filled in, this turns true with no code change anywhere.
local function worldHasCatches(worldName)
	local w = worldName and WorldProgression.Resolve(worldName)
	return w ~= nil and #(w.Pool or {}) > 0
end

local throwZones = {}
local function rebuildThrowZones()
	table.clear(throwZones)
	local gw = Workspace:FindFirstChild("GameWorld")
	if not gw then return end
	for _, d in ipairs(gw:GetDescendants()) do
		if d:IsA("BasePart") and d.Name == "ThrowZone" then
			table.insert(throwZones, d)
			-- FAIL OPEN: only ever written false for a world positively known to be
			-- empty. A client reading nil (zone seen before this ran) treats the dock
			-- exactly as it always did, so the valley can never be blocked by a race.
			d:SetAttribute("CatchesEnabled", worldHasCatches(PlayerDataManager.WorldOf(d.Position)))
		end
	end
end

task.spawn(function()
	local gw = Workspace:WaitForChild("GameWorld")
	rebuildThrowZones()
	gw.DescendantAdded:Connect(function(d)
		if d.Name == "ThrowZone" and d:IsA("BasePart") then rebuildThrowZones() end
	end)
	gw.DescendantRemoving:Connect(function(d)
		if d.Name == "ThrowZone" and d:IsA("BasePart") then task.defer(rebuildThrowZones) end
	end)
end)

-- The zone the character is standing in, or nil. Y is generous (+6) because the stance
-- mats sit above the deck bed and a jumping player should not drop out of the zone.
local function throwZoneOf(character)
	local hrp = character and character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	if not hrp then return nil end
	for _, zone in ipairs(throwZones) do
		local rel = zone.CFrame:PointToObjectSpace(hrp.Position)
		local s = zone.Size / 2
		if math.abs(rel.X) <= s.X and math.abs(rel.Z) <= s.Z and math.abs(rel.Y) <= s.Y + 6 then
			return zone
		end
	end
	return nil
end

-- perfect = the release landed inside the sweet-spot band. The band is ISSUED
-- BY THIS SERVER (GetSweetSpot, single-use, aged) and judged here against the
-- power the throw actually uses -- the client only draws it. Its second
-- ThrowRequest argument is ignored: it was client-authoritative once, and
-- FireServer(0.01, true) was accepted in playtest.
--
-- THE BAND MOVES AGAIN. It was pinned to the top of the bar for a while, which made
-- power = 1 both the strongest throw AND always inside the band: perfect became free,
-- and PERFECT_DISTANCE_MULT / PERFECT_LUCK_MULT turned into baseline rather than a
-- reward for precision. That is what let the auto-skip button score a perfect on every
-- throw and let a fixed-cadence macro farm perfects overnight -- neither had to aim.
--
-- It now rolls per charge inside BAND_MIN_LO..BAND_MIN_HI and never reaches the top, so
-- releasing in the band costs raw power (and so distance, which gates tier access) in
-- exchange for the two multipliers. Full power is still a fine choice; it just is not a
-- free perfect.
--
-- NOTE ON SPOOFING: a client that fakes its power can still aim straight at the band it
-- was told about, so perfect is not cheat-proof -- it never was. What the handshake buys
-- is that the client does not get to DECLARE a throw perfect, and that the honest cases
-- this game actually ships (the auto button, and macros driving real input) cannot hit it
-- reliably.
local PERFECT_DISTANCE_MULT = 1.1
local PERFECT_LUCK_MULT = 1.075

-- Where the sweet-spot band may land. Deliberately NOT touching the top of the bar: see
-- the GetSweetSpot comment for why pinning it there made perfect free.
local BAND_MIN_LO, BAND_MIN_HI = 0.62, 0.90

-- AUTO SKIP PENALTIES. Auto exists so players can idle for hours, which means it must be
-- the WORST way to fish for rares or it becomes the only way anyone plays. Distance gates
-- which tiers are reachable at all and luck shifts the odds inside them, so both are cut:
-- trimming luck alone would still let an overnight session brute-force the top tiers.
-- Auto can also never score perfect (see the auto branch below).
--
-- HONEST-CLIENT ENFORCEMENT, and worth being clear-eyed about: the server cannot tell an
-- auto throw from a manual one, so this trusts the client's own flag. That is fine for
-- what it is for -- the AFK button this game ships -- but it is not anti-cheat. What DOES
-- hold against a cheating client is that perfect is judged here against a band this
-- server issued, so nobody can simply declare their throws perfect.
-- 0.80 is not arbitrary. It is applied AFTER the MAX_TOTAL_DISTANCE clamp, so a maxed
-- player on auto lands at 900 * 0.80 = 720 studs. Read that against RarityConfig's gates:
-- Mythic opens at 640, Secret at 780, God at 900. Auto therefore tops out inside Mythic
-- and CANNOT reach Secret or God at all, which is what keeps the top of the ladder
-- something you have to actually play for.
--
-- It has to be after the clamp, not inside it: a late-game player's raw distance already
-- overshoots 900 by a wide margin, so a multiplier applied before the clamp is simply
-- swallowed by it and the penalty does nothing at all for exactly the players most able
-- to farm overnight. (Measured: manual and auto both came back at 900.0 until this moved.)
local AUTO_DISTANCE_MULT = 0.80
local AUTO_LUCK_MULT = 0.55
local BAND_WIDTH = 0.07     -- mirrors the client's strip width
local BAND_MAX_AGE = 30     -- seconds a charge may idle before perfect stops counting

-- [userId] = { min, max, issuedAt } -- the one band this player may cash in next
local pendingBand = {}

local function getThrowOrigin(player)
	local char = player and player.Character
	if char then
		local hand = char:FindFirstChild("RightHand") or char:FindFirstChild("Right Arm")
		local hrp = char:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
		local dir = hrp and hrp.CFrame.LookVector or Vector3.new(0, 0, 1)
		if hand then
			return hand.Position, dir
		elseif hrp then
			return hrp.Position + dir * 1.5 + Vector3.new(0, 1.5, 0), dir
		end
	end
	return Vector3.new(0, 4, THROW_Z), Vector3.new(0, 0, 1)
end

-- Ids come from SoundKit rather than living here, per the note at the top of that
-- module. TWO samples, not one pitched two ways: the skip tap is 0.39s and simply
-- cannot read as heavy, so the landing uses a 3.51s large-splash sample instead.
local SPLASH_SOUND = SoundKit.Ids.splash        -- 0.39s, the skips
local SPLASH_BIG_SOUND = SoundKit.Ids.splashBig -- 3.51s, the landing only

-- One splash sound per water contact. Created server-side so every player at the dock
-- hears each other's skips positionally, which is most of the charm.
--   index/total: 1-based contact number, used to raise the pitch across the sequence
--                the way a real stone gets lighter and quicker as it loses energy.
--   big:         the final landing -- lower, fuller, and allowed to ring longer.
local function playSplashSound(pos, big, index, total, surfaceY)
	local host = Instance.new("Part")
	host.Name = "SplashAudio"
	host.Size = Vector3.new(0.2, 0.2, 0.2)
	host.Transparency = 1
	host.Anchored = true
	host.CanCollide = false
	host.CanQuery = false
	host.CastShadow = false
	host.CFrame = CFrame.new(pos.X, surfaceY or DEFAULT_SURFACE_Y, pos.Z)
	host.Parent = Workspace

	local sound = Instance.new("Sound")
	sound.SoundId = big and SPLASH_BIG_SOUND or SPLASH_SOUND
	-- Still restrained -- this fires up to 8 times per throw and several players share
	-- the dock -- but 0.22 was under the music bed and the skips were getting lost.
	-- Raised to 0.32; the rolloff below is what keeps other people's throws in check,
	-- not the raw level.
	sound.Volume = big and 0.68 or 0.32
	-- The skip asset is 0.39s (an earlier comment here claimed 2.4s -- it was wrong).
	-- Pitching it UP brightens the transient and shortens the tail further, which is
	-- what makes a skip read as a skip rather than a belly-flop.
	local progress = (total and total > 1) and ((index - 1) / (total - 1)) or 0
	local jitter = (math.random() - 0.5) * 0.08   -- so repeated skips are not identical
	-- The landing only eases DOWN to 0.95 -- its sample is already a heavy wash, and
	-- pitching a 3.51s file much lower just turns the tail to mud.
	sound.PlaybackSpeed = (big and 0.95 or (1.45 + progress * 0.35)) + jitter
	sound.RollOffMode = Enum.RollOffMode.InverseTapered
	sound.RollOffMinDistance = 14
	sound.RollOffMaxDistance = 240
	sound.Parent = host
	sound:Play()

	-- Fade before removing the part: cutting a wash dead mid-tail clicks. The landing
	-- holds 1.8s and is faded out from 1.66s -- deliberately SHORTER than its 3.7s
	-- sample, so the lake gets a big front end without a tail that outlasts the throw.
	local hold = big and 1.80 or 0.42
	task.delay(math.max(hold - 0.14, 0.05), function()
		if sound.Parent then
			game:GetService("TweenService"):Create(sound, TweenInfo.new(0.14), { Volume = 0 }):Play()
		end
	end)
	Debris:AddItem(host, hold + 0.06)
end

-- ================================ SKIP SPLASH VFX ================================
-- Was one neon cylinder expanding plus one neon ball shrinking, which read as a flash
-- of light rather than water. Now three ideas layered:
--
--   RIPPLES   two rings, the second delayed and trailing the first. A single ring is
--             the tell that it is fake -- real water sheds a train of them. The rings
--             are also thinner and start further into transparency, so they read as a
--             disturbance on the surface instead of a glowing hoop.
--   DROPLETS  a ParticleEmitter burst instead of a shrinking ball. One part hosting an
--             emitter costs the same replication as the old ball but produces dozens of
--             droplets that arc under gravity -- by far the biggest visual win per byte.
--   COLUMN    a quick vertical spout, BIG LANDINGS ONLY, for the heavier "plunk".
--
-- The final landing was scaled up across all five layers (ripples, droplets,
-- light, column, sound): it is the payoff of the whole throw and it was reading
-- as just one more skip. It fires ONCE per throw, so the extra third ripple is
-- one additional part on one contact -- the per-skip cost is unchanged.
--
-- Part budget matters: this fires up to 8 times per throw and it is SERVER-created, so
-- every part replicates to every client at the dock. Measured on a real 8-contact throw:
-- 17 ripples + 8 droplet hosts + 1 column = 26 parts, against 16 for the old version.
-- So it is ~1.5x the parts, not free -- but they are 0.12-stud anchored non-colliding
-- decor with sub-second Debris lifetimes, and the droplet emitter buys dozens of visible
-- droplets for ONE part, which is where the fidelity actually comes from.
local SPLASH_TEX = "rbxasset://textures/particles/smoke_main.dds"

-- Events that darken the sky (WeatherClient sets ClockTime 23.4-23.9 for these). During
-- them a Neon splash still GLOWS but casts no light, so a skip 600 studs out reads as a
-- faint smudge. The splash light below is boosted while one of these is live -- and the
-- server can know because WeatherHandler publishes WeatherName on ReplicatedStorage.
local NIGHT_EVENTS = {
	["Shooting Star"] = true,
	["Blood Moon"] = true,
	["Aurora"] = true,
}

local function decorPart(p)
	p.Anchored = true
	p.CanCollide = false
	p.CanQuery = false
	p.CanTouch = false
	p.CastShadow = false
	p.Locked = true
	p.Parent = Workspace
	return p
end

local function ripple(pos, delay, startD, endD, life, alpha, surfaceY)
	task.delay(delay, function()
		local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
		local ring = Instance.new("Part")
		ring.Name = "SkipRipple"
		ring.Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder
		ring.Size = Vector3.new(0.12, startD, startD)
		ring.Material = Enum.Material.Neon
		ring.Color = Color3.fromRGB(226, 244, 255)
		ring.Transparency = alpha
		ring.CFrame = CFrame.new(pos.X, (surfaceY or DEFAULT_SURFACE_Y) + 0.04, pos.Z) * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, math.rad(90))
		decorPart(ring)
		-- Quad easing: a real ripple sprints outward then slows, where the old Linear
		-- tween expanded at a constant rate and looked mechanical.
		TweenService:Create(ring, TweenInfo.new(life, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out),
			{ Size = Vector3.new(0.12, endD, endD), Transparency = 1 }):Play()
		Debris:AddItem(ring, life + 0.15)
	end)
end

local function spawnSplash(pos, big, surfaceY)
	local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
	local scale = big and 2.6 or 1
	surfaceY = surfaceY or DEFAULT_SURFACE_Y

	-- lead ripple, plus a trailing one that chases it. The landing sheds a THIRD,
	-- slowest, widest ring -- a big impact pushes out a longer train than a skip,
	-- and the late wide ring is what makes the lake look like it took the hit.
	ripple(pos, 0, 1.6, 12 * scale, big and 0.80 or 0.62, 0.35, surfaceY)
	if big then
		ripple(pos, 0.10, 1.2, 28, 1.05, 0.58, surfaceY)
		ripple(pos, 0.26, 1.0, 40, 1.45, 0.72, surfaceY)
	else
		ripple(pos, 0.09, 1.0, 6.5, 0.44, 0.68, surfaceY)
	end

	-- droplet burst
	local host = Instance.new("Part")
	host.Name = "SkipSplash"
	host.Size = Vector3.new(0.2, 0.2, 0.2)
	host.Transparency = 1
	host.CFrame = CFrame.new(pos.X, surfaceY + 0.15, pos.Z)
	decorPart(host)

	local e = Instance.new("ParticleEmitter")
	e.Texture = SPLASH_TEX
	e.Rate = 0                                  -- burst only, via :Emit below
	e.Lifetime = NumberRange.new(0.30, big and 0.92 or 0.62)
	e.Speed = NumberRange.new(big and 16 or 9, 20 + 10 * scale)
	e.EmissionDirection = Enum.NormalId.Top
	-- narrow-ish cone: water leaves the surface upward and outward, not spherically
	e.SpreadAngle = Vector2.new(46, 46)
	e.Acceleration = Vector3.new(0, -95, 0)     -- gravity, so droplets ARC instead of drifting
	e.Drag = 1.2
	e.Size = NumberSequence.new({
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, big and 0.85 or 0.42, 0.18),
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 0.06),
	})
	e.Color = ColorSequence.new(Color3.fromRGB(236, 250, 255))
	e.Transparency = NumberSequence.new({
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 0.15),
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0.72, 0.35),
		NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 1),
	})
	e.LightEmission = 0.35
	e.LightInfluence = 0.4
	e.Rotation = NumberRange.new(0, 360)
	e.RotSpeed = NumberRange.new(-140, 140)
	e.Parent = host
	e:Emit(big and 70 or 14)

	-- ACTUAL LIGHT, not just a glowing part. Neon is emissive but illuminates nothing, so
	-- on a dark night the skips were invisible past a few hundred studs. This flashes real
	-- light onto the water and fades out.
	--
	-- Parented to the droplet host, which already exists -- so the whole effect costs ZERO
	-- extra parts. Shadows are OFF: this fires up to 8 times per throw and shadow casting
	-- is the expensive half of a PointLight (every other light in this place is already
	-- Shadows = false for the same reason).
	local weather = ReplicatedStorage:GetAttribute("WeatherName")
	local nightBoost = NIGHT_EVENTS[weather] and 2.4 or 1
	local light = Instance.new("PointLight")
	light.Color = Color3.fromRGB(198, 232, 255)   -- cool white, matching the droplets
	light.Range = (big and 48 or 20) * (nightBoost > 1 and 1.35 or 1)
	light.Brightness = (big and 4.6 or 1.7) * nightBoost
	light.Shadows = false
	light.Parent = host
	-- Fade rather than cut: a light that vanishes mid-brightness pops. Short on a skip so
	-- eight of them never overlap into one continuous glow; longer on the landing.
	TweenService:Create(light, TweenInfo.new(big and 0.80 or 0.26,
		Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), { Brightness = 0 }):Play()

	-- must outlast the droplet Lifetime above or the burst is cut mid-arc
	Debris:AddItem(host, big and 1.60 or 1.0)

	-- vertical spout, only worth the part on the landing
	if big then
		local col = Instance.new("Part")
		col.Name = "SkipColumn"
		col.Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder
		col.Size = Vector3.new(0.6, 2.4, 2.4)
		col.Material = Enum.Material.Neon
		col.Color = Color3.fromRGB(240, 251, 255)
		col.Transparency = 0.28
		col.CFrame = CFrame.new(pos.X, surfaceY + 0.3, pos.Z) * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, math.rad(90))
		decorPart(col)
		TweenService:Create(col, TweenInfo.new(0.20, Enum.EasingStyle.Quint, Enum.EasingDirection.Out),
			{ Size = Vector3.new(10.5, 2.0, 2.0) }):Play()
		task.delay(0.21, function()
			if col.Parent then
				TweenService:Create(col, TweenInfo.new(0.36, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.In),
					{ Size = Vector3.new(0.5, 0.5, 0.5), Transparency = 1 }):Play()
			end
		end)
		Debris:AddItem(col, 0.80)
	end
end

local function spawnSkippingStone(player, distance, rock, onLand, zone, cinematic)
	local origin, dir = getThrowOrigin(player)
	local horiz = Vector3.new(0, 0, 1) -- always toward the distance markers
	-- Both skip areas face +Z, so the path is still a straight run up the lane; what
	-- differs per zone is how high the surface is and where the lane starts.
	local surfaceY = surfaceYOf(zone)

	-- A detailed multi-part rock, not a bare primitive: chips, facets and flecks
	-- from RockDesign, which the shop preview and Rocco's shelf build from too, so
	-- the thing you throw is the thing you bought. Parts are anchored, so the
	-- flight below drives it with PivotTo rather than setting a CFrame.
	local stone = RockDesign.Build(rock and rock.Id,
		(rock and rock.Color) or Color3.fromRGB(105, 100, 96))
	stone.Name = "ThrownRock"
	stone:PivotTo(CFrame.new(origin))
	stone.Parent = Workspace

	-- start the skip path just past the dock's front edge so the rock skips on OPEN water, never under the deck floor
	local startFlat = Vector3.new(origin.X, surfaceY, math.max(origin.Z, skipStartZOf(zone)))
	-- fewer, clearer skips: aim for ~one skip every ~18 studs, 2..8 contacts
	local nContacts = math.clamp(math.floor(distance / 18) + 1, 2, 8)
	local points = { origin }
	for i = 1, nContacts do
		local d = distance * (i / nContacts)
		points[#points + 1] = startFlat + horiz * d
	end
	local hopLen = distance / nContacts

	local totalTime = math.clamp(0.9 + distance / 360, 1.15, 4.2)
	local segTime = totalTime / (#points - 1)

	-- nContacts + segTime ride the EXISTING payload rather than a new remote or one
	-- event per bounce: the arc is fully deterministic, so the client ticks its own
	-- counter off segTime. One payload change instead of up to 8 fires per throw.
	-- Splash k happens at k*segTime after this fires (see the loop below), and the
	-- client receives this payload and hears each splash both one-way-late, so the
	-- latency cancels and a client-side tick at k*segTime lands on the splash.
	remotes.StoneThrown:FireClient(player, origin, points[#points], totalTime, distance, nContacts, segTime)

	-- The SAME moment, but to EVERYONE. Only this function knows the arc's timing and
	-- where it ends, so the fields the client cannot derive are appended here rather
	-- than at roll time. Clients tick their own clock from receipt, exactly as they
	-- already do for StoneThrown above, so the send latency cancels the same way.
	if cinematic then
		-- The settle point, used as-is: every point after the origin is built from
		-- startFlat, whose Y is already surfaceY, so there is nothing to reconstruct.
		cinematic.EndPos = points[#points]
		cinematic.SurfaceY = surfaceY
		cinematic.TotalTime = totalTime
		cinematic.NContacts = nContacts
		cinematic.SegTime = segTime
		cinematicRemote:FireAllClients(cinematic)
	end

	task.spawn(function()
		local spin = 0
		for k = 1, #points - 1 do
			local a = points[k]
			local b = points[k + 1]
			-- clear, bouncy hop heights (flat-ish so it reads as skipping, not lobbing)
			local apex
			if k == 1 then
				apex = math.clamp(hopLen * 0.4, 3, 11)
			else
				apex = math.max(2.5, math.clamp(hopLen * 0.42, 3, 8) * (0.82 ^ (k - 2)))
			end
			local t0 = os.clock()
			while true do
				local dt = os.clock() - t0
				local alpha = math.clamp(dt / segTime, 0, 1)
				local pos = a:Lerp(b, alpha)
				local h = math.sin(alpha * math.pi) * apex
				spin = spin + 1.0
				stone:PivotTo(CFrame.new(pos.X, pos.Y + h, pos.Z)
					* CFrame.Angles(0, spin, 0)
					* CFrame.Angles(math.rad(12), 0, 0))
				if alpha >= 1 then break end
				task.wait()
			end
			-- splash at each water contact (bigger on the final landing)
			local isLast = k == #points - 1
			-- A cinematic throw's FINAL contact is the bonk: clients stage it
			-- themselves (dry clonk, ricochet), so the server plays no splash
			-- and hands the stone off by destroying its copy at the contact.
			if not (isLast and cinematic) then
				spawnSplash(b, isLast, surfaceY)
				playSplashSound(b, isLast, k, #points - 1, surfaceY)
			end
		end
		local last = points[#points]
		if cinematic then
			stone:Destroy()
		else
			stone:PivotTo(CFrame.new(last.X, surfaceY, last.Z) * CFrame.Angles(math.rad(6), 0, 0))
			Debris:AddItem(stone, 1.3)
		end
		-- Hand the settle point UP to the reveal. A Massive catch stages a cutscene of the
		-- creature rising out of the water, and this is the only place that knows exactly
		-- where the water was broken -- surfaceY comes from the zone, so it is right for the
		-- tundra deck as well as the hub dock.
		if onLand then onLand(Vector3.new(last.X, surfaceY, last.Z)) end
	end)
end

-- EVERY camp the player owns. A brainrot is one entry in data.Brainrots rendered on each
-- of their plots, so a catch made in the valley has to appear on the tundra camp too --
-- otherwise walking through the portal looks like it ate half your collection.
local function spawnBrainrotOnPlot(player, brainrotEntry, padIndex, mutation, sizeVariant)
	for _, plot in ipairs(PlayerDataManager.GetPlots(player)) do
		BrainrotSpawner.Spawn(plot, brainrotEntry, padIndex, mutation, nil, sizeVariant)
	end
end

-- Unchanged contract: no zones authored at all means no gating, exactly as when this
-- looked up a single GameWorld.ThrowZone and let the throw through if it was missing.
local function isInThrowZone(character)
	if #throwZones == 0 then return true end
	return throwZoneOf(character) ~= nil
end

local ThrowHandler = {}

-- SERVER-AUTHORITATIVE throw rate. Before this, the only throttle was a variable
-- in ClientMain, so the faucet was governed entirely by the client.
local THROW_COOLDOWN = 1.05   -- matches the client's CYCLE_SECONDS
local lastThrow = {}          -- [userId] = os.clock()

-- ONE STONE AT A TIME. The cooldown alone could never enforce this: flight time is
-- clamp(0.9 + distance/360, 1.15, 4.2) seconds, so it is ALWAYS longer than the 1.05s
-- cooldown. That gap is what let a held throw button queue a second throw while the
-- first stone was still skipping. Enforced here rather than only in ClientMain because
-- a client-side lock is advisory -- anything firing the remote directly bypasses it.
local inFlight = {}           -- [userId] = true while that player's stone is skipping
local flightToken = {}        -- [userId] = id of the current throw, so a stale
                              -- watchdog can never unlock a newer throw
local MAX_FLIGHT = 4.2        -- the upper clamp in spawnSkippingStone

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
	lastThrow[player.UserId] = nil
	inFlight[player.UserId] = nil
	flightToken[player.UserId] = nil
	pendingBand[player.UserId] = nil
end)

function ThrowHandler.Init()
	-- The sweet-spot handshake: the client asks for a band each time the charge
	-- minigame loads and draws whatever this returns. Single-use (consumed by the
	-- next ThrowRequest) and overwritten by each new ask, so there is exactly one
	-- live band per player and it can never be replayed.
	local sweetSpot = remotes:FindFirstChild("GetSweetSpot")
	if not sweetSpot then
		sweetSpot = Instance.new("RemoteFunction")
		sweetSpot.Name = "GetSweetSpot"
		sweetSpot.Parent = remotes
	end
	sweetSpot.OnServerInvoke = function(player)
		-- ROLLED PER CHARGE, and never touching the top of the bar.
		--
		-- This was previously pinned to the last BAND_WIDTH of the bar, on the reasoning
		-- that the perfect release and the full-power release should not pull against each
		-- other. The consequence was that holding to full power was ALWAYS perfect: no
		-- timing, no decision, no way to miss. That is what made the auto-skip button score
		-- a perfect every single time, and what made a fixed-cadence macro able to farm
		-- perfects overnight -- neither had to aim at anything.
		--
		-- With the band back in the middle of the bar the tension is the point: releasing
		-- in the band costs you raw power (and therefore distance, which gates tier access)
		-- but pays PERFECT_DISTANCE_MULT and PERFECT_LUCK_MULT. Full power is still a
		-- legitimate choice; it just is not a free perfect any more.
		--
		-- Still single-use and aged, so a client cannot replay one band across throws.
		local lo = BAND_MIN_LO + math.random() * (BAND_MIN_HI - BAND_MIN_LO)
		local band = {
			min = lo,
			max = math.min(1, lo + BAND_WIDTH),
			issuedAt = os.clock(),
		}
		pendingBand[player.UserId] = band
		return { min = band.min, max = band.max }
	end

	remotes.ThrowRequest.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, power, clientPerfect, auto)
		-- ICE FISHING: while the Frozen Tundra lake is frozen, World-2 throwing is OFF --
		-- players fish at the holes instead. Authoritative backstop; ClientMain also hides
		-- the throw minigame at the tundra dock. Valley throwing is unaffected.
		if ReplicatedStorage:GetAttribute("IceFishingActive")
			and PlayerDataManager.PlayerWorld(player) == "Tundra" then
			return
		end
		local now = os.clock()
		if now - (lastThrow[player.UserId] or 0) < THROW_COOLDOWN then return end
		if inFlight[player.UserId] then return end   -- previous stone is still skipping
		lastThrow[player.UserId] = now

		local data = PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
		if not data then return end
		if not PlayerDataManager.GetPlot(player) then
			local r = remotes:FindFirstChild("PurchaseResult")
			if r then r:FireClient(player, { Success = false, Message = "Claim a base first! Walk onto an available plot." }) end
			return
		end
		if typeof(power) ~= "number" then return end
		if power ~= power then return end
		power = math.clamp(power, 0, 1)
