		-- PERFECT IS SERVER-JUDGED (see the header note). clientPerfect is legacy
		-- display chatter and deliberately unread.
		local band = pendingBand[player.UserId]
		pendingBand[player.UserId] = nil   -- single-use: no replay across throws
		local isAuto = auto and true or false
		-- An auto throw can never be perfect, whatever power it happens to land on. Without
		-- this, randomising the auto release would still hand it the occasional perfect and
		-- an all-night session would collect plenty of them.
		local perfect = (not isAuto)
			and band ~= nil
			and (now - band.issuedAt) <= BAND_MAX_AGE
			and power >= band.min and power <= band.max

		if not isInThrowZone(player.Character) then return end
		-- Captured HERE, at the last validation, rather than at launch: the reveal path
		-- below yields (mint claims, season writes) and the player can wander off the deck
		-- in between. The stone should skip on the surface they threw from.
		local throwZone = throwZoneOf(player.Character)

		-- Claim the flight slot HERE -- immediately after the last cheap validation and
		-- BEFORE any of the roll / mint / season work below.
		--
		-- It used to be claimed just above the launch, ~40 lines further down, which left
		-- a window: something in between yields, so a second request cleared the gate
		-- while the first was still mid-handler. Measured: 12 requests fired 0.13s apart
		-- produced 2 stones instead of 1. Claiming at the moment of acceptance closes it,
		-- and does so without needing to know which call yields.
		local token = (flightToken[player.UserId] or 0) + 1
		flightToken[player.UserId] = token
		inFlight[player.UserId] = true

		-- Any early return past this point MUST release the slot, or the player is locked
		-- out until the watchdog fires.
		local function abandonFlight()
			if flightToken[player.UserId] == token then
				inFlight[player.UserId] = nil
			end
		end

		local rock = rockById[data.EquippedRock] or rockById["Pebble"]
		local variance = math.random(-2, 2)
		local distance = math.clamp(power * rock.MaxDistance
			* UpgradeConfig.Mult(data.Upgrades, "Power")
			* RebirthConfig.PowerMult(data.Rebirths)          -- prestige throw power
			* PlayerDataManager.BoostMult(data, "Power")      -- timed daily-wheel boost
			* (perfect and PERFECT_DISTANCE_MULT or 1) + variance, 0, MAX_TOTAL_DISTANCE)

		-- AFTER the clamp, deliberately -- see AUTO_DISTANCE_MULT's comment. Inside it, a
		-- maxed player's auto throws stayed pinned at the 900 cap and the penalty vanished.
		if isAuto then
			distance = distance * AUTO_DISTANCE_MULT
		end

		-- === Rarity: DISTANCE + LUCK weight a probabilistic roll (RarityCurve) ===
		-- Distance no longer GUARANTEES a tier -- it unlocks higher tiers and shifts the
		-- odds up; luck shifts them further; higher tiers are geometrically rarer and
		-- nothing is a lock. The old model floored the tier at your distance, which made
		-- Mythic+ a certainty for a long enough throw. Tunables + curve live in
		-- ReplicatedStorage.Modules.RarityCurve (shared with the luck HUD).
		local rebirthLuck = RebirthConfig.LuckMult(data.Rebirths)
		local weatherLuck = ReplicatedStorage:GetAttribute("WeatherLuck") or 1
		local weatherMut = ReplicatedStorage:GetAttribute("WeatherMut") or 1

		-- ADDITIVE access luck: every source contributes a BONUS (its multiplier minus 1)
		-- and the bonuses SUM onto a base of 1, instead of multiplying against each other.
		-- Stacking is now linear and self-limiting -- rock + charm + offerings + wheel boost +
		-- placed pets each add their bit, so a maxed setup lands near +15 rather than the old
		-- runaway x60. Rebirth luck is still excluded here (it feeds MUTATION odds below).
		-- Placed-brainrot luck is summed the same way PetConfig.StackedMult already sums
		-- equipped pets: two +0.5 pets make +1.0, never x2.25.
		local petLuckBonus = 0
		for _, e in ipairs(data.Brainrots) do
			if e.PadIndex and petLuckByName[e.Name] then
				petLuckBonus += (petLuckByName[e.Name] - 1)
			end
		end
		-- Weather adds a flat event bonus IDENTICAL for every player. weatherLuck is a
		-- multiplier attribute, so (weatherLuck - 1) is that bonus -- 0 when no luck event is live.
		local weatherAccessBonus = math.max(weatherLuck - 1, 0)
		local personalAccess = 1
			+ (rock.Luck - 1)
			+ (UpgradeConfig.Mult(data.Upgrades, "Luck") - 1)
			+ (OfferingConfig.LuckMult(data.Offerings) - 1)
			+ (PlayerDataManager.BoostMult(data, "Luck") - 1)
			+ petLuckBonus
		-- Perfect and auto stay as per-throw MULTIPLIERS on the summed total: they are throw
		-- quality, not a stacked source. (Folding auto into the sum would erase the AFK penalty --
		-- -0.45 off a ~15 total is nothing; x0.55 on the total is not.)
		local accessLuck = (personalAccess + weatherAccessBonus)
			* (perfect and PERFECT_LUCK_MULT or 1)
			* (isAuto and AUTO_LUCK_MULT or 1)

		-- roll a tier from the curve. A top-of-curve (Secret) roll is routed through the
		-- God index so Pete still gets his independent 1-in-a-million FixedChance shot;
		-- PickInTier(God) rolls Pete, else falls through to a Secret. pickIndex is reused
		-- by the reveal-time re-rolls below (vaulted / limited fallbacks).
		-- WHICH WORLD IS THIS THROW IN. The tundra has its own ladder and its own pool, so
		-- the curve, the pick and the pity bands all have to be asked for that world.
		-- PlayerWorld returns BoundsGuard's region name, which is what WorldProgression
		-- is keyed on.
		local throwWorld = PlayerDataManager.PlayerWorld(player)
		local curve = RarityCurve.For(throwWorld)
		-- tier name -> index within THIS world's ladder. The module-level tierIndexByName
		-- is the valley's, and the tundra's bands are not the same distances.
		local wIdx = {}
		for i, t in ipairs(curve.Rarities) do wIdx[t.Name] = i end
		local rolledTier = curve.RollTierIndex(distance, accessLuck)

		-- === Pity: cap dry streaks. Every throw that REACHES a tier's distance ticks that
		-- tier's counter up; once it passes the threshold, the HIGHEST eligible tier gets ONE
		-- boosted (never guaranteed) shot to bump this roll up to it. Counters reset when you
		-- actually catch that tier or higher (revealCatch). See PityConfig for the tunables.
		data.Pity = data.Pity or {}
		for _, pity in ipairs(PityConfig) do
			local tIdx = wIdx[pity.Tier]
			if tIdx and distance >= curve.Rarities[tIdx].MinDistance then
				data.Pity[pity.Tier] = (data.Pity[pity.Tier] or 0) + 1
			end
		end
		local pityTierName
		for i = #PityConfig, 1, -1 do   -- highest tier first: one pity bump per throw
			local pity = PityConfig[i]
			local tIdx = wIdx[pity.Tier]
			if tIdx and tIdx > rolledTier
				and distance >= curve.Rarities[tIdx].MinDistance
				and (data.Pity[pity.Tier] or 0) >= pity.Threshold
				and math.random() < pity.Chance then
				rolledTier = tIdx
				pityTierName = pity.Tier
				break
			end
		end
		-- pity fired: flash a "<TIER> PITY THROW!" banner as the rock flies. The catch that
		-- lands will be at least this tier (rolledTier was just bumped up to it).
		if pityTierName then
			local pt = curve.Rarities[wIdx[pityTierName]]
			pityRemote:FireClient(player, pityTierName, pt and pt.Color)
		end

		-- A top-of-curve roll is routed at this world's APEX tier so its FixedChance
		-- entries get their shot first and otherwise fall back to the tier below.
		-- Valley: Secret Pete. Tundra: the ten Glitched. Same mechanism, different table.
		local pickIndex = (rolledTier >= curve.TopTier) and curve.ApexIndex or rolledTier
		local brainrotEntry, tier = RarityRoll.PickInTier(pickIndex, false, throwWorld)
		-- Empty tier: never hand out a nil catch. Kept as the last line of defence --
		-- the client now refuses to charge at a dock whose world has no roster (see
		-- worldHasCatches / the CatchesEnabled attribute above), so in normal play this
		-- is unreachable. It still catches the narrower case of a world that HAS a
		-- roster whose every entry is filtered out by isLive (all vaulted / sold out).
		if not brainrotEntry then abandonFlight(); return end

		-- set by the test hook below; makes this catch exempt from the
		-- reveal-time catchability re-check (see revealCatch)
		local forcedCatch = false

		-- === TEST HOOK: one-shot forced catch ===============================
		-- Armed by setting attributes on ServerStorage. They live in the place
		-- file, so they survive the Edit -> Play transition (a module-level Lua
		-- flag would not -- the server VM is rebuilt on Play).
		--     ForceNextCatch    = "<brainrot name>"   e.g. "Chim"
		--     ForceNextCatchFor = "<username>"        optional; blank = anyone
		--
		-- CONSUMED EXACTLY ONCE: the attribute is cleared the instant it fires,
		-- so a flag left armed by accident cannot quietly keep minting. It is
		-- cleared BEFORE any yield for the same reason the LimitedStock claim is.
		--
		-- Deliberately bypasses both the weighted pool and the catchability
		-- schedule -- that is the whole point. Chim is questline-exclusive and
		-- never rolls from a throw, so there is no other way to test it.
		do
			local want = ServerStorage:GetAttribute("ForceNextCatch")
			local who = ServerStorage:GetAttribute("ForceNextCatchFor")
			if type(want) == "string" and want ~= ""
				and (who == nil or who == "" or who == player.Name) then
				local forced
				for _, e in ipairs(BrainrotConfig) do
					if e.Name == want then forced = e break end
				end
				local forcedTier
				if forced then
					for _, t in ipairs(RarityConfig) do
						if t.Name == forced.Rarity then forcedTier = t break end
					end
				end
				if forced and forcedTier then
					ServerStorage:SetAttribute("ForceNextCatch", nil)
					brainrotEntry, tier = forced, forcedTier
					forcedCatch = true
					warn(("[ThrowHandler] TEST override consumed: %s caught %s (%s)")
						:format(player.Name, forced.Name, forcedTier.Name))
				else
					warn("[ThrowHandler] ForceNextCatch names an unknown brainrot: " .. tostring(want))
				end
			end
		end

		-- ADDITIVE mutation luck, same rule as access luck above: rebirth + equipped-pet bonuses
		-- SUM onto a base of 1, and the event's own mutation value adds the same flat bonus for
		-- everyone. The old x6 clamp is GONE -- additive stacking is already self-limiting, and
		-- the clamp only existed to stop the multiplicative product exploding (which also made
		-- rebirth luck swallow pet luck whole). Equipped pets come through PetHandler.LuckMult,
		-- which is itself additive across pets, so this is one consistent sum end to end.
		local mutBoost = 1
			+ (rebirthLuck - 1)                     -- +0.07 per rebirth
			+ (PetHandler.LuckMult(player) - 1)     -- equipped egg pets (already additive)
			+ math.max(weatherMut - 1, 0)           -- event mutation bonus, same for everyone
		-- the live event's own mutation gets first refusal, then the base table (scaled by boost)
		local mutation = Mutations.Roll(mutBoost, ReplicatedStorage:GetAttribute("WeatherName"))

		-- SIZE ROLLED AT THROW TIME (2026-08-08, cinematic build). It rolled in
		-- revealCatch at landing before; the cinematic needs the answer while the
		-- stone is still airborne so the FINAL skip can play as the bonk. Every
		-- input to the roll (weatherMut) was already read above at this moment,
		-- so the odds are byte-identical -- the roll just happens 1-4s earlier.
		local sizeVariant = Sizes.Roll(weatherMut)
		-- TEST HOOK, mirror of ForceNextCatch above: consumed exactly once.
		do
			local wantSize = ServerStorage:GetAttribute("ForceNextSize")
			if type(wantSize) == "string" and wantSize ~= "" then
				if Sizes.ByName[wantSize] then
					ServerStorage:SetAttribute("ForceNextSize", nil)
					sizeVariant = wantSize
					warn("[ThrowHandler] TEST override consumed: next catch is " .. wantSize)
				else
					-- Left ARMED on purpose, exactly as ForceNextCatch leaves a bad name in
					-- place: a typo is fixed by correcting the attribute, and a hook that
					-- silently disarmed itself would look identical to one that fired.
					warn("[ThrowHandler] ForceNextSize names an unknown size: " .. tostring(wantSize))
				end
			end
		end
		-- nil on the overwhelmingly common throw, which is exactly the "no cutscene" case.
		local cinMode = sizeVariant and CinematicConfig.SIZES[sizeVariant] or nil
		local cinematic = (cinMode == "full" or cinMode == "trimmed") and {
			UserId = player.UserId,
			BrainrotName = brainrotEntry.Name,   -- may be superseded by reveal-time
			Rarity = tier.Name,                  -- fallback swaps; client prefers
			RarityColor = tier.Color,            -- ThrowResult's name if it differs
			Mutation = mutation,
			Size = sizeVariant,
			RockId = rock.Id, RockColor = rock.Color,
			Seed = math.random(1, 2 ^ 30),
		} or nil

		-- === serial identity: only for catches worth arguing over ===
		-- Top three tiers or anything mutated. Commons would flood the mint store
		-- with keys nobody will ever quote in a trade.
		local tracked = MintRegistry.IsTracked(tier.Name, mutation)
		if tracked then
			-- Warm the serial block NOW, while the stone is still in the air (the skip
			-- takes 1.15-4.2s). By the time revealCatch runs the number is already in
			-- memory, so the catch itself never waits on a DataStore. Non-yielding.
			pcall(MintRegistry.Prepare, brainrotEntry.Name, mutation)
		end

		-- throw progress counts right away; the catch is granted + revealed only once
		-- the stone finishes skipping and settles in the water (see onLand below).
		SeasonPassHandler.Notify(player, "Throw", 1)
		DarrelService.Notify(player, "Throw", 1)
		if perfect then SeasonPassHandler.Notify(player, "Perfect", 1) end

		local function revealCatch(splashPos)
			local liveData = PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
			if not liveData then return end -- player left mid-flight

			-- === hard mint cap: reserve a slot BEFORE anything is granted ===
			-- Claimed here rather than at roll time for two reasons: this is the moment the
			-- item actually becomes the player's, and TryClaim yields on UpdateAsync, which
			-- the throw handler must never do. At 1e-6 this branch runs essentially never.
			--
			-- Deliberately fail-CLOSED, unlike MintRegistry above: a serial is a garnish and
			-- is fine to lose, but minting a sixth Pete cannot be undone. If the last slot
			-- went to another server between the roll and this reveal, the player gets an
			-- ordinary catch for the tier instead of nothing.
			-- The stone flies for up to 4.2s: a weekly tide flip or a season turn
			-- mid-flight must not land an away/vaulted catch. Clock-pure and
			-- non-yielding, so it is allowed on the reveal path.
			-- forcedCatch bypasses this: a test override deliberately targets
			-- entries the schedule says are unobtainable (Maxwell is questline-only),
			-- so re-checking here would silently swap it for an ordinary catch.
			if not forcedCatch and not Waves.IsObtainable(brainrotEntry.Name) then
				local fallback, fallbackTier = RarityRoll.PickInTier(pickIndex, true, throwWorld)
				if not fallback then return end
				brainrotEntry, tier = fallback, fallbackTier
				tracked = MintRegistry.IsTracked(tier.Name, mutation)
			end

			-- === UNIQUE CAP, ON THE CATCH PATH ===
			-- New here. BrainrotMover.Give documents the one-per-player cap as checked
			-- PRE-FLIGHT by every caller that can hand an item over -- trade, booth, quest
			-- grant -- and a THROW was never one of them, because no Unique name could be
			-- rolled. Chim can be now, so without this a player holding a Chim could simply
			-- catch a second one, which is the exact thing Unique exists to forbid.
			-- Falls back to an ordinary catch for the tier, same as a LimitedStock miss --
			-- the player still gets a Mythic, just not a duplicate of a one-off.
			if uniqueByName[brainrotEntry.Name] then
				local owned = 0
				for _, e in ipairs(liveData.Brainrots) do
					if e.Name == brainrotEntry.Name then owned += 1 end
				end
				if owned >= 1 then
					local fallback, fallbackTier = RarityRoll.PickInTier(pickIndex, true, throwWorld)
					if not fallback then return end
					brainrotEntry, tier = fallback, fallbackTier
					tracked = MintRegistry.IsTracked(tier.Name, mutation)
				end
			end

			if LimitedStock.IsLimited(brainrotEntry.Name) then
				if not LimitedStock.TryClaim(brainrotEntry.Name) then
					local fallback, fallbackTier = RarityRoll.PickInTier(pickIndex, true, throwWorld)
					if not fallback then return end
					brainrotEntry, tier = fallback, fallbackTier
					-- re-evaluated because the fallback may sit in a different tier; its serial
					-- block was never warmed, so Mint() will likely return nil and the catch
					-- simply arrives without a serial
					tracked = MintRegistry.IsTracked(tier.Name, mutation)
				end
			end

			liveData.Discovered = liveData.Discovered or {}
			liveData.Discovered[brainrotEntry.Name] = true
			SeasonPassHandler.NotifyCatch(player, tier.Name)
			if tierIndexByName[tier.Name] and tierIndexByName[tier.Name] >= 4 then DarrelService.Notify(player, "Catch", 1) end
			-- Maxwell's step 1 counts Secret-rarity catches. Guarded so a quest hiccup
			-- can never break the catch itself.
			pcall(MaxwellQuest.NotifyCatch, player, tier.Name)

			pcall(TungQuest.NotifyCatch, player, tier.Name)
			-- World 2's arc: this ONE hook does both of its jobs -- counting the trial
			-- tiers and rolling the drill salvage -- because both mean "a skip finished
			-- in the tundra", and throwWorld is the only thing that decides whether it
			-- is that world's business at all.
			pcall(TundraQuest.NotifyCatch, player, tier.Name, throwWorld)
			-- Mint() never yields and never errors -- it returns nil whenever the
			-- registry is cold or the DataStore is down. A missing serial costs the
			-- player a garnish; a blocked or lost catch would cost them the catch.
			-- The pcall is belt-and-braces so no failure mode can reach the grant below.
			local serial, mintedAt, exists
			if tracked then
				local okMint, s = pcall(MintRegistry.Mint, brainrotEntry.Name, mutation)
				if okMint and type(s) == "number" then
					serial = s
					mintedAt = os.time()
					local okGet, _, live = pcall(MintRegistry.Get, brainrotEntry.Name, mutation)
					if okGet and type(live) == "number" then exists = live end
				end
			end

			-- caught brainrots go to the inventory; the player places them when they choose
			-- Rolled at THROW time now, not here -- sizeVariant is an upvalue of this closure
			-- (see the roll above) because the cinematic has to be staged while the stone is
			-- still in the air. It is still rolled on the SAME catch as the colour mutation,
			-- and stored ALONGSIDE it: the two stack, so "Golden Massive" is a real outcome.
			-- nil is the overwhelmingly common result, and nil is exactly what every brainrot
			-- saved before today already reads as -- which is why this needs no migration.
			local caught = {
				Name = brainrotEntry.Name,
				PadIndex = nil,
				Pending = 0,
				Mutation = mutation,
				Size = sizeVariant,
				Uid = PlayerDataManager.TakeUid(liveData),
			}
			if serial then
				caught.Serial = serial       -- mint number within its (Name, Mutation) class
				caught.MintedAt = mintedAt   -- os.time() of the catch; proves who had it first
			end
			table.insert(liveData.Brainrots, caught)
			-- Leaderboard stat. Counted HERE and nowhere else, so it measures catches rather
			-- than holdings: trades, booth buys and eggs must never inflate it.
			liveData.BrainrotsCaught = (liveData.BrainrotsCaught or 0) + 1
			InventoryHandler.SyncBackpack(player)

			-- server-wide hype banner for top-end catches
			if tier.Name == "Secret" or tier.Name == "God" or mutation == "Rainbow" or mutation == "Glitched" then
				local rare = remotes:FindFirstChild("RareCatch")
				if rare then
					rare:FireAllClients(player.Name, tier.Name, brainrotEntry.Name, tier.Color, mutation)
				end
			end

			remotes.ThrowResult:FireClient(player, {
				Distance = math.floor(distance),
				BrainrotName = brainrotEntry.Name,
				Rarity = tier.Name,
				RarityColor = tier.Color,
				CashPerSecond = brainrotEntry.CashPerSecond,
				Mutation = mutation,
				MutationMult = Mutations.Mult(mutation),
				-- SIZE is the second mutation axis. Size drives the emergence cutscene on the
				-- client, and SplashPos is where to stage it -- both nil on an ordinary catch,
				-- which is exactly the "no cutscene" case.
				Size = sizeVariant,
				SizeMult = Sizes.Mult(sizeVariant),
				SplashPos = splashPos,
				Perfect = perfect,
				-- all three are nil unless this catch was worth tracking AND the mint
				-- registry answered; the popup should just omit the line when nil
				Serial = serial,     -- e.g. 47 -> the popup can show "#47"
				MintedAt = mintedAt,
				Exists = exists,     -- how many of this exact class are still alive
			})

			-- pity: catching a tier clears its dry streak, and every LOWER pity tier's too
			local caughtIdx = tierIndexByName[tier.Name]
			if caughtIdx and liveData.Pity then
				for _, pity in ipairs(PityConfig) do
					local tIdx = wIdx[pity.Tier]
					if tIdx and caughtIdx >= tIdx then liveData.Pity[pity.Tier] = 0 end
				end
			end

			PlayerDataManager.PushUpdate(player)
		end

		-- launch the skip; reveal the catch the moment the stone settles
		task.delay(0.16, function()
			spawnSkippingStone(player, distance, rock, function(splashPos)
				-- Cleared AFTER the reveal, not before: revealCatch can yield on a limited
				-- mint claim, and the throw should stay locked for that. pcall so a failed
				-- reveal can never leave the player permanently unable to throw.
				local ok, err = pcall(revealCatch, splashPos)
				if flightToken[player.UserId] == token then
					inFlight[player.UserId] = nil
				end
				if not ok then
					warn("[ThrowHandler] revealCatch failed for " .. player.Name .. ": " .. tostring(err))
				end
			end, throwZone, cinematic)
		end)

		-- Watchdog: if that task ever dies before landing, the flag would strand the
		-- player unable to throw for the rest of the session. Token-guarded so it only
		-- ever clears the throw it was started for.
		task.delay(MAX_FLIGHT + 2, function()
			if flightToken[player.UserId] == token and inFlight[player.UserId] then
				inFlight[player.UserId] = nil
				warn("[ThrowHandler] flight watchdog cleared a stuck throw for " .. player.Name)
			end
		end)
	end)
end

return ThrowHandler


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ServerScriptService/Modules/TradeHandler.lua =====
-- TradeHandler (Trading Center section)
-- Pet Simulator-style trading: request -> both players build an offer ->
-- both confirm -> short countdown -> server swaps the items.
-- EVERY rule is enforced here on the server. The client UI can only ask.

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local ServerScriptService = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

local PlayerDataManager = require(ServerScriptService.Modules.PlayerDataManager)
local BrainrotMover = require(ServerScriptService.Modules.BrainrotMover)
-- no require cycle: InventoryHandler only requires PlayerDataManager/BrainrotSpawner
local InventoryHandler = require(ServerScriptService.Modules.InventoryHandler)
local Mutations = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.MutationConfig)

local remotes = ReplicatedStorage.Remotes

local REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 20 -- seconds a trade invite stays valid
local COUNTDOWN_SECONDS = 3 -- final "last chance to cancel" timer

-- Both traders share ONE session table, indexed here under each user id.
local sessions = {} -- [userId] = session
local pendingRequests = {} -- [targetUserId] = { fromUserId = ..., at = os.clock() }

local TradeHandler = {}

-- === Trading Center zone check (same pattern as the throw zone) ===

local function isInTradeZone(character)
	local gameWorld = Workspace:FindFirstChild("GameWorld")
	local center = gameWorld and gameWorld:FindFirstChild("TradingCenter")
	local zone = center and center:FindFirstChild("TradeZone")
	if not zone then return false end
	local hrp = character and character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	if not hrp then return false end
	local rel = zone.CFrame:PointToObjectSpace(hrp.Position)
	local s = zone.Size / 2
	return math.abs(rel.X) <= s.X and math.abs(rel.Z) <= s.Z and math.abs(rel.Y) <= s.Y + 6
end

-- === small helpers ===

local function otherPlayer(session, player)
	if session.players[1] == player then return session.players[2] end
	return session.players[1]
end

-- Offers are name-based, so what an offer line REALLY hands over depends on
-- which copy Take() will select. Resolve it the same way Take does (the
-- least-Mutations.Mult match, READ-ONLY - nothing here mutates data) so the
-- payload can carry the winning copy's Mutation + Serial and the other side
-- sees "Golden Tim Cheese #12" instead of a bare name taken on faith.
local function resolveOffered(data, name)
	local best, bestMult
	for _, entry in ipairs(data.Brainrots) do
		if entry.Name == name then
			local mult = Mutations.Mult(entry.Mutation)
			if not bestMult or mult < bestMult then
				best, bestMult = entry, mult
			end
		end
	end
	return best
end

local function offerDetails(player, offer)
	local details = {}
	local data = PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
	if data then
		for name in pairs(offer.Items) do
			local entry = resolveOffered(data, name)
			if entry then
				details[name] = { Mutation = entry.Mutation, Serial = entry.Serial }
			end
		end
	end
	return details
end

-- Send both players their view of the trade ("You" vs "Them").
local function pushState(session, phase, extra)
	local details = {}
	for _, p in ipairs(session.players) do
		details[p.UserId] = offerDetails(p, session.offers[p.UserId])
	end
	for _, p in ipairs(session.players) do
		local other = otherPlayer(session, p)
		local state = {
			Phase = phase,
			OtherName = other.DisplayName,
			You = {
				Items = session.offers[p.UserId].Items,
				Details = details[p.UserId],   -- [name] = { Mutation, Serial } of the copy Take() will pick
				Cash = session.offers[p.UserId].Cash,
				Confirmed = session.confirmed[p.UserId] == true,
			},
			Them = {
				Items = session.offers[other.UserId].Items,
				Details = details[other.UserId],
				Cash = session.offers[other.UserId].Cash,
				Confirmed = session.confirmed[other.UserId] == true,
			},
		}
		if extra then
			for k, v in pairs(extra) do state[k] = v end
		end
		remotes.TradeState:FireClient(p, state)
	end
end

local function closeSession(session, message)
	if session.closed then return end
	session.closed = true
	session.countdownToken += 1
	for _, p in ipairs(session.players) do
		sessions[p.UserId] = nil
		if p.Parent then
			remotes.TradeState:FireClient(p, { Phase = "Closed", Message = message })
		end
	end
end

-- Any change to an offer un-confirms BOTH sides and stops any countdown.
-- This is the core anti-scam rule.
local function resetConfirmations(session)
	session.confirmed = {}
	session.countdownToken += 1
end

local function createSession(playerA, playerB)
	-- __noSave = the DataStore read failed for that profile, so NOTHING this
	-- session does can persist. Items traded OUT of it come back on rejoin (a
	-- dupe) and items traded INTO it evaporate. Refuse to open the session.
	for _, p in ipairs({ playerA, playerB }) do
		local d = PlayerDataManager.Get(p)
		if not d or d.__noSave then
			remotes.TradeState:FireClient(p, { Phase = "Error", Message = "Your profile did not load - rejoin before trading." })
			local other = (p == playerA) and playerB or playerA
			remotes.TradeState:FireClient(other, { Phase = "Error", Message = p.DisplayName .. "'s profile did not load, so this trade can't start." })
			return
		end
	end
	local session = {
		players = { playerA, playerB },
		offers = {
			[playerA.UserId] = { Items = {}, Cash = 0 },
			[playerB.UserId] = { Items = {}, Cash = 0 },
		},
		confirmed = {},
		countdownToken = 0,
		closed = false,
	}
	sessions[playerA.UserId] = session
	sessions[playerB.UserId] = session
	pushState(session, "Active")
end

-- === the actual swap ===

local function transferItems(giver, giverData, receiver, receiverData, offer)
	local moved = {}
	for name, count in pairs(offer.Items) do
		for _ = 1, count do
			-- hand over the RECORD that was actually taken, so the mutation travels
			-- with the item instead of being silently dropped
			local record = BrainrotMover.Take(giver, giverData, name)
			if record then
				BrainrotMover.Give(receiver, receiverData, record)
				table.insert(moved, record)
			end
		end
	end
	return moved
end

-- "Golden Tim Cheese #12, Pete" - enough detail in one audit line to
-- reconstruct a failed-save trade by hand.
local function describeRecords(records)
	local parts = {}
	for _, r in ipairs(records) do
		local s = r.Name
		if r.Mutation then s = r.Mutation .. " " .. s end
		if r.Serial then s = s .. " #" .. tostring(r.Serial) end
		table.insert(parts, s)
	end
	if #parts == 0 then return "none" end
	return table.concat(parts, ", ")
end

-- The swap has already committed in memory; it must eventually land on disk
-- for BOTH sides or one side dupes and the other loses. Save() retries 3x
-- internally - if it still failed, keep retrying in the background. NEVER
-- roll back the in-memory state: the other half may already be saved.
local function retrySave(player, tag)
	task.spawn(function()
		while true do
			task.wait(30)
			if player.Parent == nil then return end -- left; the PlayerRemoving save path owns it now
			local data = PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
			if not data or data.__noSave then return end
			if PlayerDataManager.Save(player) then
				warn(("[TradeAudit] %s: retry save SUCCEEDED for user %d"):format(tag, player.UserId))
				return
			end
			warn(("[TradeAudit] %s: retry save still failing for user %d"):format(tag, player.UserId))
		end
	end)
end

local function executeTrade(session)
	local a, b = session.players[1], session.players[2]
	local dataA, dataB = PlayerDataManager.Get(a), PlayerDataManager.Get(b)
	if not dataA or not dataB then return false, "Player data missing." end
	local offerA, offerB = session.offers[a.UserId], session.offers[b.UserId]

	-- Final ownership check, right before the swap. If anything changed
	-- since the offers were built (sold a brainrot, spent cash), fail safely.
	for _, side in ipairs({ { data = dataA, offer = offerA }, { data = dataB, offer = offerB } }) do
		if side.data.Cash < side.offer.Cash then
			return false, "A player no longer has the offered cash."
		end
		for name, count in pairs(side.offer.Items) do
			if not BrainrotMover.InfoByName[name] then return false, "Unknown brainrot in offer." end
			if BrainrotMover.CountOwned(side.data, name) < count then
				return false, "A player no longer owns the offered brainrots."
			end
		end
	end

	-- UNIQUE cap. Must be checked HERE, not in BrainrotMover.Give: Take() mutates the
	-- giver first, so a refusal inside Give would destroy the item mid-transfer. Failing
	-- in this block is safe because nothing has moved yet.
	-- Each side's incoming count is netted against what it is simultaneously giving
	-- away, so trading a unique item FOR the same unique item still works.
	for _, dir in ipairs({
		{ recvData = dataB, incoming = offerA, outgoing = offerB },
		{ recvData = dataA, incoming = offerB, outgoing = offerA },
	}) do
		for name, count in pairs(dir.incoming.Items) do
			if not BrainrotMover.WithinUniqueCap(name,
				BrainrotMover.CountOwned(dir.recvData, name),
				dir.outgoing.Items[name] or 0, count) then
				return false, ("%s is one-per-player \u{2014} a player would end up with more than one."):format(name)
			end
		end
	end

	local movedA = transferItems(a, dataA, b, dataB, offerA)
	local movedB = transferItems(b, dataB, a, dataA, offerB)

	-- the swap moved entries that may back Tools in either player's Backpack;
	-- rebuild both so no Tool is left pointing at a brainrot that changed owners
	InventoryHandler.SyncBackpack(a)
	InventoryHandler.SyncBackpack(b)

	dataA.Cash = dataA.Cash - offerA.Cash + offerB.Cash
	dataB.Cash = dataB.Cash - offerB.Cash + offerA.Cash

	PlayerDataManager.PushUpdate(a)
	PlayerDataManager.PushUpdate(b)
	-- Save() returning false after a committed swap = one side of the trade is
	-- now only real in memory. Log a durable audit line with everything needed
	-- to hand-restore it, then keep retrying. Never roll back in-memory state.
	local savedA = PlayerDataManager.Save(a)
	local savedB = PlayerDataManager.Save(b)
	if not (savedA and savedB) then
		warn(("[TradeAudit] SAVE FAILED after trade %d <-> %d | savedA=%s savedB=%s | %d gave: %s + $%d cash | %d gave: %s + $%d cash"):format(
			a.UserId, b.UserId, tostring(savedA), tostring(savedB),
			a.UserId, describeRecords(movedA), offerA.Cash,
			b.UserId, describeRecords(movedB), offerB.Cash))
		if not savedA then retrySave(a, "trade " .. a.UserId .. "<->" .. b.UserId) end
		if not savedB then retrySave(b, "trade " .. a.UserId .. "<->" .. b.UserId) end
	end
	return true
end

local function tryStartCountdown(session)
	local a, b = session.players[1], session.players[2]
	if not (session.confirmed[a.UserId] and session.confirmed[b.UserId]) then return end

	session.countdownToken += 1
	local token = session.countdownToken
	pushState(session, "Countdown", { Seconds = COUNTDOWN_SECONDS })

	task.delay(COUNTDOWN_SECONDS, function()
		-- token changed = someone cancelled/unconfirmed/changed the offer
		if session.closed or token ~= session.countdownToken then return end
		if not (session.confirmed[a.UserId] and session.confirmed[b.UserId]) then return end

		-- Close the session BEFORE executeTrade runs. executeTrade yields inside
		-- PlayerDataManager.Save (DataStore write) AFTER the swap has committed;
		-- if the session were still live during that yield, a Confirm fired in
		-- the gap could schedule a second countdown and run the swap twice.
		-- Closing first makes any concurrent TradeAction hit the closed guard.
		session.closed = true
		session.countdownToken += 1
		sessions[a.UserId] = nil
		sessions[b.UserId] = nil

		local ok, err = executeTrade(session)
		local finalPhase = ok and "Completed" or "Closed"
		for _, p in ipairs(session.players) do
			if p.Parent then
				remotes.TradeState:FireClient(p, { Phase = finalPhase, Message = not ok and (err or "Trade failed.") or nil })
			end
		end
	end)
end

-- === remote handlers ===

function TradeHandler.Init()
	remotes.TradeRequest.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, targetUserId)
		if typeof(targetUserId) ~= "number" then return end
		-- reject NaN / infinity / fractional ids before they reach GetPlayerByUserId
		if targetUserId ~= targetUserId or targetUserId == math.huge or targetUserId == -math.huge then return end
		targetUserId = math.floor(targetUserId)
		local target = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(targetUserId)
		if not target or target == player then return end
		if sessions[player.UserId] or sessions[target.UserId] then return end
		if not (isInTradeZone(player.Character) and isInTradeZone(target.Character)) then
			remotes.TradeState:FireClient(player, { Phase = "Error", Message = "Both players must be in the Trading Center." })
			return
		end
		-- profiles whose DataStore read failed can never persist a trade - block
		-- at the invite, not after both players have built an offer
		local pdata = PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
		if not pdata or pdata.__noSave then
			remotes.TradeState:FireClient(player, { Phase = "Error", Message = "Your profile did not load - rejoin before trading." })
			return
		end
		local tdata = PlayerDataManager.Get(target)
		if not tdata or tdata.__noSave then
			remotes.TradeState:FireClient(player, { Phase = "Error", Message = target.DisplayName .. "'s profile did not load - they can't trade right now." })
			return
		end

		-- If they already invited US, treat this as an instant accept.
		local mutual = pendingRequests[player.UserId]
		if mutual and mutual.fromUserId == target.UserId and os.clock() - mutual.at <= REQUEST_TIMEOUT then
			pendingRequests[player.UserId] = nil
			createSession(target, player)
			return
		end

		-- Tell any earlier requester for this target that they were superseded,
		-- so they aren't left waiting on a request that can never be accepted.
		local existing = pendingRequests[target.UserId]
		if existing and existing.fromUserId ~= player.UserId then
			local prev = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(existing.fromUserId)
			if prev then
				remotes.TradeState:FireClient(prev, { Phase = "Error", Message = target.DisplayName .. " got another trade request first." })
			end
		end

		pendingRequests[target.UserId] = { fromUserId = player.UserId, at = os.clock() }
		remotes.TradeState:FireClient(target, { Phase = "Incoming", FromUserId = player.UserId, FromName = player.DisplayName, Timeout = REQUEST_TIMEOUT })
		remotes.TradeState:FireClient(player, { Phase = "Sent", ToName = target.DisplayName })
	end)

	remotes.TradeRespond.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, accept, fromUserId)
		local request = pendingRequests[player.UserId]
		if not request then return end
		-- The client echoes back who the popup showed. If a newer request
		-- overwrote this slot after the popup rendered, the ids won't match and
		-- we ignore the stale accept rather than pairing the wrong two players.
		if typeof(fromUserId) == "number" and math.floor(fromUserId) ~= request.fromUserId then return end
		pendingRequests[player.UserId] = nil

		local from = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(request.fromUserId)
		if accept ~= true then
			if from then
				remotes.TradeState:FireClient(from, { Phase = "Error", Message = player.DisplayName .. " declined the trade." })
			end
			return
		end
		if os.clock() - request.at > REQUEST_TIMEOUT then return end
		if not from or not from.Parent then return end
		if sessions[player.UserId] or sessions[from.UserId] then return end
		-- profiles whose DataStore read failed can never persist a trade
		local pdata = PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
		if not pdata or pdata.__noSave then
			remotes.TradeState:FireClient(player, { Phase = "Error", Message = "Your profile did not load - rejoin before trading." })
			return
		end
		local fdata = PlayerDataManager.Get(from)
		if not fdata or fdata.__noSave then
			remotes.TradeState:FireClient(player, { Phase = "Error", Message = from.DisplayName .. "'s profile did not load - they can't trade right now." })
			return
		end
		createSession(from, player)
	end)

	remotes.TradeAction.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, action)
		if typeof(action) ~= "table" or typeof(action.Type) ~= "string" then return end
		local session = sessions[player.UserId]
		if not session or session.closed then return end
		local data = PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
		if not data then return end
		local offer = session.offers[player.UserId]

		if action.Type == "AddItem" then
			local name = action.Name
			if typeof(name) ~= "string" or not BrainrotMover.InfoByName[name] then return end
			local offered = offer.Items[name] or 0
			if BrainrotMover.CountOwned(data, name) <= offered then return end -- can't offer more than you own
			offer.Items[name] = offered + 1
			resetConfirmations(session)
			pushState(session, "Active")

		elseif action.Type == "RemoveItem" then
			local name = action.Name
			if typeof(name) ~= "string" then return end
			local offered = offer.Items[name] or 0
			if offered <= 0 then return end
			offer.Items[name] = offered > 1 and offered - 1 or nil
			resetConfirmations(session)
			pushState(session, "Active")

		elseif action.Type == "SetCash" then
			local amount = tonumber(action.Amount)
			if not amount then return end
			amount = math.floor(amount)
			if amount ~= amount or amount == math.huge then return end -- reject NaN / inf
			amount = math.clamp(amount, 0, data.Cash)
			offer.Cash = amount
			resetConfirmations(session)
			pushState(session, "Active")

		elseif action.Type == "Confirm" then
			session.confirmed[player.UserId] = true
			pushState(session, "Active")
			tryStartCountdown(session)

		elseif action.Type == "Unconfirm" then
			session.confirmed[player.UserId] = nil
			session.countdownToken += 1
			pushState(session, "Active")

		elseif action.Type == "Cancel" then
			closeSession(session, player.DisplayName .. " cancelled the trade.")
		end
	end)

	Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
		pendingRequests[player.UserId] = nil
		for targetId, request in pairs(pendingRequests) do
			if request.fromUserId == player.UserId then
				pendingRequests[targetId] = nil
			end
		end
		local session = sessions[player.UserId]
		if session then
			closeSession(session, player.DisplayName .. " left the game.")
		end
	end)

	print("TradeHandler online")
end

return TradeHandler


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ServerScriptService/Modules/TungQuest.lua =====
-- TungQuest: Tung Tung Tung Sahur's questline -> the on-ramp to World 2.
-- Tung hates brainrots. Accept, then CAPTURE a quota by rarity (5 Epic / 5 Legendary
-- / 2 Mythic -- see TungQuestConfig) via skip-rock catches; claim to unlock the
-- portal in his cellar (sets data.TungPortalUnlocked). The portal / World 2 are
-- future work -- this only sets the flag. Mirrors the MaxwellQuest pattern
-- (state machine + Talk/State remotes, server-authoritative).
--
-- SERVER LOGIC ONLY: no dialogue/tracker UI yet. The `TungTalk` RemoteEvent and the
-- TungQuest.Accept/Claim functions are the seam a future NPC-prompt/dialogue wires
-- into; `TungState` is pushed for a future tracker.
--
-- State in data.TungQuest:
--   0 = not accepted   1 = capturing (progress in data.TungCatch by tier)
--   2 = quota met, reward ready   3 = done, cellar portal unlocked
-- Counters in data.TungCatch = { Epic, Legendary, Mythic } tick on catch while == 1.
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local ServerScriptService = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")

local PlayerDataManager = require(ServerScriptService.Modules.PlayerDataManager)
local TungQuestConfig = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.TungQuestConfig)

local remotes = ReplicatedStorage.Remotes

local TungQuest = {}

local function getRemote(name, class)
	local r = remotes:FindFirstChild(name)
	if not r then r = Instance.new(class); r.Name = name; r.Parent = remotes end
	return r
end
local talkRemote  = getRemote("TungTalk", "RemoteEvent")
local stateRemote = getRemote("TungState", "RemoteEvent")

local function freshCounts() return { Epic = 0, Legendary = 0, Mythic = 0 } end

-- true once every tier quota is satisfied
local function quotaMet(data)
	local c = data.TungCatch or {}
	for _, r in ipairs(TungQuestConfig.Requirements) do
		if (c[r.Tier] or 0) < r.Count then return false end
	end
	return true
end

-- Push the whole quest picture (for a future dialogue/tracker). Step/Of = total
-- captures / total needed so a generic tracker pill can show one number.
local function sendState(player, note)
	local data = PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
	if not data then return end
	local c = data.TungCatch or {}
	local have, need, tiers = 0, 0, {}
	for _, r in ipairs(TungQuestConfig.Requirements) do
		local got = math.min(c[r.Tier] or 0, r.Count)
		have += got; need += r.Count
		tiers[r.Tier] = { Have = got, Need = r.Count }
	end
	stateRemote:FireClient(player, {
		State = data.TungQuest or 0,
		Tiers = tiers,
		Step = have, Of = need,
		Unlocked = data.TungPortalUnlocked and true or false,
		Note = note,
	})
end
TungQuest.SendState = sendState

-- advance 1 -> 2 once the whole quota is met
local function checkQuotaGate(player, data)
	if (data.TungQuest or 0) == 1 and quotaMet(data) then
		data.TungQuest = 2
		PlayerDataManager.PushUpdate(player)
		return true
	end
	return false
end

-- accept: 0 -> 1 (offered to anyone who talks to Tung)
local function accept(player)
	local data = PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
	if not data then return end
	if (data.TungQuest or 0) == 0 then
		data.TungQuest = 1
		if type(data.TungCatch) ~= "table" then data.TungCatch = freshCounts() end
		PlayerDataManager.PushUpdate(player)
	end
	checkQuotaGate(player, data)
	sendState(player)
end
TungQuest.Accept = accept

-- claim: 2 -> 3, unlock the cellar portal flag
local function claim(player)
	local data = PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
	if not data then return end
	checkQuotaGate(player, data)
	if (data.TungQuest or 0) ~= 2 then sendState(player); return end
	data.TungQuest = 3
	data.TungPortalUnlocked = true
	PlayerDataManager.PushUpdate(player)
	sendState(player, "portal")
end
TungQuest.Claim = claim

-- Called from ThrowHandler.revealCatch for EVERY catch (guarded by pcall there),
-- with tierName = the rarity tier. Counts toward the quota while the quest is active.
function TungQuest.NotifyCatch(player, tierName)
	local data = PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
	if not data or (data.TungQuest or 0) ~= 1 then return end
	local need = TungQuestConfig.ByTier[tierName]
	if not need then return end                       -- not a tracked tier
	if type(data.TungCatch) ~= "table" then data.TungCatch = freshCounts() end
	if (data.TungCatch[tierName] or 0) >= need then return end   -- this tier already full
	data.TungCatch[tierName] = (data.TungCatch[tierName] or 0) + 1
	if checkQuotaGate(player, data) then
		sendState(player, "quota")                    -- just completed the whole list
	else
		PlayerDataManager.PushUpdate(player)
		sendState(player, "capture")
	end
end

function TungQuest.Init()
	talkRemote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, action)
		if action == "claim" then claim(player) else accept(player) end
	end)
	local function onJoin(player)
		task.spawn(function()
			local tries = 0
			while not PlayerDataManager.Get(player) and tries < 60 do task.wait(0.1); tries += 1 end
			local data = PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
			if data then
				task.wait(1)
				checkQuotaGate(player, data)
				sendState(player)
			end
		end)
	end
	Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onJoin)
	for _, p in ipairs(Players:GetPlayers()) do onJoin(p) end
	print("TungQuest online")
end

return TungQuest


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ServerScriptService/Modules/UpgradeHandler.lua =====
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local ServerScriptService = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")
local PlayerDataManager = require(ServerScriptService.Modules.PlayerDataManager)
local UpgradeConfig = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.UpgradeConfig)
local remotes = ReplicatedStorage.Remotes

local UpgradeHandler = {}

function UpgradeHandler.Init()
	remotes.BuyUpgrade.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, upgradeId)
		local data = PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
		if not data or typeof(upgradeId) ~= "string" then return end
		local def = UpgradeConfig.ById[upgradeId]
		if not def then return end

		data.Upgrades = data.Upgrades or {}
		local level = data.Upgrades[upgradeId] or 0
		local result = remotes:FindFirstChild("PurchaseResult")

		if level >= def.MaxLevel then
			if result then result:FireClient(player, { Success = false, Message = def.Name .. " is maxed out!" }) end
			return
		end
		local price = UpgradeConfig.Price(upgradeId, level)
		if not price then return end
		if data.Cash < price then
			if result then result:FireClient(player, { Success = false, Message = "Need $" .. price .. " for " .. def.Name }) end
			return
		end

		data.Cash -= price
		data.Upgrades[upgradeId] = level + 1
		if result then result:FireClient(player, { Success = true, Message = def.Name .. " Lv." .. (level + 1) .. "!" }) end
		PlayerDataManager.PushUpdate(player)
	end)
	print("UpgradeHandler online")
end

return UpgradeHandler


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ServerScriptService/Modules/WeatherHandler.lua =====
-- WeatherHandler: timed lake events that spike luck + mutation odds for LIVE throws.
-- Publishes WeatherLuck / WeatherMut / WeatherName attributes on ReplicatedStorage
-- (ThrowHandler reads them) and fires WeatherState to clients for the banner + sky.
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local remotes = ReplicatedStorage.Remotes
local Mutations = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.MutationConfig)

local CLEAR = { Name = "Clear", Luck = 1, Mut = 1, Duration = 180, IsEvent = false }

-- Weight = how often this event is picked, relative to the others. The design
-- figures sum to 112.4 rather than 100, so they are normalised by the running
-- total below and act as relative weights -- the ratios are what was specified.
-- Each event's paired mutation and its odds live in MutationConfig.Events.
-- Luck AND Mut are both 1 on every event. An event grants exactly one thing:
-- a chance at its own mutation (see MutationConfig.Events). It does not make
-- you catch rarer brainrots and does not nudge the base variant odds -- the
-- mutation's own cash multiplier is the entire reward.
-- Duration is not fixed per event any more; each occurrence rolls 4-7 minutes.
local EVENTS = {
	{ Name = "Fog",          Luck = 1, Mut = 1, Weight = 30,  Tint = { 200, 210, 220 }, Emoji = "\u{1F32B}\u{FE0F}" },
	{ Name = "Sandstorm",    Luck = 1, Mut = 1, Weight = 25,  Tint = { 232, 178, 108 }, Emoji = "\u{1F3DC}\u{FE0F}" },
	{ Name = "Thunderstorm", Luck = 1, Mut = 1, Weight = 21,  Tint = { 120, 140, 180 }, Emoji = "\u{26C8}\u{FE0F}" },
	{ Name = "Blizzard",     Luck = 1, Mut = 1, Weight = 15,  Tint = { 226, 240, 255 }, Emoji = "\u{2744}\u{FE0F}" },
	{ Name = "Aurora",       Luck = 1, Mut = 1, Weight = 11,  Tint = { 120, 255, 190 }, Emoji = "\u{1F30C}" },
	{ Name = "Shooting Star", Luck = 1, Mut = 1, Weight = 6.9, Tint = { 170, 200, 255 }, Emoji = "\u{1F320}" },
	{ Name = "Blood Moon",   Luck = 1, Mut = 1, Weight = 2.5, Tint = { 255, 120, 120 }, Emoji = "\u{1F314}" },
	{ Name = "Golden Hour",  Luck = 1, Mut = 1, Weight = 1,   Tint = { 255, 215, 140 }, Emoji = "\u{2600}\u{FE0F}" },
}

local WARN_SECONDS = 20          -- heads-up before an event starts
local EVENT_MIN, EVENT_MAX = 240, 420   -- 4 to 7 minutes

-- Pacing: after an event ends, wait at least this long before rolling again, so
-- events come no more often than once every ~20 minutes. Each roll only has a
-- CHANCE to spawn one, so some windows stay clear.
local EVENT_COOLDOWN = 20 * 60   -- 20-minute minimum gap after an event
local ROLL_INTERVAL  = 5 * 60    -- how often we roll for the next event
local ROLL_CHANCE    = 0.5       -- chance a given roll actually spawns an event

local TOTAL_WEIGHT = 0
for _, e in ipairs(EVENTS) do TOTAL_WEIGHT += e.Weight end

local function pickEvent()
	local r = math.random() * TOTAL_WEIGHT
	local cum = 0
	for _, e in ipairs(EVENTS) do
		cum += e.Weight
		if r < cum then return e end
	end
	return EVENTS[#EVENTS]
end

local WeatherHandler = {}
local current = CLEAR
local currentEndsAt = 0

local function payload(w, endsAt)
	-- carry the event's mutation so the banner can advertise the real reward
	local ev = Mutations.Events[w.Name]
	return {
		Name = w.Name, Luck = w.Luck, Mut = w.Mut,
		IsEvent = w.IsEvent ~= false and w.Name ~= "Clear",
		EndsAt = endsAt, Tint = w.Tint, Emoji = w.Emoji,
		MutName = ev and ev.Name or nil,
		MutChance = ev and ev.Chance or nil,
		MutMult = ev and ev.Mult or nil,
	}
end

function WeatherHandler.Apply(w, durationOverride)
	current = w
	currentEndsAt = os.time() + (durationOverride or w.Duration or 180)
	ReplicatedStorage:SetAttribute("WeatherName", w.Name)
	ReplicatedStorage:SetAttribute("WeatherLuck", w.Luck)
	ReplicatedStorage:SetAttribute("WeatherMut", w.Mut)
	ReplicatedStorage:SetAttribute("WeatherEndsAt", currentEndsAt)
	remotes.WeatherState:FireAllClients(payload(w, currentEndsAt))
end

-- Apply an event BY NAME, looking up its real Tint/Emoji from the EVENTS table above.
-- Exists so callers outside this module (the dev weather command) cannot drift from the
-- authored definitions by hand-rolling a payload -- a wrong Tint or a missing Emoji would
-- silently give the banner the wrong colour and no icon.
-- Returns false plus the valid names when the name does not match.
function WeatherHandler.ApplyByName(name, duration)
	if typeof(name) ~= "string" then return false, nil end
	local want = name:lower()
	if want == "clear" or want == "none" or want == "off" then
		WeatherHandler.Apply(CLEAR)
		return true, "Clear"
	end
	-- exact match first, then unique prefix, so "/wx thun" works but an ambiguous stub does not
	local exact, prefix, prefixCount
	for _, e in ipairs(EVENTS) do
		local lower = e.Name:lower()
		if lower == want then exact = e end
		if lower:sub(1, #want) == want then
			prefix = e
			prefixCount = (prefixCount or 0) + 1
		end
	end
	local pick = exact or (prefixCount == 1 and prefix or nil)
	if not pick then return false, nil end
	WeatherHandler.Apply(pick, duration or math.random(EVENT_MIN, EVENT_MAX))
	return true, pick.Name
end

-- every event name, for the dev command's help text
function WeatherHandler.EventNames()
	local t = {}
	for _, e in ipairs(EVENTS) do t[#t + 1] = e.Name end
	return t
end

-- Broadcast an incoming event. Rides the existing WeatherState remote with a
-- Warning flag, so clients that only care about the live event ignore it.
function WeatherHandler.Warn(w, seconds)
	local ev = Mutations.Events[w.Name]
	remotes.WeatherState:FireAllClients({
		Warning = true,
		Name = w.Name,
		Emoji = w.Emoji,
		Tint = w.Tint,
		StartsAt = os.time() + seconds,
		Seconds = seconds,
		MutName = ev and ev.Name or nil,
		MutChance = ev and ev.Chance or nil,
		MutMult = ev and ev.Mult or nil,
	})
end

function WeatherHandler.Init()
	WeatherHandler.Apply(CLEAR)

	Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
		task.wait(1.5)
		if player.Parent then
			remotes.WeatherState:FireClient(player, payload(current, currentEndsAt))
		end
	end)

	task.spawn(function()
		-- first event can arrive after a short roll period; every event afterwards
		-- is gated behind the 20-minute cooldown set at the end of the loop.
		local waitBeforeRolling = ROLL_INTERVAL
		while true do
			task.wait(waitBeforeRolling)

			-- roll for an event; keep rolling on the interval until one spawns, so
			-- events still have their chance without being guaranteed on every try.
			while math.random() >= ROLL_CHANCE do
				task.wait(ROLL_INTERVAL)
			end

			local ev = pickEvent()
			-- tell everyone what's coming, then hold for the countdown
			WeatherHandler.Warn(ev, WARN_SECONDS)
			task.wait(WARN_SECONDS)

			local dur = math.random(EVENT_MIN, EVENT_MAX)
			WeatherHandler.Apply(ev, dur)
			task.wait(dur)
			WeatherHandler.Apply(CLEAR)

			-- one just spawned -> wait at least 20 minutes before rolling again
			waitBeforeRolling = EVENT_COOLDOWN
		end
	end)

	print("WeatherHandler online")
end

return WeatherHandler


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ServerScriptService/Modules/WheelBoard.lua =====
-- WheelBoard: the physical daily-spin wheel you walk up to.
--
-- Sits due east of the leaderboard arc at the same radius, facing back into it, so the
-- three boards and the wheel read as one ring you stand inside.
--
-- The wheel FACE is a fully transparent square part carrying a SurfaceGui. Drawing the
-- disc in the GUI rather than out of parts is what makes clean 60-degree wedges possible
-- at all -- a part-built pie either overlaps and z-fights or leaves gaps, which is
-- exactly the trap the old stone platform fell into. A SurfaceGui renders regardless of
-- its part's transparency, so the square never shows.
--
-- Spinning rotates the GUI's inner frame, not the part, so the rim, hub and pointer can
-- stay still without counter-rotating.
--
-- Built at runtime but ADOPTED if already present at the current LayoutVersion, the same
-- as the leaderboards: drag it anywhere in Studio and a server start will not move it.

local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local WheelConfig = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.WheelConfig)

local M = {}
local C = Color3.fromRGB

-- Bumped to 5: the floating CallOut was scaled down. Build() early-returns when the
-- existing model's LayoutVersion matches, so a geometry change that does NOT bump this
-- silently never reaches the wheel already sitting in the place.
M.LAYOUT_VERSION = 5

-- leaderboard arc centre + radius, so the wheel lands opposite the boards
local ARC = Vector2.new(-29.21, -28.75)
local ARC_R = 17.0
local GROUND_Y = 4.02

local FACE_D  = 8.0      -- wheel diameter in studs
local PPS     = 60       -- SurfaceGui pixels per stud -> 480px canvas
local HUB_Y   = GROUND_Y + 7.2   -- centre height of the wheel

local WOOD_D = C(104, 66, 38)
local WOOD_M = C(170, 116, 68)
local INK    = C(12, 9, 7)
local CREAM  = C(255, 242, 219)
local AMBER  = C(255, 200, 96)

local built = nil

local function part(parent, name, size, cf, colour, material, transparency)
	local p = Instance.new("Part")
	p.Name = name; p.Size = size; p.CFrame = cf
	p.Color = colour or WOOD_D
	p.Material = material or Enum.Material.Wood
	p.Transparency = transparency or 0
	p.Anchored = true; p.CanCollide = true; p.CanQuery = true; p.CastShadow = false
	p.TopSurface = Enum.SurfaceType.Smooth; p.BottomSurface = Enum.SurfaceType.Smooth
	p.Parent = parent
	return p
end

local function label(parent, name, size, pos, text, colour, textSize, align)
	local l = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	l.Name = name; l.Size = size; l.Position = pos
	l.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	l.Text = text; l.TextColor3 = colour; l.TextSize = textSize
	l.Font = Enum.Font.FredokaOne
	l.TextXAlignment = align or Enum.TextXAlignment.Center
	l.TextStrokeColor3 = INK; l.TextStrokeTransparency = 0.4
	l.RichText = false
	l.Parent = parent
	return l
end

--============================== the wheel face =============================--
-- Same fan-of-bars construction as the old panel, and the same gotcha applies:
-- GuiObject.Rotation pivots about an object's CENTRE, not its AnchorPoint, so each bar
-- is centred at half radius along its own ray.
local function drawWheel(gui, px)
	local R = px / 2
	local SLOTS, N = WheelConfig.SLOTS, #WheelConfig.SLOTS
	local SEG = 360 / N

	local mask = Instance.new("Frame")
	mask.Name = "Mask"
	mask.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	mask.BackgroundColor3 = C(26, 32, 26)
	mask.BorderSizePixel = 0
	mask.ClipsDescendants = true
	mask.Parent = gui
	local cr = Instance.new("UICorner")
	cr.CornerRadius = UDim.new(0.5, 0)
	cr.Parent = mask

	local spinner = Instance.new("Frame")
	spinner.Name = "Spinner"
	spinner.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	spinner.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	spinner.Parent = mask

	local function radial(frame, angleDeg, len)
		local a = math.rad(angleDeg)
		frame.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
		frame.Position = UDim2.new(0.5, math.sin(a) * len / 2, 0.5, -math.cos(a) * len / 2)
		frame.Rotation = angleDeg
	end

	local STEP = 2
	local barW = math.ceil(2 * R * math.sin(math.rad(STEP) / 2)) + 3
	for i, slot in ipairs(SLOTS) do
		for b = 0, math.floor(SEG / STEP) - 1 do
			local bar = Instance.new("Frame")
			bar.Name = ("S%dB%d"):format(i, b)
			bar.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(barW, R)
			bar.BackgroundColor3 = slot.Colour
			bar.BorderSizePixel = 0
			bar.Parent = spinner
			radial(bar, (i - 1) * SEG + b * STEP + STEP / 2, R)
		end
	end
	for i = 1, N do
		local sp = Instance.new("Frame")
		sp.Name = "Spoke" .. i
		sp.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(4, R)
		sp.BackgroundColor3 = INK
		sp.BackgroundTransparency = 0.3
		sp.BorderSizePixel = 0
		sp.ZIndex = 2
		sp.Parent = spinner
		radial(sp, (i - 1) * SEG, R)
	end
	for i, slot in ipairs(SLOTS) do
		local mid = math.rad((i - 1) * SEG + SEG / 2)
		local r = R * 0.62
		local l = label(spinner, "L" .. i, UDim2.fromOffset(120, 54),
			UDim2.new(0.5, math.sin(mid) * r, 0.5, -math.cos(mid) * r),
			slot.Icon .. "\n" .. slot.Short, C(255, 255, 255), 22)
		l.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
		l.Rotation = (i - 1) * SEG + SEG / 2
		l.ZIndex = 3
	end
	return spinner
end

--=================================== build =================================--
local function construct(parent)
	local model = Instance.new("Model")
	model.Name = "DailyWheel"
	model.Parent = parent

	-- due east of the arc, turned to face back into it (LookVector -X => yaw +90)
	local pos0 = Vector3.new(ARC.X + ARC_R, 0, ARC.Y)
	local facing = CFrame.new(pos0) * CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(90), 0)

	-- Two side posts, not one central one. A single post up the middle sat in FRONT of
	-- the face plane and covered the hub and the bottom two wedges; flanking posts hold
	-- the wheel at the hub the way a real carnival wheel is mounted and leave the face
	-- completely clear.
	local RIM_R = (FACE_D + 0.9) / 2
	local POST_X = RIM_R + 0.75
	local base = part(model, "Base", Vector3.new(POST_X * 2 + 1.6, 0.8, 4.0),
		facing * CFrame.new(0, GROUND_Y + 0.4, 0), WOOD_M)
	model.PrimaryPart = base
	for _, sx in ipairs({ -1, 1 }) do
		part(model, "Post", Vector3.new(1.0, HUB_Y - GROUND_Y - 0.4, 1.0),
			facing * CFrame.new(sx * POST_X, (HUB_Y + GROUND_Y + 0.4) / 2, 0), WOOD_D)
	end
	-- stub axle bridging each post to the wheel, so it reads as mounted rather than floating
	for _, sx in ipairs({ -1, 1 }) do
		local axle = part(model, "Axle", Vector3.new(0.5, 0.5, POST_X - RIM_R + 0.6),
			facing * CFrame.new(sx * (RIM_R + (POST_X - RIM_R) / 2), HUB_Y, 0.28)
				* CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(90), 0), WOOD_M)
		axle.Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder
		axle.CanCollide = false
	end

	-- backing disc, a touch larger than the face so it reads as a rim
	part(model, "Rim", Vector3.new(0.5, FACE_D + 0.9, FACE_D + 0.9),
		facing * CFrame.new(0, HUB_Y, 0.28) * CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(90), 0),
		WOOD_D, Enum.Material.Wood).Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder

	-- the face itself: invisible, exists only to carry the SurfaceGui
	local face = part(model, "Face", Vector3.new(FACE_D, FACE_D, 0.2),
		facing * CFrame.new(0, HUB_Y, 0), CREAM, Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic, 1)
	face.CanCollide = false
	-- Invisible AND click-through. Unlike the leaderboards, this SurfaceGui has nothing
	-- interactive on it, so it needs no hit testing -- and an 8x8 invisible slab that
	-- swallows every viewport click in front of the wheel makes the thing miserable to
	-- edit in Studio. Locked keeps it out of click-selection but still in the Explorer.
	face.CanQuery = false
	face.Locked = true

	local gui = Instance.new("SurfaceGui")
	gui.Name = "WheelFace"
	gui.Face = Enum.NormalId.Front
	gui.SizingMode = Enum.SurfaceGuiSizingMode.PixelsPerStud
	gui.PixelsPerStud = PPS
	gui.LightInfluence = 0
	gui.AlwaysOnTop = false
	gui.Parent = face
	drawWheel(gui, FACE_D * PPS)

	local hub = part(model, "Hub", Vector3.new(0.45, 1.5, 1.5),
		facing * CFrame.new(0, HUB_Y, -0.28) * CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(90), 0), WOOD_M)
	hub.Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder
	hub.CanCollide = false

	-- Pointer at 12 o'clock. A square turned 45 degrees in the wheel's own plane reads as
	-- a downward arrowhead, which a plain block did not. Its tip is sunk slightly into the
	-- rim so it looks fitted; that sits at a different depth from the rim, so no z-fight.
	local ptr = part(model, "Pointer", Vector3.new(1.15, 1.15, 0.35),
		facing * CFrame.new(0, HUB_Y + (FACE_D + 0.9) / 2 + 0.42, -0.45)
			* CFrame.Angles(0, 0, math.rad(45)), AMBER, Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic)
	ptr.CanCollide = false

	-- headboard: title + live state, on a SurfaceGui so it is readable from a distance
	local sign = part(model, "Sign", Vector3.new(7.6, 2.0, 0.4),
		facing * CFrame.new(0, HUB_Y + FACE_D / 2 + 2.1, 0), WOOD_M)
	local sgui = Instance.new("SurfaceGui")
	sgui.Name = "SignFace"
	sgui.Face = Enum.NormalId.Front
	sgui.SizingMode = Enum.SurfaceGuiSizingMode.PixelsPerStud
	sgui.PixelsPerStud = 60
	sgui.LightInfluence = 0
	sgui.Parent = sign
	local sbg = Instance.new("Frame")
	sbg.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	sbg.BackgroundColor3 = C(28, 44, 30)
	sbg.BorderSizePixel = 0
	sbg.Parent = sgui
	label(sbg, "Title", UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 58), UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 4), "DAILY SPIN", AMBER, 44)
	label(sbg, "State", UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 44), UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 62), "", CREAM, 28)

	-- odds plaque beside the wheel, so the in-world version still shows the chances
	-- clear of the new side post, which now occupies +/- POST_X
	local plaque = part(model, "Odds", Vector3.new(4.4, 5.6, 0.4),
		facing * CFrame.new(-(POST_X + 3.2), HUB_Y - 0.4, 0)
			* CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(-24), 0), WOOD_M)
	local pgui = Instance.new("SurfaceGui")
	pgui.Name = "OddsFace"
	pgui.Face = Enum.NormalId.Front
	pgui.SizingMode = Enum.SurfaceGuiSizingMode.PixelsPerStud
	pgui.PixelsPerStud = 60
	pgui.LightInfluence = 0
	pgui.Parent = plaque
	local pbg = Instance.new("Frame")
	pbg.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	pbg.BackgroundColor3 = C(28, 44, 30)
	pbg.BorderSizePixel = 0
	pbg.Parent = pgui
	label(pbg, "Head", UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 40), UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 6), "CHANCES", AMBER, 30)

	-- Listed by odds, highest first. The WHEEL itself stays interleaved on purpose -- the
	-- two boosts sit opposite each other and the 1% jackpot between two commons, so the
	-- pointer is never parked beside two big prizes. Only the readout is sorted.
	local ordered = table.clone(WheelConfig.SLOTS)
	table.sort(ordered, function(a, b)
		if a.Weight ~= b.Weight then return a.Weight > b.Weight end
		return a.Amount ~= nil and b.Amount == nil   -- stable tie-break for the two 15%s
	end)

	for i, slot in ipairs(ordered) do
		local y = 50 + (i - 1) * 46
		local sw = Instance.new("Frame")
		sw.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(8, 34)
		sw.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(10, y)
		sw.BackgroundColor3 = slot.Colour
		sw.BorderSizePixel = 0
		sw.Parent = pbg
		label(pbg, "N" .. i, UDim2.fromOffset(150, 34), UDim2.fromOffset(26, y),
			slot.Label, CREAM, 21, Enum.TextXAlignment.Left)
		label(pbg, "O" .. i, UDim2.fromOffset(70, 34), UDim2.fromOffset(186, y),
			slot.Weight .. "%", AMBER, 21, Enum.TextXAlignment.Right)
	end

	-- the thing you actually walk up to
	local promptPart = part(model, "PromptPart", Vector3.new(3.0, 5.0, 3.0),
		facing * CFrame.new(0, GROUND_Y + 2.5, -2.2), CREAM, Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic, 1)
	promptPart.CanCollide = false
	-- ProximityPrompt fires on distance, not raycasts, so this needs no hit testing either
	promptPart.CanQuery = false
	promptPart.Locked = true
	local prompt = Instance.new("ProximityPrompt")
	prompt.Name = "SpinPrompt"
	prompt.ActionText = "Spin"
	prompt.ObjectText = "Daily Wheel"
	prompt.KeyboardKeyCode = Enum.KeyCode.E
	prompt.HoldDuration = 0.3
	prompt.MaxActivationDistance = 14
	prompt.RequiresLineOfSight = false
	prompt.Parent = promptPart

	-- Orange ring on the ground marking the walk-in zone. Built from segments rather than
	-- one disc so it reads as an outline, and every segment is sized off the chord at its
	-- INNER radius, so neighbours meet without overlapping.
	local RING_R, RING_W, RING_N = 13.0, 0.75, 64
	local dRing = 2 * math.pi / RING_N
	local segLen = 2 * (RING_R - RING_W / 2) * math.sin(dRing / 2)
	for k = 1, RING_N do
		local a = (k - 0.5) * dRing
		local dir = Vector3.new(math.cos(a), 0, math.sin(a))
		local pos = Vector3.new(pos0.X, GROUND_Y + 0.06, pos0.Z) + dir * RING_R
		local seg = Instance.new("Part")
		seg.Name = "ZoneRing"
		seg.Size = Vector3.new(segLen + 0.04, 0.12, RING_W)
		seg.CFrame = CFrame.lookAt(pos, pos + dir)
		seg.Color = Color3.fromRGB(255, 146, 40)
		seg.Material = Enum.Material.Neon
		seg.Anchored = true
		seg.CanCollide = false
		seg.CanQuery = false
		seg.CastShadow = false
		seg.Locked = true          -- decoration; never steal a viewport click
		seg.Parent = model
	end

	-- Floating call-out above the wheel: a big SPIN and a live countdown.
	-- It used to be sized to be "readable from across the map" -- which is exactly the
	-- problem, since a screen-space billboard does not shrink with distance the way a
	-- SurfaceGui does. It is now capped (below) AND scaled to ~2/3, so it reads as a
	-- marker above the wheel instead of a HUD element pinned over the world.
	local callAnchor = part(model, "CallAnchor", Vector3.new(0.6, 0.6, 0.6),
		facing * CFrame.new(0, HUB_Y + FACE_D / 2 + 5.4, 0), CREAM, Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic, 1)
	callAnchor.CanCollide = false
	callAnchor.CanQuery = false
	callAnchor.Locked = true
	local bb = Instance.new("BillboardGui")
	bb.Name = "CallOut"
	bb.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(200, 80)
	bb.StudsOffset = Vector3.new(0, 0, 0)
	bb.AlwaysOnTop = false
	-- 220 read as "always on" in practice -- the wheel sits in the plaza and the callout
	-- was legible from most of the camp. 140 keeps it a landmark you notice on approach.
	bb.MaxDistance = 140
	bb.Parent = callAnchor
	-- heights scaled with the frame; TextScaled means the glyphs follow automatically
	local big = label(bb, "Big", UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 42), UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0),
		"SPIN", Color3.fromRGB(255, 158, 38), 36)
	big.TextScaled = true
	local sub = label(bb, "Sub", UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 30), UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 44),
		"", Color3.fromRGB(126, 255, 148), 20)
	sub.TextScaled = true

	model:SetAttribute("LayoutVersion", M.LAYOUT_VERSION)
	return model
end

local function bind(model)
	local face = model:FindFirstChild("Face")
	local gui = face and face:FindFirstChildOfClass("SurfaceGui")
	local mask = gui and gui:FindFirstChild("Mask")
	local spinner = mask and mask:FindFirstChild("Spinner")
	local sign = model:FindFirstChild("Sign")
	local sbg = sign and sign:FindFirstChildOfClass("SurfaceGui")
	local state = sbg and sbg:FindFirstChildOfClass("Frame") and sbg:FindFirstChildOfClass("Frame"):FindFirstChild("State")
	local prompt = model:FindFirstChild("PromptPart")
		and model.PromptPart:FindFirstChildOfClass("ProximityPrompt")
	local anchor = model:FindFirstChild("CallAnchor")
	local callOut = anchor and anchor:FindFirstChildOfClass("BillboardGui")
	local callSub = callOut and callOut:FindFirstChild("Sub")
	if not (spinner and state and prompt) then return nil end
	-- Applied on adopt as well as on build, so a wheel authored before this change stops
	-- swallowing viewport clicks without needing a LayoutVersion bump (which would drag
	-- it back to the coded coordinates and undo any repositioning).
	for _, n in ipairs({ "Face", "PromptPart" }) do
		local d = model:FindFirstChild(n)
		if d then d.CanQuery = false; d.Locked = true end
	end
	return { Model = model, Spinner = spinner, State = state, Prompt = prompt, CallSub = callSub }
end

function M.Build(force)
	local gw = Workspace:FindFirstChild("GameWorld") or Workspace
	local existing = gw:FindFirstChild("DailyWheel")
	if existing and not force and existing:GetAttribute("LayoutVersion") == M.LAYOUT_VERSION then
		local b = bind(existing)
		if b then built = b; return existing, "reused" end
	end
	-- PRESERVE THE PLACED POSITION ACROSS A REBUILD.
	-- LAYOUT_VERSION exists so a GEOMETRY change reaches a wheel already sitting in the
	-- place. But the rebuild also snapped it back to the hardcoded ARC spot, so bumping the
	-- version silently teleported a wheel someone had dragged in Studio -- measured as a
	-- 45.2 stud jump on X (33.00 -> -12.21) when a version-4 model met code wanting 5. That
	-- is what made the wheel "appear somewhere else in play mode" with nothing in the place
	-- to explain it. Capturing the pivot and restoring it means position now survives every
	-- future bump, while the adopt-if-current path above still skips the rebuild entirely.
	-- Note: with no PrimaryPart the pivot is the bounding-box centre, so a bump that changes
	-- the overall bounds can still shift it by a stud or so. Vastly better than 45.
	local keepPivot = existing and existing:GetPivot() or nil
	if existing then existing:Destroy() end
	local model = construct(gw)
	if keepPivot then model:PivotTo(keepPivot) end
	built = bind(model)
	return model, "built"
end

function M.Get() return built end

-- sign text: ready, or how long until the next free spin
function M.SetState(text)
	if built and built.State then built.State.Text = text end
	if built and built.CallSub then built.CallSub.Text = text end
end

function M.SetPromptEnabled(on)
	if built and built.Prompt then built.Prompt.Enabled = on and true or false end
end

return M


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ServerScriptService/Modules/WheelHandler.lua =====
-- WheelHandler: the free daily spin.
--
-- The server owns the roll and the clock. The client asks to spin, the server decides
-- whether it may, picks the slot, pays out, and replies with the winning index -- the
-- client's only job is to animate to that index. Nothing about the outcome is ever taken
-- from the client, and the cooldown is re-checked here rather than trusted from the UI.
--
-- Cooldown is a ROLLING 24 hours from the last spin (os.time based), not calendar
-- midnight. That is the literal reading of "resets every 24 hours", and it avoids the
-- timezone question entirely -- but it does mean the free spin drifts later each day if
-- a player always claims it immediately.

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local ServerScriptService = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")

local PlayerDataManager = require(ServerScriptService.Modules.PlayerDataManager)
local WheelConfig = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.WheelConfig)
local WheelBoard = require(ServerScriptService.Modules.WheelBoard)

local M = {}
local remotes = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Remotes")

-- Per-player RNG seeded off the server's own clock. math.random's global state is shared
-- with every other system on this server; a dedicated stream keeps the wheel's odds
-- independent of how many throws or mutations happened to roll first.
local rng = Random.new()

local function getRemote(name, class)
	local r = remotes:FindFirstChild(name)
	if not r then
		r = Instance.new(class or "RemoteEvent")
		r.Name = name
		r.Parent = remotes
	end
	return r
end

local spinRemote  = getRemote("WheelSpin")
local stateRemote = getRemote("WheelState")
-- Broadcast, not FireClient. The wheel is shared scenery standing in the world, so
-- everyone nearby should watch it turn -- not just whoever pressed E.
local spunRemote  = getRemote("WheelSpun")

-- seconds until this player may spin again; 0 means ready now
local function cooldownLeft(data)
	local last = tonumber(data.LastSpinAt) or 0
	if last <= 0 then return 0 end
	return math.max(0, (last + WheelConfig.COOLDOWN) - os.time())
end

local function stateFor(player, data, extra)
	data = data or PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
	if not data then return nil end
	local payload = {
		Cooldown = cooldownLeft(data),
		LuckLeft = PlayerDataManager.BoostRemaining(data, "Luck"),
		PowerLeft = PlayerDataManager.BoostRemaining(data, "Power"),
	}
	if extra then
		for k, v in pairs(extra) do payload[k] = v end
	end
	return payload
end

function M.SendState(player, extra)
	local payload = stateFor(player, nil, extra)
	if payload then stateRemote:FireClient(player, payload) end
end

-- Headline text on the wheel's sign. Shows the shortest cooldown among players currently
-- online, so someone walking past sees "ready" whenever it is ready for anyone. Per-player
-- truth still comes from the state remote; this is only the sign.
local function refreshSign()
	local best
	for _, plr in ipairs(Players:GetPlayers()) do
		local d = PlayerDataManager.Get(plr)
		if d then
			local left = cooldownLeft(d)
			if not best or left < best then best = left end
		end
	end
	if not best then
		WheelBoard.SetState("walk up and press E")
	elseif best <= 0 then
		WheelBoard.SetState("FREE SPIN READY")
	else
		WheelBoard.SetState(("next free spin in %dh %02dm")
			:format(math.floor(best / 3600), math.floor((best % 3600) / 60)))
	end
end

-- Applies one slot's reward. Returns a short description for the client toast.
local function award(player, data, slot)
	if slot.Kind == "Cash" then
		-- through GrantCash so it lands in LifetimeEarned and counts on the leaderboard,
		-- the same way daily rewards and quest payouts do
		PlayerDataManager.GrantCash(data, slot.Amount)
		return slot.Label
	end

	if slot.Kind == "Boost" then
		data.Boosts = data.Boosts or {}
		local now = os.time()
		local current = tonumber(data.Boosts[slot.Stat]) or 0
		-- EXTEND rather than replace: winning a boost while one is already running should
		-- never shorten it, which is what a flat "now + duration" would do.
		local base = math.max(current, now)
		data.Boosts[slot.Stat] = base + WheelConfig.BOOST_TIME
		return slot.Label
	end

	return slot.Label
end

-- The one place a spin can happen. Both entry points -- the in-world prompt and the
-- remote -- funnel through here, so the cooldown and payout cannot diverge between them.
function M.TrySpin(player)
	local data = PlayerDataManager.Get(player)
	if not data then return false end

	-- read-only sessions happen when the DataStore load failed; letting them spin
	-- would hand out a prize that is discarded at logout
	if data.__noSave then
		M.SendState(player, { Error = "Your save could not be loaded. Try rejoining." })
		return false
	end

	if cooldownLeft(data) > 0 then
		-- the UI and the prompt both hide themselves on cooldown, so reaching here means
		-- a stale client or someone firing the remote directly; just resend the truth
		M.SendState(player)
		return false
	end

	local index, slot = WheelConfig.Roll(rng)
	data.LastSpinAt = os.time()
	local text = award(player, data, slot)

	PlayerDataManager.PushUpdate(player)
	M.SendState(player, {
		Result = index,        -- the slot the client must land the wheel on
		ResultId = slot.Id,
		ResultText = text,
	})
	spunRemote:FireAllClients(index, player.Name, text)
	refreshSign()
	return true
end

function M.Init()
	spinRemote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player)
		M.TrySpin(player)
	end)

	-- clients ask for state on open, and once on join
	stateRemote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player)
		M.SendState(player)
	end)

	Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
		task.delay(3, function()
			if player.Parent then
				M.SendState(player)
				-- refresh here too: the sign otherwise reads "walk up and press E" until the
				-- next 20s tick, because at join time no profile had loaded yet
				pcall(refreshSign)
			end
		end)
	end)
	Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function()
		task.defer(function() pcall(refreshSign) end)
	end)

	-- the physical wheel: walking up and pressing E runs the same path as the remote
	local model = WheelBoard.Build()
	local board = WheelBoard.Get()
	if board then
		board.Prompt.Triggered:Connect(function(player)
			M.TrySpin(player)
		end)
	end

	task.spawn(function()
		while true do
			pcall(refreshSign)
			task.wait(20)
		end
	end)

	print(("WheelHandler online (%d slots, %dh cooldown, wheel %s)")
		:format(#WheelConfig.SLOTS, WheelConfig.COOLDOWN / 3600,
			model and "in world" or "MISSING"))
end

return M


===== FILE: game-src/place-full/ServerScriptService/TeleportService.server.lua =====
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local ServerScriptService = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")

local PlayerDataManager = require(ServerScriptService.Modules.PlayerDataManager)
local SessionLock = require(ServerScriptService.Modules.SessionLock)
-- The Worlds tab. Its destinations are portal Dests, so fast travel lands exactly
-- where walking through would -- see travelToWorld near the portal setup below.
local WorldTravelConfig = require(ReplicatedStorage.Modules.WorldTravelConfig)
local WorldTravelService = require(ServerScriptService.Modules.WorldTravelService)
-- Roblox's own service, not this module. Named RbxTeleport because a local called
-- TeleportService inside a script called TeleportService is a trap waiting to happen.
local RbxTeleport = game:GetService("TeleportService")
local remotes = ReplicatedStorage.Remotes

-- Fixed destinations (position, look direction)
local THROW_POS = Vector3.new(0, 6, 22)
local SHOPS_POS = Vector3.new(0, 9.53, -260) -- middle of the lodge interior (on PlazaFloor, among the stalls)
